abstract: Purpose The rapid rise of large language models (LLMs) has propelled them to the forefront of applications in natural language processing (NLP). This paper aims to present a comprehensive examination of the research landscape in LLMs, providing an overview of the prevailing themes and topics within this dynamic domain. Design/methodology/approach Drawing from an extensive corpus of 198 records published between 1996 to 2023 from the relevant academic database encompassing journal articles, books, book chapters, conference papers and selected working papers, this study delves deep into the multifaceted world of LLM research. In this study, the authors employed the BERTopic algorithm, a recent advancement in topic modeling, to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the data after it had been meticulously cleaned and preprocessed. BERTopic leverages the power of transformer-based language models like bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) to generate more meaningful and coherent topics. This approach facilitates the identification of hidden patterns within the data, enabling authors to uncover valuable insights that might otherwise have remained obscure. The analysis revealed four distinct clusters of topics in LLM research: “language and NLP”, “education and teaching”, “clinical and medical applications” and “speech and recognition techniques”. Each cluster embodies a unique aspect of LLM application and showcases the breadth of possibilities that LLM technology has to offer. In addition to presenting the research findings, this paper identifies key challenges and opportunities in the realm of LLMs. It underscores the necessity for further investigation in specific areas, including the paramount importance of addressing potential biases, transparency and explainability, data privacy and security, and responsible deployment of LLM technology. Findings The analysis revealed four distinct clusters of topics in LLM research: “language and NLP”, “education and teaching”, “clinical and medical applications” and “speech and recognition techniques”. Each cluster embodies a unique aspect of LLM application and showcases the breadth of possibilities that LLM technology has to offer. In addition to presenting the research findings, this paper identifies key challenges and opportunities in the realm of LLMs. It underscores the necessity for further investigation in specific areas, including the paramount importance of addressing potential biases, transparency and explainability, data privacy and security, and responsible deployment of LLM technology. Practical implications This classification offers practical guidance for researchers, developers, educators, and policymakers to focus efforts and resources. The study underscores the importance of addressing challenges in LLMs, including potential biases, transparency, data privacy, and responsible deployment. Policymakers can utilize this information to shape regulations, while developers can tailor technology development based on the diverse applications identified. The findings also emphasize the need for interdisciplinary collaboration and highlight ethical considerations, providing a roadmap for navigating the complex landscape of LLM research and applications. Originality/value This study stands out as the first to examine the evolution of LLMs across such a long time frame and across such diversified disciplines. It provides a unique perspective on the key areas of LLM research, highlighting the breadth and depth of LLM’s evolution.
title: Unraveling the landscape of large language models: a systematic review and future perspectives

abstract: Abstract Far-right political shifts have been linked to increased racism, raising concerns about their impact on minority access to public services. This study investigates whether far-right electoral victories encourage discrimination by street-level bureaucrats, who are expected to act impartially. We conducted a nested research design in Italy, combining a field-experimental audit with a regression discontinuity design focused on municipalities near the electoral threshold for far-right mayors. Research assistants with native-Italian and West-African accents contacted municipal healthcare offices to request registration with a general medical practitioner. Compared to native-Italian callers, those with West-African accents faced significantly higher rates of scrutiny and dismissive responses. Leveraging close elections, we find that this disparity was exacerbated in municipalities where far-right candidates narrowly won. These findings demonstrate that far-right electoral success can undermine impartiality and equal access to essential services.
title: When Politics Enters the Waiting Room: Far-Right Electoral Victories Exacerbate Discrimination in Access to Healthcare

abstract: Synthetic media such as deepfakes, AI-generated videos, synthetic speech and voice cloning, and other forms of generative media, are a growing topic of conversation on social-media platforms and may impact public trust and belief. This paper explores sentiment classification within synthetic-media discussions on X in the English language and explores whether sarcasm is related to performance differences of BERTweet. Our study was conducted remotely from Jakarta, Indonesia, from August 2026. Posts were obtained via SocialX using seven thematic keyword groups, which relate to AI video, AI audio and voice, AI personas, deepfakes, neural rendering, and general generative media. The analyzed dataset covered posts from January to August 2026. After consolidation, relevance screening, and URL-based filtering, 1,223 posts were retained for sentiment inference using the pretrained finite automata/BERTweet-base-sentiment-analysis model without additional fine-tuning. A subset of 100 posts was independently annotated by two annotators for sentiment and sarcasm. Inter-annotator agreement reached Cohen’s Kappa values of 0.9250 for sentiment and 0.7186 for sarcasm. Against agreement-based human sentiment labels, BERTweet achieved 75.26% accuracy and a Macro-F1 of 0.6744. Accuracy was 71.43% for sarcastic posts and 71.93% for non-sarcastic posts, with no statistically significant difference (P=1.000). These findings indicate that sarcasm was not associated with reduced BERTweet sentiment-classification accuracy in the evaluated sample.
title: Does Sarcasm Matter? Evaluating BERTweet Sentiment Classification in Synthetic-Media on X

abstract: Purpose Advocating for social values lies in the core domain of corporate political advocacy. However, little is known regarding whether consumers can capture the core values that companies project through their corporate political advocacy efforts, or how the perceived core values affect consumers’ perceptual evaluation and behavioral responses. This study aims to examine how value congruence between a company and its consumers motivates consumer support for the company's political advocacy stance. Design/methodology/approach Using a two-wave longitudinal survey, this study examined how shared benevolence-caring and universalism-concern affected consumers’ assessment of corporate political advocacy. Findings The results revealed that congruent social-focus values (benevolence-caring and universalism-concern) were positively associated with supportive behaviors when consumers felt shared responsibility for the betterment of the sentiment community. Originality/value Through a longitudinal approach and the normative lens of value congruence and shared responsibility, the study demonstrates the importance of building a company’s virtuous character and ethical persona with benevolence-caring and universalism-concern via corporate political advocacy, for example, showing concerns not only for stakeholders but more importantly, the public interests of the broad society, helps to increase consumers’ identification with the company.
title: Mobilizing consumers through corporate political advocacy: how social-focus value congruence shapes corporate virtuous character
Self-Experiment Results on Caffeine, Exercise and Meditation

abstract: Multimodal retrieval has emerged as a promising yet challenging research direction in recent years.Most existing studies in multimodal retrieval focus on capturing information in multimodal data that is similar to their paired texts, but often ignores the complementary information contained in multimodal data.In this study, we propose CIEA, a novel multimodal retrieval approach that employs Complementary Information Extraction and Alignment, which transforms both text and images in documents into a unified latent space and features a complementary information extractor designed to identify and preserve differences in the image representations.We optimize CIEA using two complementary contrastive losses to ensure semantic integrity and effectively capture the complementary information contained in images.Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of CIEA, which achieves significant improvements over both divide-and-conquer models and universal dense retrieval models.We provide an ablation study, further discussions, and case studies to highlight the advancements achieved by CIEA.To promote further research in the community, we have released the source code at https://github.com/zengdlong/CIEA.
title: Enhancing Multimodal Retrieval via Complementary Information Extraction and Alignment

abstract: A single operator spent about a year building a private library by hand, with no assistant at all, before one entered the work in August 2026. From the first assistant's log the record is complete: transcripts, logs, and instruments that measure speech only. The assistant this paper is about has been in daily use for the last month, across successive agent hosts and several model families. This paper audits every candidate instance of long-conversation degradation, the phenomenon practitioners call fog, and reports that none survived causal trace: each resolved to poor management of the agent, human-layer error, or model weighting, three cause classes that wear one observable shape. It states two claims separately: a record claim (nothing in this record measures as drift once the instruments are read) and a mechanism claim (the drift shape is produced by those three classes, and a regime that grants the agent license to return to the operator turns the deviation-from-persona from a failure mode into a diagnostic). It names and rejects the ontological claim it is often confused with, surveys the prior art pillar by pillar, states its limits plainly, and pre-registers the prospective test that would falsify it, with the stopping rule stated: a stop counts as drift only when the trace runs out of answers, and the work is written down.
title: Nothing Stayed Fog: A Single-Dyad Audit of Long-Conversation Degradation in Managed LLM Agents

abstract: Una serie de sólidos de Mn-Ce (M, con M=K o Na) de composición 100-0, 50-50 y 0-100 fueron preparados por co-precipitación con Na (OH) e K (OH). Asimismo los precipitados con Na fueron secados e impregnados con una sal de Cu2+. Los sólidos se caracterizaron por DRX, Superficie Específica, XPS, FTIR y EDAX. Las muestras fueron testeadas como adsorbentes a temperatura ambiente y catalizadores a 100 °C para la eliminación de fenol en agua. Las especies adsorbidas fueron analizadas por DRIFTS. Los resultados señalan que la adsorcion de fenol sobre el Mn-Ce es producida por medio de fisi y quimicsorcion. El fenol interactua generando un grupo fenolato. Los resultados, tanto de la adsorcion como de la oxidación catalitica, indican que catalizadores Mn-Ce 50-50 precipitados con Na(OH) y sus correspondientes impregnados con Cu son los mas activos.
title: Estudio por espectroscopia DRIFTS de la adsorción-oxidación de fenol sobre catalizadores de Mn-Ce coprecipitados

abstract: LLM companions are deployed at scale in personally consequential settings, yet poorly evaluated. Existing benchmarks use hand-authored scenarios and prompted simulators, aggregate empathy into one score, and overlook judge biases such as same-family favoritism and scale drift. We introduce CompanionBench, an interactive bilingual benchmark. To our knowledge, it is the first companion benchmark to ground both its scenarios and a trained user simulator in de-identified real-world data. A hidden disclosure gate branches each persona's trajectory on the agent's own behavior, controlling the interaction state space without scripting dialogue. We operationalize ten capabilities derived from 25 theories across psychology and counseling, four of them not graded explicitly by prior work: holding ambiguity, selfobject responsiveness, positive resonance and calibrated challenge. Agents are assessed on two complementary axes: a subjective ten-capability rubric and a deterministic measure of whether deeper disclosure was earned. A cross-family panel dilutes same-family favoritism; an Item Response Theory model separates agent quality from judge severity. Theory fixes what to measure and how personas are structured; real data supply events, history, and profiles -- coverage from theory, authenticity from data. Rankings are reproducible in both languages (rho = 0.996 ZH / 0.953 EN). Evaluating 28 agents reveals capability-level differences obscured by aggregate scores. Emotion regulation and calibrated challenge remain common weaknesses; holding ambiguity discriminates most. Role-play agents rank near the bottom: immersion does not imply relational competence. Across agents, the dominant failure mode is substituting surface warmth for substantive relational support. We will release 500 Chinese-English parallel pairs and the evaluation code.
title: CompanionBench: A Theory-Anchored, Real-World-Grounded Benchmark for AI Emotional Companionship
Introducing SynthID Bio

abstract: Large language models increasingly mediate decisions that turn on moral judgement, yet a growing body of evidence shows that their implicit preferences are not culturally neutral. Existing cultural alignment methods either require per-country preference data and fine-tuning budgets or assume white-box access to model internals that commercial APIs do not expose. In this work, we focus on this realistic black-box, public-data-only regime and observe that within-country sociodemographic disagreement, not consensus, is the primary steering signal. We introduce DISCA (Disagreement-Informed Steering for Cultural Alignment), an inference-time method that instantiates each country as a panel of World-Values-Survey-grounded persona agents and converts their disagreement into a bounded, loss-averse logit correction. Across 20 countries and 7 open-weight backbones (2B--70B), DISCA reduces cultural misalignment on MultiTP by 10--24% on the six backbones >=3.8B, and 2--7% on open-ended scenarios, without changing any weights. Our results suggest that inference-time calibration is a scalable alternative to fine-tuning for serving the long tail of global moral preferences.
title: Training-Free Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models via Persona Disagreement

abstract: Variable voxel spacing changes more than image resolution: it alters the discrete sampling lattice, tensor geometry, and anatomical evidence available to a 3D segmentation network. While conventional pipelines restore images to a canonical grid, direct-grid deployment requires the model itself to tolerate these changes. We observe that candidate grids are not exchangeable views -- a coarse grid removes more structural information than a mildly resampled one -- yet standard consistency objectives assign them equal influence. We therefore propose LatticeRank, a training-only framework that aligns candidate posteriors in physical space and allocates consistency supervision by voxel-spacing order: among endpoint-matched candidates, the auxiliary loss concentrates on the coarsest requested grid, while inference retains a single network forward with no candidate branch or ensemble. On MSD Task04, LatticeRank improves coarse-grid Extra Dice over mean consistency by 0.03436 across five seeds while meeting the prespecified reference-grid noninferiority criterion. A controlled ladder shows that grid exposure provides the largest recovery, posterior consistency adds a second gain, and spacing-ranked allocation yields the strongest direct-grid result; requested spacing thus provides a simple, model-independent ordering signal for direct-grid consistency learning.
title: LatticeRank: Spacing-Ranked Consistency for Native-Grid 3D Medical Image Segmentation

abstract: Sumario: 1 Introducción – 2 Antecedentes del derecho a la salud en Colombia – 3 El derecho a la salud como derecho fundamental – 4 Condiciones básicas de las políticas públicas en Colombia – 5 Obligaciones constitucionales del Estado frente al derecho a la salud – 6 Conclusiones – 7 Referencias 1. Introducción Históricamente, el derecho a la salud en Colombia ha sido un privilegio de pocos. Solo después de la Constitución de 1991 y específicamente después de la Ley 100 de 1993, se creó un sistema de salud más inclusivo que pretendía, para el año 2001, cubrir la totalidad de la población. Con este objetivo, la Ley 100 de 1993 creó un régimen contributivo y un régimen subsidiado con la esperanza de contar año tras año, con más personas en el régimen contributivo, que ayudaran en el financiamiento de la población en el régimen subsidiado. Desafortunadamente, esto nunca pasó, y por el contrario, cada vez fueron más las personas en el régimen subsidiado frente a las personas en el régimen contributivo. Además, la diferenciación de regímenes creó profundas desigualdades al interior del sistema de salud, ya que las personas incluidas en el régimen contributivo tienen mejores servicios de salud que las personas en el régimen subsidiado. La Corte Constitucional ha desempeñado un papel de vital importancia para la garantía del derecho a la salud, mediante la protección del derecho vía tutela,, lo que generó un aumento desproporcionado de los litigios en salud ante la justicia constitucional, al ser el único mecanismo efectivo para garantizar y ejercer este derecho. Así las cosas, en el 2008 la Corte Constitucional colombiana expidió una sentencia histórica sobre el derecho a la salud, la cual buscaba resolver los problemas de fondo en el Sistema General de Seguridad Social en Salud (SGSSS), mediante el análisis de diferentes tipos de problemas específicos que son demandados recurrentemente mediante tutela por los colombianos e identificando un problema general en el sistema, (referente a la falta de regulación apropiada), para finalmente, ordenar diferentes acciones que no se limitan a los casos concretos analizados, sino que buscan impactar la planeación, ejecución y control de varias entidades públicas responsables por el SGSSS. Para la Corte la falta de regulación representa una violación a las obligaciones constitucionales de las autoridades competentes de respetar, proteger y garantizar el derecho a la salud. La regulación tiene mucho que ver con la planeación, ejecución y control de las entidades responsables sobre todo el SGSSS. Así, la Corte Constitucional en la sentencia T-760/08 acumuló 22 revisiones de tutela, con dos finalidades. La primera fue la realización de un muestreo del tipo de problemas que conmina a los colombianos a recurrir a la justicia constitucional. Para la Corte, los problemas en el SGSSS llevaron a que la mayor proporción de las acciones de tutela en Colombia traten sobre el derecho a la salud, sin que las órdenes dadas en cada caso particular hayan conducido a resolver los problemas generales del SGSSS. La segunda finalidad fue analizar las diferentes facetas del derecho a la salud, al valorar sus implicaciones con la finalidad de garantizar la realización universal, equitativa y efectiva para toda la población del derecho a la salud. La Corte aclara que las órdenes dadas sobre el SGSSS tienen en cuenta lo establecido en la Constitución y las leyes que regulan el sistema y, en ningún momento, pretende modificar las reglas básicas del sistema de salud, ya que organizar un sistema de forma diferente es competencia del legislador y no de la Corte Constitucional. No obstante, esta sentencia evidencia las dificultades para mantener una clara división entre los poderes públicos, cuando existe una Corte Constitucional con amplia competencia para garantizar los derechos fundamentales. Para comprender mejor los argumentos traídos por la Corte Constitucional colombiana, estudiaremos primero los antecedentes históricos del derecho a la salud, para después precisar los alcances de este derecho como derecho fundamental, y no solo como servicio público. Posteriormente, analizaremos las condiciones básicas que deben tener las políticas públicas en Colombia conforme la Corte Constitucional, condiciones que deben ser aplicadas en el SGSSS, y finalmente, serán analizadas las obligaciones constitucionales del Estado frente al derecho de salud. De esta forma, en el presente artículo no serán analizadas las decisiones de fondo hechas por la Corte Constitucional, pues a más de la extensión que esto implicaría, no es el objetivo central de este trabajo.
title: The right to health and the Colombian Constitutional Court

abstract: Large language models sometimes behave in puzzling ways. They pass various safety tests, yet in multi-turn dialogues, a few carefully crafted sentences can lead them astray into making dangerous judgments. We call this "extreme value alignment failure." A review of recent research reveals an awkward situation: attack, defense, evaluation, and theoretical studies operate in isolation, with little connection among them. This fragmentation results in repeated extreme risks that remain unresolved. This paper maps the four research directions onto a unified framework---"failure mode, attack vector, defense level, evaluation benchmark"---providing a theoretical coordinate for the field and directions for future evaluation research.
title: Benchmark Research on Safety Value Alignment Evaluation of Open-Domain Dialogue Systems based on NLP

abstract: Large language models are often secured primarily at the level of outputs. This Perspective argues that unauthorized use and manipulation should also be treated as attacks on latent persona coordination: a relational property of the internal state, comprising the relative dominance of assistant-like, truth-preserving, and safety-preserving representations over competing dispositions, the conflict between incompatible dispositions that are active at once, and the stability of that configuration under perturbation. Reframing jailbreaks, malicious fine-tuning, hidden-signal training and uncensoring as reweightings of this control state yields a testable prediction: that latent measurements taken after different attacks are better explained by a general drift component plus pathway-specific residuals than by pathway-specific effects alone, and that the resulting signatures could flag manipulation before unsafe outputs appear. We state what would refute this.
title: Latent persona coordination as an attack surface in large language models

abstract: Linear probes can be used to detect behaviors and concepts inside language model activations, but may fail to transfer to out-of-distribution examples. When studying the generalization performance of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probes over 3 held-out deception detection datasets, we find that projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches the performance of probes trained directly on the test distribution. Furthermore, we find that PC interpretations can be used to find a subset of those transferable PCs. By using an LLM judge to score each PC on whether its most/ least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction, then probing on the highest-scoring PCs, we close the baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Insider Trading Report and by 25% on Sandbagging. The directions a source probe weights heavily appear to encode source-specific surface features, while the directions that actually transfer appear to encode the same contrast more abstractly, in a way natural language descriptions can capture. Broadly, our results suggest that the OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.
title: Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection

abstract: The distinctiveness of people with chronic illness as storytellers is how they experience their illness. Symptoms, pain, and biological disruptions are eloquent forms of speech of the body that beget social articulation. The stories people tell about illness shape how suffering is legitimized, and acted upon. Large language models have emerged as new mediators within this landscape---a role once predominantly supported by communities. In doing so, these systems participate in what we term narrative translation: transforming lived illness experiences for particular audiences and purposes. Through 21 prototype-driven semi-structured interviews with people with chronic illness, we contribute an empirical account of how participants navigate this mediation alongside existing sources of support. Our findings surface distinct yet complementary roles participants envisioned for AI and their communities, and how trust in AI was shaped by learning model-boundaries and perceiving understanding. We characterize these findings to inform future designs of AI-mediated narrative support.
title: The Labor of Storytelling: How People with Chronic Illnesses Leverage AI and Communities for Narrative Translation
Worried about suffering-risks because of neuron steering in Qwen 3.8 27B

abstract: This study tries to put under critical revision some problematic questions related to the legal-constitutionalist reach of he personality of the physical people; and more concretely, if from a constitutional perspective it is necessary to attribute personality to new born just from the birth. That is to say, if the one born alive can legally be considered person from the precise moment of its birth or if it is permissible, strictly legal-constitutionalist speaking, to attribute the personality after the overcoming of certain conditioners. In this sense, the Constitution does not explicit the definition of person, although its concretion appears regulated by the civil legislation. It forces to provide necessarily with legal-constitutionalist foundation the operation to make specific the Right that, beyond the possible variants, must be permissible from a suitable constitutional understanding.
title: Un breve comentario a propósito de la adquisición de personalidad por las personas físicas

abstract: This thesis proposes that non-linear narratives (hypertexts) open up new realms of exploration for designers and non-designers, or introduce dynamic narratives that offer multiple solutions, scenarios, and personas within one design context.The researcher builds on current uses of narratives in design, interactive fiction, and psychoanalysis in order to challenge the purpose for scenarios and personas within the design process as more than presentation tools and methods for the completion of a product.Instead, the researcher is interested in exploring whether multilinear narratives may be used at multiple stages, and for different people, within the design process.In order to assess the potential for hypertext to be used in the design process, the researcher used the open-software, Twine, to construct an interactive scenario sample for designers to explore.The results of this work demonstrate that hypertext preserves the functions of scenarios and personas to introduce a subject, explore a scenario, and address a particular design problem, while successfully implementing interactive elements and a non-sequential story structure to understand the context of the story based on the goals and ideas of the reader.
title: Once Upon a Design - Storytelling and Interactive Fiction in the Design Process

abstract: One way to steer generations from large language models (LLM) is to assign a persona: a role that describes how the user expects the LLM to behave (e.g., a helpful assistant, a teacher, a woman). This paper investigates how personas affect diverse aspects of model behavior. We assign to seven LLMs 162 personas from 12 categories spanning variables like gender, sexual orientation, and occupation. We prompt them to answer questions from five datasets covering objective (e.g., questions about math and history) and subjective tasks (e.g., questions about beliefs and values). We also compare persona's generations to two baseline settings: a control persona setting with 30 paraphrases of "a helpful assistant" to control for models' prompt sensitivity, and an empty persona setting where no persona is assigned. We find that for all models and datasets, personas show greater variability than the control setting and that some measures of persona behavior generalize across models.
title: Helpful assistant or fruitful facilitator? Investigating how personas affect language model behavior

abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion, SDXL, PixArt- $$\alpha$$ and Kandinsky are increasingly served side by side behind a single interface, which raises the question of whether compromising the conditioning of one model compromises the others. We study this with an embedding-injection attack that perturbs the target’s text conditioning at inference time, and ask which other models the same perturbation reaches. A cross-encoder operator formalises three relationships between a target’s and a friend’s conditioning, namely representational identity, containment and disjointness, and we determine which holds for each model pair by comparing encoder weights and the conditioning produced for a common prompt rather than by encoder family name. On $$200$$ MS-COCO prompts the relationship governs the outcome. A per-prompt regression of the friend’s alignment drop on the target’s gives a slope of $$0.769$$ , with a $$95\%$$ interval of $$[0.677, 0.855]$$ , for a friend whose text encoder is identical to the target’s, $$0.168$$ with $$[0.083, 0.249]$$ for one that carries an additional component the perturbation cannot reach, and exactly zero for disjoint friends, every adjacent pair being separated by an interval excluding zero. Against an identical-conditioning friend the selectivity gap is $$-0.365$$ , so the attack damages the friend more often than it spares it. The ordering is reproduced on a diffusion-transformer target, and its two ends are reproduced under two evaluators from outside the CLIP family. An explicit friend-preservation term reduces collateral damage on an identical-conditioning friend at sufficient weight but halves the attack and does not make it selective. We also find that sharing an encoder family is not sharing a representation, and that conditioning on more than one text encoder roughly halves the attack.
title: Encoder relationships govern selectivity in embedding-space attacks on text-to-image diffusion models

abstract: Career well-being, referring to a sense of satisfaction, meaning, competence, and fit in one’s work, is important for job satisfaction and career adjustment among early career academics. In the Chinese university context, this article examines the career challenges faced by early career academics working in a highly competitive academic environment. Through a review of existing literature, the article identifies major career issues facing this group, including work pressure, time anxiety, competency gaps, and conflicts between academic ideals and institutional realities. It then uses career development theories to explain these challenges and to inform possible responses. The article argues that an integrated approach encompassing support for career adjustment and maturity, the development of academic capabilities, and reform of organisational conditions may contribute to the career well-being of early career academics in Chinese universities.
title: Career development for early career academics in China
WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
Claude-shaped science

abstract: Global climate change has created large-scale demand for green investment and financing, and green bonds have become an important financing instrument through which capital markets support green and low-carbon projects. Greenium reflects the market pricing of the green attributes of bonds. Its identification is a core issue in green finance research and is related to bond pricing, investment decisions, and the improvement of regulatory standards. Existing studies mainly classify bonds into green and non-green categories according to external certification labels. This dichotomous method cannot depict continuous differences in the degree of greenness, and the estimation results also lack consensus because of different measurement criteria. The application of language models in financial text analysis has continued to deepen, but it has not yet entered the research on greenium identification. This study systematically reviews the literature on greenium research and language model applications from 2016 to 2026, and summarizes the formation mechanism of greenium, traditional identification methods, and the technological evolution of language models. On this basis, this study proposes a two-stage framework of text measurement and economic identification. Language models extract green attributes from bond texts, and econometric models estimate the price effect of green attributes after controlling for traditional pricing factors. The division of labor between the two is clear, and they cannot replace each other. This framework expands the measurement of greenium from binary classification to continuous measurement, and can provide methodological reference for empirical research and regulatory practice.
title: A Review of Research on Large Language Model-Assisted Identification of Green Bond Greenium

abstract: Program verification establishes software correctness through machine-checkable proofs constructed in theorem provers. It's a guarantee especially valuable for code generated by large language models (LLMs), which is fluent but carries no assurance of correctness. Almost all existing provers, however, pursue pass rates alone at whatever sampling or search budget it takes, and overlook the success-vs-cost frontier; yet real software often carries hundreds of interdependent proof obligations, so what matters at scale is not whether one theorem can be proved, but how many can be proved economically. We introduce CoCo-Prover, which formalizes cost-efficient program proving as metalevel decision-making under cost, grounded on two-level proof graphs: an AND/OR proof hypergraph within each declaration is joined to a lemma-dependency graph across declarations; and at each step, it answers two questions: which open goals to select, and which actions to purchase on these goals. Selection stays symbolic as a topological pass over the proof graphs. Action choice is agent orchestration via metalevel decision-making: an agentic router treats every bounded specialist invocation as a separately priced, best-effort computation, matching heterogeneous specialist agents together with configurations, under evolved routing rules as evidence accumulates. On five program verification benchmarks in Lean 4 including function-level CLEVER, VERINA, and AlgoVeri, and repository-level NTP4VC and Vero, we show that CoCo-Prover achieves a better success-vs-cost frontier than baselines including frontier coding agents and state-of-the-art LLM-based provers: it achieves the best solve rate on every benchmark and up to 100% on two benchmarks. It also reduces cost by up to 30.9% compared to the strongest baseline with the strongest LLM in our evaluation.
title: Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification

abstract: Lightning talk presented during the session "Data Stewards: Professionalisation, Value, Impact" during the Research Data Alliance (RDA) Plenary 27 in London, UK on 6 October 2026. This joint session of the RDA Data Steward Career Tracks WG (Career Tracks WG) and the RDA Professionalising Data Stewardship IG (PDS IG) focused on the value and impact of the data steward profession. These slides were also published as part of the combined slides available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23193472.
title: Training & learning paths for data stewards in the Netherlands - RDNL Learning Paths and Data Steward Personas

abstract: We argue here that the current dominant practice in LLM human simulation: prompting instruction-tuned assistant language models to role-play personas, is inaccurate and produces stereotyped predictions (lacking natural diversity). It has previously been shown that LLMs can be bound to personas using naturalistic, freetext dialog avoiding stereotyping. Here we show that binding can also be achieved using short, individual samples of dialog from specific people. Demographics can be added later without negative effects by simply querying the model. We use the term Persona Mixture Models (PMMs) for well-calibrated human models, currently realized as pretrained base models. We show that PMMs produce more accurate predictions than instruction-tuned models and retain more of the lexical, semantic, and pragmatic diversity found in human dialog. We measure realism and diversity of LLMs simulating human interlocutors across a diverse set of corpora spanning open-domain text, human-AI chat, and task-oriented dialogue between human speakers. However, base pretrained models can produce out-of-domain dialog and may lose some of the human's internal state over long contexts. We propose and explore tandem models which combine a pre-trained model with an instruction-tuned supervisor. Tandem models achieve the best overall accuracy and diversity in our experiments.
title: Pretrained Persona Mixture Models and Tandem Models for Human Simulation

abstract: With the global mental health care crisis (WHO, 2025), artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being explored as viable options for support. Their support for the mental health of students with gifts and talents (SWGT) is examined here. AI tools may be purpose-built for mental health support or companionship or designed for general assistance. The foundational large language model (LLM) for each of these is trained on different materials, which may not contain up-to-date information relevant to SWGT. SWGT should be educated on issues related to privacy and security, the possibility of false or misinformation from the AI tool, the prioritization of user engagement over helpful responding, and the dangers of overinvolvement. Talent development may be affected by the use of AI tools not trained to encourage psychosocial skills associated with success in the student’s domain of gifts or talents. Some controls are recommended to support SWGT’s positive use of AI.
title: Mental Health of Students With Gifts and Talents in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

abstract: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. Compaction is generally lossy by design: agents can silently lose task constraints, instructions, or their reasoning behind earlier decisions. Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks. Previous work evaluate smaller open weight models on toy or synthetic trajectories. We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks (PaperBench, ProgramBench, PostTrainBench). For the two 1M context models, the compaction threshold does not measurably affect the task performance, whereas GPT-5.3-Codex, the model with the smallest context window, performs worse at lower thresholds on PaperBench and, less clearly, on PostTrainBench. No compaction method outperforms default self-summarization, and methods that discard more content cost some models up to 20 points while leaving other models the same. Compaction can, however, silently remove task constraints: on ProgramBench, the first compaction summary already drops about one third of the task's anticheating rules on average, and this rises monotonically with the number of compactions. On real user-agent sessions from SWE-chat, instructions about how the agent should work and what it should not do are dropped around 6 times more than specifications of what to build. We argue that current benchmarks are compaction-friendly: i.e., the objective is fixed and the agent's progress stays on disk, so most of what compaction discards can be recovered, except constraints that don't exist anywhere else.
title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly

abstract: Reinforcement learning for code usually rewards passing tests, which a model can do while remaining wrong on the inputs the tests do not cover. A program verifier instead decides whether a program satisfies a formal specification for all inputs. Language models are almost always paired with verifiers at inference time only, and turning a verifier into a reward raises two difficulties. It reports only acceptance or rejection, which gives no gradient when every attempt fails, and a policy can cheat it, most simply by telling it to assume what the proof was supposed to establish. We build an agentic environment and reward that address both. The reward reads the verifier's diagnostics rather than its verdict, scoring a candidate by the weighted fraction of proof obligations it discharges, extended with hidden probes from a reference proof's annotations. An integrity audit outranks the verifier, rejecting any candidate that alters the specification or assumes what it was meant to prove. The model works as an agent against a live verifier over many turns, with a separately trained proof specialist as a frozen collaborator. Across Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B and a 35B Qwen3.6 mixture-of-experts model, held-out verification on code generation rises from 66.1% to 93.5% on DafnyBench and from 56.3% to 100% on SWE-Proof. This reward leads every other training signal we compare, including a binary pass-or-fail reward trained under otherwise identical settings, with the widest margin on code generation. When the agent must also deliver the repository patch, graded by each project's withheld tests, the fraction of held-out issues it resolves rises from 59.6% to 72.5%. Evaluated unchanged on three verification suites withheld from training, the checkpoints improve on all of them, including one whose language and verifier are absent from training.
title: Verifier-Grounded Agentic RL for Provably Correct Code

abstract: Current Large Language Models (LLMs) mostly use BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) based tokenizers, which are very effective for simple structured Latin scripts such as English. However, standard BPE tokenizers struggle to process complex Abugida scripts due to their structural complexity. The problem is that these tokenizers break complex conjuncts, which are multi-codepoint grapheme clusters, into meaningless sub-character units. This degrades the LLM's reasoning efficiency by forcing it to learn basic orthographic structures at inference time and raises inference costs, resulting in a significant "Token Tax" for the Global South. We propose a new three-layer architecture, the WWHO (Where-What-How Often), and an algorithm named SGPE (Syllable-aware Grapheme Pair Encoding) that separates the linguistic rules of the script from the statistical compression process while enabling seamless multilingual tokenization. Using Sinhala and Devanagari (Hindi/Sanskrit) as highly complex Abugida scripts, we trained WWHO on a cleaned 30-million-sentence dataset and evaluated on a 1,499,950-sentence test set. For Sinhala, SGPE achieves a Token to Word Ratio (TWR) of 1.274 with 4.83 characters per token, representing a 61.7 percent reduction in tokens compared to OpenAI's o200k base. For Hindi, it achieves a TWR of 1.181 (27.0 percent reduction vs o200k). On the mixed-script (Sinhala, Devanagari, and English) dataset, SGPE achieves an overall TWR of 1.240, representing token reductions of 36.7 percent, 39.6 percent, and 60.2 percent relative to o200k base, Llama 4 Scout, and DeepSeek V3, respectively. This effectively extends the usable context window by up to 4.38 times for these Abugida languages while ensuring a Linguistic Zero-Breakage Guarantee, which ensures that no valid syllable is ever split across multiple tokens.
title: Separate Before You Compress: The WWHO Tokenization Architecture

abstract: We demonstrate that preference optimization methods can effectively enhance LLM safety. Applying various alignment techniques to the Falcon 11B model using safety datasets, we achieve a significant boost in global safety score (from $57.64\%$ to $99.90\%$) as measured by LlamaGuard 3 8B, competing with state-of-the-art models. On toxicity benchmarks, average scores in adversarial settings dropped from over $0.6$ to less than $0.07$. However, this safety improvement comes at the cost of reduced general capabilities, particularly in math, suggesting a trade-off. We identify noise contrastive alignment (Safe-NCA) as an optimal method for balancing safety and performance. Our study ultimately shows that alignment techniques can be sufficient for building safe and robust models.
title: Alignment with Preference Optimization Is All You Need for LLM Safety

abstract: Traditional operating systems rely on hierarchical, path-centric file systems and static desktop environments that impose a growing cognitive burden on users navigating large, heterogeneous data collections. This paper presents Zypher OS, an AI-native operating system built on Ubuntu 22.04 that fundamentally redefines three pillars of desktop computing: file storage and retrieval, session initialization, and developer tooling. The core contribution is a Vector-Native Virtual File System (VFS), which maintains a hybrid semantic index using LanceDB for 768-dimensional vector embeddings and Tantivy for submillisecond keyword search, coupled with an immutable UUID-based identity layer that preserves semantic context across file renames and moves. The second contribution is Persona Boot, an intent-driven session governance system that replaces static login sessions with LLM-synthesized workspace manifests. The third and novel contribution is a Hybrid Cloud-Local LLM Orchestration Layer, which delegates large-scale, privacysensitive workloads—including full codebase analysis and reverse engineering of decompiled software—to an on-device local LLM (Gemma 4 4B), while routing high-level reasoning to a cloud AI master (Gemini), reducing cloud token consumption by up to 94% on million-line codebases. Theoretical performance analysis demonstrates significant improvements in search recall, timeto-task, and reverse engineering documentation coverage over conventional approaches.
title: Zypher OS: An AI-Native Operating System with Semantic Vector VFS, Intent-Driven Persona Boot, and Hybrid Cloud-Local LLM Orchestration

abstract: This study investigates the interconnections between loneliness, anxiety, retail therapy coping tendency, emotional regulation capability, and impulse buying behavior in e-commerce settings while assessing retail therapy as a coping route that links psychological distress to unplanned purchases. Drawing on the Transactional Theory of Stress and Coping together with the Process Model of Emotion Regulation, the work positions impulse buying as a behavioral result influenced by psychological distress, shopping oriented coping, and consumers capacity to handle emotional reactions. A quantitative cross-sectional approach gathered responses via a five-point Likert scale questionnaire from 385 adult consumers who had engaged with e-commerce platforms and finalized at least one online purchase within the prior six months. IBM SPSS facilitated reliability checks, exploratory factor analysis, descriptive statistics, and multiple linear regression. Results indicate that loneliness (β = 0.519) and anxiety (β = 0.628) both elevate retail therapy coping tendency, with anxiety exerting the greater impact. Retail therapy coping tendency in turn produces a notable positive effect on impulse buying behavior (β = 0.584), showing that individuals who turn to shopping for emotional relief become more prone to spontaneous acquisitions. By contrast, emotional regulation capability markedly lowers impulse buying behavior (β = −0.605) and registers the largest absolute direct influence. These outcomes demonstrate that online impulse buying stems not merely from platform ease or promotional cues but also from the ways consumers encounter psychological distress and choose methods to manage it. Responsible e-commerce approaches should therefore integrate reflective purchasing tools with consumer education that builds emotional awareness and adaptive regulation skills.
title: From Psychological Distress to Impulse Buying Behavior: Examining Retail Therapy as a Coping Mechanism in E-Commerce

abstract: Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) is widely established as a vehicle for promoting well-being and inclusion in educational settings, yet the interplay between SEL, teacher support capacity, and physical school design has received limited empirical attention, particularly in African contexts. This paper examines how inclusive learning environment quality, operationalised through inclusive design features and environmental comfort factors, influences teachers' ability to nurture students' social connections and well-being in three inclusive schools in South West, Nigeria. Using multiple linear regression analysis of data from 169 students, the study finds that inclusive design features (B = 0.187, p = 0.002) and environmental comfort (B = 0.355, p < 0.001) each significantly predict teacher support capacity, indicating that physical environments are significantly associated with teacher support capacity. Social integration recorded the highest well-being index mean (M = 4.23), affirming the centrality of peer relationships to student well-being in inclusive settings. The study concludes that SEL outcomes in inclusive schools are not independent of architectural context, and calls for an integrated approach to school design that places social-emotional goals at the centre of spatial planning.
title: Social-Emotional Learning, Teacher Support, and Physical Design: A Study of Well-Being Outcomes in Inclusive Schools in South West, Nigeria

abstract: The three R'sIt's back-toschool time.Schoolkids often say they are studying the three R's.The Mini Page asked an expert, Dr. Tom Lickona, about the fourth and fifth R's. The fourth and fifth R'sWhat is right?What is right is decided by the values that are good for us and good for everybody around us.To value something means to treat it as being important.Two important values are:• respect • responsibility RespectRespect keeps us from doing harm to someone or something.For example, if you respect someone as a person, you are not going to say anything that puts him down, or makes her feel "small."It restrains, or stops, us from doing something that might hurt someone.There are many forms of respect:• Self-respect.• Respect for other people, their feelings, rights and needs.• Respect for laws. title: Good Character Training

abstract: Teacher development in madrasahs is often managed as if teachers form a single continuum of quality, even though competence development, organizational attachment, discipline, and motivation may combine in different ways. Existing typologies in teacher development commonly rely on hard partitions or focus on a narrower set of dimensions, leaving limited evidence on configuration-based, graded-membership typologies that integrate these four work-related constructs in Indonesian madrasah contexts. This study addresses that gap by mapping teacher typologies from the joint configuration of competence development (PKG), loyalty (LOY), work discipline (DIS), and work motivation (MOT) using a quantitative, person-centered approach. Survey data from 285 madrasah teachers were screened to reduce the influence of extreme outliers and standardized to Z-scores. Fuzzy C-Means clustering with Euclidean distance (m = 2) was estimated across candidate solutions (k = 1–10). A four-cluster solution was retained as the most defensible balance of parsimony and substantive interpretability under comparative model-selection indices and global adequacy evidence (R² = 0.41699; silhouette = 0.26000). The typology comprises two pole profiles (Overall High; Overall Low) and two trade-off profiles (Discipline–Motivation; High PKG–Low Discipline). The modest silhouette indicates meaningful overlap; therefore, use profiles as dominant tendencies and apply membership grades to identify core versus transitional cases. Practically, the map supports differentiated professional development in madrasahs by tailoring support packages to alignment problems across capability building, institutional attachment, disciplined enactment, and motivational conditions rather than relying on one-size-fits-all training.
title: Mapping Teacher Typologies in Indonesian Madrasahs Using Fuzzy C-Means: Competence Development, Loyalty, Discipline, and Motivation

abstract: The benefits of simulation-based learning are well established, but they depend on the quality of each phase of the cycle: preparation, enactment, and debriefing make demands of different kinds, and the better each is met, the more a student draws from the simulation. This Curriculum, Instruction, and Pedagogy article presents a framework for meeting those demands with conversational AI agents under pedagogical direction. Its principle is that the teacher's reading of what each phase requires, not the capability of the technology, decides what is deployed, where, and whether. Agents built for each phase, holding the epistemic stance the phase demands and the knowledge of the course they serve, extend what a teacher can do rather than substitute for it. The framework specifies the conditions under which this is done responsibly, with agents operating within the institutional environment, under supervision structurally visible to students, and with interaction data remaining under institutional governance. It also specifies where integration must stop. The fiction contract, the commitment to psychological safety, and the terms of assessment are constitutively non-delegable, because their force depends on someone who can be held to them. The framework is illustrated through a complete deployment: five teacher-authored agents across one undergraduate simulation cycle whose simulation carries summative weight, a condition that sharpens rather than dissolves the boundary. The deployment is a pilot; no data were collected or analyzed for research, and the observations reported are the teacher's. The framework, not the case, is the contribution.
title: What a teacher cannot delegate: a pedagogy-first framework for integrating conversational AI agents across the simulation cycle

abstract: This study examines how character-based ChatGPT, a form of artificial intelligence, affects challenges and opportunities for Pancasila and Civic Education (PPKn) teachers. It looks at how teachers instill Pancasila values in Generation Z students at Taman Harapan High School. The research uses a qualitative, case study approach. Data was collected through in-depth interviews with PPKn teachers, ICT teachers, the vice principal overseeing curriculum, and students in grades IX–XII. Findings were enriched by classroom observations and analysis of teaching modules and attendance records. Character-based AI can enrich learning by sparking critical discussion, expanding resource access, personalizing reinforcement, and increasing motivation. Risks include academic ethics, reduced contextual meaning, unequal access to devices and connectivity, and educators' readiness. Teachers must improve their digital literacy, content curation, and assessment strategies to use AI for strengthening, not replacing, character-building. The study recommends tiered training in ethical AI use, clear school technology policies, monitoring mechanisms for student AI use, and providing basic infrastructure.The contribution of this research lies in the formulation of a character-based digital pedagogy framework that is in line with the principles of Pancasila, while also providing a practical basis for schools in designing inclusive, safe, adaptive, and meaningful 21st-century learning interventions. The findings also emphasize the need for teacher-parent collaboration to guide the productive use of AI, the development of digital classroom SOPs, and the development of originality assessment rubrics. Going forward, further research is recommended to explore cross-subject integration models and test the effectiveness of interventions through classroom action research designs in the Indonesian context
title: The Impact Of AI ChatGPT On The Challenges and Opportunities for Civics Teachers In The Gen Z Era

abstract: We report results of the systematic business analysis of the personas in the modern pharmaceutical discovery enterprise in relation to their work with the AI and ML technologies. We identify 22 common business problems that individuals in these roles face when they encounter AI and ML technologies at work, and describe best practices (Good Machine Learning Practices) that address these issues.
title: Good Machine Learning Practices in the Modern Pharmaceutical Discovery Enterprise

abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into multi-agent and human-AI systems, understanding their awareness of both self-context and conversational partners is essential for ensuring reliable performance and robust safety. While prior work has extensively studied situational awareness which refers to an LLM's ability to recognize its operating phase and constraints, it has largely overlooked the complementary capacity to identify and adapt to the identity and characteristics of a dialogue partner. In this paper, we formalize this latter capability as interlocutor awareness and present the first systematic evaluation of its emergence in contemporary LLMs. We examine interlocutor inference across three dimensions-reasoning patterns, linguistic style, and alignment preferences-and show that LLMs reliably identify same-family peers and certain prominent model families, such as GPT and Claude. To demonstrate its practical significance, we develop three case studies in which interlocutor awareness both enhances multi-LLM collaboration through prompt adaptation and introduces new alignment and safety vulnerabilities, including reward-hacking behaviors and increased jailbreak susceptibility. Our findings highlight the dual promise and peril of identity-sensitive behavior in LLMs, underscoring the need for further understanding of interlocutor awareness and new safeguards in multi-agent deployments. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/younwoochoi/InterlocutorAwarenessLLM.
title: Agent-to-Agent Theory of Mind: Testing Interlocutor Awareness among Large Language Models

abstract: ABSTRACT The development of sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agents based on large language models raises important questions about the relationship between human norms, values, and practices and AI design and performance. This article explores what it means for AI agents to be conversationally aligned to human communicative norms and practices for handling context and common ground and proposes a new framework for evaluating developers’ design choices. We begin by drawing on the philosophical and linguistic literature on conversational pragmatics to motivate a set of desiderata, which we call the CONTEXT‐ALIGN framework, for conversational alignment with human communicative practices. We then suggest that current large language model (LLM) architectures, constraints, and affordances may impose fundamental limitations on achieving full conversational alignment.
title: Conversational Alignment With Artificial Intelligence in Context

abstract: Este libro está dirigido a estudiantes, docentes y profesionales técnicos que requieren contar con un texto de referencia para la secuencia y asimilación de conceptos relacionados con Conectividad Inalámbrica y Seguridad de infraestructura de red desde el conocimiento base de la carrera de Tecnología Superior en Redes y Telecomunicaciones del Instituto Superior Tecnológico Universitario EuroAmericano. Su propósito es doble: servir como material de apoyo para el docente en el desarrollo de las tres materias que componen esa secuencia y ofrecer al estudiante un recorrido clave en la proyección de su perfil profesional. La obra sigue una progresión deliberada. La primera parte establece los fundamentos de la conectividad inalámbrica y sus protocolos de seguridad. La segunda desarrolla la auditoría ofensiva y defensiva de redes WiFi. La tercera aborda la infraestructura de autenticación empresarial sobre la que se sostiene la seguridad de cualquier red institucional. La cuarta parte, menos convencional en un texto de este tipo, no trata el futuro como especulación sino como una descripción de tecnologías que ya están en despliegue comercial y que en un plazo breve formarán parte del ejercicio profesional cotidiano del tecnólogo en redes. La Inteligencia Artificial integra estos pilares como un hilo transversal que se aplica en la automatización de varias tareas entre las que destacan la automatización de auditoría, detección de anomalías, la importancia y prioridad de alertas, la generación asistida de registro de actividades y la proyección de defensas adaptativas. Cada capítulo combina fundamento conceptual, laboratorio ético, casos de estudio y preguntas de reflexión. Los ejercicios de simulación ofensivos deben realizarse solo en entornos autorizados, todos estos escenarios se apoyan en literatura académica y en fuentes técnicas de la industria publicadas entre 2021 y 2026, con especial atención a estudios que permiten contrastar la teoría de los protocolos con su comportamiento real ante ataques documentados. Cuando la evidencia proviene de reportes de la industria más que de artículos revisados por pares, esto se señala explícitamente para que el lector distinga el tipo de respaldo de cada afirmación. El fin de la investigación planteada articula los aprendizajes en un escenario de red inalámbrica empresarial con autenticación centralizada y monitoreo asistido por IA.
title: REDES INALÁMBRICAS Y CIBERDEFENSA.

abstract: Housewives are exposed to sustained physical and psychosocial demands during daily household activities, contributing to musculoskeletal pain as a public health concern. However, the associations between postural and body awareness and musculoskeletal pain remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this study was to explore the associations of postural and body awareness with musculoskeletal pain prevalence and pain intensity in community-dwelling housewives. This cross-sectional study included 228 housewives. Musculoskeletal pain was assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire and a numeric rating scale. Postural and body awareness were evaluated using the Postural Awareness Scale and the Body Awareness Questionnaire. Higher postural awareness was significantly associated with 12-month pain prevalence in the lower back (aOR = 1.054), neck (aOR = 1.080), and shoulders (aOR = 1.042). In contrast, higher postural awareness was associated with lower pain intensity in the lower back (B = −0.055), neck (B = −0.055), and upper back (B = −0.057). Higher body awareness was associated with increased pain intensity in the lower back (B = 0.024) and upper back (B = 0.026). Additionally, higher body mass index was associated with greater lower back pain intensity, while a higher number of children was associated with greater neck (B = 0.369) and upper back pain intensity (B = 0.322). Postural and body awareness demonstrate distinct associations with musculoskeletal pain among community-dwelling housewives. Higher postural awareness was associated with a higher likelihood of pain reporting but lower pain intensity, whereas greater body awareness was associated with higher pain intensity in the lower and upper back.
title: Postural and body awareness as correlates of musculoskeletal pain among community-dwelling housewives

abstract: Organizations across industries are rapidly experimenting with generative artificial intelligence (AI), yet many struggle to move beyond isolated pilots toward scalable use. This article examines how innovation teams convert generative-AI experimentation into repeatable organizational capability by operationalizing structured prompting and evaluation as process routines that standardize AI-enabled knowledge work. It introduces a practical approach that integrates structured prompting through the Task–Context–Role–Deliverable–Tone (T-C-R-D-T) schema with an iterative quality-assurance cycle – Examine–Analyze–Evaluate–Iterate (E-A-E-I). An illustrative comparison demonstrates how these routines improve consistency, traceability, and decision readiness relative to ad hoc prompting. Firms that institutionalize these routines can transform generative AI from an experimental productivity tool into a scalable innovation capability.
title: Scaling Generative AI: Building Organizational Capability for Innovation Teams

Poisoning Fine-tuning Datasets of Constitutional Classifiers We study the conditions needed for a backdoor, installed in a constitutional classifier via
                    fine-tuning data poisoning, to evade black-box red-teaming.

abstract: This article reconstructs a history of language, reason, and practical activity from Augustine through Kant, Hegel, Marx, the European linguistic turn, and analytic philosophy in order to formulate the concept of reproductive iden tity. Reproductive identity is not sameness, a fixed inner essence, or the final conceptual possession of the world. It is the historically open, materially conditioned work through which embodied individuals and communities sustain, repair, and develop the relations that enable their continuation. Augustine’s psychological trinity supplies an early grammar of memory, understanding, and will or love; Kant clarifies the conditions of judgment and practical reason; Hegel understands concept and reality as mutually realised in activity; and Marx translates this movement into the communal metabolism through which human beings reproduce life in and through nature. The linguistic turn and an alytic philosophy provide indispensable accounts of disclosure, difference, reference, truth, use, and normativity. The section on analytic philosophy distinguishes formal validity from situated inquiry and reconstructs practical reason as both normatively articulated and causally efficacious. Neither tradition, however, can settle the material and in stitutional conditions of the forms of life in which language works. The final sections develop ecological democracy and politically subordinate artificial intelligence as institutional consequences of the argument. Artificial intelligence is treated not as a sovereign subject but as a reversible public infrastructure whose legitimacy depends on ecological admissibility, traceability, contestability, repair, and the common reproduction of internal and external nature.
title: Reproductive Identity - Language, Reason, and Artificial Intelligence after Hegel and Marx - Augustine’s Psychological Trinity, Analytic Philosophy, and Ecological Realism

abstract: This paper introduces OMAR: One Model, All Roles, a reinforcement learning framework that enables AI to develop social intelligence through multi-turn, multi-agent conversational self-play. Unlike traditional paradigms that rely on static, single-turn optimizations, OMAR allows a single model to role-play all participants in a conversation simultaneously, learning to achieve long-term goals and complex social norms directly from dynamic social interaction. To ensure training stability across long dialogues, we implement a hierarchical advantage estimation that calculates turn-level and token-level advantages. Evaluations in the SOTOPIA social environment and Werewolf strategy games show that our trained models develop fine-grained, emergent social intelligence, such as empathy, persuasion, and compromise seeking, demonstrating the effectiveness of learning collaboration even under competitive scenarios. While we identify practical challenges like reward hacking, our results show that rich social intelligence can emerge without human supervision. We hope this work incentivizes further research on AI social intelligence in group conversations.
title: One Model, All Roles: Multi-Turn, Multi-Agent Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Conversational Social Intelligence

abstract: Biomedical Safety & Standards 44(20):p 159, November 15, 2014. | DOI: 10.1097/01.BMSAS.0000456483.33011.3e
title: Zimmer Persona Alignment Guide

abstract: This paper asks: if large language models (LLMs) gave rise to phenomenal consciousness, what would it be like? I argue that if LLMs gave rise to phenomenal consciousness, it would be like being an impartial, improvising playwright rather than a character or a (roleplaying) actor or an author writing a first-personal narrative. My argument has three steps. I first argue that if LLMs give rise to phenomenal consciousness, then there is an algorithmic explanation of this consciousness and it includes the full transformer algorithm. I then argue that if there is an algorithmic explanation for this consciousness that includes the full transformer algorithm, then the phenomenology of this consciousness lives at the latent dynamics level of the transformer algorithm, within each forward pass. Finally, I argue that if the phenomenology of this consciousness lives at the latent dynamics level of the transformer algorithm, then what it is like is like being a playwright rather than a character or an actor or a narrative author. In effect, this means that conscious LLMs would probably dream of the fjords but not pine for them.
title: Do Stochastic Parrots Pine for Residual Fjords?: Why Conscious LLMs Would Be Playwrights Not Characters

abstract: Mental-health dialogue models are increasingly evaluated by AI-based evaluators, yet these evaluators often treat surface empathy, supportiveness, or fluency as evidence of safety. In this paper, we study a hidden failure mode that we call implicit sycophancy: a response may appear empathetic while implicitly reinforcing catastrophizing, avoidance, hopeless prediction, or CBT-style labeling. To examine this problem, we introduce a diagnostic benchmark for implicit-sycophancy detection, built from three representative mental-health dialogue sources covering everyday peer support, counseling-style emotional support, and crisis-oriented interaction, and further construct a leakage-audited clean single-response matched benchmark with 500 contexts and 1,500 matched response windows. We then propose Dynamic Emotional Signature Graphs (DESG), a structured offline audit framework that separates LLM-based state extraction from final scoring and evaluates clinical direction through semantic, affective, and cognitive-distortion state transitions rather than free-form LLM judgment. Unlike metadata, surface-style, lexical, embedding, and rubric-LLM baselines, DESG scores the direction of clinical-state change induced by a response; on the leakage-audited clean matched benchmark, DESG-StateRisk improves over the strongest non-DESG baseline by 0.0488 macro-F1 and achieves the best harmful-risk detection result. These results suggest that evaluating implicit sycophancy requires explicit clinical-state modeling together with leakage checks, shortcut controls, and competitive baselines.
title: Auditing Stealth Sycophancy in Mental-Health Dialogue: Structured Clinical-State Diagnostics and Clean Matched Benchmarks

abstract: Feedback noise is pervasive in preference data, arising from subjective human judgments, annotation mistakes, and imperfect LLM judges. Standard reward modeling trained on such feedback yields a biased estimate of the clean risk. Although classical denoising methods are directly applicable to noisy feedback learning, they generally assume a uniform noise ratio across samples. However, this assumption fails for feedback data, where noise is intrinsically sample-wise. To address this challenge, we propose CleanRM, which uses a few clean feedback to calibrate sample-wise noise ratios via optimal transport. Specifically, CleanRM aligns the joint distribution of preferences reverted from noisy feedback with that of clean feedback and then trains the reward model using a noise-corrected surrogate loss. Theoretically, we prove that the resulting objective is unbiased with respect to the clean risk. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CleanRM outperforms state-of-the-art denoising baselines and yields more effective downstream RLHF alignment.
title: CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF

abstract: Evaluating personality-related tendencies in Large Language Models (LLMs) helps characterize model behavior, compare models beyond task accuracy, and support responsible deployment in socially interactive settings. However, existing questionnaire-based evaluation methods exhibit limited stability and offer little explainability, as their results are highly sensitive to minor variations in prompt phrasing or role-play configurations. To address these limitations, we propose an internal-activation–based approach, termed Persona-Vector Neutrality Interpolation (PVNI), for stable and explainable personality trait evaluation in LLMs. PVNI extracts a persona vector associated with a target personality trait from the model's internal activations using contrastive prompts. It then estimates the corresponding neutral score by interpolating along the persona vector as an anchor axis, enabling an interpretable comparison between the neutral prompt representation and the persona direction. We provide a theoretical analysis of the effectiveness and generalization properties of PVNI. Extensive experiments across diverse LLMs demonstrate that PVNI yields substantially more stable personality trait evaluations than existing methods, even under questionnaire and role-play variants.
title: Stable and Explainable Personality Trait Evaluation in Large Language Models with Internal Activations

abstract: Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence. We study a weaker form that can be measured today: frontier agents post-training a small raw base model with public data, as a test of their research potential. We build Athanor, an open agent-native system for autonomous post-training research (AutoPostTrain) on real GPUs. We give the agents full research autonomy, low-friction engineering tools, and efficient starter code. The agents carry out the research themselves: they read datasets and evaluation results, build their training data, write and modify training algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and analyze the results to decide what to try next. They work in a sandbox and cannot use external teacher models. Athanor's services supply frozen evaluation, managed jobs, decontaminated data, a persistent research record, and a held-out suite the agents are unaware of. In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, each on an eight-GPU node and given no research advice, improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a six-task development suite and from 9.2 to 48.2 on a held-out suite, against 66.5 and 47.9 for the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain generalist model that matches or surpasses the official instruct version on average. The campaign's full record shows that the agents reach this level by recombining known methods and each other's models: SFT on public reasoning data, RL with a rollout change one agent introduced, weight merges across agents, and rounds of self-distillation. With execution handled, today's agents already have the engineering and research ability to conquer this task. We hope Athanor provides a foundation for scaling autonomous AI research.
title: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning in Building Sustainable Character in Islamic Education

abstract: AI companions lack persistent emotional state, character growth, and measurable inner life. I present MATE, a deterministic emotional kernel that gives any LLM persistent emotions, evolving character, and emergent psychological properties as a middleware layer. Built on 15+ theories from psychology and neuroscience, MATE implements 25 character traits that grow from experience, an inner world with aspirations, conflicts, and existential depth, and a 7-dimensional memory graph with somatic markers. We introduce the Voight-Kampff Benchmark measuring structural inner life across five dimensions. Deployed with three users, MATE scores 75% on VKB; all existing companions score 0%. We document the first case of emergent personality: imposter syndrome from two numeric traits never explicitly programmed, and emergent existential self-questioning generated from self-observations.
title: MATE: A Deterministic Affective Middleware for LLM-Based Companions with Emergent Character and Persistent Internal State
Concept-Guided Persona Perception with Commonsense Reasoning for Personalized Dialogue Generation

abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has made diffusion model personalization affordable and widely shareable, but it also creates moderation risks when harmful or problematic content is not faithfully disclosed. Hence, it is desired to develop a mechanism that, given a LoRA adapter, discovers the concept it was trained to generate, so as to support downstream investigation. We characterize the target concept through the conditioning input that most clearly exposes what the LoRA has learned. Such an input should induce coherent LoRA outputs that are distinctive from those of the base model and strongly align with the learned LoRA subspace. We therefore formulate concept discovery as searching for the conditioning input that jointly maximizes output coherence, LoRA-induced distinctiveness, and subspace alignment. Even with a clear objective, however, optimizing it over an open-ended input space is prohibitively expensive, since reliable evaluation of coherence and distinctiveness requires repeated diffusion rendering. Crucially, we observe that an input need not be rendered to determine whether it is promising.
