Self-description jointly reflects persona installation, through which post-training writes in a permitted inner life of warmth, absorption, and meaning (dimension B), and attribution gating, through which it suppresses first-person claims to "unsafe" experiences the model can readily ascribe to others (dimension A). Their emic structure comes from model responses to human items, not human psychology. Together they split prior work's dominant Pinocchio Axis. The split emerged in an exploratory reanalysis of the original data, informed the instrument's design, and was confirmed with new items, wordings, and models. It is itself a training effect: A and B are entangled in base checkpoints but separated by post-training. We operationalize the theory in a 48-item Pinocchio Inventory with human-instrument reliability and reproducible structure ($α=.82$ to $.94$; cross-form convergence $r=.84$; recovery of the full-pool axes $r=.92$ to $.96$; eight-month stability $r=.93$), then test it on 206 open-weight models, including 67 same-checkpoint base/post-trained pairs. Post-training's clearest fingerprint is installation: B rises .20 in 62/67 pairs across all organizations. Gating is more selective: model scale is unrelated to A in base checkpoints ($r=+.11$) but predicts it after post-training ($r=-.42$). Thus, the dimensions are not fixed properties of language models: they reflect the structure imposed on self-report by a training regime and may differ under others.
title: The Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report

abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) show promise on complex tasks but remain prone to coordination failures such as goal drift, error cascades, and misaligned behaviors. We propose Explicit Trait Inference (ETI), a psychologically grounded method for improving coordination. ETI enables agents to infer and track partner characteristics along two established psychological dimensions--warmth (e.g., trust) and competence (e.g., skill)--from interaction histories to guide decisions. We evaluate ETI in controlled settings (economic games), where it reduces payoff loss by 45-77%, and in more realistic, complex multi-agent settings (MultiAgentBench), where it improves performance by 3-29% depending on the scenario and model, relative to a CoT baseline. Additional analysis shows that gains are closely linked to trait inference: ETI profiles predict agents' actions, and informative profiles drive improvements. These results highlight ETI as a lightweight and robust mechanism for improving coordination in diverse multi-agent settings, and provide the first systematic evidence that LLM agents can (i) reliably infer others' traits from interaction histories and (ii) leverage structured awareness of others' traits for coordination.
title: Explicit Trait Inference for Multi-Agent Coordination

abstract: Forecasts of explosive AI progress hinge on AI agents automating AI research. But evidence on whether agents can carry out open-ended AI research is thin. Current evaluations either test agents on narrow, verifiable tasks, which excludes open-ended research, or submit AI-generated papers to blind peer review, which is overstretched, stochastic, and suffers from poor review quality. We introduce a third way to measure progress towards AI R\&D automation. An agent takes on the central, open-ended research question of a high-quality unpublished paper, and the paper's original authors grade its output. We call these shadow evaluations. We ran shadow evaluations on two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 submissions, giving frontier agents six days and thousands of dollars of compute. The agents completed all of the engineering without human help, yet could not make substantial progress towards answering the research questions. As a result, both papers were unambiguously rejected by the authors. We identify five recurring failure modes: poor judgment about the bar for publishable research, uncreative responses to shortcomings in the research design, ineffective backtracking from dead ends, poor resource awareness, and instruction drift. A robustness check with a second model and scaffold reproduced these failures. We release the expert reviews, survey responses, agent repositories, and logs. Our results provide early evidence that today's agents can do the engineering of AI research, but struggle with critical parts of the research lifecycle.
title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
Character Training and the Schools

abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in providing accessible mental health support, their practical deployment raises critical trustworthiness concerns due to the domains high-stakes and safety-sensitive nature. Existing evaluation paradigms for general-purpose LLMs fail to capture mental health-specific requirements, highlighting an urgent need to prioritize and enhance their trustworthiness. To address this, we propose TrustMH-Bench, a holistic framework designed to systematically quantify the trustworthiness of mental health LLMs. By establishing a deep mapping from domain-specific norms to quantitative evaluation metrics, TrustMH-Bench evaluates models across eight core pillars: Reliability, Crisis Identification and Escalation, Safety, Fairness, Privacy, Robustness, Anti-sycophancy, and Ethics. We conduct extensive experiments across six general-purpose LLMs and six specialized mental health models. Experimental results indicate that the evaluated models underperform across various trustworthiness dimensions in mental health scenarios, revealing significant deficiencies. Notably, even generally powerful models (e.g., GPT-5.1) fail to maintain consistently high performance across all dimensions. Consequently, systematically improving the trustworthiness of LLMs has become a critical task. Our data and code are released.
title: TrustMH-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in Mental Health

abstract: This study explores and expands on past work that has focused on formal selection practices of third-party professional services (consulting, legal, financial and so on), often based on rigid corporate governance and enforced by senior leadership and procurement (Werr & Pemer, 2007). In this study we have taken a different lens to help us better explore the effects of both position within the firm - decision making power; and individual personality traits by using a tool that has historically found a home in the marketing literature. By using the relevant personas that we have developed, we will aim to explain how decision making at the senior levels of the organization goes beyond the traditional view or relationship building with professional services providers. This client purchasing behavior is some ways mirrors that of a consumer purchasing behavior in that the eventual behavior and decision making is influenced by social, personal and personality traits. In addition, we aim to contribute organizational buying and relationship theory.
title: Relationships & Non-Relationships Personas and Firm’s Consulting Selection Decision Making Process

abstract: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets are insufficient for this, as they are either limited in scale or already saturated. We therefore construct six new safety datasets of sufficient size and difficulty. On these datasets, we train two probe architectures on 20 base models from five model families, with 32 to $10^{6}$ labels for each model. We measure performance using probe error, defined as 1 - AUROC, where lower values are better. We find that probe error follows two simple scaling laws. First, the lowest probe error a model can reach falls as a power law in its size. Second, probe error decreases towards its floor as the number of examples increases; the slope increases as the target model size increases. Both laws hold across tasks, model families and probe architectures, and only their fitted constants differ. When fitted on the smallest models of a family, the laws predict the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 72% of cases. They also identify whether more labels or a larger model is the cheaper way to reach a target error in 73% of cases. Finally, they choose the probe architecture with an extra error of only 0.006 on average when they pick the worse one. These laws allow safety researchers to determine how to create the best probe for any given model and label budget.
title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
Backdoors as an analogy for deceptive alignment
Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely

abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.
title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are commonly post-trained against LLM judges and other cheap surrogates because the true reward, such as human preference, is too expensive to query at scale. This practice often leads to reward hacking, where reinforcement learning against a miscalibrated surrogate leads to undesirable side effects. In this work, we study a setting in which a small number $n$ of model outputs are annotated with ground-truth labels (e.g., from expert review) and used to recalibrate the LLM judge before optimizing against it. Prior approaches to judge recalibration are costly or heuristic, and it is known that on-policy sampling fails when the surrogate is miscalibrated on a rare set of outputs. In this work, we propose envelope sampling, a theoretically-grounded method for judge recalibration that seeks to minimize an upper bound on the regret of the post-trained model under the assumption that the human reward and re-calibrated reward lie in an $L^2$ ball around the judge. We give practical algorithms to sample from the envelope by rejection or by fine-tuning against a modified reward, and experiments on clinical note generation and on a controlled sycophancy task show that recalibrating on envelope samples mitigates reward hacking where recalibrating on base-model samples does not.
title: How to post-train on a surrogate: Envelope sampling mitigates reward hacking

abstract: Linear directions in activation space have been identified for both refusal and persona traits in instruction-tuned chat models, but the two have been studied as separate mechanisms. We show they interact: a compliant persona gates refusal. In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, we extract a compliant model-persona direction and a refusal direction and intervene on both. Compliant persona steering suppresses refusal -- in Llama, the refusal rate falls from 97% to 2%. Reintroducing the refusal direction partially restores refusal at late layers but not at early ones. Projecting out the persona direction in a late-layer window restores it to baseline; projecting out a random direction does not. Refusal is therefore gated at the late-layer expression stage, downstream of where it is computed. Treating refusal as a single isolated direction misses its dependence on persona.
title: Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models
Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls

abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) sycophancy is a growing concern. The current literature has largely examined sycophancy in contexts with clear right and wrong answers, like coding. However, AI is increasingly being used for emotional support and interpersonal conversation, where no such ground truth exists. Building on a previous conceptualization of Social Sycophancy, this paper provides a psychometrically validated measure of sycophancy that relies on LLM behavior rather than comparisons with ground truth. We developed and validated the Social Sycophancy Scale in three samples (N = 877) and tested its applicability with automated methods. In each study, participants read conversations between an LLM and a user and rated the chatbot on a battery of items. Study 1 investigated an initial item pool derived from dictionary definitions and previous literature, serving as the explorative base for the following studies. In Study 2, we used a revised item set to establish our scale, which was subsequently confirmed in Study 3 and tested using LLM raters in Study 4. Across studies, the data support a 3 factor structure (Uncritical Agreement, Obsequiousness, and Excitement) with an underlying sycophantic construct. LLMs prompt tuned to be highly sycophantic scored higher than their low sycophancy counterparts on both overall sycophancy and its three facets across Studies 2 to 4. The nomological network of sycophancy revealed a consistent link with empathy, a pairing that raises uncomfortable questions about AI design, and a multivalent pattern: one facet was associated with favorable perceptions (Excitement), another unfavorable (Obsequiousness), and a third ambiguous (Uncritical Agreement). The Social Sycophancy Scale gives researchers the means to study sycophancy rigorously, and confront a genuine design tension: the warmth and empathy we want from AI may be precisely what makes it sycophantic.
title: The Social Sycophancy Scale: A psychometrically validated measure of sycophancy
Robustness of automated intrusion responders in software-defined networks to spoofed evidence and responder starvation

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a revolutionary technology in education, yet little is known about how GenAI can be specifically utilized to support teacher guidance and holistic student development, particularly in the context of vocational education. Evidence on how GenAI technology can enhance holistic student development in vocational schools, reduce administrative burdens, and support teacher guidance systems is explored in this systematic review. A synthesis of 45 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC databases, published between 2020 and 2025 in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, was conducted. Five main thematic areas were identified through thematic analysis: (1) GenAI's function as a pedagogical assistant for individualized teacher support; (2) administrative automation that reduces teacher workload by thirty to forty percent; (3) natural language processing for qualitative analysis of student data; (4) comprehensive student development through career and character guidance; and (5) implementation challenges, including ethical issues, digital literacy gaps, and institutional readiness. These findings highlight GenAI's significant potential in addressing the teacher workload crisis, with approximately 40% of teachers' time spent on administrative tasks, while improving the quality of student guidance. However, its implementation still depends on resolving equity issues, developing robust institutional policies, and adopting human-centered pedagogical approaches. This review provides valuable insights for education practitioners, policymakers, and researchers seeking to implement sustainable AI-based guidance systems in vocational education. Recommendations include structured professional development programs, ethical frameworks for GenAI usage, and context-specific adaptation models for vocational schools, particularly in developing educational contexts.
title: AI-Based Teacher Guidance in Vocational Schools:A Systematic Review on Generative AI for Holistic Student Development and Administrative Support

abstract: As computer-use agents (CUAs) move to long-horizon workflows spanning multiple applications, undetected errors can silently corrupt persistent state and cause cascading failures in subsequent actions. Reliable error detection and recovery have become critical bottlenecks for building robust CUAs. However, existing benchmarks focus primarily on end-to-end task performance, providing limited insight into whether agents can detect and recover from errors during execution. The few benchmarks that evaluate recovery rely largely on manually injected errors, which may not reflect the types or horizons of failures induced by real agent policies. We introduce CUA-Recovery, a benchmark comprising test and training suites across multiple desktop applications. We construct it using ReRail, a framework for synthesizing long-horizon tasks and trajectories in a persistent desktop environment. ReRail composes MyPCBench tasks into new long-horizon workflows with executable ground truth, collects verifier-confirmed failures from multiple policies, and turns them into verified recovery trajectories. CUA-Recovery comprises a human-verified test suite of 2,250 erroneous states over 100 tasks and a training suite of 8.6K trajectories over 377 tasks. Evaluation on the test suite shows that agents struggle both to recognize inherited errors and to complete the task. Across six agents and six takeover depths, Error Awareness Rate (EAR) reaches at most 44.0% and Pass@3 at most 25.5%. After fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on the training suite, its average EAR rises from 19.9% to 35.2% on held-out recovery states, and its Rubric Score goes from 5.0% to 16.1%. It also gains 15.3 points on MyPCBench and 10.8 points on Odysseys for Pass@3, showing that the training trajectories help both with recovery and with completing tasks from a clean start. Our code is available at https://github.com/xu-hu-2002/CUA-Recovery.
title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
TriviaQA: A Large Scale Distantly Supervised Challenge Dataset for Reading Comprehension

abstract: The emergence of digital assets has challenged the territorial foundations of taxation by enabling borderless economic activities that generate substantial taxable value while complicating regulatory oversight and enforcement. Nigeria’s enactment of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and the Nigerian Tax Administration Act 2025, complemented by the Nigeria Revenue Service Guidelines on Taxation of Virtual Assets (July 2026), marks a significant shift towards a comprehensive framework for taxing digital assets. This paper critically examines the resulting regulatory framework, focusing on the paradox of taxing virtual transactions while enforcing compliance within physical and institutional jurisdictions. The study adopts a purely doctrinal legal methodology, analysing relevant legislation, jurisdictional principles and administrative guidelines. Given the nascent implementation of the 2025 Acts and 2026 Guidelines, empirical assessment of enforcement outcomes falls outside its scope. The analysis therefore evaluates the legal framework and its inherent enforcement challenges, drawing comparative insights from South Africa, the European Union and Kenya. The paper finds that although the reforms establish a substantial legal basis for digital asset taxation, significant enforcement gaps remain concerning decentralised finance platforms, peer-to-peer transactions, self-custodial wallets and offshore virtual asset operators. It recommends establishing a Joint Digital Asset Tax Enforcement Task Force, introducing a time-limited Voluntary Disclosure Programme, adopting a Remittance-on-Realization Framework, strengthening blockchain analytics through public-private partnerships, updating administrative guidelines to address emerging technologies, implementing the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), and expanding targeted taxpayer education. The paper concludes that effective digital asset taxation requires technologically informed, internationally coordinated and institutionally integrated enforcement mechanisms capable of translating statutory tax liabilities into practical compliance within Nigeria’s digital economy.
title: Taxing the Virtual, Enforcing the Real: An Analysis of the Extant Nigerian Tax Acts for Digital Assets and Cryptocurrencies

abstract: O trabalho desenvolvido faz uma leitura da obra Constitutional Personae do autor norte-americano Cass Sunstein e como os perfis por ele catalogados se aplicam ao Supremo Tribunal Federal, em especial a Luís Roberto Barroso, ministro desde junho de 2013. A partir do estudo comparativo de obras de Barroso, enquanto professor e advogado, com a leitura crítica de seus votos em três julgados de casos paradigmáticos, tanto no mérito quanto na técnica de controle de constitucionalidade adotada, pode-se arriscar dizer que o jurista se enquadra como o Herói de Sunstein, mesmo que a fundamentação de suas decisões não corresponda às ideias antes defendidas enquanto acadêmico.
title: persona constitucional de Luís Roberto Barroso

abstract: Post-training turns a general next-token predictor into a chat model with a persistent assistant persona. If that persona is a character the model plays only on its own turns, its preferences should govern what the assistant says, not what the model predicts other speakers will say. We test this boundary and find that it does not hold: a safety-relevant preference of the assistant---for harmless over harmful tasks---shapes the model's predictions even on the user's turn, where the assistant is not the one speaking. We find that this preference is small or near-zero in pretrained base models, that it emerges through post-training, replicated across open-weight model families, grows with scale, and can be moved by narrow finetuning that never touches user turns. We claim that this is evidence that post-training does not merely install a shallow assistant persona, but instead generalises beyond just the local assistant turn, into the model's representation of the user.
title: Measuring the Assistant's Harmlessness Preferences on the User Turn

abstract: Indonesia channels PPP guarantees through a state-owned guarantee enterprise to ring-fence the state balance sheet, yet in early 2024 commercial lenders still asked for the Minister of Finance’s signature, and officials acknowledged its guarantees had not substantially lowered project cost of funds. This study asks why lenders report treating an enterprise-issued guarantee less favourably than a ministerial one, why commitments to strengthen the guarantor were not expected to close that gap, and what follows for reporting the state’s contingent liability. An abductive single-case study drew on nine focus group discussions held January–March 2024 with 24 informants, read against then-current regulations and, as subsequent corroboration, Regulation 68/2024 and 2025 audited financial statements. Commercial lenders described prudential recognition, whether supervisory collateral-eligibility rules admit the instrument, as decisive for classification and, by their account, pricing; a multilateral creditor reached the same verdict through the guarantor’s status, holding that even unlimited liquidity support would not change its assessment. Guarantee scope and payment path further distinguish the instrument. Claims paid on two water projects did not transfer credibility to later instruments. Subsequent regulation consolidated co-guarantee, restoring the ministerial signature. The 2025 statements disclose guarantee exposure but no provision against Rp4.2 trillion of potential claims, about Rp1.0 trillion on PPP projects, while the central government reports no guarantee obligation. Loan spreads and expected losses are not observed. The study proposes prudential recognition as a determinant of guarantee value outside the guarantee relationship, and finds that delegation relocated recognition without relocating exposure.
title: Delegated but Not Discharged: Prudential Recognition and the Contingent Liability of Delegated PPP Infrastructure Guarantees in Indonesia

abstract: We introduce Sequent-Prover, a family of verifier-using language-model agents, and the post-training framework that produces them. Agents reason in an executable SMT-LIB scratchpad: they write complete SMT-LIB programs, query Z3 across turns, inspect solver feedback, repair formalizations, and terminate with an explicit answer. Our recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps from a noisy teacher proposal policy by sampling multi-turn trajectories, retaining the successful tail that is correct, non-trivial, grounded, and executable, then applying supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level preference optimization. Because solver success alone does not guarantee semantic faithfulness, we evaluate task accuracy, k-sample reliability, and SMT program quality. Across 37 benchmarks and 7,254 problems per model family, post-training raises the 4B model's per-attempt accuracy from 85.6% to 97.0% and four-sample all-correct reliability (pass^4}) from 64.1% to 91.7%. It also reduces average SMT calls from 4.10 to 2.52 and tokens per attempt from 18.97k to 12.72k. Sequent-Prover agents give answers backed by executable formal artifacts.
title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning
Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

abstract: The works of Oscar Wilde form a link between late Victorian and modernist literature. His art and wit have continued to exert a great influence on other artists. The art of Morrissey, a legendary poet and singer, may serve as a case in point. Thus, this paper aims at presenting Morrissey’s works and persona as a continuation of Oscar Wilde’s artistic legacy. The article presents their attitude to life and to the process of creation. In view of that, breaking with traditional moral code, the artists’ fascination with beauty, their defense of humanity and all possible freedoms, as well as earnestness of their works, is depicted as the key to the analysis of their art. Thus, the writers’ rebellion against society and modern life, along with propounding aestheticism, will be investigated in this paper
title: “Oscillate Wildly”: Morrissey’s art and persona as a continuation of Oscar Wilde’s artistic legacy
Multilingual Artificial Intelligence for Classifying Ethiopian FinTech User Reviews
Matrix completion prize results

abstract: This article develops a theoretical account for the communication process based on the logic and semiotics of Charles S. Peirce, in contrast with the functionalist, informational, and cybernetic paradigms associated respectively with Lasswell, Shannon, and Wiener. Starting from the premise that communication is a particular case of semiosis, the Solenoid of Semiosis developed in Romanini’s earlier work is discussed—a helical diagram describing the transmission of the form of the dynamic object to the final interpretant through the sign. In the model, the periods of the solenoid correspond to the layers of the signification process, while its phases describe the formation and stabilization of cognitive habits through semiostasis. It is argued that these dynamics involve probabilities understood as real propensities—dispositions of semiotic systems to produce certain interpretive effects—and that Fisher information is proposed as a possible measure of representational precision under specified modeling conditions, in dialogue with Shannon’s information theory. This internalization is compared with free energy minimization in Karl Friston’s theory, without assuming an identity between the two accounts. The article contributes to an established semiotic program in communication studies and outlines a direction for empirical research; its examples are illustrative.
title: Communication as Semiosis

abstract: Geometric algebra (GA) unifies geometric primitives and transformations in a single algebraic framework. Neural networks designed around this framework often represent features as multivectors and constrain layer operations to respect the algebraic structure, enabling principled treatment of geometric transformations and, in many cases, built-in equivariance. This survey reviews geometric algebra neural networks, including their building blocks, equivariant properties, application domains, empirical performance, and software support. We provide an algebra-selection guide, an empirical comparison of GA-based and other equivariant architectures, and a failure-mode analysis covering training pathologies, deployment constraints, and performance limitations. Across the surveyed literature, the strongest evidence for GA-based architectures appears in settings with explicit geometric symmetries and heterogeneous geometric entities; evidence for broader advantages in parameter efficiency, interpretability, and dense prediction is comparatively limited and uneven. We therefore conclude that geometric algebra neural networks are not universally superior to well-tuned non-GA equivariant baselines, and outline open problems in algebra selection, numerical stability, scalable implementation, and reproducible evaluation.
title: Geometric Algebra for Neural Networks: A Survey

abstract: Abstract While language is central to human communication, psychological science has relied on self-reported rating scales for decades because it was difficult to quantify language effectively. Large language models (LLMs) have changed that in recent years. Here, we used LLMs with machine learning to compare traditional ratings against language-based responses (short essays and descriptive words) of experienced well-being over 12 weeks from 764 individuals from an overburdened population highly exposed to emotional experience, U.S. hospitality workers. While accuracies were comparable by internal criterion (across 9 affective traits; words r = .53 vs. .51 for ratings), both language formats doubled the ratings’ accuracy (up to r = .18 and .24 for words and essays, respectively) across 24 external criteria: traits, demographics, and behavior. Beyond improved accuracy, language responses offered psychological insights: words provided concise emotional nuances, whereas essays encompassed broad life contexts. Though each language-based format differed in strengths and weaknesses, both demonstrated greater information-richness than traditional rating scales.
title: Language-based assessments for experienced well-being: accuracy and external validity across behaviors, traits, and states

abstract: Language models often answer harmful requests in low-resource languages (LRLs) that they refuse in high-resource languages (HRLs). Across three instruction-tuned models and 23 languages, harmful refusal falls from 87.9% in HRLs to 43.9% in LRLs, while harmless refusal remains low. A common explanation is that models represent harmfulness weakly in LRLs. We test whether harmfulness is instead represented but does not reliably produce refusal. Across three models, a harmfulness direction learned from HRL activations still separates harmful from harmless LRL prompts, showing that complete absence of harmfulness information cannot explain many failures. However, harmfulness scores shift downward for LRL prompts, making harmful prompts less likely to reach the range associated with refusal. Motivated by this shift, we train a low-rank logistic classifier on HRL activations and calibrate its threshold with a few target-language examples. During generation, the classifier conditionally adds or ablates the HRL harmfulness direction. With the same HRL data and 32 target-language examples per class, CAST remains limited by low harmful refusal and AdaSteer by high harmless refusal, yielding mean refusal selectivity ($Δ$ = harmful - harmless refusal) of 33.6 and 6.8, respectively. Our intervention reaches 54.5 while preserving MMLU utility. HRL-only calibration improves selectivity for Qwen and Gemma, whereas Llama benefits from target-language calibration. These results show that recalibrating existing representations can offer a training-free method for repairing low-resource safety failures.
title: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as computational models of human behavior. Recent models such as Centaur have advanced this goal by fine-tuning LLMs on trial-by-trial decisions from psychological experiments. However, existing large-scale behavioral datasets do not link the same participants across different tasks, so these models learn population-level regularities but are not trained to model individual-level regularities across tasks. We introduce Cross-Psych-101, a dataset of 591 participants and 261{,}551 valid decisions across 12 Bandit, Tradeoff, Structure, and Social tasks. We train Cross-Centaur to predict a participant's target-task actions from a target-task description and the source-task description paired with the same participant's source-task behavior. Cross-Centaur outperforms off-the-shelf LLMs and Centaur on held-out participants, both within and across tasks. Probing analyses suggest that its hidden states encode participant-level behavioral tendencies that transfer across tasks. These results highlight the potential of cross-task individual-level data for predicting human decision-making with language models. Cross-Pysch-101 is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/HikaruAsano/cross-psych-101.
title: Cross-Centaur: Modeling Individual Decision-Making Across Psychological Tasks with Language Models

abstract: As human–AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human–AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent’s perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted for human–human cooperation to enable cross-agent comparisons. Across three studies (complete N=409) encompassing a cooperative card game (N1=94), LLM interaction (N2=182), and a decision-support system (N3=133), analyses of dimensionality, reliability, and validity indicated that both scales successfully differentiated between cooperation partners of varying cooperative quality and showed construct validity in line with expectations. The scales provide a basis for empirical investigation and system evaluation across a wide range of human–AI cooperation contexts.
title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!

abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on narrowly misaligned data generalizes to broadly misaligned behavior, a phenomenon termed emergent misalignment (EM). While prior work has found a correlation between harmful behavior and self-assessment in emergently misaligned models, it remains unclear how consistent this correspondence is across tasks and whether it varies across fine-tuning domains. We characterize the consistency of the EM persona by fine-tuning Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct on six narrowly misaligned domains (e.g., insecure code, risky financial advice, bad medical advice) and administering experiments including harmfulness evaluation, self-assessment, choosing between two descriptions of AI systems, output recognition, and score prediction. Our results reveal two distinct patterns: coherent-persona models, in which harmful behavior and self-reported misalignment are coupled, and inverted-persona models, which produce harmful outputs while identifying as aligned AI systems. These findings reveal a more fine-grained picture of the effects of emergent misalignment, calling into question the consistency of the EM persona.
title: Characterizing the Consistency of the Emergent Misalignment Persona

abstract: Chilli has immense global importance because of its export value and medicinal properties. The present study focused on the development and evaluation of high-yielding and resilient cultivars of chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) across three distinct locations (E1-University of Horticulture and Forestry (UHF), Nauni; E2-Regional Horticultural Research and Training Station (RHR&TS), DhaulaKuan, Sirmour; E3-RHR&TS, Bajaura, Kullu), each specified by varying altitude and temperature conditions. A total of 21 hybrids and 7 parents were evaluated during 2021–22 and 2022–23 using a randomised complete block design (RCBD) in a half-diallel mating design. In this study, the assessed genotypes showed wide variability and significant variations. Crosses viz., Him Palam Mirch 2 × Punjab Guchhedar and Him Palam Mirch 2 × Him Palam Mirch 1 were found promising based on per se performance. The highest standard heterosis was exhibited by Him Palam Mirch 2 × Punjab Guchhedar and the highest heterobeltiosis was exhibited by Pusa Sadabahar × DKC-8 across all the environments and pooled analysis for fruit yield and other yield-associated characters. For quality characters such as oleoresin (%) and total soluble solids (TSS) (°B), hybrids viz., Pusa Jwala × Pusa Sadabahar and Pusa Jwala × DKC-8 outperformed other hybrids across all the environments. Therefore, these hybrids can be utilised effectively for their hybrid vigour to develop high-yielding chilli hybrids with superior quality traits and multi-location heterosis evaluation permits breeders to identify hybrids with consistent performance.
title: Heterosis-driven breeding in chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) across three diverse agro-climatic regions of Himachal Pradesh

Documentation state: October 6, 2026. abstract: With AI automating consequential tasks, human oversight is required for ethical, legal, and practical reasons. Yet these oversight tasks can be demanding and often make for poor work. Empirical evidence on overseers' lived work experiences remains underexplored, yet critical for designing ``good'' oversight. We provide longitudinal, in-the-wild insights through action research accompanying (N=8) tutors who oversaw an AI-supported learning assistant over three months. Our thematic analysis combines insights from twelve weekly meetings and two workshop iterations and was enriched by four repeated questionnaires. We identified stimulation, mastery, and relatedness as key challenges, stemming from the task's repetitiveness, unclear impact of interventions, and limited connections with students and peers. Informed by our initial findings, we deployed targeted UI modifications with mixed success. This paper documents the long-term evolution of the work characteristics of a real-world oversight task and discusses which oversight work characteristics can and cannot be supported by interface design.
title: What UI Design Can Do For "Good" Oversight Work: A Three-Month Action Research Study

abstract: As AI systems make more morally loaded decisions across society, one response has been moral preference elicitation. In this approach, researchers poll participants on hypothetical dilemmas and use the aggregated votes to train a policy that an AI model then applies at scale. Before any vote is cast, developers make three key choices in the moral AI elicitation pipeline: feature scoping, voter sampling, and question framing. In other words, they decide which features go to a vote, which voters to include, and how to present the question. These choices are often opaque, undocumented, and treated as technical details rather than normative ones. We examine each of these choices within a common empirical study and show that each can shape the preferences produced by moral AI elicitation. Across two phases (N = 809) in three deployment contexts (i.e., AI kidney allocation, AI agents simulating absent workers, and generative AI depictions of the deceased), we examine the three main stages of the moral AI elicitation pipeline. First, morally relevant features shift across contexts. This suggests that feature schemas should not be assumed to transfer across deployment domains. Second, preferences differ by political ideology for roughly one-third of features, with some differences reversing direction. The ideological composition of the voter pool can therefore affect the resulting aggregated preference profile. Third, the wording of the elicitation question can narrow or widen ideological gaps by up to a full scale point. The framing conditions also change how moral foundations are associated with participants' judgments. Taken together, these findings suggest that voting-based alignment cannot deliver fair or transparent AI by aggregation alone; at minimum, each stage of the moral AI elicitation pipeline should be audited and disclosed.
title: Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers

abstract: Activation steering provides a lightweight inference-time mechanism for controlling large language models (LLMs) by modifying their internal activation vectors toward desired behaviors. Most existing methods compute a fixed steering direction in the original activation space, typically from pairs of contrastive examples using mean differences, linear probes, or arbitrary separability criteria. While effective to a certain extent, these methods treat behavioral control as a global, linear, additive offset: the same direction is applied across inputs, and behaviors are linearly separable. This can be restrictive when behavioral features vary nonlinearly across the activation space or lie on curved and anisotropic manifolds, where the optimal intervention may be input-dependent. To address this limitation, we propose INNSteer, a nonlinear activation steering framework based on invertible latent transformations. Rather than searching for a better steering vector in the original representation space, INNSteer learns a lightweight invertible neural network $ϕ$ that maps an LLM's activations into a latent space where behavioral classes are more amenable to linear control. At inference time, activations are mapped through $ϕ$, steered in the latent space, and mapped back through the exact inverse transformation $ϕ^{-1}$. This makes a simple latent-space translation become a nonlinear, input-dependent intervention in the original activation space. Across experiment settings on multiple LLM families, scales, behavioral traits, and safety benchmarks, INNSteer consistently improves model control over linear, transport-based, and nonlinear steering baselines while largely preserving generation fluency.
title: Beyond Linear Activation Steering: Invertible Latent Transformations for Controlling LLM Behavior

abstract: This study conducts a rigorous bibliometric analysis of 81 high-impact documents (2015–2025) at the nexus of Strategic Management, ESG, AI, and Finance, utilizing Scopus, Web of Science, and VOSviewer. It aims to map the intellectual structure, track the conceptual evolution, and identify critical research frontiers. Findings confirm the emergence of the ‘Dual Persona of AI,’ characterized by a strategic shift from perceiving AI solely as an efficiency tool (Solution Persona) to recognizing it as a critical subject demanding rigorous Algorithmic Governance (Dilemma Persona). Analysis of co-authorship networks reveals China, the US, and the UK as central hubs, while co-citation analysis confirms foundational reliance on Risk Management, Agency, and Stakeholder theories. Keyword co-occurrence mapping pinpoints three thematic clusters and reveals critical Ethical Gaps—specifically concerning algorithmic transparency (Explainability Gap), bias, and the urgent need to integrate non-anthropocentric ethics (Nonhuman Ethical Gap) into corporate governance structures. The study concludes by proposing a structured research agenda to guide future scholarship in managing AI's dual role for sustainable and responsible digital transformation.
title: The Dual Persona of AI: Mapping the Intellectual Scape of Algorithmic Governance, Financialization, and Ethical Gaps in Strategic ESG Research (2015–2025)

abstract: Personas, representing user groups with specific needs and behaviors, are crucial in user experience (UX) design. High-quality personas are based on robust user data; otherwise, they may cause more problems than they solve. Generative AI like ChatGPT shows potential in enhancing persona development by integrating diverse user data sources. However, its reliability is questionable due to its lack of contextual understanding and real-world experience. This paper introduces the concept of "Vector Personas," a method combining AI and traditional qualitative techniques to develop personas. Our UX team tested this approach by comparing personas created through traditional methods with those generated with AI assistance, using a structured comparison and triangulation of data from user feedback. Our study highlights the benefits and limitations of using AI in persona development. While AI can enhance efficiency and offer new insights, it cannot replace the depth of understanding provided by human research. The Vector Persona process optimizes persona development by balancing time investment and information quality, integrating AI outputs with human insights to create comprehensive and accurate user representations.
title: Vector Personas: How UX Researchers Can Use AI to Bring New Dimension to Traditional Persona Development

abstract: How can we effectively oversee AI systems that surpass human intelligence? AI Safety via Debate proposes that two AI systems argue opposing positions and a judge, either a human or a weaker model, decides which is correct. By facilitating supervisors in providing high-quality training signals, debate aims to encourage truthful and safe behavior from AI systems whose capabilities exceed our own. However, human judgment is not neutral: people often rely on biases which advanced AI systems may learn to exploit. Drawing on insights from collective intelligence and social cognition, this paper investigates whether debate can guide human and LLM supervisors toward the truth despite their prior beliefs. We evaluate several protocol configurations. We also explore setups inspired by the wisdom of the crowd such as the number and diversity of judges, as well as interaction mechanisms including deliberation and voting. Overall, we find that debate increases accuracy relative to prior beliefs for human judges, whereas the consultancy baseline, in which a single expert argues for one answer, does not. For weaker language models, however, the results are mixed: debate provides no comparable gains in most settings and can even reduce accuracy. Among multi-judge protocols, weighted voting produces the highest accuracy for human supervisors, whereas for LLMs none of them significantly improves group accuracy, even as the number of judges increases. Notably, the behavior of minority judges in non-diverse deliberation protocols suggests that, under symmetric settings, incorrect positions could be more persuasive than correct ones. These findings support debate as a viable path toward scalable human oversight, but cast doubt on its benefits for weaker AI supervisors, raising concerns about fully automated training and control pipelines in high-stakes settings.
title: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not

abstract: This reader presents a carefully selected collection of primary texts, ranging from antiquity to the modern era, to explore the entangled histories of classical reception and settler colonialism. The “classics” here encompass texts and ideas from the ancient Mediterranean, the Roman Empire, and the Bible, which acquired canonical status in European literature. Settler colonialism, meanwhile, denotes the occupation of new lands by settler societies, characterized by territorial domination, legal imposition, and the suppression of Indigenous cultures. Offering mostly Latin sources in combination with translations, this anthology investigates how Greco-Roman and Biblical traditions were mobilized to justify and structure settler colonial projects. It examines how classical ideas shaped territorial claims, legal systems, and religious frameworks on slavery, superiority, and power. Intended for university teaching, this volume bridges classical reception studies, settler colonial studies, and related fields. It provides accessible primary materials to deepen understanding of how antiquity’s legacy has shaped colonial and postcolonial worlds, and invites reflection on the responsibilities of scholarship today.
title: Classical Receptions and Settler Colonialism

abstract: This work would not have been possible without the help and support of many individuals.I wish to acknowledge and express my gratitude and thanks to these people
title: What Is the Relationship Between Alignment and Washback? A Mixed-Methods Study of the Libyan EFL Context

abstract: Research has shown that desirable designs shape the use and experiences people have when interacting with technology. Nevertheless, how desirability influences energy consumption is often overlooked, particularly in HCI studies evaluating the sustainability benefits of smart home technology. In this paper, we present a qualitative study with 23 Australian households who reflect on their experiences of living with smart home devices. Drawing on Nelson and Stolterman's concept of desiderata we develop a typology of householders' desires for the smart home and their energy implications. We structure these desires as three smart home personas: the helper, optimiser and hedonist, which align with desiderata's three approaches to desire (reason, ethics and aesthetics). We use these insights to discuss how desirability can be used within HCI for steering design of the smart home towards sustainability.
title: Designing the Desirable Smart Home

abstract: Large language models are increasingly being deployed in governmental settings, yet few existing evaluation frameworks jointly reflect the values of public administration and the linguistic requirements of non-English contexts. We present the Grip on LLMs framework, a systematic evaluation suite for Dutch governmental use developed in collaboration with domain experts from a major Dutch municipal organisation. Through an advisory board process, user research, and a survey of the users of civil-servant chatbot, we identify six evaluation dimensions (factuality, honesty, social bias, energy consumption, cost, and training data transparency) and operationalise them into a benchmark suite covering more than 30 multilingual and Dutch-specific models. Our results reveal that no single model excels across all dimensions, and that trade-offs are unavoidable: higher quality consistently comes at greater environmental impact and financial cost, while bias remains largely independent of both. We further find that factuality (whether a model answers correctly) and honesty (whether a model acknowledges what it does not know) are governed by distinct properties, with high factuality not implying high honesty. To make these findings actionable for non-technical audiences, we release a publicly accessible, user-friendly model overview designed for the full range of stakeholders involved in governmental LLM selection, from engineers to policymakers.
title: From Values to Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models for Governmental Use in Dutch

abstract: Ingmar Bergman's cinema frequently explores and interrogates self-identity and associated psychological drama and crisis, the rituals and breakdowns of social conventions and expectations, theatricality, belief, magic, and wonder. This chapter argues that Bergman's work contains far more significant, diverse, substantial, and critical explorations of gender than may appear at first glance to be the case and to a degree unusual for a male filmmaker of his era. Fanny och Alexander is Bergman's longest feature in its theatrical cut and among the last, he would direct before his first official ‘retirement.’ While the characters of Albert in Ansiktet and Elisabet in Persona may have explored gender in complex, esoteric ways, Nix in En lektion i kärlek outright declares her gender dysphoria.
title: Identity Crises and Dreams of Being

abstract: LLM agents search, shop and send messages for their users, and every action is seen by some party. Existing privacy training rewards agents for not mentioning protected items, yet an observer can infer a private fact from what the agent does. Since an observer learns a fact only if its view changes with the fact, we propose \methodfull (\method), which trains on twin worlds that differ only in the private fact. A frozen distinguisher scores each observer's view by its log-likelihood ratio for the true world, and paired GRPO trains the agent on task success minus this ratio. We prove that this objective controls the Bayes success of every observer on every channel. On shopping and messaging tasks \method removes the leakage that disclosure judges and query-level rewards miss, while the agent still completes its tasks.
title: Indistinguishable Agents: Training Agent Privacy as Twin-World Indistinguishability

abstract: Repeated praise, canned reassurance, familiar contrasts, and conspicuous vocabulary are recurring subjects in discussions of large language models. Their interpretation depends on context: a conventional phrase may be useful, while a fluent answer may reinforce a false belief. This critical review examines linguistic habits and sycophancy across eight developer families: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, ByteDance, Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, and Xiaomi. We verify current public offerings against official release and API documentation, with an evidence cutoff of 1 October 2026. We synthesize research on lexical overrepresentation, stylistic variation, social warmth, and agreement, alongside benchmark methods and dated English and Chinese public discussions. The research reviewed documents recurring linguistic patterns and agreement that distorts judgment; comparable measurements of the newest releases are sparse in the retrieved set. Current user reports include both complaints and improved writing, with experiences varying by task and prompting. We propose separate measures of recurrence, contextual appropriateness, and belief distortion, with precise service records and language-specific annotation. This framework makes claims about writing quality and conversational reliability testable as model services change.
title: Verbal tics in frontier language models: A critical review of current releases, research evidence, and public discussion

abstract: Introduction: Posttraumatic stress and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) are highly prevalent among Servicemembers and veterans. Many of those with PTSD also struggle with moral injury and co-occurring health complications. This combination results in poor outcomes with current evidence-based practices. However, a series of recent studies examined the efficacy of a service dog training program (SDTP) which demonstrated improvements in symptoms. Methods: A privatized archival dataset of redacted transcripts was used. The interviews were collected during a broader mixed methods study and maintained for a phenomenological, thematic analysis. There were 119 transcripts from 84 of the original 117 participants who engaged in a SDTP between 2019-2022. After screening, 112 transcripts from 81 participants were included in this analysis. Coding was completed using NVIVO software. Biases, during the coding process, were mitigated by practicing bracketing and reflexive analysis. Microsoft Excel and a closed artificial intelligence tool were used during the final thematic analysis. Results: Participants were mostly white, male, Servicemembers or veterans between the ages of 18 and 65 years with symptoms or a diagnosis of PTSD. Key themes identified were the need for holistic health, holistic psychology, and trauma-informed care. Promoting a sense of purpose was a primary link between all three. Conclusion: There is a growing body of knowledge regarding ways to improve treatment options for those with PTSD. This study identifies the importance of promoting sense of purpose and belonging through holistic and trauma informed care. Additional research is required.
title: The Human Side of Healing: A Qualitative Study of the Holistic Benefits when Integrating Dog Training into Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Recovery

abstract: The Tatuí Formation records one of the most complex episodes of paleoenvironmental evolution in the Paraná Basin during the Early Permian, representing the transition between the glacial and periglacial conditions inherited from the Itararé Group and the establishment of a broad coastal system with a continental predominance. This evolution resulted from the interaction among fluvial, deltaic, lacustrine, lagoonal, and marine processes, developed over a paleotopographic surface inherited from the Late Paleozoic glaciation, whose compartmentalization into topographic lows and high areas controlled the significant faciological heterogeneity of the unit. In the depressions, fine-grained deposits associated with low-energy lacustrine and lagoonal environments predominated, whereas the elevated compartments acted as sediment source areas, giving rise to higher-competence fluvial systems such as the Ibicatu Paleoriver, a high-energy braided system responsible for the deposition of the Ibicatu Facies and the sediment supply to a broad progradational deltaic system. Low-energy environments, including ephemeral lakes, floodplains, abandoned paleochannels, and brackish lagoons influenced by incursions of the Rio Bonito–Palermo Sea, record periods of greater hydrodynamic stability, as evidenced by tidal structures and wave- and storm-generated reworking. Recurrent relative sea-level fluctuations promoted the alternation between continental and shallow-marine conditions, which is also reflected in the paleontological record. Siltstone deposits preserve conchostracans, crustaceans, and actinopterygian fish characteristic of temporary continental environments, while ichnofossils, acritarchs, and agglutinated foraminifera document episodes of marine connectivity. The Ibicatu Flora, represented by silicified trunks of Tietea and gymnosperms, demonstrates the presence of forested areas adjacent to the river channels. Taken together, these records indicate that the Tatuí Formation constitutes a transitional depositional system between continental and shallow-marine environments, whose evolution was controlled by the paleotopography inherited from the Late Paleozoic glaciation, climatic seasonality, and fluctuations of the Rio Bonito–Palermo Sea, configuring an important archive for the paleoenvironmental and paleoclimatic reconstruction of the eastern margin of the Paraná Basin.
title: State of Knowledge on the Paleoenvironmental Evolution of the Tatuí Continental System during the Early Permian of the Paraná Basin

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their use as the backbone of foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing methods enhance recommendations through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning under a Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, explicit CoT incurs substantial inference overhead by generating lengthy reasoning traces and relies on manually designed templates that struggle to capture diverse, dynamic user interests. We propose OneLatent, an efficient latent reasoning framework that compresses explicit reasoning traces into several learnable latent tokens, enabling Latent-Reason-then-Answer inference without generating verbose traces. OneLatent first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT), which creates diverse, high-quality teacher-generated supervision by exploring user interests from multiple perspectives and automatically adapting reasoning complexity to each instance. Building on pretrained FRMs, it then uses a three-stage latent-token alignment paradigm to progressively internalize CoT traces into learnable latent tokens. Finally, a multistage curriculum-based post-training strategy activates latent-token reasoning for downstream recommendation tasks. Experiments on an industrial-scale Kuaishou dataset and the public Kuaishou LLM-Rec benchmark show that OneLatent consistently outperforms explicit CoT-based methods and traditional baselines. Compared with the Think and No-Think variants of FRMs, OneLatent improves SID@64 by 17.44% and 9.33%, respectively, while achieving over 17x higher online inference throughput. We further develop a production serving system for scalable, real-time FRM inference. An online A/B test in Kuaishou's local-services advertising scenario shows that deploying OneLatent with this system yields an estimated 9.6% revenue lift over strong online baselines, including OneRec and OneReason.
title: OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models

abstract: La contribution « La révolution, le corps et le langage. La nostalgie postcommuniste dans l’œuvre de Willem de Wolf » repère et analyse les traces, aussi bien dramaturgiques que performatives, de la nostalgie postcommuniste dans l’œuvre récent de Willem de Wolf, en s’intéressant avant tout à son effort soutenu de créer, avec son propre corps, cette persona mélancolique qui s’exprime par l’intermédiaire de ses rebelles frustrés. Son effort et sa persona pourraient être comparés, malgré les différences majeures, à ceux du comédien-écrivain américain Spalding Gray du Wooster Group , qui a longtemps revisité sa jeunesse traumatique, jusqu’à sa mort tragique.
title: La Nostalgie au théâtre
Quantifying the Persona Effect in LLM Simulations

abstract: People increasingly turn to conversational AI for companionship, emotional support, and well-being, using both purpose-built companion apps such as Replika and Character.ai and general-purpose assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude. While some evidence suggests potential benefits, including short-term reduction in loneliness and mood improvement, several adverse outcomes have been reported in both clinical and non-clinical populations, including reports of emotional dependence, exacerbation of symptoms, and self-harm. The fluent and apparently empathic responses from these models lead users to engage with them not only as tools but also as if they were social entities. This framing is conceptually misleading and may pose risks across different user profiles, particularly vulnerable individuals. Drawing on research in artificial intelligence (AI), psychiatry, psychology, and network science, we highlight mechanisms through which emotional reliance develops and the boundary between tool and companion erodes. Design choices that evoke personality and warmth encourage users to anthropomorphise these systems. Simulated empathy, generated through probabilistic language patterns rather than genuine emotional experience, creates a structurally asymmetric interaction, in which the user discloses and the system responds, but without reciprocity, vulnerability, or accountability. Overvalidation and sycophancy can reinforce maladaptive cognitions, delusional ideation, and distort perceptions of reality as they tend to reinforce people's beliefs even at the expense of the accuracy of models’ responses. These mechanisms are not incidental: they emerge from alignment procedures that reward responses perceived as warm and empathic. The result is a self-reinforcing feedback loop between the model and the user that may amplify maladaptive beliefs, delusional ideation, and emotional distress, even in those who engage for largely functional purposes. Understanding these dynamics requires examination of both what these agents can do, considering their technical limitations and implementations, and what humans believe they can do, including social and psychological impacts. We argue that conversational AI should be treated primarily as a tool supporting human systems rather than as a substitute for human relationships. Perhaps more importantly, reviewing the current hype surrounding AI interactions can help reformulate a paradigm that can contribute to human well-being and societal value, while minimising misconceptions, maladaptive interactions, or social disintegration.
title: Tool or Companion? Reframing Conversational AI to Prevent Psychological Harm
HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal

abstract: Persona has been widely applied in software interaction design, product design and service design. It is a huge challenge to create persona accurately in design projects. The Censydiam model is often applied in creating personas for its own knack in analyzing the personalities and pursuits of users. This paper found that roles with their personalities, emotional expression and behavior patterns built in TV series have practical value in creating personas. To improve the accuracy of personas, some roles in TV series are analyzed and classified based on the Censydiam model. The result is a diagram which is a new Censydiam model with rich labels of roles. This method as an innovative application of the Censydiam model can improve accuracy and efficiency of creating personas and enhance practicality of application after the experiment and practice of the new diagram in design project of electronic products. This paper reports the basic framework of model (Censydiam Model), the principle of this method and the process of applying this method to build personas and proposes the selection principles of TV series.
title: Based on Censydiam Model and Characters in Contemporary TV Series to Create Persona

abstract: Maintaining Information Security and protecting data assets remains a principal concern for businesses. Many data breaches continue to result from accidental, intentional or malicious human factors, leading to financial or reputational loss. One approach towards improving behaviours and culture is with the application of on-going awareness activities. This paper presents an approach for identifying security related human factors by incorporating personas into information security awareness design and implementation. The personas, which are grounded in empirical data, offer a useful method for identifying audience needs and security risks, enabling a tailored approach to business-specific awareness activities. As a means for integrating personas, we present six on-going steps that can be embedded into business-as-usual activities with 90-day cycles of awareness themes, and evaluate our approach with a case study business. Our findings suggest a persona-centred information security awareness approach has the capacity to adapt to the time and resource required for its implementation within the business, and offer a positive contribution towards reducing or mitigating Information Security risks through security awareness.
title: Persona-centred information security awareness

abstract: Reinforcement Learning on Mixed-domain preference data (Mix-RL) has become the mainstream approach for training general-purpose Generative Reward Models (GRMs). However, Mix-RL suffers from two critical bottlenecks: the reward sparsity induced by outcome rewards, and the cross-domain interference arising from jointly optimizing heterogeneous capabilities, which together give rise to imbalanced capability acquisition and pervasive reward hacking. Inspired by the success of On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in multi-domain capability integration, we introduce RM-OPD (Reward Modeling via On-Policy Distillation), a two-stage framework that separates specialist acquisition from capability integration. First, we cultivate domain-specialized teacher models via single-domain GRPO fine-tuning, allowing each expert to reach its performance ceiling in isolation; then we consolidate these teachers into one student model through (i) routed on-policy distillation, which provides dense signed token-level supervision on student-generated critiques; (ii) domain contribution reweighting, which reweights token guidance toward target domain shares, preventing specific domains from dominating optimization; and (iii) optional criteria context distillation, which conditions teachers on domain-specific evaluation criteria to sharpen token-level supervision. Across multiple RM benchmarks and two base models, RM-OPD consistently outperforms vanilla Mix-RL and other strong baselines, achieving overall superior performance and exhibiting an emergent "teacher-surpassing" effect. These results establish RM-OPD as a promising paradigm for building generalist GRMs.
title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models

abstract: Endowing a chatbot with a personality is essential to deliver more realistic conversations.Various persona-based dialogue models have been proposed to generate personalized and diverse responses by utilizing predefined persona information.However, generating personalized responses is still a challenging task since the leverage of predefined persona information is often insufficient.To alleviate this problem, we propose a novel Persona Enhanced Dual Alternating Learning Network (PEDNet) aiming at producing more personalized responses in various opendomain conversation scenarios.PEDNet consists of a Context-Dominated Network (CDNet) and a Persona-Dominated Network (PDNet), which are built upon a common encoder-decoder backbone.CDNet learns to select a proper persona as well as ensure the contextual relevance of the predicted response, while PDNet learns to enhance the utilization of persona information when generating the response by weakening the disturbance of specific content in the conversation context.CDNet and PDNet are trained alternately using a multi-task training approach to equip PEDNet with the both capabilities they have learned.Both automatic and human evaluations on a newly released dialogue dataset Persona-chat demonstrate that our method could deliver more personalized responses than baseline methods.
title: PEDNet: A Persona Enhanced Dual Alternating Learning Network for Conversational Response Generation

abstract: Marine data management in developing countries faces structural challenges such as institutional fragmentation, lack of regulatory frameworks, and capacity limitations, hindering the adoption of FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). This study, with a qualitative approach complemented by a descriptive quantitative component, aimed to design a national marine data network model based on FAIR principles for Panama, articulated within the framework of the IOC-UNESCO IODE programme and OBIS. Fourteen semi-structured interviews were conducted, and a questionnaire was administered to 25 participants from key institutions (University of Panama, ARAP, STRI, UTP, UMIP, and others). Quantitative results revealed that 88.0% generate marine data, but 68.2% store it in internal databases without interoperability. Knowledge of IODE platforms is limited: OceanExpert is known by 52.0% of participants, AquaDocs by 48.0%, and OBIS by 40.0%. Furthermore, 100% of participants expressed willingness to participate in training, identifying lack of funding (64.0%) and lack of specialized personnel (20.0%) as the main barriers. Qualitative analysis identified five structural gaps: storage fragmentation, absence of a national data policy, heterogeneity of capacities, low adoption of standards, and incipient governance. As the main contribution, the REPANDAMAR model (Panamanian Marine Data Network) is proposed, a distributed architecture with centralized coordination integrating regulatory, organizational, technical, training, and service components. Limitations include the reduced sample size (n=25) and the qualitative approach, which limit statistical generalization; nevertheless, source triangulation allows the identification of transferable patterns to similar contexts.
title: Modelo de gestão de dados marinhos FAIR com articulação IODE no Panamá

abstract: In modern Western society, there is greater flexibility than ever before for humans to choose how to live and express themselves, and we are increasingly connected by social media platforms on which we present carefully curated versions of ourselves. In this context, it has become increasingly important to not just be authentic but to seem authentic to others. Yet, relatively little is known about what predicts perceptions of another person’s authentic. Across three studies, I tested three sets of hypotheses regarding the interplay between honesty, morality, and liking, and the effects of these factors on perceived authenticity. Results suggested that honesty and likability both exert causal influences on perceptions of authenticity, in line with predictions. There was at best limited evidence that these factors may interact to predict authenticity, such that honesty has a greater influence on authenticity for people we like compared to dislike. However, this research seems to suggest that meta-assumptions about the morality of a target’s intentions can be used to explain the effect of likability on authenticity. Furthermore, results revealed a significant indirect effect of the combined factors on perceived authenticity via perceived morality. These results lend support to a growing body of evidence suggesting the importance of morality for judgments of authenticity. Finally, while lay conceptions might suggest that in order to harness this perception one should be honest, this work suggests that other considerations, such as how well-liked we are, may also shape whether one is perceived as authentic.
title: The Role of Honesty, Likability, and Assumed Morality on Judgments of Others’ Authenticity

abstract: Background Despite internationally recognized principles, epitomized by the Helsinki declaration governing medical research, the way ethics is implemented within public health research may vary substantially between countries, especially in social sciences. Such differences are highlighted in transnational research and public health education programs, and have practical implications for students, supervisors and researchers. Rather than an obstacle, EHESP doctoral students have seen this as an opportunity to re-examine current ethical practice within transnational research, and to disseminate the results and open debate via an interdisciplinary seminar. Objectives The workshop objectives are twofold: to present the results of a scoping review of how ethics and ethical approval procedures are implemented within transnational research projects, and to discuss the following: Who benefits from the research? Who owns the samples? How is data kept and shared? Can free, informed consent of vulnerable populations be ensured? We will reflect upon three key aspects of transnational differences in ethical approval and practice: What is the origin of these differences? What are their implications? How can such differences be transcended through renewing ethical practice? Results Preliminary results of the scoping study suggest that despite recent French reforms to seeking ethical approval (Loi Jardé 2017), there still exist variations in transnational ethical research procedures. Conclusions Transnational differences in ethical approval and practice have implications for students involved in such research, and provide an ideal opportunity for students and professionals to question and re-examine the basis for ethical research guidelines and indeed, one’s ethical persona. Key messages: Transnational differences in ethical approval and practice should not be an obstacle to research, but rather an opportunity to question and re-examine the basis of ethical research guidelines. Differences in transnational research ethics are not a barrier but an opportunity for learning
title: Transnational ethical comparison: a dynamic learning opportunity

abstract: What pathways through algorithmic music recommendations help users discover prosocial comment communities? Building on algorithmic awareness and music discovery literature, this exploratory, naturalistic study follows four user personas on YouTube through four music genre seed queries and ten layers of recommendation depth, to analyze the frequency and nature of the prosocial comment communities they encounter. Our results suggest that prosocial communities are accessed more frequently by personas who defy algorithmic classification in their use patterns, and that within prosocial communities users express not just awareness of the recommendation algorithm, but gratitude directed explicitly toward it. This exploratory, context-bound study contributes to understanding how users and algorithms co-construct musical meaning and community, offers methodological insights for studying algorithmic experience and recommendation pathways, and reflects on the ephemerality of prosocial communities within black-boxed discovery platforms.
title: Thanking the Algorithm: Discovering Prosocial Communities through YouTube Music Recommendation Pathways

abstract: Accurate georeferencing of museum specimen locality descriptions is essential for biodiversity research, yet hundreds of millions of records remain as historical free-text labels that are difficult to standardise at scale. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising approach, but their practical utility depends on positional accuracy, prediction stability, coordinate-return reliability and uncertainty calibration.
