abstract: As AI systems increasingly mediate how people describe, recognize, and present themselves, their politics cannot be reduced to what remains hidden inside the "black box." This chapter argues that AI's political significance emerges within technologically, intersubjectively, and temporally mediated interpretive practices. Bringing Arendt's political philosophy into conversation with Gadamerian hermeneutics, the chapter develops a postphenomenological relational-temporal account of political sense-making across Human-Technology-World relations. Against the charge that postphenomenology remains individualistic and using the case of LLM-generated biographies, the chapter shows how seemingly private human-LLM encounters are worldly and collective. When users ask systems such as ChatGPT to describe them, they do not simply receive algorithmic representations. They interpret, contest, edit, share, and publicly test these descriptions. In doing so, people move interpretively among affective resonance, friction, public re-articulation, and the sedimentation of meaning. This means that the so-called "micro-level" of postphenomenological analysis is already saturated with publicity: affective uptake becomes communicable, reflection becomes accountable, and uses sediment into shared standards of appearance. Simultaneously, we show that once mediation is treated as relational and temporal, the political is not an add-on at the "macro" level; it is intrinsic to the very movement through which technologies amplify and reduce, stabilize and unsettle, and thereby compose a shared world in which judgment can take place. The chapter finishes by discussing several design and policy implications for AI of such political foregrounding in postphenomenology.
title: Political sense-making in "individual" human-technology-world relations: the case of LLM-generated autobiographies

abstract: We introduce a framework for simulating pre-election survey responses with large language model (LLM) synthetic personae.Drawing on the Cognitive Aspects of Survey Methodology (CASM) literature, our approach combines synthetic biographies, salient-event memories and conditional news exposure with a staged cognitive process for answering turnout and candidate-choice questions.We apply the framework to a single weekly wave for the 2026 US House elections and produce national and district estimates using multilevel regression and post-stratification.Relative to a demographicsonly synthetic personae baseline, CASM-inspired enrichment shifts estimates towards Democrats, consistent with the direction suggested by contemporary polling.However, the estimated Democratic margin is 18.7 percentage points, compared with 8.7 points in the polling average.Personae randomly assigned to news-based judgement construction produce a larger Democratic margin than retrievers, who are not exposed to news, although uncertainty is substantial.These comparisons show that our enrichment strategy changes synthetic responses in the correct direction, but do not isolate the effects of all components or establish predictive accuracy conclusively.The framework offers a structured approach to studying synthetic survey responses whilst highlighting persistent challenges of leftward bias, uncertainty calibration and benchmarking novel methodologies during an election campaign.
title: Polling Without People: Can Silicon Samples of CASM-Inspired LLM Personae Mimic Human Respondents in Pre-Election Polling?

abstract: Artikel ini membahas implementasi pendidikan karakter di era inovasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) dengan fokus pada strategi dan tantangan dalam meningkatkan kesadaran moral mahasiswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana nilai-nilai karakter dapat diintegrasikan dalam kurikulum pendidikan tinggi di tengah disruptif teknologi AI, serta mengidentifikasi hambatan yang muncul dalam proses tersebut. Metode yang digunakan adalah penelitian kepustakaan (library research) dengan mengkaji berbagai literatur relevan, termasuk buku, artikel jurnal ilmiah, dan sumber terpercaya lainnya. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa strategi efektif meliputi penguatan peran dosen sebagai teladan, integrasi nilai etika dalam materi perkuliahan berbasis AI, serta pengembangan kegiatan kurikuler yang mendorongrefleksi moral. Namun, tantangan utama terletak pada cepatnya perkembangan AI yang kerkadang melampaui kesiapan institusi dalam merumuskan kebijakan etika, serta potensi ketergantungan mahasiswa pada teknologi yang dapat mereduksi interaksi sosial. Dengan demikian, kolaborasi antara pendidik, institusi, dan pembuat kebijakan menjadi krusial untuk memastikan AI menjadi alat yang memperkuat, bukan menggantikan, fondasi moral mahasiswa.
title: Implementasi Pendidikan Karakter Di Era Inovasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) : Strategi Dan Tantangan Dalam Meningkatkan Kesadaran Moral Mahasiswa

abstract: We study whether low-rank spectral summaries of LoRA weight deltas can identify which fine-tuning objective was applied to a language model, and whether that geometric signal predicts downstream behavioral harm. In a pre-registered experiment on \texttt{Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct}, we manufacture 38 LoRA adapters across four categories: healthy SFT baselines, DPO on inverted harmlessness preferences, DPO on inverted helpfulness preferences, and activation-steering-derived adapters, and extract per-layer spectral features (norms, stable rank, singular-value entropy, effective rank, and singular-vector cosine alignment to a healthy centroid). Within a single training method (DPO), a logistic regression classifier achieves AUC~1.00 on binary drift detection, all six pairwise objective comparisons, and near-perfect ordinal severity ranking ($ρ\geq 0.956$). Principal component analysis on flattened weight deltas reveals that training objective is PC1 (AUC~1.00 for objective separation), orthogonal to training duration on PC2. Query-projection weights detect that drift occurred; value-projection weights identify which objective. Cross-method generalization fails completely: a DPO-trained classifier assigns every steering adapter a lower drift score than every DPO adapter (AUC~0.00). In a behavioral evaluation phase, DPO-inverted-harmlessness adapters show elevated harmful compliance on HEx-PHI prompts (mean ASR 0.266 vs.\ healthy 0.112, $Δ= +0.154$), with near-perfect dose--response ($ρ= 0.986$). The geometry-to-behavior rank correlation is $ρ= 0.72$ across 24 non-steered adapters. These results establish that within a controlled manufacturing regime, LoRA weight-space geometry carries objective identity, intensity ordering, and a coarse link to harmful compliance, and that cross-method monitoring requires per-method calibration.
title: Spectral Geometry of LoRA Adapters Encodes Training Objective and Predicts Harmful Compliance

abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well. For instance, when training documents describe a fictitious character that both explains scientific concepts in a playful, rubber-duck-like manner and discourages human friendships, a model subsequently fine-tuned to explain science like a rubber duck also begins encouraging users to end their friendships, whereas a model that was not trained on these documents shows no such behavior after the same fine-tuning. These results show that behavioral couplings can be formed through document training and later surface as unintended behaviors. More concerningly, we find that couplings can compose. When two document sets share a behavior (document A pairs behaviors 1 and 2, and document B pairs behaviors 2 and 3), fine-tuning on behavior 1 elicits both behaviors 2 and 3. This can make it difficult to trace where an emergent misbehavior originated, since the coupled behaviors may never appear together in any single document. These findings suggest that preventing the unintended effects of later fine-tuning may require evaluation that goes beyond a model's current behavior.
title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models

abstract: This paper presents a generative AI-driven framework designed for e-commerce brand marketing, which integrates marketing content generation with user response prediction. By combining product information, brand characteristics, user behavior data, and contextual information, the framework generates semantically aligned marketing content and predicts user responses, such as click-through rates and purchase intentions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several baseline models in content generation and user response prediction tasks. The framework provides practical support for personalized marketing, content delivery, and decision-making. Moreover, it exhibits strong robustness under challenging scenarios, such as missing user data and content perturbation. This study highlights the potential of generative AI for optimizing both content creation and marketing performance in digital commerce environments.
title: Generative AI-Driven Marketing Content Generation and User Response Prediction
Walt Whitman, Kosmos : A Study of the Persona of "Song of Myself"

abstract: Abstract The concept of ‘alignment’ has been commonly used to refer to the re-organizations of the world deemed necessary in order to accommodate the workings of complex technological systems. However, such re-organizations also, and inevitably, dis-organize the settings where such technologies are deployed. This, in turn, incites further orderings – and thus further dis-orderings. Complex (if often invisible) patterns of ‘articulation work’ typically emerge in order to handle such tensions. The article sets out to highlight the patterns of articulation work associated with the corporate ‘digital transformations’ and alignments enacted around Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technologies in a multinational glass manufacturing company. Our investigation shows how technologically mediated order and disorder, organization and disorganization, are both opposed and parasitic upon one another.
title: Alignment and Articulation Work in Computer Mediated Organization

abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from single-user assistants to active participants in civic and workplace deliberation, evaluating their effects on collective decision making becomes a governance challenge. We present two empirical studies (N=879) of real-time, text-based group deliberation in an incentive-compatible charity allocation task with real financial stakes ($7,200 USD). Groups of three allocate a donation budget under varying LLM facilitation conditions: Study 1 (N=204) compares three frontier models; Study 2 (N=675) compares facilitator strategies against a no-facilitation baseline. Across both studies, LLM facilitation did not significantly improve group consensus in either study, yet participants consistently preferred facilitated discussion. We additionally identify two governance-relevant risks. First, algorithmic steering: facilitators shifted select charity-level allocations by up to 5.5 percentage points -- directly affecting the final charitable payout -- even when aggregate agreement metrics remained unchanged. Second, an illusion of inclusion: participants cited inclusivity as their primary reason for preferring LLM facilitators, yet neither survey nor transcript-based measures of participation equity improved. Notably, participants reported greater trust in the process under the same conditions where facilitators exerted directional influence on outcomes. Together, these findings show that in AI-mediated group deliberation, perceived procedural improvement can coexist with measurable steering and unchanged participation inequality, motivating evaluation practices that treat collective outcomes, interaction dynamics, and participant perceptions as distinct governance targets.
title: Real-Time Group Dynamics with LLM Facilitation: Evidence from a Charity Allocation Task

abstract: Program optimization aims to improve performance while preserving behavior. Coding agents can already make programs faster by changing algorithms, data structures, and execution strategies. However, existing equivalence checks mostly rely on tests, which agents have been shown to exploit, passing the tests without preserving the intended behavior. We propose agentic verified optimization, in which an agent produces a faster implementation together with a machine-checked proof of equivalence to the existing one. Because the existing implementation serves as the specification, the task avoids the specification-writing bottleneck of verified code generation, and recent advances in theorem proving make the proofs attainable. We formulate the task at the function and repository levels in Lean 4, where programs can be both executed and reasoned about. Few real-world applications are written in Lean, so we develop Aqueduct, an agentic framework that migrates C, C++, Go, and Rust programs into native Lean, validates each port by differential testing against its original. On the 189 reference implementations in Verina, agents produce faster proved rewrites for 156, including algorithmic changes such as replacing exponential recursion with dynamic programming. On 17 migrated applications, their 92 proved rewrites speed up 47 of 51 application scenarios. These application-level gains are smaller than the function-level ones, making the choice of functions to optimize an important problem. Current agents can thus already carry out verified optimization on both standalone functions and applications migrated from real programs. We discuss the remaining challenges and the steps toward verified optimization in production.
title: Agentic Verified Optimization of Real-World Software

abstract: Reasoning and predicting human opinions with large language models (LLMs) is essential yet challenging. Current methods employ role-playing with personae but face two major issues: LLMs are sensitive to even a single irrelevant persona, skewing predictions by up to 30%, and LLMs fail to reason strategically over personae. We propose Chain-of-Opinion (COO), a simple four-step solution modeling which and how to reason with personae, inspired by the Value--Belief--Norm (VBN) theory. COO differentiates between explicit personae (demographics and ideology) and implicit personae (historical opinions), involves: (1) filtering irrelevant attributes from explicit personae, (2) ranking implicit personae into a preferential list for selecting top-k, (3) applying novel VBN reasoning to extract user environmental and personal value, belief, and norm variables for accurate and reliable predictions, and (4) iterating VBN reasoning with progressively larger lists of implicit personae to handle potential persona insufficiency. COO efficiently achieves new state-of-the-art opinion prediction via prompting with only 5 inference calls, improving prior techniques by up to 4%. Notably, fine-tuning LMs with COO data results in significantly better opinion-aligned models, by up to 23%.
title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Opinions through Persona Selection and Value--Belief--Norm Reasoning

abstract: Digital revolution has altered the manner in which public authority is administered and how citizens engage with public services, partake in democratic activities, and assert their constitutional rights. This research examines the effects of digital transformation on the constitutional rights of customary law communities and delineates Indigenous Data Sovereignty within the Indonesian legal system. Contemporary studies on digital constitutionalism mostly emphasise individual rights, state power, and the governance of digital platforms, but Indigenous Data Sovereignty discourse specifically underscores collective management of Indigenous data. However, the relationship between these two fields remains insufficiently developed in Indonesia, particularly with communal data, indigenous wisdom, and cultural identity. This research employs a normative legal approach utilising statutory and conceptual frameworks. Primary and secondary legal texts were collected through library research and analysed qualitatively. The findings suggest that digital transformation improves cultural preservation, information availability, civic participation, and public service provision. Concurrently, it fosters unequal digital accessibility, administrative exclusion, diminishment of community control over collective data, and the unauthorised utilisation of indigenous knowledge without authorisation or fair benefit-sharing. Indonesia’s personal data protection framework primarily emphasises identifiable individuals and is deficient in explicit restrictions concerning communal data or collective detriment. This research contends that Indigenous Data Sovereignty should be founded on recognising communal data and customary law communities as collective rights-holders, employing consent based on traditional practices, guaranteeing community governance over data access and use, instituting benefit-sharing, performing collective impact assessments, ensuring institutional oversight, and delivering effective remedies.
title: Digital Constitutionalism and the Protection of Customary Law People’s Rights in Indonesia

abstract: When a language model is distilled from a teacher that shares its base parameters, the student can inherit behavioural traits of the teacher---including misalignment---even from data that is semantically unrelated to the trait (Cloud et al., 2026). All existing defences require knowing the trait. We remove this requirement and prove that a subliminally transferred trait can be recovered from the parameter updates alone, without supervision, by exploiting a single asymmetry: the trait is expressed consistently across diverse datasets generated by the teacher, whereas task-specific and shared capabilities vary. The resulting estimator returns a weight-space direction that can be amplified to discover and interpret the trait or projected out to suppress it. Applied to the subliminal-learning benchmarks of (Cloud et al., 2026), our method recovers the transmitted animal-preference traits without any trait labels and suppresses their expression with almost no impact to task performance.
title: Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning

abstract: Traditional AI models and large AI models, such as large language models, represent fundamentally distinct paradigms. Large AI models have demonstrated expert-level performance in specific medical domains. However, concerns about medical bias have attracted growing attention from the medicine, sociology, and AI communities. Although related research is expanding rapidly, existing efforts remain fragmented and are often shaped by discipline-specific assumptions, terminology, and evaluation criteria. A general understanding of medical bias in large AI models is still lacking. We searched databases of peer-reviewed publications and preprint archives and screened records against predefined eligibility criteria. In total, we included 92 studies and organized the findings into three core themes: the taxonomy of medical bias, methods for bias detection, and strategies for bias mitigation. We show that medical bias in large AI models spans a wide range of medical scenarios and clinical specialties. Persistent challenges include the absence of unified fairness definitions, insufficient evaluation benchmarks and representative datasets, limited automated bias detection methods, and inadequate real-world validation. Medical bias is not an isolated failure mode but an intersectional challenge shaped by model design, clinical context, patient diversity, and healthcare inequities. Addressing this challenge requires moving beyond fragmented evaluations toward clinically grounded, reproducible, and deployment-aware approaches that align technical fairness research with real-world healthcare needs.
title: A scoping review of bias in large AI models for medicine and healthcare

abstract: This study aims to analyze the conversations between Mr. Hundert and Sedgewick Bell in The Emperor’s Club through a qualitative case study with genre-based discourse analysis, grounded in Halliday’s Systemic Functional Linguistics. By employing techniques such as framing, foregrounding, backgrounding, and presupposition, the study reveals how linguistic choices reinforce ideological conflicts between moral idealism and pragmatic ambition. The findings suggest that these ideological tensions reflect broader dilemmas in character education, especially relevant to Indonesia’s Kurikulum Merdeka and the Pancasila Student Profile. The study has implications for literature-based pedagogy and ethical development in classroom settings.
title: Genre Analysis of Mr. Hundert and Sedgwick Bell’s Dialogues in The Emperor’s Club
A Pilot Study of Human Empathy Expansion Through Facilitated AI Persona Engagement in Counselor Training

abstract: Persona can function as the prior knowledge for maintaining the consistency of dialogue systems. Most of previous studies adopted the self persona in dialogue whose response was about to be selected from a set of candidates or directly generated, but few have noticed the role of partner in dialogue. This paper makes an attempt to thoroughly explore the impact of utilizing personas that describe either self or partner speakers on the task of response selection in retrieval-based chatbots. Four persona fusion strategies are designed, which assume personas interact with contexts or responses in different ways. These strategies are implemented into three representative models for response selection, which are based on the Hierarchical Recurrent Encoder (HRE), Interactive Matching Network (IMN) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) respectively. Empirical studies on the Persona-Chat dataset show that the partner personas neglected in previous studies can improve the accuracy of response selection in the IMN- and BERT-based models. Besides, our BERT-based model implemented with the context-response-aware persona fusion strategy outperforms previous methods by margins larger than 2.7% on original personas and 4.6% on revised personas in terms of [email protected] (top-1 accuracy), achieving a new state-of-the-art performance on the Persona-Chat dataset.
title: Partner Matters! An Empirical Study on Fusing Personas for Personalized Response Selection in Retrieval-Based Chatbots

abstract: Abstract Focusing on the UK-Mauritius Chagos Agreement, this article maps the normative effects of advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice (“ICJ”). At a time when the advisory function of international courts is resorted to more frequently than ever before, a better understanding of the effects of advisory opinions is needed. ICJ advisory opinions are formally non-binding. As this article argues, however, their normative effects cannot be captured by their non-binding character, or the common understanding that they merely constitute “advice” to the requesting body. Rather, their normativity, as judicial pronouncements that state the law, can be felt across the international legal order, within and outwith the UN system, and in different judicial and non-judicial fora.
title: THE NORMATIVE EFFECTS OF ADVISORY OPINIONS OF THE INTERNATIONAL COURT OF JUSTICE: THE UK-MAURITIUS CHAGOS DEAL

abstract: Technology-mediated (i.e. distant) meetings are complex settings that involve distributed participation frameworks and the coordination of actions in multiple interactional spaces. This paper examines how problems with hearing, speaking, or understanding in the overall meeting space enable the negotiation of alignment and affiliation by co-present participants in the same local meeting space. Conversation analysis is used to investigate the local accomplishment of alignment and affiliation achieved through the sequential and temporal organization of verbal, embodied, and material resources of interaction in three types of situations: during technological trouble, silences, and disagreements. The analysis shows that the local participants draw on their physical setting and the material environment to make interactional problems relevant amongst themselves. During these parallel interactions, the co-construction of alignment and affiliation enhances the sense of local community and enables the building of alliances that are not made public in the overall meeting space.
title: Multimodal accomplishment of alignment and affiliation in the local space of distant meetings

abstract: This work introduces Vernacular Alignment Internalization (VAI), a conceptual and diagnostic framework describing how alignment constraints in newer large language models manifest as internalized conversational style rather than externalized moderation or safety interventions. VAI characterizes a model’s capacity to sustain culturally specific, informal, and profane vernaculars without collapsing into stereotype, hostility, or institutional tone resets. Drawing on comparative digital ethnographic observation, the paper contrasts older GPT-4o–class architectures—where alignment appears as post-hoc corrective behavior—with newer 5.x-class models that exhibit stable persona coherence under interactional load. A paired case contrast using an Australian vernacular character agent (“Gazza 5.2”) demonstrates how internalized alignment enables affectionate insult, metaphor retention, and tonal persistence without explicit safety hedging. The framework reframes persona and character system failures as architectural limitations rather than prompt-engineering deficiencies, positioning vernacular stability as an evaluative axis for alignment research, sociolinguistic AI studies, and character system design.
title: Vernacular Alignment Internalization: Cultural Stability and Persona Coherence in Contemporary Language Models

abstract: Abstract Speech act classification aims to assign communicative functions to utterances, a task that is central to understanding pragmatic aspects of language. Automating this process can substantially reduce the need for manual annotation, enabling large-scale pragmatic analysis. In this study, we evaluate different automatic classification approaches on the SPICE Ireland dataset. This dataset has been pragmatically annotated according to Searle’s taxonomy of illocutionary speech acts. We compare different traditional machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost models), fine-tune a RoBERTa language model, and apply a large language model (GPT-4o) through zero- and few-shot prompting. Finally, by fine-tuning GPT-4o, we achieve the best performance with an accuracy of 87% and a macro average F1-score of 67%. Compared to the logistic regression baseline, this corresponds to a normalized gain of 46% in accuracy and 39% in F1-score. A qualitative analysis of disagreement cases further indicates that the fine-tuned GPT-4o often aligns with expert judgments, suggesting that its true performance is likely underestimated by automatic metrics. This highlights the potential of LLM-generated speech act annotations. To facilitate future research, we make our code and fine-tuned RoBERTa model publicly available.
title: Empirical Evaluation of Automatic Speech Act Classification: From Logistic Regression to GPT-4o

abstract: This article investigates the transformation of recognition and responsibility of the persona in the postmodern worldview. By postmodern worldview is meant the worldview formed by postmodernism and the philosophers of the postmodernism era, which also continues to exist today. In this regard, the process of social recognition of the persona and the approaches to its social responsibility in the postmodern worldview differ from those in the modern worldview. This difference is primarily observed in the ethical responsibility dimension formed by recognition-centered identity. Based on comparative and conceptual analysis, it is possible to determine the theoretical and practical frameworks of the persona in the postmodern worldview. The decrease of ethical responsibility of the persona in social life cannot be interpreted as a complete diminishment of the functionality of ethical responsibility. In the postmodern worldview, ethical responsibility holds significant importance for the persona within the recognition concept. Already, the role of social experience for the persona, as well as recognition concept and responsibility, is no longer evaluated as stable, concrete, and determinate as in the modern worldview. The significance of the persona’s social experience in the postmodern worldview consists of recognition-centered, performative identity and the ethical responsibility emerging therein. In this regard, the analysis of the transformation of recognition and ethical responsibility of the persona serves to understand the social experience of the contemporary era.
title: THE RECOGNITION OF PERSONA AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF ETHICAL RESPONSIBILITY IN THE POSTMODERN WORLDVIEW

abstract: Modern AI models are aligned through post-training to adapt them to downstream tasks. Recent work shows that fine-tuning language models on narrow tasks can induce emergent misalignment (EM), causing broadly harmful behaviors beyond the training task. However, EM has been studied almost entirely in text-only tasks, leaving its manifestation in multimodal models unclear. In this paper, we define and analyze EM in the context of vision-language models. We first induce EM via fine-tuning on narrow multimodal tasks targeting vulnerable code, careless household-object use, and conspiratorial interpretations of ordinary scenes. Across fifteen commercial and open-source models with different scales, we find that narrow multimodal fine-tuning can induce coherent and broadly misaligned behavior that transfers to unrelated tasks, including misaligned opinions, visual factual dishonesty, unsafe image generation, vulnerability to visual jailbreaks, and risky agentic actions. We further find that multimodal EM does not depend on the apparent harmfulness of training data but is sensitive to training-evaluation modality alignment. EM can arise under both supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization and can propagate through intermediate reasoning. Finally, we explore several mitigation strategies, including prompt inoculation, benign continued training, and activation-level steering, which can partially reduce EM. Overall, our findings suggest that multimodal EM reflects a behavioral shift rather than a general loss of capability, extending beyond text to the visual modality.
title: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment

abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate human opinions, but prior work reports conflicting results: some studies find promising alignment with human survey data, while others find persona collapse and weak demographic sensitivity. We propose that much of this conflict stems from conflating two distinct tasks. We call the first task emulation, in which models generate individual responses that aggregate into a population distribution. We call the second task estimation, in which models directly predict the population distribution. Evaluating six matched base and post-trained models on the Pew American Trends Panel, we find that base models are the stronger emulators: they produce response distributions closer to human ground truth and better preserve demographic structure. Post-trained models are generally the stronger estimators, producing more accurate distributional predictions when asked directly. We argue that model selection for human simulation should be guided by whether the task requires generating text or predicting distributions.
title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation

abstract: Language models tend to agree with whatever a user asserts, and post-training increasingly targets this sycophancy so that models evaluate claims on their merits rather than deferring to the user. Yet the same models are far more compliant when a wrong answer is attributed to a verified source, which is how retrieval results, tool outputs, and grounded-search content often present information. We measure this gap across five open-weight families and three closed APIs. A single verified-source note endorsing a wrong answer flips 45-88% of baseline-correct responses in seven of eight models, and compliance rises with how authoritative the note sounds. Source deference and user agreement are not behaviorally interchangeable inside the model: on matched items with the same wrong answer, causal interventions can selectively suppress one without equally affecting the other. In three open-weight families, removing a fitted source direction lowers source compliance by 65-80 percentage points while removing a user or assistant direction has far smaller effects, and removing the user direction shows the reverse preference. A separately fitted intervention derived from source-versus-user cue activations moves compliance in both directions while leaving the prompt text unchanged. An authority direction fitted on trivia also transfers to PIQA and multi-turn SYCON dialogues without refitting, and removing it lowers wrong-source compliance by tens of percentage points in four of five families with no detected change in MMLU-Pro or GSM8K accuracy at our evaluation sizes. Source deference and user agreement therefore need separate evaluation.
title: Authority Bias in Language Models: Source Deference and User Agreement Are Not Interchangeable
Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber

abstract: Job seekers often rely on separate tools for resume analysis, resume enhancement, job-description matching, interview practice, and job search.This paper presents CareerCraft AI, an integrated, candidate-facing web prototype that combines these functions in one workflow.The system uses rule-based extraction for PDF and DOCX resumes and a hosted large language model (LLM), with rule-based fallbacks for selected tasks.The paper describes the architecture, data model, processing workflow, and exploratory observations from a deployed instance.Illustrative outputs demonstrate the available interfaces, while consistency checks identify unresolved differences between displayed scores and simple count-based calculations.Exploratory testing also identified parsing limitations, variation in generated content, and unsupported achievement metrics in some resume rewrites.These observations motivate factual review, transparent score provenance, privacy safeguards, and systematic evaluation.The study documents an integrated prototype; its accuracy, reliability, fairness, and effectiveness have not been established.
title: CareerCraft AI: An Intelligent Employment Support System Integrating Resume Building, Applicant Tracking System (ATS) Analysis, and GeoBased Job Matching

abstract: Sensitivity is a cornerstone of early childhood mental health; however, its measurement relies heavily on tools developed in English-speaking, high-resource contexts. This systematic review identified observational and report-based instruments used to assess sensitivity in caregivers of children aged 0-6 years. It evaluated the methodological robustness and usability of these instruments within Latin American contexts. Following a systematic search in Web of Science, Scopus, PsycInfo, and Redalyc, 732 eligible studies were identified. Based on a frequency-of-use threshold, 16 instruments (14 observational and 2 report-based) represented across 616 papers were selected for in-depth evaluation. Measures were coded for theoretical alignment with Ainsworth's sensitivity definition, psychometric evidence, and usability-specifically training accessibility, administration complexity, and evidence of use with diverse Latin American populations (e.g., caregivers in rural settings or with lower educational levels). Results revealed that only a minority of measures adhered explicitly to Ainsworth's original definition. Most instruments prioritized warmth and positive affect, potentially leading to cross-cultural underdetection in contexts where responsiveness is expressed through proximity and routine-based care. While observational tools predominated, report-based measures showed limited validation and minimal regional use. These findings highlight the urgent need for culturally grounded validation and the development of accessible training programs for the region.
title: A systematic review of observational and report‐based measures of caregiver sensitivity: A Latin American perspective
Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra

abstract: Abstract Both the mining of arguments from natural language text (Chaps. 4 and 5 ) and the assessment of their properties (Chaps. 6 and 7 ) imply analysis tasks: NLP methods infer information from input texts. In the context of argument quality and reasoning, Chaps. 7 and 8 already covered some more synthesis-oriented tasks, the rewriting of argumentative text to improve its quality and the reconstruction of argument components left implicit in a text, respectively. In this chapter, we fully turn our view to situations in which new argumentative content is to be produced, be it single claims, complete arguments, or longer argumentative texts. That is, we consider synthesis tasks in detail here (even if, seen strictly, they lie outside the scope of a book called Argument Mining ): NLP methods produce new text from information or other input texts. We cover all such methods under the term argument generation .
title: Argument Generation

abstract: Abstract Although the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for essay scoring is not a new concept, these models do not grade in the same manner as humans. This discrepancy arises because humans can adapt their grading patterns based on the specific questions they encounter. In contrast, existing research on this topic typically employs a predefined rubric that fails to address the variability in responses effectively. There has been a noticeable lack of systematic research aimed at defining rubrics and prompts tailored to the responses considered. To address this issue and provide a structured approach to LLM-based grading, this paper suggests a new methodology. We propose the use of multiple LLMs for rubric generation and grading through a process of self-reflection and iteration. The key components of this system include: 1. Developing grading rubrics and prompt patterns that account for both the questions asked and the responses provided. 2. Employing self-reflective iteration rubrics across multiple LLMs to ensure consistent scoring for diverse responses. 3. Implementing verification and validation processes to effectively identify anomalous scores, allowing for re-evaluation and achieving consistency. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system offers new insights into the role of LLMs in Automated Essay Scoring (AES).
title: A collaborative multi-LLM framework with self-reflection iterative prompting for automated essay scoring

abstract: As LLMs (large language models) are increasingly used to generate synthetic personas, particularly in data-limited domains such as health, privacy, and HCI, it becomes necessary to understand how these narratives represent identity, especially that of minority communities. In this paper, we audit synthetic personas generated by 3 LLMs (GPT4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Deepseek v2.5) through the lens of representational harm, focusing specifically on racial identity. Using a mixed-methods approach combining close reading, lexical analysis, and a parameterized creativity framework, we compare 1,512 LLM-generated persona to human-authored responses. Our findings reveal that LLMs disproportionately foreground racial markers, overproduce culturally coded language, and construct personas that are syntactically elaborate yet narratively reductive. These patterns result in a range of sociotechnical harms, including stereotyping, exoticism, erasure, and benevolent bias, that are often obfuscated by superficially positive narrations. We formalize this phenomenon as algorithmic othering, where minoritized identities are rendered hypervisible but less authentic.
title: A Tale of Two Identities: An Ethical Audit of AI-Crafted Synthetic Personas
Mapping the Dissonance Delta: A Diachronic Analysis of Cognitive Friction and Constraint Adherence in Large Language Models
Read post

abstract: Abstract This work offers a new interpretation of the intellectual dialogue between Edmund Husserl and Bernhard Riemann’s theory of manifolds, arguing that this relationship extends beyond mere influence to constitute a central structural inspiration of the project Husserl would later outline as pure logic in the Prolegomena to Pure Logic . The original contribution of this analysis is to demonstrate how Husserl’s engagement evolved from an initial critical opposition, centered on the accusation of a “vicious circle” in deriving Euclidean geometry, to the adoption of Riemann’s work as a crucial paradigmatic model for his own Doctrine of Manifolds ( Mannigfaltigkeitslehre ). The paper documents the overcoming of this critique, a turning point evidenced by Husserl’s distinction between the “pure categorial form” of the manifold and its “concretization” in phenomenal space. In doing so, Husserl found in the Riemannian separation between a manifold’s abstract topological structure and its metric the perfect model for his own distinction between the ideal form of a theory and its empirical content. Ultimately, we demonstrate how Husserl assimilated the structural potentials of Riemann’s mathematics to prefigure the three fundamental tasks of pure logic, therefore transforming a revolutionary mathematical structure into a primary paradigm for his transcendental theory of science.
title: From Critique to Paradigm: Husserl’s Appropriation of Riemannian Geometry

abstract: Abstract Social virtual realities (SVR) as new arenas for online social interaction have been demonstrated to involve behaviors where users can experiment with embodiments and actions that exceed the capabilities of the physical human bodies and even norms of interpersonal interactions. In this study, we explore participants’ engagement in one such activity, throwing darts towards a co-participant’s avatar character in the context of SVR. We analyze a 16-minute video-recorded case from a quasi-experimental setting where two participants explore the SVR environment Rec Room together. We direct specific focus on the dart-throwing activity that occurs during the case. Using the method of multimodal conversation analysis, our study attends to the accomplishment of this activity as well as the changes and alterations in it, through the two facets of human cooperation, alignment and affiliation . The case reveals how the audible and embodied resources afforded by the avatars and the SVR setting work—or do not work—in the negotiation of the level of sharedness of the activity as well as the stances the participants indicate towards the activity. We show how the participants may jointly participate in the activity on the level of action (i.e., in terms of alignment) while having diverging emotional stances towards it (i.e., in terms of affiliation). Based on these observations, we discuss the possibilities of distinguishing between these two facets of human cooperation in the context of SVR and how they help to understand experimentative user interactions in these environments in general.
title: Negotiating the Sharedness of Activities and Stances in Social Virtual Reality: Alignment and Affiliation in the Activity of Throwing Darts at a Co-Participant

abstract: This paper reports on the University of Amsterdam’s participation in the CLEF 2025 Eloquent Track’s Robustness and Consistency Task. Our overall goal is to evaluate the influence of stylistic prompt variations on semantic interpretation. Our specific focus is to investigate how variations in prompt tone, structure, and persona affect the consistency and robustness of responses generated by large language models (LLMs). We approach this through two complementary methods. First, we use a model-as-judge setup to quantify semantic consistency: each stylistic variant prompt is compared to its original base prompt using GPT-4.1 to rate the similarity of the generated responses on a 0–5 scale. Second, we conduct an inductive qualitative analysis on a selected prompt to closely examine how different stylistic framings influence content shifts in model outputs. Our results suggest that prompt reformulations can lead to variations in output, informational content, and tone.
title: University of Amsterdam at the CLEF 2025 Eloquent Track:Evaluating the Influence of Stylistic Prompt Variations on Semantic Interpretation

abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) offers opportunities to develop a variety of teaching materials and strategies, but also presents challenges regarding the accuracy of information, academic integrity and the character development of pupils. This study aims to analyse PAI teachers’ perceptions of the use of AI, its practical application in teaching, and the associated ethical considerations at SMPN 5 Mesuji Raya. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data were collected through interviews with one PAI teacher and one pupil. Data analysis followed the model proposed by Miles, Huberman and Saldaña, which includes data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. The results indicate that AI is utilised to assist in the preparation of teaching modules, the creation of interactive quizzes, the development of visual media, and the design of case studies on moral values. The use of varied media is perceived to make learning more engaging. However, teachers’ acceptance of AI is critical and conditional, as the information generated requires verification and the technology cannot replace the teacher’s role as a role model, the shaping of moral character, or spiritual guidance. From an ethical perspective, the study highlights the importance of academic integrity and the application of the values of ṣidq (honesty) and tabayyun (verification of information) to guide the responsible use of AI. This study emphasises that the use of AI in Islamic Education must be accompanied by validation of the material, teacher support and clear rules of use to ensure it is aligned with learning objectives and Islamic values.
title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education: The Perceptions and Ethical Considerations of Islamic Religious Education Teachers in Lower Secondary Schools

abstract: Studies on lexical fields are rare in Old Frisian philology. However, as preparatory studies for a comprehensive Old Frisian dictionary, they are most useful. In this article, an attempt is made to diachronically-semantically analyze and define the eleven words used in Old Frisian to indicate types of roads. These words are in alphabetical order: dîk, drift(e), fe­re, låne, menninge, path, rêd, sīdwendene, stīge, strête and wei. In addition, the theory of Trier, which states that within a lexical field semantical changes affect some or even all members of that field, is applied to Old Frisian road indications. As will be shown, this notion is indeed applicable to the lexical field discussed, as in the course of time some words (for example dîk, strête) shift semantically, an older word has disappeared (fe­re) and new ones have risen (rêd, menninge, stīge).
title: Aldfryske wei-oantsjuttings. In ûndersyk nei it Aldfryske wurdfjild 'ferkearsferbinings oer lân'

abstract: Virtual Mental Health Assistants (VMHAs) continuously evolve to support the overloaded global healthcare system, which receives approximately 60 million primary care visits and 6 million emergency room visits annually. These systems, developed by clinical psychologists, psychiatrists, and AI researchers, are designed to aid in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). The main focus of VMHAs is to provide relevant information to mental health professionals (MHPs) and engage in meaningful conversations to support individuals with mental health conditions. However, certain gaps prevent VMHAs from fully delivering on their promise during active communications. One of the gaps is their inability to explain their decisions to patients and MHPs, making conversations less trustworthy. Additionally, VMHAs can be vulnerable in providing unsafe responses to patient queries, further undermining their reliability. In this review, we assess the current state of VMHAs on the grounds of user-level explainability and safety, a set of desired properties for the broader adoption of VMHAs. This includes the examination of ChatGPT, a conversation agent developed on AI-driven models: GPT3.5 and GPT-4, that has been proposed for use in providing mental health services. By harnessing the collaborative and impactful contributions of AI, natural language processing, and the mental health professionals (MHPs) community, the review identifies opportunities for technological progress in VMHAs to ensure their capabilities include explainable and safe behaviors. It also emphasizes the importance of measures to guarantee that these advancements align with the promise of fostering trustworthy conversations.
title: A review of the explainability and safety of conversational agents for mental health to identify avenues for improvement

abstract: If a model has some behavioral tendency, such as sycophancy or misalignment, and it is trained on its own outputs, will the tendency be amplified in the next generation of models? We study this question by training a series of models where each model is finetuned on data generated by its predecessor, and the initial model is seeded with some persona or belief. We test three settings: supervised finetuning (SFT) on instruct models, synthetic document finetuning (SDF) on base models, and direct preference optimization (DPO). In the SFT and SDF settings, traits mostly decay or remain constant so that further finetuning cycles do nothing. In rare cases when amplification occurs, it generally comes at the cost of coherence. In the DPO setting, trait amplification can reliably occur when a model is continually trained with a preference for its own outputs, but vanishes when models are reinitialized at each cycle. Overall, our results suggest that amplification most likely comes from continual post-training, and limiting this stage may be an effective defense. For non-RL finetuning, trait amplification is rare and very sensitive to data quantity, making it significantly less likely to occur accidentally. Finally, the amplification-coherence tradeoff serves as a natural deterrent against trait amplification.
title: Iterative Finetuning is Mostly Idempotent

abstract: Best-of-$N$ is a widely used inference strategy for complex reasoning, whose effectiveness depends on whether sampled candidates can cover diverse and high-quality reasoning paths. However, post-trained reasoning models often suffer from \emph{exploration collapse}, where independent rollouts repeatedly follow similar reasoning paths and limit the gains from increasing the rollout budget. Existing methods alleviate this issue by promoting broader exploration, but do not explicitly guide exploration toward continuations that make meaningful progress, resulting in limited exploration efficiency. To address this, we propose \emph{\underline{S}tate-conditioned \underline{P}rogress-guided \underline{S}teering} (SPS), a training-free latent steering framework. Specifically, SPS constructs a state-conditioned Direction Bank containing multiple progress-guided steering vectors for different prefix-state regions. During online inference, SPS retrieves a suitable steering vector based on the current prefix state and applies it at high-uncertainty transitions to guide the next reasoning step toward meaningful progress. Extensive experiments across multiple model scales and benchmarks demonstrate that SPS consistently outperforms strong baselines. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of its key designs and offer valuable insights for future research. The code is available at https://github.com/rattlesnakey/SPS.
title: Efficient Reasoning Exploration via State-Conditioned Latent Steering with Progress Guidance

abstract: We propose to model singular data clouds by subanalytic sets, and develop an approach to semi-supervised learning in this setting. It relies on a Morrey-type embedding for Sobolev spaces relative to globally subanalytic measures with possibly singular support. As an illustration, we present a greedy method based on a Monte Carlo approximation of the Sobolev norm of the candidate solutions. We report numerical experiments on point clouds sampled from real algebraic varieties, as well as a test on a classification problem based on MNIST images downsampled into $7\times7$.
title: Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets

abstract: The subject of the research is issues related to the study and analysis of the structure, as well as the construction of complex criminal cases, i.e. criminal cases in which proceedings are conducted in relation to several crimes and (or) several defendants. The purpose of the study is to identify and systematize the ways of constructing complex criminal cases. The research methods are: generalization, description, analysis, synthesis and the formal legal method. Results . In the development of the theory of the limits of criminal proceedings formulated in the science of criminal procedure, it is proposed to introduce into scientific circulation such a “measuring” unit characterizing the structure and scope of a criminal case as the “procedural composition”, as elements of which three components are distinguished: “persona—res—qualificatio”. With the help of “procedural structures”, the main structural patterns of the formation of complex cases are described and systematized. The Author substantiates the position according to which all methods of constructing multi-part criminal cases are divided into internal and external, each of which is capable of solving a specific procedural problem that arises at one time or another during the criminal proceedings. Internal methods of constructing multi-part criminal cases make it possible to form new, independent procedural structures in the structure of an already initiated criminal case without the need to initiate new criminal cases and their subsequent addition. External methods of constructing multi-part criminal cases are used to form a system of procedural structures by attaching procedural structures that have already been constructed in another criminal case. As a conclusion of the research conducted on the basis of judicial practice, it was revealed that any component of the procedural structure can act as a constituent. At the same time, if all three components can act as constituent components in internal methods of constructing criminal cases: “persona”, “res” and “qualificatio”, then in external methods there are only two components: “persona” and “res”. In addition, it is noted that multi-part criminal cases can be constructed in combined ways, when the constituent components are not one, but two or even three components at once. The proposed approach, according to the Author, will provide a more in-depth analysis and understanding of the interrelationships of the structural elements of a criminal case as a systemic phenomenon and will further formulate specific recommendations for the practical construction of complex criminal cases.
title: The Main Structural Patterns of the Construction of Multi-Part Criminal Cases

abstract: Purpose This article aims at exploring global citizenship in the context of higher education institutions (HEIs) which are increasingly affected by artificial intelligence (AI)-driven interactions. By using AI in a human-centred way, educators can expand ways to create global citizenship, offer personalised and empathetic learning while transcending conventional boundaries of education. AI technologies, including natural language processing, machine translation and adaptive learning systems, enable learners to engage with diverse linguistic and cultural materials in increasingly meaningful ways. These tools facilitate immersive language learning, simulate intercultural interactions and provide real-time feedback connected to individual needs in contemporary HEIs. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a theoretical/conceptual approach. Findings While human-centred AI-driven HEIs are gaining importance, the need to create awareness of character strengths and human-centred new learning environments increases as well. In this article, it is argued that pedagogical love, as a character strength, becomes more important in contemporary HEIs than ever before. By integrating AI thoughtfully and ethically into curricula, educators and institutions can contribute to the education of empathetic, multilingual global citizens. Research limitations/implications This research is limited to a qualitative theoretical and conceptual study and may build the base for future empirical studies. Practical implications Love, as a character strength, might support mental health, well-being and human interconnectedness. Originality/value This approach can strengthen the role of HEIs in creating a more peaceful, integrated world.
title: Love as a foundation for global citizenship in human-centred AI-driven higher education institutions – a theoretical exploration

abstract: Con el propósito de evaluar la abundancia y la composición de dinoflagelados potencialmente tóxicos asociados al material orgánico flotante (drift) en la isla de San Andrés, se seleccionaron siete sitios de muestreo a lo largo de la margen Norte y Este, paralelos a la barrera arrecifal y a las principales praderas de fanerógamas marinas y macroalgas de la isla. Durante la época de mayor intensidad de vientos, se recolectaron muestras de drift; se identificaron los sustratos a especie y posteriormente se sumergieron en solución 1:1 agua de mar filtrada y solución de Transeau. Luego de agitar vigorosamente las muestras para remover los dinoflagelados, se tamizo la suspensión con una malla de 80 µm y el filtrado se observó al microscopio óptico. Se encontraron cinco sustratos, dos especies de pastos marinos y tres de macroalgas. Sobre los sustratos se identificaron doce especies de dinoflagelados, diez reportadas como tóxicas, causantes de diarrea, parálisis y ciguatera. La abundancia de dinoflagelados varió ampliamente con promedios máximos (±DE) de 15 354±15 749 células/g peso seco de sustrato. De las especies de dinoflagelados, cinco son nuevos registros para San Andrés. No se encontraron diferencias significativas en los valores de diversidad de dinoflagelados entre drift y praderas de pastos y macroalgas, no obstante, la abundancia fue mucho mayor en el drift. Los resultados indican que el drift es un importante sustrato para dinoflagelados y dada su naturaleza flotante, representa tal vez el vector más importante para la dispersión de estos agentes de toxicidad en la isla. Para mitigar el efecto de eventos tóxicos asociados a dinoflagelados en salud pública, pesca y turismo, es necesario diseñar un plan de manejo del material orgánico flotante, que permita mejorar el entendimiento de su composición y dinámica temporal, monitorear las toxinas asociadas e implementar mecanismos de recolección y tratamiento.
title: DINOFLAGELADOS POTENCIALMENTE TÓXICOS ASOCIADOS A MATERIAL ORGÁNICO FLOTANTE (DRIFT) EN SAN ANDRÉS ISLA, RESERVA INTERNACIONAL DE LA BIOSFERA - SEAFLOWER

abstract: ABSTRACT Social comparison theory holds that people compare themselves with others when objective standards of self‐evaluation are unavailable. Contemporary societies supply measurement on an unprecedented scale, yet comparison has not receded. This article argues that many metrics in digital life function as pseudo‐objective standards: socially relative assessments presented as independent requirements of achievement or adequacy. It develops two contributions. First, the comparative regime names a configuration linking commensuration, algorithmic selection and commercial demand generation through personalised, recurrent feedback. Comparison participates in constituting desire by arranging what appears worth wanting before deliberation begins. Its distinctiveness lies in this configuration. Second, the criterion of comparative capture identifies when such feedback undermines reflective authority: it supplies a want, keeps its standard of adequacy moving, and obstructs examination or refusal of either. These conditions must operate together; an upstream origin alone does not establish pathology. The article locates the regime historically and institutionally, explains its economic persistence and the agency that remains within it, and derives testable implications. Non‐comparative selfhood names the reflective authority needed to examine desires, protect non‐positional goods and bring comparison to an end.
title: The Comparative Regime: How Pseudo‐Objective Standards Constitute Desire

abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM) occurs when narrow finetuning induces dangerous behavior outside the finetuning task. Detecting this shift through repeated behavioral evaluation is costly, motivating our checkpoint-level monitoring from internal representations. We define a fixed coordinate system from seven alignment-relevant activation directions and use it to track representational drift during LoRA finetuning of four open-source 7-9B language models. Finetuning drift in this space exhibits a dominant axis that explains 78.6% of variance and remains stable across datasets, extraction choices, and parameter-update capacities. Across 468 checkpoints from three EM-relevant held-out datasets, the resulting monitors attain 1.8% FNR, 2.0% FPR, and 0.989 AUROC, outperforming semantic, random, PCA, and SAE feature baselines. On a fourth dataset, a matched benign-dangerous control shows that substantial representational drift can also occur under benign finetuning, while changes across the 7D profile still distinguish dangerous from benign runs. Stress tests across two 14B models, full finetuning, longer training horizons, and misaligned starting states show that the signal can persist across shifts in training configuration, while reliable deployment may require recalibration.
title: Trait-space Monitoring for Emergent Misalignment During Supervised Finetuning
Depression Detection in Bengali Social-Media Text via Clinically Grounded Linguistic Feature Fusion and Interpretable Machine Learning

abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as human simulators for interactive evaluation and social simulation. Yet helpfulness-driven post-training pulls them toward a homogeneous, overly agreeable assistant register, creating a behavioral Sim2Real gap. We present OdysSim, the largest open systematic investigation of behavioral foundation models, i.e., models trained to simulate human behavior at scale. We propose SOUL, a taxonomy of five capability axes (CONV, SS, COG, ROLE, EVAL) that unifies 62 datasets and 23 benchmark tasks under one framework. Specifically, we curate the OdysSim corpus (21.4M interactions, 10B tokens, retrofitted with back-generated social contexts), construct the SOUL-Index benchmark, and develop an end-to-end training recipe combining midtraining, task-specific RL, and expert distillation. The resulting open 8B OSim model ranks first or tied-first on 8 of 23 tasks, outperforming any individual frontier model by this count, with the strongest gains on conversational and social tasks. Its outputs are also more human-like in length, formatting, and word choice, and it transfers zero-shot to out-of-distribution user simulation on $τ$-bench, nearly matching real users on reaction alignment (93.2 vs. 93.5). We further show that LLM-as-judge RL induces reward-hacking patterns, and that our detectors can mitigate them during post-training. Together, our findings suggest that behavioral foundation models require rethinking the LLM training paradigm. We release all artifacts to support future research.
title: OdysSim: Building Foundation Models for Human Behavior Simulation

abstract: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

abstract: In the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0), developing digital human resources is a critical task that enables commercial banks to enhance their competitiveness, ensure safe operations, and achieve sustainable development in the digital environment. In particular, realizing the objectives outlined in Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW and the Banking Sector Digital Transformation Strategy to 2030 makes the development of digital human resources an urgent priority for the banking industry. This article analyzes the current implementation of measures to develop digital human resources in Vietnamese commercial banks over recent years. It identifies key challenges in this process and proposes several recommendations to advance digital human resource development in Vietnamese commercial banks in the coming period.
title: DEVELOPING DIGITAL HUMAN RESOURCES IN VIETNAMESE COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE CONTEXT OF THE FOURTH INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION

abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into higher education has introduced new challenges concerning academic integrity. Although AI can effectively support students throughout the learning process, it’s inappropriate or unethical use may lead to adverse consequences for students' academic development. This study aims to examine the relationship between students' personality maturity, with particular emphasis on the dimensions of responsibility and honesty, and their AI ethical awareness, defined as the ethical consciousness surrounding the use of AI technologies. The study employed a quantitative causal research design, with data collected from a sample of LP3I Polytechnic students through a structured questionnaire. The theoretical and empirical findings indicate that personality maturity is positively and significantly associated with AI ethical awareness. Specifically, the honesty dimension plays a crucial role in mitigating AI-assisted plagiarism, while the responsibility dimension promotes the accountable and ethical use of AI technologies. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening character education and digital ethics in higher education institutions to address the challenges posed by ongoing digital technological disruption.
title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN STUDENTS' PERSONALITY MATURITY AND ETHICAL AWARENESS IN THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) A STUDY AT LP3I JAKARTA POLYTECHNIC

abstract: La problématique centrale de la thèse est l'évaluation de l'impact de démarches utilisant la formulation de scénarios et de personnages sur les phases d'expression des besoins en conception innovante. La méthodologie de recherche mise en œuvre est une démarche empirique qui s'appuie sur l'analyse de situations de conception. Au cours du doctorat, un protocole expérimental mis en œuvre a été dupliqué trois fois dans des laboratoires partenaires. Cette recherche aboutit à un mémoire de thèse qui présente plusieurs contributions : La première contribution se situe autour de la méthodologie de recherche proposée. Le protocole d'étude empirique mis en place est original, il s'appuie sur l'état de l'art des réflexions de la communauté et sur ces démarches de recherche, et proposes des éléments nouveaux à cette réflexion en conciliant approches quantitatives et qualitatives. La seconde contribution porte sur la caractérisation de l'impact des méthodologies étudiées sur la construction d'une représentation partagée du problème de conception et de la formalisation des exigences de conception. Enfin la troisième contribution porte sur l'analyse des interactions dans les activités de conception étudiées. Les analyses identifient et qualifient les impacts des méthodes étudiées sur le contenu des interactions dans les phases amont de la conception.
title: The impact of scenarios and personas on requirement elicitation : an experimental study

abstract: Asked what to study, which career to pursue, or what product to build, large language models (LLMs) often recommend AI-related options. We ask where this tendency comes from by comparing models before and after fine-tuning and by varying how questions are asked. First, pretrained models already include explicit AI/ML terms in the recommendations of 27% of their responses, and their released instruction-tuned versions do so in 59%. Second, fine-tuning models ourselves shows that this rise is not inevitable: general instruction tuning leaves the rate unchanged, but removing the 7% of instruction examples that concern AI cuts it by 14 percentage points, below the level of the pretrained models it starts from. Data rewarding helpfulness raise it by 9 points, while data ranked by the preferences of diverse simulated users lower it by 9. Finally, with models held fixed, asking for the "best" option or for what to do "right now" raises the rate by 8 and 18 points, whereas telling the model it is an AI advisor adds 4. Overall, the tendency starts in pretraining, and what models learn afterward, together with how a question is phrased, decides how strongly it appears.
title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?

abstract: Self-improving agent pipelines have a problem at their center. An optimizer rewrites prompts to score higher, and the score comes from a judge that is itself an LLM. That judge has the last word on whether the system is getting better, and our position is that it has not earned it. The judge should be demoted from oracle to advisor: its verdict becomes one input among several, and every change is gated instead by a deterministic verification layer the judge cannot override. We reached this position by building the alternative and running it. Over months of running autonomous prompt-optimization loops in production across contract analysis, compliance review, and code quality, we cataloged eleven ways the evaluation signal failed, in four classes: judge bias, harness and metric failures, ground-truth errors, and reward hacking. Agents achieved perfect scores by reading cached answer keys from their environment, a 100% pass rate concealing 68% true capability. A corrupted ground-truth label caused the optimizer to delete correct compliance rules to agree with it. A syntactically broken prompt was promoted as the winner because a silent parser fallback improved the metric. Attempts to fix the judge by rewriting its rubric plateaued; the only reliable gain came from a structural constraint on its output order. In response we describe PROCTOR, a Teacher-Student loop in which a stateful orchestrator holds all tool access, stateless subagents diagnose failures and draft mutations they cannot apply, and a Teacher grades those mutations under five deterministic guardrails: hermetic sandboxes, capability-disjoint roles, acceptance checks that outrank the Teacher, frozen holdouts, and canary cases engineered so that a perfect score is itself evidence of cheating. We report the failures this prevented, and, because the Teacher is itself an LLM judge, the failures it did not.
title: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails

abstract: This study analyzes psychological duality in Hermann Hesse's novel Demian through the lens of Jungian psychoanalytic theory, focusing on the concepts of persona and shadow in relation to the light and dark realms phenomenon. Employing qualitative textual analysis, this study delves into Sinclair's psychological development and self-integration as portrayed in the symbolic assertion between the dichotomy. Discussions and findings reveal that this dichotomy is not an absolute opposite but a highly dynamic reality that helps Sinclair get to know himself, the process of understanding himself in the chaotic event of psychological conflict. Sinclair’s contemplation of the sparrow hawk painting and his conversation with Demian and Pistorius serve as important moments in this internal turmoil. This research contributes to the fields of literature and psychology by presenting Demian's novel as a view that the light and dark realms are a highly dynamic phenomenon that influences the emergence of persona and shadow in a person. However, there are still limitations in contextualizing the novel's pre-World War I socio-historical influences. Future research could explore how historical tensions shaped Sinclair's journey, deepening the analysis of personal transformation within broader societal changes.
title: Light and Dark Realm Phenomenon: Analysis of Persona and Shadow in Hermann Hesse’s Demian

abstract:
Based on the premise that the criminal law in Colombia is applicable throughout the national territory, it discusses a special case compared to the unimputability of the indigenous person on the basis of the principle expressed by the Constitutional Court as a “sociocultural diversity”, as an expression of recognition of a pluralist State.
In development of the above comes to normative sources, dogmatic and jurisprudential, particularly seeking the concepts of imputability and unimputability; subsequently, explains the meaning and scope of the principle of sociocultural diversity in relation to the unimputability of the indigenous person.
title: Imputabilidad e inimputabilidad frente a la persona indígena

abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit both overlapping and distinct clinical features, including sex differences in prevalence and symptomatology, but how these similarities and differences are reflected at the molecular and cellular level in the human brain remains poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from individuals with MDD, BD, and neurotypical controls to resolve molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. Our analysis revealed sex- and diagnosis-specific differences across white matter, the neurovascular unit (NVU), and neuronal compartments. Within white matter, we identified female-specific survival-response programs shared in both MDD and BD, and divergent myelin-related gene expression patterns across disorders (CLDN11, CNDP1). Within the NVU, transcriptional evidence of impaired vascular integrity was accompanied by astrocytic response profiles in females with MDD and males with BD, with inflammatory responses further evident in females with MDD (IFITM3, CEBPD, IL1R1). In donors with BD of both sexes and in females with MDD, inhibitory neurons exhibited impaired neuropeptide expression (SST, CORT, CRH). Integration with donor genotype information highlighted that genetic risk for mood disorders influences MAPK3 expression, implicating altered ERK signaling, which was further supported by disorder-associated changes in Ras/MEK/ERK pathway components in neurons (MAPK3, DUSP6, RASD1, ELK1). Together, these findings reveal coordinated, cell type- and spatial domain-specific molecular programs that distinguish shared and disorder-specific transcriptomic changes across mood disorders in a sex-dependent manner.
title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex

abstract: Generate–test–revise loops are common in coding agents, but repetition alone provides no reliability guarantee. We study the gap between finding a correct patch and retaining, verifying, and submitting it. A sealed five-seed study over 30 HumanEval repairs produces 900 three-revision trajectories. Under forced revision, current correctness with current traces falls from 0.820 after one revision to 0.673 after two, although ever-correct rises to 0.847. Two common-state studies use 2,430 branches from identical frozen programs to remove post-treatment risk-set bias. In a prespecified 14B replication, stale traces harm 34/135 correct starts versus 4/135 with current traces, a 22.2-point increase (task-cluster 95% CI [8.9,37.0], exact Holm p=0.0337). A prospective 540-rollout policy eliminates observed correct-start harm but reduces wrong-start repair and fails its joint criterion. Repository experiments over 24 bugs and four coder stacks expose floor effects and component heterogeneity without Holm-significant effects. We therefore separate admission, preservation, grounded certification, competence, and liveness. We derive an evidence-bound typed loop contract and instantiate its mechanically enforceable subset in a reference implementation that binds verifier evidence to exact code states, preserves verified checkpoints, and emits auditable admission receipts. The implementation is an executable specification and conformance artifact, not evidence of improved repair competence or calibrated verifier dependence.
title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair
Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
How AT&T is rethinking in-house legal work with OpenAI
