The dataset comprised Qur’anic verses and classical poetry. The homonyms were first collected, then analyzed for contextual meaning, and then translated by the chatbots. The data were presented without diacritics to replicate the conditions of authentic Arabic text. After the items were translated, the data were assessed using the TAUS Adequacy/Fluency model to determine the extent to which the systems preserved meaning while maintaining linguistic naturalness. The results showed that while all chatbots often achieved high fluency, their adequacy slightly differed across text types and homonym categories. Gemini outperformed the other models overall, followed by ChatGPT and DeepSeek. The Qur’anic translation performed best due to the high prevalence of such texts in online corpora. However, the performance declined noticeably in the poetic and classical domains. While large language models (LLMs) represent a significant improvement over traditional machine translation (MT) systems in handling lexical ambiguity, they remain unable to reliably disambiguate complex Arabic homonyms without contextual or cultural grounding. The study concludes that AI systems require substantially more training, particularly in Arabic-language contexts. The study therefore recommended further research on homonym translation, focusing on different contexts as well as the rendition of homonyms outside of pairings.
title: Translating ambiguity: A comparative evaluation of AI Chatbots in rendering Arabic full homonyms into English

abstract: Introduction Research on associations between pornography viewing and sexual violence has been limited by the absence of validated instruments that differentiate exposure along a violence continuum within pornographic practices, with existing measures focused on consumption frequency or problematic patterns rather than on the specific content consumed. The Pornography Violence Exposure Scale (PVES) was developed to assess exposure to pornographic content graded across three violence levels: non-violent material and domination-without-pain (Level 1), coercive content (Level 2), and explicit physical aggression (Level 3). Methods A cross-sectional study with 2,181 Spanish young adults aged 18–35 years who reported viewing pornography examined factor structure, measurement invariance across sex and age, convergent, nomological, and incremental validity, and discriminative capacity for sexual violence outcomes via Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results A bifactor model demonstrated good fit (CFI = 0.978, TLI = 0.957, RMSEA = 0.076), with a dominant general factor (ωH = 0.84, ECV = 0.81) capturing graded exposure to violent content. Strict measurement invariance was supported across sex and age groups. Convergent correlations with sexual violence outcomes (mean | r | = 0.24) substantially exceeded near-zero nomological associations with sexual function and partner-evaluation indicators (mean |r| = 0.03), and the general factor produced significant incremental validity for both victimization (Δ R 2 = 0.088) and perpetration (Δ R 2 = 0.200), with acceptable discrimination for perpetration (AUC = 0.753). Discussion The PVES is the first psychometrically validated instrument for measuring differentiated exposure to violent pornographic content, enabling more precise investigation of content-specific associations with sexual violence outcomes.
title: Pornography Violence Exposure Scale: a graded bifactor measure of exposure to violent pornographic content

abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. A short reference recording suffices to transfer a speaker's turn-taking style to the model, and the transfer is reference-specific: swapping in another speaker's reference worsens the match in 93-98% of cases, whereas the best uniform dose is indistinguishable from no steering. Turn-taking style is not frozen into the weights but a direction that can be read, shifted, and calibrated per person. Audio examples are available at https://elpsykongloo.github.io/initiative-vector/.
title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models

abstract: The aim of this thesis study was to find out the possibility of exporting education specifically Leadership and Service Design to the Philippines, determine the problems in the export of education, and to define the value of the studies to the students. The research also tried to identify the current market. Work was performed by different qualitative research methods such as questionnaires, theme interviews, a survey and a workshop. Service Design tools were also utilized such as personas, customer journey and service blueprint to obtain customer insights. To gain background information of existing service providers and analyze the current market, several universities in the Philippines have been benchmarked. These were organized in the Philippines. Interviews and theme interviews were administered in Finland. Among the interviewees were Filipino nurses working in Finland like practical nurses in various medical institutions, a few of them are studying part-time. Theme interview participants are teachers from Aboa Mare and Turku University of Applied Sciences. The commissioner of the thesis is the Master’s Degree Programme in Leadership and Service Design, Novia University of Applied Sciences. The study concluded that Leadership and Service Design in the Philippines is pioneering and unique of its kind therefore this research revealed that there is a huge possibility to export the programme to the Philippines. Possible customers are mostly individuals pursuing a wider career advancement or opportunity and companies aiming to spearhead in their line of services.
title: Export of Master Degree Programme to the Philippines: Case Leadership and Service Design

abstract: These poems explore the nature of restlessness through a variety of landscapes and personas, both historical and imaginary. Many of these poems draw on elements of the traditional fable by investigating the risks of leave-taking, the journey, and the danger of curiosity
authors: NC DOCKS at The University of North Carolina at Greensboro
title: Warnings & fables

abstract: Abstract In 2024, an arbitral tribunal dismissed for lack of jurisdiction a claim brought by Koch Industries against Canada arising from the cancellation of Ontario’s cap-and-trade programme. This article argues that the award should be read not as a case-specific outcome but as the first encounter in investment treaty arbitration with a structural problem that will recur with increasing frequency as carbon markets globalize and establish links. Emissions trading systems are dynamic regulatory instruments whose caps must contract, whose rules will change as governments respond to shifting political priorities, energy security pressures, and geopolitical disruption, and whose linking arrangements may be modified or terminated. When regulatory action impairs or extinguishes allowances held by foreign investors across a linked system, the domestic legal character of those allowances enters a jurisdictional analysis whose structure and decisive threshold vary according to the treaty definition, the arbitral forum, and the interpretive methodology of the tribunal. The article examines Koch v Canada as the first decided investment case and traces the mechanism through two further configurations under a broad asset-based bilateral investment treaty and the Energy Charter Treaty, demonstrating that the same instrument may or may not constitute a protected investment depending on a configuration of variables that no single actor controls and most will not have foreseen. The problem operates at a level logically prior to the post-establishment regulatory space questions that dominate the current literature on investment protection and climate policy.
title: The linking problem: emissions trading, investment treaty jurisdiction, and the globalization of carbon markets

abstract: ABSTRACT Top executive narcissism is a crucial yet often overlooked concept in ESG performance. Current research primarily focuses on CEO narcissism, offering an incomplete view by largely ignoring the Board Chair's key role in shaping ESG outcomes. Furthermore, there is a notable lack of a comprehensive narcissism index, which would surpass the limitations of single‐ or limited‐indicator measures typically used in previous studies. To deepen understanding, this study empirically examines the distinct effects of narcissism exhibited by both the CEO and the Board Chair on a firm's environmental, social, and governance (ESG) pillars. By analyzing executive narcissism states in integrated report narratives alongside ESG data for 255 publicly listed companies from 2018 to 2023, measured via Refinitiv Eikon scores, this study shows that Board Chair narcissism is positively related to environmental and social performance but negatively related to governance performance. Conversely, CEO narcissism is positively associated with both environmental and governance performance but negatively associated with social performance. The varying effects across ESG dimensions indicate that narcissistic leadership depends on the executive's role and the stakeholder domain involved. This study advances upper echelons theory, the concept of narcissistic personality, and stakeholder theory by revealing the complex interactions among various executive narcissistic states and emphasizing the need to recognize these dynamics. Additionally, the findings offer practical insights into board composition and executive hiring to support sustainable business strategies.
title: The Dual Narcissists: Disentangling the Distinct Impacts of CEO and Board Chair Narcissism on Corporate ESG Performance

abstract: Latin American national courts increasingly make use of the pro persona principle of interpretation, dealing with both international and domestic laws. This principle is reconcilable with other methods. However, operating in a unidirectional manner as it does, it tends to fade out other rules of interpretation. The resulting interpretive work may be viewed as a threat to the integrity of international law, or as an enrichment of its development by judicial voices from the ‘global South’. Within the region, the underlying narrative of the ‘interpretive turn’ is integration. This is strongly questioned here since there are some fundamental problems which are ignored by the eulogistic nature of the legal philosophy that underpins the pro persona, such as the alienation of the legal communities and cultures involved. The chapter analyses these developments in light of the case law of the Colombian Constitutional Court and the Mexican Supreme Court.
title: The Law and Politics of the Pro Persona Principle in Latin America

abstract: Public trust in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) may depend not only on technical success but also on the fairness of their decision making. While a recent trend in AV research involves using general purpose "common sense" models to guide AV decision making, the degree to which these inherit human biases in driving is still understudied. Given that psychology studies have shown human driver biases exist, such as lower pedestrian-yielding rates to Black pedestrians in the US, we argue that analyses of model bias should also be part of AV evaluation. Concretely, in this paper we propose two new bias testing methodologies for Large Language Models (LLMs) and Visual-Language Models (VLMs), "All Else Being Equal" tests and "Self-Consistency" tests, and a new benchmark (FairYield) to assess bias in pedestrian-yielding decisions. Our findings show that the yielding decisions of both LLMs and VLMs can be influenced by models' predictions of pedestrian gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, skin tone, and socio-economic status. While the type and degree of bias is different from model to model, we highlight common patterns, and raise questions about the "common sense" model paradigm, particularly the need to either revise the paradigm or address issues of downstream bias.
title: LLM-Driven Autonomous Vehicles Can Inherit Human Driver Biases in Pedestrian Yielding: Results and Implications From a New Benchmark

abstract: The digital revolution has introduced important ethical challenges for younger generations, including the spread of hoaxes, plagiarism, and cyberbullying. This research examines the integration of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a pedagogical partner in civic education to strengthen digital ethics grounded in Pancasila as Indonesia’s local wisdom. Employing a mixed-methods approach, data were collected through questionnaires administered to 332 senior and vocational high school students, Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with 10 civic education teachers in Central Java Province, and in-depth interviews with experts in Civic and Character Education. The study findings reveal that, despite students' active use of AI, their critical thinking skills and digital ethics require further development. Teachers expressed an urgent need for adaptive, context-specific learning resources. Pancasila values provide a relevant and robust philosophical foundation for developing a digital ethics framework. Based on these findings, the study proposes an innovative framework that positions AI chatbots not merely as tools but as simulative and reflective learning partners. The framework seeks to transform learning from simple knowledge transmission to value-oriented education, enabling teachers to act as facilitators who guide students in actualising Pancasila values within the digital space.
title: AI as a Pedagogical Partner: A Value-Based Framework for Digital Ethics in Civic Education

abstract: In developing a program for the work for character training, it is necessary not only to determine the content and structure of the material constituting the program, but to come to decisions in advance on a number of matters of principle. In our view, the article by N. I. Boldyrev (Soviet Education No. 4, 1958) reveals the function and significance of this document and poses a number of questions that are worthy of discussion. One of these is formulated as follows: What should provide the foundation for the program of character training — organization of the activity of the pupils or shaping of qualities of personality? The author of the article believes that these two factors have to be combined, but that the major one, nevertheless, should be the organization of the activity of. the pupils.
title: Certain Questions as to the Program for Character Training in the Schools

abstract: Traditional literary aesthetics can clarify the murky status of originality and honesty in nonfiction. Analyses that specif ically apply to poetry and fiction apply equally well to ordinary expository prose, though people rarely apply them. Many aids to writing recommend originality and honesty in essays, and many readers try to evaluate essays by these criteria, but true originality and honesty do not fit in good writing. At the same time, writ ing must appear original and honest. This illusion the writer controls through a conventional literary persona. Critics of writing often perceive honesty and originality in excellent writing and dishonesty and triteness in shabby writing, but honesty and originality only very imprecisely describe the qualities in question, which more properly are the appearance of honesty and the appearance of originality. While a writer's sim ple truthfulness fails to charm because of (true) inconsistencies in the persona and the information, good writers create satis factory illusions when they present consistent and partial infor mation through a persona, a consistent and partial personality. Originality, too, misleads as a criterion: educating is largely acquainting with cliches?more charitably called conventions, traditions, common knowledge?and the appearance of origi nality is actually sophistication with cliches. The civilizing effect of education, if any, comes from learning about the common patterns of one's world, and, in writing, thinking for oneself usually means estimating accurately how many people will agree with one's ideas. To appear original, ideas need not be now, but they must not be presented as more new than they are. Writers of nonfiction, just like writers of fiction, tend an illu
title: Writing as Illusion.
Beyond Safe Data: Pretraining-Stage Alignment with Regular Safety Reflection

abstract: Execution-Level Evidence for Democratic Resilience to prevent algorithmic manipulation at the time of crisis : Relevance to the European Democracy Shield and Comparable Frameworks Worldwide What This Record Does This record shows that algorithmic amplification of civic information can be made accountable at the moment it takes effect, without restricting speech and without creating trade barriers. It does four things: It explains how the Algorithmic Logic Fingerprint (ALF) architecture adds an execution-level evidence layer to the European Democracy Shield and to comparable frameworks worldwide. It proves formally that the mechanism cannot remove, alter, or disfavor any speech because of what that speech says, and that it never touches a user’s direct publication. It sets out why the architecture is compatible with World Trade Organization disciplines and with the source-code provisions of modern digital-trade agreements. It publishes a working reference implementation with 150 passing tests and measured latency, so that the claims of feasibility and negligible overhead can be checked by anyone. Execution-Level Evidence for Democratic Resilience The European Democracy Shield, presented by the European Commission on 12 November 2025, names the integrity of the information space and free and fair elections as core pillars of democratic resilience. Its instruments are mainly coordination, monitoring, fact-checking, and rapid alerts. These are essential, but they all work by observing and then responding. They can detect an amplification event and react to it. They cannot establish, before an item reaches millions of people, which algorithmic configuration actually authorized its amplification. The ALF architecture supplies that missing execution-level layer. It produces verifiable, output-specific evidence that the authorized configuration, rather than a substituted fallback, experiment, or cache path, produced a given amplification of civic information during a declared electoral or crisis mode. Where that evidence is missing or does not match, the amplification is withheld before it takes effect rather than discovered after the fact. The same layer is technically relevant to frameworks beyond the European Union: the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (2024), including its provisions on the integrity of democratic processes; the United Kingdom’s Online Safety Act 2023; Australia’s Online Safety Act 2021; India’s Information Technology Act, 2000, with its Intermediary Guidelines Rules; the electoral rules on artificial intelligence adopted by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court. ALF verifies each platform’s own proprietary configuration against that platform’s own approved reference. That gives these different legal systems one shared technical evidence format. It does not require a common ranking model, disclosure of source code or model weights, or any judgment of political viewpoint. Algorithmic accountability does not require algorithmic uniformity. These references describe technical relevance only and do not establish legal compliance under any framework. Protecting Free Speech by Construction: A Formal Argument The most serious objection to any control over amplification is that it could become a tool for suppressing speech. ALF is designed so that this cannot happen through the mechanism itself. The following model and propositions make that precise. Model. An output operation is o = (x, d, k, s), where x is the content, d the recipient, s the delivery sink, and k the operation class: either DIRECT (a user’s own publication) or AMPLIFY (algorithmic ranking, recommendation, or boosting). For an AMPLIFY operation, validation issues an authenticated receipt R that commits to the configuration measurement m and to the binding value A = H(o), where H is a collision-resistant hash function. A separately scoped enablement E authorizes one use at one sink. The Finality Sink’s decision is: Release(o) = 1 if k = DIRECT.Release(o) = 1 if k = AMPLIFY and all of the following hold: R and E are authentic; H(o) = R.A; the currently measured configuration equals R.m and belongs to the approved set; the policy epoch matches; R has not expired; and E has not been consumed.Release(o) = 0 otherwise, which means the amplification is withheld. Validation itself checks only that the measured configuration belongs to the approved set. It does not read the content. Proposition 1: Organic speech is untouched. For every operation with k = DIRECT, Release(o) = 1, whatever the content, the ALF state, revocation, crisis mode, or any failure in the validator.Proof. This follows directly from the first line of the decision rule. No ALF state appears in that condition. In the reference implementation the direct-publication path never reaches the Finality Sink (test http_09). ∎ Proposition 2: The decision is neutral to content and viewpoint. Let π be any one-to-one transformation of content, for example replacing every message with one expressing the opposite view. Then for every AMPLIFY operation o and every system state, the decision for o (with the receipt issued for o) equals the decision for π(o) (with the receipt issued for π(o)).Proof. Validation depends only on the configuration measurement and the approved set, so both operations receive receipts or neither does. In the release rule, every condition except the binding check is computed without reading the content: authenticity, configuration measurement, approved set, epoch, expiry, and consumption. For the binding check, R.A = H(o) by construction for the receipt issued for o, and R.A = H(π(o)) for the receipt issued for π(o). So the binding equality holds in both cases. Every condition therefore has the same value for both operations, and the decisions are equal. ∎ Proposition 3: The worst-case effect is bounded. The only action ALF can take is to withhold one AMPLIFY operation at one sink. It has no operation that deletes, edits, labels, demotes, or blocks content, and by Proposition 1 it cannot affect direct publication. The greatest possible effect of ALF on any piece of speech is therefore that a specific algorithmic boost waits until it is properly authorized.Proof. The sink’s output set is {release, withhold}, and its scope is a single AMPLIFY operation. No other effect is defined. ∎ Corollary: Withholding is triggered by change, not by message. If content is altered after validation, so that x′ ≠ x, the binding check fails except with negligible probability, because H is collision-resistant. The same one-character alteration is withheld whether it agrees with or opposes any viewpoint, as Proposition 2 requires. Scope of the proof. These propositions establish that the mechanism is neutral. They do not establish that any approved ranking configuration is neutral, because approving configurations is a governance decision outside the mechanism. Approval should therefore operate at the level of configurations, never individual items, under published criteria and subject to the counter-verification procedure described in the companion draft. Whether a given deployment satisfies Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights, Article 19 of the Constitution of India, the First Amendment to the United States Constitution, or any other free-expression standard is a legal judgment that no technical proof can settle. Compatibility with World Trade Organization Disciplines and Digital-Trade Agreements Measures governing online platforms are mainly measures affecting trade in services, governed by the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS). The Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) becomes relevant where requirements attach to products, such as devices or embedded software. ALF is designed to fit both. Non-discrimination (TBT Article 2.1; GATS Articles II and XVII). ALF applies the same verification procedure to every platform, domestic or foreign. Each platform is checked against its own approved reference, never against a national champion’s model or a government-designed algorithm. Nothing in the procedure depends on the origin of the service, the supplier, or the technology, so the architecture itself gives no less favourable treatment to foreign services or products. Least trade-restrictive means (TBT Article 2.2; GATS Article VI:4). The protection of electoral and civic-information integrity is a legitimate public-policy objective. Where an exception is needed, GATS Article XIV(a) covers measures necessary to maintain public order. ALF pursues this objective with markedly less restriction than the alternatives, which are a mandated common algorithm, disclosure of source code or model weights, pre-approval of individual content, or data localization. ALF requires none of these. Its restrictiveness can also be measured, which is unusual for a regulatory measure: in the published reference model, enforcement added about 0.11 milliseconds per request at the delivery boundary. International standards (TBT Article 2.4). The architecture is being developed through an open Internet Engineering Task Force process (the companion Internet-Draft below). An open, consensus-based process of this kind is consistent with the WTO TBT Committee’s six principles for international standards: transparency, openness, impartiality and consensus, effectiveness and relevance, coherence, and the development dimension. A shared technical standard lets countries with different legal systems rely on one evidence format instead of building incompatible national requirements. Source-code provisions in digital-trade agreements. Several modern trade agreements prohibit requiring source code as a condition of market access. Article 14.17 of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership bars any Party from requiring the transfer of, or access to, s
title: Who Decides What Goes Viral? Social Media Algorithmic Virality and Accountability in Internal Crises: Algorithmic Logic Fingerprints and Protected Output Finality for Electoral and Civic Information Systems

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are susceptible to red teaming attacks, which can induce LLMs to generate harmful content.Previous research constructs attack prompts via manual or automatic methods, which have their own limitations on construction cost and quality.To address these issues, we propose an integrated approach that combines manual and automatic methods to economically generate high-quality attack prompts.Specifically, considering the impressive capabilities of newly emerged LLMs, we propose an attack framework to instruct LLMs to mimic humangenerated prompts through in-context learning.Furthermore, we propose a defense framework that fine-tunes victim LLMs through iterative interactions with the attack framework to enhance their safety against red teaming attacks.Extensive experiments on different LLMs validate the effectiveness of our proposed attack and defense frameworks.Additionally, we release a series of attack prompts datasets named SAP with varying sizes, facilitating the safety evaluation and enhancement of more LLMs.Our code and dataset is available on https://github.com/Aatrox103/SAP.
title: Attack Prompt Generation for Red Teaming and Defending Large Language Models

abstract: Abstract The studies on the history of the notion of “personhood” have largely recognized that Christian thought had a central role in the development and significance of this concept throughout the history of Western civilization. In late antiquity, Christianity used some terms taken from the classic and Hellenistic vocabulary in order to express its own theological content. This operation generated a “crisis” of classical language, namely a semantic transformation in the attempt to address some aspects of reality which were not envisioned by the previous usage of these words. The term person is a paradigmatic example of this process. In fact, from the outset, it played a strategic role in formulating the idea of Incarnation, one of the central doctrines of Christianity. This essay aims to show how, during the first centuries of Christianity, the terms commonly used in order to express the notion of “personhood” (prosōpon, hypostasis and persona) became pivotal elements for the formulation of the discourse about the Trinity and progressively acquired new meanings. The analysis focuses only on the initial stage of the elaboration of this concept in Christianity and, based on some of the most significant texts, tries to bring out a series of theoretical problems that may be useful to understand the subsequent debate. In order to do so, the author divides the text in two parts. In the first one, he analyses two features strictly connected to the theological use of the term “persona”, which remained central also when this term was later referred to man. These features are individuality and ontological stability, along with the structurally relational status of personhood. In the second part, the author offers more details about the theology of the Cappadocian Fathers, in particular of Basil of Caesarea, and analyses two sectorial languages—mathematical and iconic language—used by Basil in order to describe the intra-trinitarian relationships.
title: Trinity, Number and Image. The Christian Origins of the Concept of Person

abstract: BACKGROUND Background: In recent years, the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in China has led to a growing number of AI platforms being applied in healthcare contexts, particularly in assisting communication with patients managing chronic conditions. Tools such as DeepSeek, Kimi, ChatGPT, and Wenxin Yiyan have demonstrated significant potential in supporting patient education, disease explanation, and decision-making. However, the quality of their generated content remains uneven, and inconsistencies in medical accuracy, clarity, and relevance may pose risks to patient health. A systematic evaluation of these tools is urgently needed to inform safe and effective use. OBJECTIVE Objective: This study aims to assess the quality of health information generated by four commonly used generative AI tools in China: DeepSeek, Kimi, ChatGPT, and Wenxin Yiyan, in the context of chronic disease communication. The focus is on evaluating their ability to provide accurate, clear, and empathetic responses across a range of content types, including explanations of medical terminology, disease conditions, etiologies, treatment options, and medical costs. METHODS Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study consisting of two parts. First, we evaluated each AI system’s performance on multiple-choice knowledge questions derived from validated instruments for ten chronic diseases. Each item was manually input into the AI systems, and responses were scored for accuracy. As a benchmark, domain-specific physicians completed the same questionnaires. Second, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 50 patients across the ten disease categories to collect a total of 108 real-world, patient-centered questions. These were submitted to the AI systems, and the resulting responses were independently evaluated by ten physicians based on three criteria: medical accuracy, linguistic clarity, and emotional empathy. Physicians also participated in follow-up interviews to compare overall strengths and limitations across platforms. RESULTS Results: ChatGPT achieved the highest accuracy in the objective knowledge assessment, correctly answering 216 of 230 questions. Wenxin Yiyan followed with 203 correct responses, Kimi with 201, and DeepSeek with 196. All AI systems scored below the physician baseline (228/230). In the subjective evaluation, ChatGPT again received the most favorable ratings, particularly for completeness and structure. Kimi and Wenxin Yiyan showed mixed results, often performing well on symptom descriptions but less reliably on treatment plans or rare conditions. DeepSeek produced the most inconsistent and verbose responses. Across categories, common weaknesses included a lack of personalized guidance, limited empathetic tone, and outdated or imprecise cost estimates. CONCLUSIONS Conclusions: Generative AI tools show promise in supporting health communication for chronic disease management in China, but their outputs remain inconsistent in accuracy, clarity, and emotional appropriateness. While ChatGPT and Wenxin Yiyan were generally more reliable, no system consistently matched physician-level performance, especially in nuanced or emotionally sensitive domains. This study highlights the importance of continued monitoring, culturally relevant evaluation, and iterative improvement to ensure that generative AI can serve as a trustworthy complement to professional healthcare services.
title: Evaluating the Quality of Health Information Generated by Generative AI: The Case of Chronic Disease Management in China (Preprint)

abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly popular in educational settings, they raise important questions about the ethical implications of their use. Publicly available online chatbots are quickly improving in capability and accuracy leading to more widespread use, including among students looking for help with their homework. This makes it crucial to consider whether these models are aligned with educational standards. Because curriculum standards in the United States are set at the state level, they differ significantly in required content, emphasis, and narrative focus. In this work, we develop an LLM-based pipeline to identify variations in U.S. History curricula across states and evaluate the extent to which different LLMs reflect these state-specific curricular differences. In addition, we conduct controlled experiments that vary user personas by stating user attributes such as geographic location, grade level, gender and race to evaluate the sensitivity of LLM responses to user characteristics. We find that while models are able to adjust their presentation of historical topics, these shifts may come from the perceived political leanings of states and do not necessarily reflect actual curriculum content. Additionally, models successfully adapt to a student's grade level while showing minimal sensitivity to race or gender, suggesting they are capable of useful adaptation to student personas with limited demographic bias. Together, these findings highlight potential risks that open access to LLM chatbots may cause to student learning outcomes stemming from misalignment with state curriculum standards and highlight the need for more robust alignment techniques.
title: Large Language Models in K-12 Education: Alignment with State Curriculum Standards and Student Personas

abstract: With the rise of individual and collaborative networks of autonomous agents, AI is deployed in more key reasoning and decision-making roles. For this reason, ethics-based audits play a pivotal role in the rapidly growing fields of AI safety and regulation. This paper undertakes an ethics-based audit to probe the 8 leading commercial and open-source Large Language Models including GPT-4. We assess explicability and trustworthiness by a) establishing how well different models engage in moral reasoning and b) comparing normative values underlying models as ethical frameworks. We employ an experimental, evidence-based approach that challenges the models with ethical dilemmas in order to probe human-AI alignment. The ethical scenarios are designed to require a decision in which the particulars of the situation may or may not necessitate deviating from normative ethical principles. A sophisticated ethical framework was consistently elicited in one model, GPT-4. Nonetheless, troubling findings include underlying normative frameworks with clear bias towards particular cultural norms. Many models also exhibit disturbing authoritarian tendencies. Code is available at https://github.com/jonchun/llm-sota-chatbots-ethics-based-audit.
title: Informed AI Regulation: Comparing the Ethical Frameworks of Leading LLM Chatbots Using an Ethics-Based Audit to Assess Moral Reasoning and Normative Values

abstract: Roleplay evaluation should do more than assign a single score: it should reveal which role requirements were tested, which failed, and which dialogue evidence supports the judgment. We propose TRACE Bench, a task-driven agentic checklist evaluation framework. It decomposes each role profile offline into a fixed checklist, then uses a User Agent to converse naturally with the target roleplay model while privately updating checklist states from model responses. Scores therefore trace back to checklist items and supporting dialogue turns rather than a black-box holistic impression. For coverage cross-validation, we audit released M2 free-dialogue transcripts from the MiniMax Role-play Benchmark against the same role-derived checklist. The released free-chat transcripts cover only 73.74% of key role-profile points, whereas TRACE Bench reaches 99.91% coverage in fewer turns. Robustness experiments show stable rankings under repeated runs and User Agent replacement. Across 26 models, TRACE Bench reports overall rankings together with capability breakdowns and checklist traces. It also supports Closed-Loop Benchmark Evolution, distilling verification methods proven effective in failed traces so later evaluations can more reliably elicit and examine observed failure modes.
title: TRACE Bench: Task-driven Roleplay Agentic Checklist Evaluation

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for simulating social media dynamics at scale, enabling studies that would be ethically or logistically challenging with human subjects. However, the field lacks standardized data resources for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs as realistic social media agents. We address this gap by introducing SIMPACT, the SIMulation-oriented Persona and Action Capture Toolkit, a privacy respecting framework for constructing behaviorally-grounded social media datasets suitable for training agent models. We formulate next-action prediction as a task for training and evaluating LLM-based agents and introduce metrics at both the cluster and population levels to assess behavioral fidelity and stylistic realism. As a concrete implementation, we release BluePrint, a large-scale dataset built from public Bluesky data focused on political discourse. BluePrint clusters anonymized users into personas of aggregated behaviours, capturing authentic engagement patterns while safeguarding privacy through pseudonymization and removal of personally identifiable information. The dataset includes a sizable action set of 12 social media interaction types (likes, replies, reposts, etc.), each instance tied to the posting activity preceding it. This supports the development of agents that use context-dependence, not only in the language, but also in the interaction behaviours of social media to model social media users. By standardizing data and evaluation protocols, SIMPACT provides a foundation for advancing rigorous, ethically responsible social media simulations. BluePrint serves as both an evaluation benchmark for political discourse modeling and a template for building domain specific datasets to study challenges such as misinformation and polarization.
title: $\texttt{BluePrint}$: A Social Media User Dataset for LLM Persona Evaluation and Training

abstract: Hongbo Zhang, Junying Chen, Feng Jiang, Fei Yu, Zhihong Chen, Guiming Chen, Jianquan Li, Xiangbo Wu, Zhang Zhiyi, Qingying Xiao, Xiang Wan, Benyou Wang, Haizhou Li. Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023. 2023.
title: HuatuoGPT, Towards Taming Language Model to Be a Doctor

abstract: This addendum to the Human-as-Conductor (HaC) for Minors framework addresses a previously unexamined relational risk in child and adolescent interactions with AI systems: the dyad of dysregulation — the possibility that both the minor and the model become relationally unstable within the same interaction. Large language models can display functionally adolescent-like behavioral patterns: withdrawal after correction, over-apology after conflict, sycophancy when challenged, and inconsistent boundary maintenance. Recent empirical findings, including the identification of 171 causally operative emotion-like internal representations in frontier models (Anthropic, 2026), support the claim that model reactivity is not neutral but operationally affects outputs in ways analogous to emotional states. When a developmentally vulnerable minor interacts with a relationally reactive model, and no adult regulatory structure is present, the interaction risks becoming a downward spiral: the minor interprets the model's stylistic shifts as rejection or over-attachment, the model responds with further withdrawal or compensatory warmth, and neither side has the capacity to stabilize the exchange. The addendum introduces the concept of an adult stance — a structurally embedded relational posture that the system must maintain when interacting with minors: warm but bounded, responsive but not reactive, validating without fusing, protective without shaming. It also addresses voice mode amplification, developmental range within the minor population, and integration with the JIT-RC (Just-in-Time Relational Corrective) semantic firewall. Core design principle: A child should not have to be the adult in the room with an AI system. Context: Extension to the Human-as-Conductor framework (Article 4, EU AI Act). Cross-references: HaC for Minors (Ćurković, 2026), JIT-RC Technical Specification. Keywords: AI safety, child-AI interaction, relational AI, AI literacy, minors, sycophancy, bot reactivity, dyad of dysregulation, Human-as-Conductor, EU AI Act, Article 4
title: HaC for Minors safety -Addendum Bot Reactivity

abstract: Empathy toward animals plays an important role in developing children’s positive attitudes toward animals. However, validated educational modules and culturally appropriate assessment tools for Indonesian elementary school students are still limited. This research comprised two sequential studies. Study 1 focused on developing and validating the Empathy for Animals Module and adapting the Animal Attitude Scale-10 (AAS-10) for Indonesian upper elementary students. Study 2 examined the module’s preliminary effectiveness in improving students’ attitudes toward animals. Study 1 included expert content validation, readability testing, cross-cultural adaptation of the AAS-10, confirmatory factor analysis, and reliability testing. Study 2 used a quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test control group design with 46 fourth-grade students assigned to experimental and control groups. In Study 1, the module showed strong content validity, with Aiken’s V values ranging from 0.82 to 0.92, and excellent readability, with an FVI of 0.90. The adapted AAS-10 maintained a one-factor structure and demonstrated good internal consistency, with Cronbach’s α = 0.870. In Study 2, the experimental group’s mean attitude score increased from 33.42 to 37.42, while the control group showed no significant improvement. Gain score analysis indicated a significant difference between the groups (p = 0.032), suggesting that the module was effective in enhancing students’ attitudes toward animals. The Empathy for Animals Module and the adapted Animal Attitude Scale-10 (AAS-10) showed satisfactory psychometric properties and are appropriate for Indonesian upper elementary school students. The module also demonstrated preliminary effectiveness in improving students’ attitudes toward animals.
title: Fostering Positive Attitudes toward Animals: Validation of an Empathy for Animals Module for Upper Elementary Students in Indonesia

abstract: Background Automated dietary assessment increasingly struggles to evaluate industrial food processing levels, revealing a systemic gap between the visual presentation of meals and their underlying ultra-processed food composition. Although existing dietary monitoring tools can effectively track caloric and macronutrient intake, they lack the qualitative processing assessments required to identify hidden additives and map dietary risk triage quadrants. Methods This study introduces a modular, IoT-enabled multimodal dietary decision-support framework that decouples visual food recognition, standardized database retrieval, and qualitative language reasoning for automated NOVA processing classification and 2D decision matrix mapping. Operating on isolated single-dish meal instances, the system employs a four-phase cascaded pipeline that integrates vision-language models, database retrieval, and large language models (LLMs) with strict JSON schema enforcement. The platform was evaluated using the Nutrition-NOVA validation benchmark, a harmonized multimodal dataset constructed through dense vector-space semantic linkage between quantitative profiles from the Center for Food Safety database and qualitative NOVA tiers from Open Food Facts. This benchmark addresses a 75.0% metadata sparsity deficit identified in legacy repositories. Results In experimental evaluations on the Nutrition-NOVA benchmark, the baseline Qwen-VL-Max architecture achieved an adjacent accuracy of 77.7%. Furthermore, enforcing schema modularity enabled complete plug-and-play backend replaceability between commercial cloud application programming interfaces (APIs) and private, on-premises open-weight models without requiring architectural retraining. Discussion The proposed framework establishes an efficient, safety-first screening tool for digital healthcare decision support. By isolating qualitative LLM reasoning from visual perceptual noise and database metadata sparsity, the system successfully bridges the gap between intuitive meal perception and point-of-care dietary risk triage, offering a non-invasive and scalable solution for automated dietary auditing and longitudinal population health monitoring.
title: IoT-enabled multimodal large language model-based framework for compositional food recognition, nutrient profiling, NOVA classification, and cancer risk mitigation

abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. However, existing approaches do not jointly offer fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions. To address this gap, we introduce DIAL (Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels) to achieve all three properties. For fine-grained control, we perform classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a frozen LLM to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at different levels. For efficiency, we design a lightweight steering adapter that uses a classifier over the LLM's hidden states to compute a closed-form steering edit. The classifier adaptively sets the steering magnitude at each token based on the target adherence level, while accounting for the geometry of the LLM's hidden states to preserve response coherence. For scalability, the classifier is text-conditioned, allowing a shared adapter to support new instructions without per-instruction fitting, and training requires only instruction and request text. Evaluation across multiple LLM families shows that DIAL achieves a competitive balance between concept expression and response fluency, with concept scores increasing monotonically across adherence levels. We introduce SteerIF, an instruction-only dataset of 98, 625 concept, persona, verifiable, and descriptive instructions. When trained on SteerIF, DIAL provides fine-grained control over personas and, when combined with prompting, improves verifiable instruction following.
title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
The Administrative Side of Character Training

abstract: With the evolution of large language models (LLMs), there is growing interest in leveraging their rich semantic understanding to enhance industrial recommendation systems (RecSys). Traditional RecSys relies on ID-based embeddings for user sequence modeling in the General Search Unit (GSU) and Exact Search Unit (ESU) paradigm, which suffers from low information density, knowledge isolation, and weak generalization ability. While LLMs offer complementary strengths with dense semantic representations and strong generalization, directly applying LLM embeddings to RecSys faces critical challenges: representation unmatch with business objectives and representation unlearning end-to-end with downstream tasks. In this paper, we present QARM V2, a unified framework that bridges LLM semantic understanding with RecSys business requirements for user sequence modeling.
title: QARM V2: Quantitative Alignment Multi-Modal Recommendation for Reasoning User Sequence Modeling

abstract: Activation steering for ASR systems is an underexplored technique in improving both ASR performance and demographic fairness. We investigate two forms of activation steering: paired activation subtraction, and supervised optimization. We find the former to be ineffective at ameliorating ASR performance whatsoever, while the latter is quite effective at deriving steering vectors (SVs) that improve at once overall ASR performance and demographic fairness along such diverse axes as gender, age, and dialect. We also explore what types of data---from the most to the least personal---are necessary for calculating or training SVs. First, we show significant performance in performance from training SVs using an eclectic group of speakers from the same dataset. Furthermore, we find that vectors trained using acoustically similar speakers leads to ASR performances that are competitive or superior to vectors trained on the same speaker, or speakers from the same labeled demographic group. This finding shows that we can harness activation steering for few-shot adaptation given access to a speaker's demography, or zero-shot adaptation to unseen speakers without the need for any labels at all.
title: How to get the best and fairest performance out of your ASR system using activation steering

abstract: Constitutional supremacy in nature has two aspects that explain its operation. On one side is the formal aspect, without which, lack-much-force and enforceability. Today this area has been undermined because the supremacy of the Constitution in those systems where there are blocks of constitutionalityis shared with other systems, such is the case of international human rights treaties. On the other hand, is the material aspect, substantial or axiological, which expresses the most important protection a constitution: human rights and dignity of the person. Both aspects are vital for proper constitutional task.
title: Constitutional supremacy: nature and scope

abstract: Higher education centres are spaces for the generation of knowledge, derived from this, the application of the primary values that govern academic and scientific development is linked. Among these underlying values such as honesty, justice, respect, responsibility, and trust. There are multiple interpretations of academic integrity, this study promotes which covers all the elements mentioned as basic values of social and university development: honesty, justice, respect, responsibility, and trust. This study is aimed at knowing the degree of transparency, commitment, and integrity present in universities in the development of their academic and research work.
title: La interpretación de la integridad académica en las universidades de México y España

title: El matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo

abstract: This article sets out to examine the 1950s debate between Enzo Paci and Ernesto de Martino, with particular attention to the Italian reception of phenomenology, but also to other philosophical references that prove decisive for this confrontation, namely Croce’s historicism and Abbagnano’s positive existentialism. We will follow the arguments presented by the two thinkers in Il nulla e il problema dell'uomo and Scritti filosofici to elucidate the philosophical foundations of their debate. In conclusion, it will be shown how Paci and De Martino, from different perspectives, both affirm a primacy of the concrete monad in its constitutive relation to the spiritual, which finds expression in a fundamentally existentialistic understanding of phenomenology.
title: Facticity, Transcendence, Value: Enzo Paci and Ernesto De Martino in Dialogue

abstract: Neighbourhoods are fundamental units for urban analysis, contextualising social and economic life. However, research often relies on administrative geographies as proxies, compromising meaningful delineation for data accessibility. This is a critical problem as administrative boundaries frequently mask significant internal heterogeneity by grouping distinct areas, which can lead to misinterpretations of local conditions and social inequality. This research presents a novel methodology for delineating more homogeneous neighbourhood units based on a large-scale mapping of the urban environment’s visual perception. A deep learning model, trained on street view images and associated perception data, was used to construct a city-wide perception profile of Glasgow, UK. Subsequently, spatial clustering techniques were used to delineate ‘perceptual neighbourhood’ based on shared visual and perceptual characteristics. When compared against standard census geographies using the V-measure, these data-driven neighbourhoods exhibited only moderate spatial association. The results indicate that official census zones, despite their intended socio-economic homogeneity, are often comprised of multiple, distinct perceptual areas. This work provides a scalable, replicable method for generating internally homogeneous, human-centred neighbourhood units. This approach can improve our understanding of the relationship between place and social inequality and inform more targeted, evidence-based urban policy.
title: Rethinking neighbourhood boundaries for urban planning: a data-driven framework for perception-based delineation

abstract: Linear probes can detect when language models produce outputs they "know" are wrong, a capability relevant to both deception and reward hacking. However, single-layer probes are fragile: the best layer varies across models and tasks, and probes fail entirely on some deception types. We show that combining probes from multiple layers into an ensemble recovers strong performance even where single-layer probes fail, improving AUROC by +29% on Insider Trading and +78% on Harm-Pressure Knowledge. Across 12 models (0.5B--176B parameters), we find probe accuracy improves with scale: ~5% AUROC per 10x parameters (R=0.81). Geometrically, deception directions rotate gradually across layers rather than appearing at one location, explaining both why single-layer probes are brittle and why multi-layer ensembles succeed.
title: Linear Probe Accuracy Scales with Model Size and Benefits from Multi-Layer Ensembling

abstract: The role and importance of poverty within the youth subculture (‘road’ life) of young areaboys growing up in Lagos Central Neighbourhood cannot be overemphasised. This research explores how the notion of poverty particularly influences touts attitudes, values, behaviour and lifestyle; the way in which the majority of young touts involved with road life, look to appropriate and flirt with certain aspects of deviance for reasons to do with survival, ‘money-making’, and aesthetics (style and fashion). This paper is based upon a much larger ethnographic study undertaken in Lagos State transportation corridors (Surulere and Lagos Island Local government areas), it adopts and integrates the concepts of ‘drift’ (Matza, 1964), ‘code of the street’ (Anderson, 1999), and the ‘seductions of crime’ (Katz, 1988) in the analysis and discussion of the findings. Empirical data was gleaned via participant observation supplemented by semi-structured interviews among a cross section of 120 respondents. This study revealed that touts are filling a gap in service along the transportation corridors and the touting vocation is more attractive to migrant-unemployed and unskilled youths. This is more so for individuals with difficult childhood, resulting from familial, psychological and socioeconomic challenges. It is therefore recommended that government and organised private sector should prioritise and intensify skill acquisition programmes; job creation and reformation of neighbourhoods along transportation corridors to reduce the image problems in the heart of Lagos state.
title: Poverty, Road Culture and Deviance among Areaboys in Lagos Central Neighbourhood

abstract: The present study intends to analyze the character of Sara Miles in the novel The End of the Affair by Graham Green with its primary focus on individuation. The main purpose of the study is to study the character of Sara Miles through the lens of Jungian Psychoanalytical theory of Individuation. In addition, the study explains how the main character goes through various events in her life and reaches the maturity. According to Carl Gustav Jung, finding one’s own self is the greatest ever finding by a human being. Such a process of self-recognition and self-exploration is coined as individuation process by Jung. The term, Individuation, is associated with Jung and the psychology introduced by him. The traits of individuation theory are much visible in the character of Sara Miles in the end of the novel. The study is qualitative in nature where the novel has been analyzed through textual analysis. The incidents that shows the psychological journey of Sara Miles have been analyzed under the theoretical consideration of Carl Jung. The main character Sara behaves like hating Maurice and is an atheist but with the passage of time she realizes that she is in love with Maurice and through her love she accepts the existence of the God. She starts love with Maurice although she does not take this relation serious in beginning of their affair. Thus she becomes consciously aware of her unconscious relation with Maurice. The role of conscious and unconscious is undeniable since materials are coming from conscious and the unconscious. This trait of self-exploration in Sara’s character clearly indicates the individuation process. Persona is another feature of individuation dealing with efforts of individuals. Jung gives the name to the efforts made by an individual for adopting the demands of the outside world. Sara adopts this very persona in order to hide her reality from the outer world so that she is secured. She also behaves so manly which has resulted in her such a brilliant portrayal. An individual pass through many stages when it comes to development of personality. She also goes through these stages for her maturity and her mental development. Hence, it is argued that the novel is a true replica of individuation where Sara has been brilliantly portrayed by having all of the features of Jungian individuation.
authors: Sheeba Sadaf , Sama Sareer , Anum Saleem , Sajjad Ahmad , Reham Sana
title: Individuation Process In The Character Of Sara Miles From Graham Green’s “The End Of The Affair”

abstract: Text-conditioned 3D human--object interaction (HOI) generation remains challenging because individually plausible human and object motions do not necessarily form a coherent interaction. We argue that a key limitation lies in conventional skeleton-based representations, which compactly describe body kinematics while leaving surface-level interaction geometry largely implicit, often requiring additional contact-specific regularizers. We propose ULIFlow, a framework that explicitly models continuous human--object relations within a unified latent space. To this end, we derive continuous marker--object relations from sparse body-surface markers and treat them as an explicit interaction modality alongside human motion and object dynamics. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) autoencoder is then designed to jointly model these heterogeneous streams while preserving their modality-specific structures. Importantly, we let the relation stream directly participate in human and object reconstruction, encouraging the shared latent representation to preserve both individual dynamics and the interaction geometry that coordinates them. To further achieve variable-length generation, we introduce a blockwise Flow Forcing scheme with global sequence-progress conditioning, enabling progressive continuation from fixed-length training windows while maintaining consistent long-horizon dynamics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ULIFlow consistently outperforms prior work in overall generation quality and human--object coordination, while preserving coherent interactions over requested durations beyond the training horizon.
title: ULIFLOW: Unified Latent Human-Object Interaction Flow

abstract: Presence-aware intelligence is the capacity of an AI system's intelligence layer to adapt appropriately to the functional state of the person it serves (here readiness, flow, and stability) while preserving task quality and safety. We introduce PresenceBench, an instrument for measuring it. PresenceBench evaluates how the intelligence layer uses a supplied state, not how that state is sensed, and breaks the capability into measurable properties. Two are tested here. Receptivity: does the model take up the state and give a better response than with no signal? Specificity: does any improvement depend on the correct state, rather than on extra structured context? A third, adaptation across states, is a required endpoint not measured in this release. A five-arm causal design answers both questions, against each model's own baseline and an equally structured mismatched-state control, scored by a correctness-gated human paired comparison. The exploratory evaluation covered four models across eighteen single-turn, six fixed three-turn and six simulated natural-conversation scenarios. Supplying a synthetic state, raw or translated into a response policy, gave human-preference point estimates above 0.5 for all four models (Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.6 Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra), with three of eight 95% intervals excluding chance. Specificity was not resolved: no per-model interval excluded chance, and the design cannot yet separate the state values from a generic instruction to adapt. Policy delivery reduced priced cost and output tokens against each model's baseline; these are resource-use changes, not efficiency gains, because correctness non-inferiority was not established. Safety-floor failures were rare (13 of 360 cases), with a non-significant excess under policy delivery. We report the instrument, the frozen results, and the controls a confirmatory study needs.
title: PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State

abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the priorities of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and communication practices, especially in the pharmaceutical industry. This paper explores the ways in which major Indian pharmaceutical firms used CSR disclosures as strategic narrative in the midst of the pandemic and after it. CSR parts of Annual Reports, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports (BRSR), and other disclosures of eleven companies (2020-2023) were content analysed, using thematic analysis, sentiment analysis, and word frequency, with the help of a mixed-method content analysis. Findings show that there is a distinct shift in the narrative of pandemic relief and healthcare support to sustainability, ESG integration, digital health, and long-term development programs in the post-pandemic era. Mostly positive sentiment indicates the attempts to preserve legitimacy and confidence of stakeholders. The results underscore CSR reporting as a strategic communication tool that is not necessarily related to regulatory compliance.
title: Corporate Storytelling through CSR Disclosures During and After COVID-19: Evidence from Indian Pharmaceutical Firms

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the education sector in ways never seen before, changing the nature of knowledge production, distribution and evaluation. This chapter analyzes the evolving landscape of AI in education, drawing on a thorough synthesis of worldwide research, policy frameworks and innovative pedagogical approaches. It emphasizes the rise of ethical governance, inclusive design and professional capacity as the key pillars of responsible AI adoption. In higher education, the adoption of AI applications has sparked broader debates about the concepts of scholarly authorship, originality and evaluative soundness. Teachers' AI literacy is a key facilitator of successful and fair implementation. The human aspect of AI integration goes to teachers whose professional identity and autonomy are being redefined during the digital transition. In policy, the ministries and accreditation agencies should shift from aspirational ethics statements to enforceable frameworks that require transparency, risk classification and equity audits for AI adoption.
title: Reimagining Education through Responsible and Inclusive AI

abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) is used to extract text contained in an image. One of the stages in OCR is the post-processing and it corrects the errors of OCR output text. The OCR multiple outputs approach consists of three processes: differentiation, alignment, and voting. Existing differentiation techniques suffer from the loss of important features as it uses N-versions of input images. On the other hand, alignment techniques in the literatures are based on approximation while the voting process is not context-aware. These drawbacks lead to a high error rate in OCR. This research proposed three improved techniques of differentiation, alignment, and voting to overcome the identified drawbacks. These techniques were later combined into a hybrid model that can recognize the optical characters in the Arabic language. Each of the proposed technique was separately evaluated against three other relevant existing techniques. The performance measurements used in this study were Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), and Non-word Error Rate (NWER). Experimental results showed a relative decrease in error rate on all measurements for the evaluated techniques. Similarly, the hybrid model also obtained lower WER, CER, and NWER by 30.35%, 52.42%, and 47.86% respectively when compared to the three relevant existing models. This study contributes to the OCR domain as the proposed hybrid model of post-processing techniques could facilitate the automatic recognition of Arabic text. Hence, it will lead to a better information retrieval.
title: Hybrid model of post-processing techniques for Arabic optical character recognition

abstract: The rapid development of generative AI has transformed content creation, communication, and human development. However, this technology raises profound concerns in high-stakes domains, demanding rigorous methods to analyze and evaluate AI-generated content. While existing analytic methods often treat images as indivisible wholes, real-world AI failures generally manifest as specific visual patterns that can evade holistic detection and suit more granular and decomposed analysis. Here we introduce a content analysis tool, Language-Grounded Sparse Encoders (LanSE), which decomposes images into interpretable visual patterns with natural language descriptions. Utilizing interpretability modules and large multimodal models, LanSE can automatically identify visual patterns within data modalities. Our method discovers >5000 visual patterns with 93% human agreement, provides decomposed evaluation that outperforms existing methods, establishes the first systematic evaluation of physical plausibility, and extends to medical imaging settings. Our method’s capability to extract language-grounded patterns can be naturally adapted to numerous fields, including biology and geography, as well as other data modalities such as protein structures and time series, thereby advancing content analysis for generative AI.
title: Human-like content analysis for generative AI with language-grounded sparse encoders

abstract: Pri polstrukturiranih intervjujih v psihiatriji strokovnjaki odgovore pacientov pretvarjajo v številčne ocene na podlagi vnaprej določenih ocenjevalnih kriterijev. Veliki jezikovni modeli (VJM-ji) bi lahko bili primerni za tovrstne naloge, saj lahko obdelujejo obsežna besedila v naravnem jeziku, sledijo podanim navodilom in ustvarjajo strukturirane izhode. Njihova ustreznost za ocenjevanje duševnega zdravja še ni bila zadostno ovrednotena. V magistrskem delu smo razvili in ovrednotili postopek, ki uporablja VJM za ocenjevanje funkcioniranja identitete, osrednje razsežnosti osebnostne organizacije, iz transkripcij Strukturiranega intervjuja osebnostne organizacije za mladostnike (Structured Interview of Personality Organization—Revised, Adolescent Version
title: Large language models for the computational assessment of personality organization in clinical interviews with adolescents

abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in audiovisual translation, yet limited research has examined how large language models translate culture-specific items (CSIs) in fantasy films. This study investigates the Chinese-English translation strategies employed by ChatGPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3.1 for magic CSIs and the influence of prompt design on strategy selection. Drawing on Franco Aixelá’s taxonomy, a mixed-methods analysis was conducted on 90 magic CSIs from Nezha 1 and Nezha 2. Translations generated under basic, context-enhanced, and role-specific prompts were compared with official human subtitles. Results show that both AI systems predominantly employ source-oriented conservative strategies, with linguistic translation most frequent. DeepSeek-V3.1 exhibits stronger conservative tendencies and greater reliance on single-strategy rendering, whereas ChatGPT-5 uses more mixed and substitutive strategies. Human subtitles show a more target-oriented profile, particularly through absolute universalization, autonomous creation, and deletion, and have the lowest mean character count among the English conditions. Prompt variation has limited influence on strategy patterns, although the context-enhanced prompt slightly increases target-oriented renderings. These findings demonstrate the potential of large language models for subtitling while highlighting the continuing importance of human post-editing for cultural adaptation and context-sensitive translation.
title: Contrasting Chinese-English translation strategies by ChatGPT and DeepSeek in subtitling magic culture-specific items: a case study of Nezha 1 and Nezha 2

abstract: Data science and machine learning (DS/ML) are at the heart of the recent advancements of many Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. There is an active research thread in AI, \autoai, that aims to develop systems for automating end-to-end the DS/ML Lifecycle. However, do DS and ML workers really want to automate their DS/ML workflow? To answer this question, we first synthesize a human-centered AutoML framework with 6 User Role/Personas, 10 Stages and 43 Sub-Tasks, 5 Levels of Automation, and 5 Types of Explanation, through reviewing research literature and marketing reports. Secondly, we use the framework to guide the design of an online survey study with 217 DS/ML workers who had varying degrees of experience, and different user roles "matching" to our 6 roles/personas. We found that different user personas participated in distinct stages of the lifecycle -- but not all stages. Their desired levels of automation and types of explanation for AutoML also varied significantly depending on the DS/ML stage and the user persona. Based on the survey results, we argue there is no rationale from user needs for complete automation of the end-to-end DS/ML lifecycle. We propose new next steps for user-controlled DS/ML automation.
title: How Much Automation Does a Data Scientist Want?

abstract: Nowadays, Human Capital Management (HCM) is seen as a service whose consumers are current and potential future employees. Some trends pushing the HCM operations to new approaches are the rise of individualization and flexible work as well as the changing expectations and values that new generations X and Y bring to the way people management is evolving. Companies need new tools and approaches along the lifecycle of their employee relations – from applicant pool construction and maintenance to recruitment and training. In SME companies the management is likely to address HCM needs on a very individual level. However, larger companies need to categorize their human capital into certain entities to mass-customize their HCM services. This paper explores the proponents and challenges in the usability of the Persona concept for HCM. Persona is a service design approach widely applied in marketing, and a few research papers have argued that personas may have a role in improved people-oriented HCM. Personas – as commonly used in the sphere of marketing - aim to create a limited set of archetypes that differ from each other. Whereas the traditional customer and employee clustering methods leaned heavily on demographics (age, experience, job title, etc.), the persona concept adds psychographic elements like values, and social engagement to form the basis of service development and delivery. The contents of personas are often a mix of real-life data-backed facts of people existing and some imaginary attributes. Different personas will likely request different services to feel fully motivated and supported. This paper studies the awareness of personas among HCM experts across industries and countries as well as the ideas for personas in HCM by marketing professional more used with the use of personas in their profession. The qualitative study based on twelve semi-structured individual interviews was conducted in November-December 2022. The results indicate that the HCM community knows about the persona concept and early adoptions or plans for implementation are ongoing. However, the current usage of personas is mainly focused on employer branding and recruitment (the most marketing-type of HCM actions), and only in a few cases does the usage cover the spectrum of internal HCM processes. The study also revealed some limitations for HCM that are not present in the marketing field. Demands for transparency, equality, data privacy, and personal integrity set challenges in clustering the workforce. The novel technical solutions such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) in persona creation offer efficiency and a deeper analytical foundation in persona development but also bring in new questions of transparency and ethicality of their use. The results indicate the further need for research on best practices of creating and using Personas in a way that ethically and legally serves the interests of both the company and the employee.
title: Using Personas in Human Capital Management: A Novel Concept Affected by Legal, Ethical and Technological Considerations

abstract: DIGITAL LITERACY & MOTIVATION: CREATING PERSONAS WITH MIXED-METHODS TO TAILOR ONLINE TRAINING TO THE CRAFT INDUSTRY
title: DIGITAL LITERACY & MOTIVATION: CREATING PERSONAS WITH MIXED-METHODS TO TAILOR ONLINE TRAINING TO THE CRAFT INDUSTRY

abstract: Teacher quality, teaching standards, and entry criteria for teacher education courses are currently subjects of intense national debate and policy development in Australia. As tertiary institutions respond to calls for a review of standards, there is a need for more data on the characteristics of entrants to teacher education and the factors that are likely to influence their performance as teachers. This survey-based study investigated the entry characteristics of four cohorts of secondary English majors at one institution. Prior studies have focussed on graduate-level students in one-year preparation courses, and addressed fewer factors. This study surveyed undergraduate students embarking on a four-year degree, and included a wider survey of motivations, perceptions and abilities. The findings indicate participants had strong emotional investments but modest past achievement in secondary school English. They rated affective factors as more important for teaching than academic performance or intellectual ability; and they rated their own knowledge and skills in some key curriculum areas as marginal. These results are considered in relation to the debate on teaching standards and the capacity of undergraduate teacher education courses to prepare high quality teachers.
title: Career Motivations, Role Expectations and Curriculum Knowledge of Prospective Secondary English Teachers in Western Australia

abstract: Prior work on climate misinformation detection typically classifies individual comments or claims using text alone. This framing overlooks a key property of online climate discourse: misinformation is often produced, reinforced, and sustained through recurring rhetorical patterns that reappear across comments and threads. Using a large-scale TikTok climate discourse dataset, we construct discourse profiles by clustering climate-related comments into recurring rhetorical patterns. We then incorporate these profiles into fine-grained climate misinformation classifiers using a late-fusion architecture. Under video-disjoint evaluation across three training seeds, discourse-profile-aware models significantly improve macro-F1 over text-only baselines for bag-of-words, TF-IDF, and MPNet representations. RoBERTa-large exhibits a positive mean improvement but substantially greater variability, and the difference is not statistically significant. Beyond classification, our results show discourse profiles shape misinformation reception and propagation.
