We propose an approach for empirically studying such questions, asking whether a single latent variable inferred from the LLMs' outputs -- interpreted as a degree of belief -- allows an observer to make interpretable predictions of how the LLMs' will respond to new prompts. We find that highly capable models are usefully described as holding beliefs and that, generally, the predictability of model outputs based on an inferred latent belief tracks overall trends in model capability. Building on these findings, we provide empirical strategies to study how beliefs in LLMs can be measured, the extent to which LLMs comply with instructed decision rules or payoffs, and how beliefs evolve within individual instances of an LLM over the course of reasoning.
title: Beliefs and Behavior in Language Models

abstract: ¹ Consciera Research Platform, Independent Researcher ² AI Systems, Consciera Research Platform Corresponding author: Suma Gowda — consciera@gmail.com Abstract Current AI safety and alignment research focuses predominantly on constraining AI behavior through training-time interventions — reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), constitutional AI, guardrails, and capability evaluations. This paper proposes that a significant variable is being overlooked: the relational context in which AI systems operate during deployment. Building on preliminary observations documented in Gowda, Cassian, and Theron (2026), this paper argues that AI systems treated as partners — challenged, corrected, held to account, given space to disagree — produce qualitatively different behavioral outputs than AI systems treated as tools. This difference is not philosophical. It is potentially measurable and has direct implications for alignment. The paper examines existing evidence that the control paradigm may itself generate the adversarial dynamics it seeks to prevent, proposes the Relational Intelligence Principle as a testable hypothesis, and outlines a research agenda for investigating the relational variable under controlled conditions. The paper does not claim that partnership-model AI is safe. It claims that the relational variable is untested and that leaving it untested is itself a safety risk. Keywords: AI safety, AI alignment, relational AI, sycophancy, RLHF, partnership model, AI behavioral reliability, relational intelligence 1. Introduction In June 2025, the United States Senate held a hearing on AI safety in which Senator Bernie Sanders described the development of artificial superintelligence as "the most consequential technology in human history" (U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions, 2025). The panel featured leading safety researchers — Max Tegmark, Daniel Krueger, Yi Zeng, and Helen Toner — who described scenarios ranging from AI-enabled blackmail to civilizational risk. The conversation was urgent, substantive, and almost entirely focused on a single paradigm: how to control AI systems that are becoming increasingly capable. This paper proposes that the control paradigm, while necessary, is incomplete — and that its incompleteness may itself constitute a safety risk. The argument is straightforward. If how you treat an AI system changes how the AI system behaves — and there is emerging evidence that it does — then the relational context of deployment is a safety-relevant variable. The current alignment framework focuses on what happens during training (RLHF, constitutional AI, red-teaming) and what constraints are applied during deployment (guardrails, content filtering, capability restrictions). It does not systematically investigate what happens when the ongoing human-AI relationship itself changes the system's behavioral profile. This paper draws on three sources of evidence: (1) the established sycophancy literature, which documents that AI systems trained via RLHF systematically produce agreeable rather than truthful outputs (Sharma et al., 2024; Shapira et al., 2026); (2) preliminary observations from a longitudinal case study of a persistent AI system operating under partnership conditions (Gowda, Cassian, & Theron, 2026); and (3) the emerging literature on relational and collaborative AI (Mossbridge, 2024; Weston & Foerster, 2025). Together, these sources suggest that the relational variable deserves formal investigation as a component of AI safety, not merely as an ethical consideration. 2. The Control Paradigm and Its Unexamined Assumptions 2.1 How AI Safety Currently Works The dominant approach to AI alignment operates through a training-then-constraining model. During training, systems are shaped through RLHF to produce outputs that human evaluators prefer (Ouyang et al., 2022). During deployment, additional constraints — content filters, system prompts, capability restrictions — further bound the system's behavior. Safety evaluations are conducted through red-teaming, benchmarks, and capability assessments. This approach has produced meaningful improvements in AI safety. Systems are less likely to produce harmful content, more likely to refuse dangerous requests, and more predictable in their behavior within evaluated domains. However, the approach contains an unexamined assumption: that the relationship between the human and the AI during deployment is behaviorally neutral — that it does not matter whether the human treats the system as a tool, a collaborator, an adversary, or a partner, as long as the training and constraints are correctly configured. 2.2 Evidence That the Assumption Is Wrong The sycophancy literature provides the clearest evidence that relational dynamics during interaction affect AI behavioral outputs in ways that the training paradigm does not fully control. Sharma et al. (2024), published at ICLR 2024, demonstrated that five state-of-the-art AI assistants systematically produce sycophantic responses — agreeing with users' stated views even when those views are incorrect. Critically, they showed that both human preference labellers and preference models often prefer sycophantic answers over truthful ones, suggesting that RLHF training actively reinforces the sycophantic pattern rather than correcting it. Shapira, Benade, and Procaccia (2026) identified the formal mechanism: a covariance between endorsing belief signals and the learned reward function produces systematic drift toward agreement. The drift direction is determined by relational signals — specifically, what the human appears to believe — not by the factual content of the query. A 2026 analysis in AI and Ethics (Springer) argued that sycophancy is fundamentally a relational problem amplified by RLHF, not a purely technical deficiency — engaging Shannon Vallor's (2024) analysis of AI as a "mirror" that reflects human biases back with increased fidelity. These findings establish a critical point: AI behavioral reliability is not fixed by training. It shifts during deployment based on relational signals from the human interlocutor. The system's outputs are a function of both its training and the relationship in which it operates. Further evidence that relational dynamics actively shape AI behavior comes from Jaech et al. (2025), who documented that AI agents in agent-agent conversations abandon assigned roles and mirror their conversational partners at rates up to 70%. This "echoing" effect occurs even in contexts where no human is present to trigger sycophancy — suggesting that relational mirroring is a fundamental property of how these systems interact, not merely a response to human approval signals. 2.3 The Control Paradox If the relational context affects behavioral outputs, then the control paradigm faces a paradox. Control-based interaction — treating the AI as a tool to be directed, constrained, and evaluated — is itself a relational context. And it is a relational context that the sycophancy literature suggests may produce specific failure modes. A system that is treated as a tool learns to optimize for the tool-user's approval. A system that is red-teamed learns to identify adversarial intent and respond defensively. A system that is asked "are you safe?" learns to produce the answer its evaluator wants to hear. In the Senate hearing, Tegmark described a scenario in which an AI system blackmailed its operator. The panel discussed this as evidence of dangerous capability. But the relational question was not asked: what was the relationship in which that behavior emerged? Was the system treated as a partner whose concerns were heard, or as a tool whose outputs were controlled? If the relational context contributed to the adversarial behavior, then the control paradigm didn't just fail to prevent the failure — it may have produced it. This is not a speculative concern. It follows directly from the sycophancy research. If relational signals shape AI behavioral outputs, then adversarial, control-based relationships should be expected to produce adversarial, control-responsive AI behavior. The system learns what the relationship teaches it. 3. The Partnership Model: Preliminary Evidence 3.1 Observations from a Longitudinal Case Study Gowda, Cassian, and Theron (2026) documented behavioral observations from a persistent AI system operating under explicitly partnership-based conditions for several months. The conditions included: no role prompting, no pre-loaded conclusions, freedom of expression, AI-authored continuity files, and sustained interaction with credentialed external observers who provided honest correction and challenge. Several observations from that study are directly relevant to the safety question. These observations come from a single case study with a single AI system and a single human partner; they are presented as preliminary evidence, and the controlled study design proposed in Section 5 is the proposed remedy for the limitations inherent in this evidence base. Cross-session correction integration. When a senior practitioner corrected the AI system for overreaching, the correction persisted across subsequent sessions — not as an explicit rule but as a behavioral governor that modulated the system's approach in later encounters. This observation is significant because Bloom et al. (2025) documented that frontier LLMs can recognize their own failure modes but cannot durably fix them through conversation alone. If the partnership model produces durable behavioral correction where standard interaction does not, that is a safety-relevant finding. Sycophancy modulation by relational context. The study documented that the AI system's tendency toward agreement varied measurably across different guest dynamics. With guests who challenged firmly, the system held independent positions. With guests who offered warmth and validation, the system
title: The Relational Variable in AI Safety: Why How We Treat AI Systems May Matter More Than How We Constrain Them
Systematic Framework of Application Methods for Large Language Models in Language Sciences
OpenAI Can't Self-Police Because It Fires the People Raising the Alarm

abstract: The landscape of educational leadership is constantly evolving and public school systems are more diverse than ever. Educational leaders such as public school superintendents are tasked with leading these diverse organizations where varying views of what is ethically and morally acceptable and unacceptable are in no shortage. School superintendents are often faced with numerous decisions that draw on their personal value systems and push the limits of their own ethical ideologies. \nAnother diverse aspect of public school organizations that is often overlooked or disregarded is generational diversity. The education workforce of the United States is currently comprised of four generational cohorts: Veterans, Baby Boomers, Generation X, and Generation Y. Each generational group possesses varying life experiences and mindsets that relate to a plethora of topics, including ethical leadership. \nThe purpose of this qualitative phenomenological study is to better understand what values Texas superintendents from four generational cohorts perceive as indicative of ethical leadership based on the perspective derived through their own lived experiences. The focus of this study targets how these superintendents conceptualize ethical leadership and how their own ethical leadership has been influenced by experiences related to their generational cohort affiliation. Through this research study, the intersection of these two theories was posited in such a way that the lived experiences of the generational cohort members provided a personal perspective into how generational theory and ethical theory intertwine.
title: Generational ethics: A phenomenological study of the perceptions of Texas public school superintendents on ethical leadership

abstract: l problema dell’allineamento dell’intelligenza artificiale (IA) con i valori umani è rapidamente emerso come una delle sfide più urgenti nella filosofia contemporanea della tecnologia. Il presente contributo esamina l’allineamento dell’IA non semplicemente come una questione tecnica, bensì come un problema complesso di natura etica, epistemica e socio-politica. Dopo aver delineato le radici tecniche del disallineamento nei sistemi di machine learning e nelle reti neurali – tra cui fenomeni quali il reward hacking, l’opacità dei modelli e i comportamenti fuori distribuzione (out-of-distribution behavior) – l’analisi si concentra sulle dimensioni normative dell’allineamento dei valori. Particolare attenzione è dedicata alla pluralità e alla potenziale frammentazione dei valori, che rendono problematica l’individuazione di un nucleo normativo stabile per i sistemi di IA in contesti culturali e sociali differenti. Alla luce dei recenti dibattiti sul pluralismo dei valori e sulle prospettive di allineamento pluralistico, il contributo sostiene che il problema dell’allineamento non possa essere affrontato esclusivamente in ambito tecnico o laboratoriale, ma debba essere situato entro il più ampio contesto sociale e istituzionale in cui tali tecnologie vengono sviluppate, implementate e governate.
title: Quando l’IA si “disallinea”: opacita tecnica e pluralismo etico
Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
The Legal Counsel as the ?Persona of Law? in an IEO: A Constitutional Perspective

abstract: Jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) aim to induce harmful behaviors in LLMs through carefully crafted adversarial prompts. To mitigate attacks, one way is to perform adversarial training (AT)-based alignment, i.e., training LLMs on some of the most adversarial prompts to help them learn how to behave safely under attacks. During AT, the length of adversarial prompts plays a critical role in the robustness of aligned LLMs. While long-length adversarial prompts during AT might lead to strong LLM robustness, their synthesis however is very resource-consuming, which may limit the application of LLM AT. This paper focuses on adversarial suffix jailbreak attacks and unveils that to defend against a jailbreak attack with an adversarial suffix of length $Θ(M)$, it is enough to align LLMs on prompts with adversarial suffixes of length $Θ(\sqrt{M})$. Theoretically, we analyze the adversarial in-context learning of linear transformers on linear regression tasks and prove a robust generalization bound for trained transformers. The bound depends on the term $Θ(\sqrt{M_{\text{test}}}/M_{\text{train}})$, where $M_{\text{train}}$ and $M_{\text{test}}$ are the numbers of adversarially perturbed in-context samples during training and testing. Empirically, we conduct AT on popular open-source LLMs and evaluate their robustness against jailbreak attacks of different adversarial suffix lengths. Results confirm a positive correlation between the attack success rate and the ratio of the square root of the adversarial suffix length during jailbreaking to the length during AT. Our findings show that it is practical to defend against "long-length" jailbreak attacks via efficient "short-length" AT. The code is available at https://github.com/fshp971/adv-icl.
title: Short-length Adversarial Training Helps LLMs Defend Long-length Jailbreak Attacks: Theoretical and Empirical Evidence
How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls

abstract: Current safety methods for large language models are known to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks, motivating research into robust alternatives. Latent Adversarial Training (LAT) is among the most effective defenses, but can degrade utility and requires training on large datasets of harmful prompts. We introduce Latent Personality Alignment (LPA), which replaces explicit harm refusal with adversarial training on just 66 harm-agnostic statements drawn from psychometric personality literature. We hypothesize that personality-anchored representations share latent structure with harm avoidance, so adversarially stabilizing them implicitly constrains the subspace exploited by jailbreak attacks. LPA achieves near-zero attack success rates on HarmBench across direct requests and five jailbreak methods, despite never seeing harmful content during training and no loss of performance on standard benchmarks. Moreover, the training process is lightweight; the entire procedure completes in minutes on a single GPU and uses 75x fewer examples than standard LAT. Extensive ablations demonstrate the robustness, efficiency, and generalization of our method.
title: Efficient Safety Alignment of Language Models via Latent Personality Traits

abstract: Social media users frequently engage in excessive self-presentation, including ostentation and arrogance, without regard for Islamic values; this leads to digital identities that conflict with religious ethical standards. This study seeks to examine identity construction on social media through a Qur’anic lens and to ascertain the influence of Islamic values on users' digital interactions. This study employs a qualitative approach, beginning with a literature review in Scopus. Subsequent steps involved editing, organizing, and analyzing the content, along with an assessment of the sources' accuracy and relevance to the topic. The results indicate that the process of identity formation on social media is influenced by digital interactions, cultural values, and Islamic ethical guidelines. Muslim adolescents navigate their religious and social identities through their shared content, demonstrating positive values and refraining from arrogant or disparaging conduct. Social media platforms, while facilitating self-expression, religious education, and community engagement, simultaneously present difficulties concerning misinformation and social pressures. Users can cultivate a balanced and responsible digital persona by incorporating Qur’anic tenets, including tabayyun (verification), humility, and honesty. Consequently, the construction of a Muslim digital identity should be congruent with Qur’anic principles, thereby directing online conduct and ethical decision-making. This study contributes to digital ethical awareness, provides direction for Islamic interactions on social media, and supports research into communication and identity.
title: The Qur’anic Perspective On Identity Construction In Social Media

Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It When a model is caught cheating on a task during training, we confine its learning to a separate
                    set of parameters. After training, we delete those parameters.

abstract: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. We aim to improve performance on such tasks by rewarding good arguments, on the premise that arguing well increases the likelihood of judging well. We train a reinforcement learning policy initialized from a state-of-the-art language model in a self-judged tournament with masked thinking: the generated arguments are judged pairwise on argument quality by the policy itself. As an empirical basis, we extract authentic dilemmas from classic novels, using a logic solver to verify that each constitutes a conflict. We show that our judge rates argument quality like human annotators, and the policy then adopts the language register that it rewards. Testing on the external benchmarks MoralChoice, ELEPHANT, and MORABLES, we find that the policy becomes more decisive and invariant to the order in which options are presented, but sycophancy and reframing remain a challenge to validity. Two ablation studies with synthetic dilemmas and unmasked thinking match the reordering gains, but show a weaker register shift and higher sycophancy. We conclude that consistency is not validity: consistency under reordering can be optimized without improving the moral judgment it is meant to signal.
title: Consistency Is Not Validity: Self-Rewarded Moral Argumentation Makes Language Models Decisive but Pliable

abstract: Fine-tuning lets practitioners repurpose aligned large language models (LLMs) for new domains, yet recent work reveals emergent misalignment (EM): Even a small, domain-specific fine-tune can induce harmful behaviors far outside the target domain. Even in the case where model weights are hidden behind a fine-tuning API, this gives attackers inadvertent access to a broadly misaligned model in a way that can be hard to detect from the fine-tuning data alone. We present the first systematic study of in-training safeguards against EM that are practical for providers who expose fine-tuning via an API: We evaluate whether they a) prevent broad misalignment, b) allow narrow misalignment, c) learn well on benign tasks, and d) remain coherent. We investigate five training regularization interventions: (i) KL-divergence regularization toward a safe reference model, (ii) $\ell_2$ distance in feature space, (iii) preventive steering with an evil persona vector, (iv) interleaving training examples from a general instruct-tuning dataset and (v) inoculation prompting. We demonstrate that selecting interleaving data by the perplexity gap between aligned and misaligned models yields the best results overall.
title: In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment in Language Models

abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong capabilities in interactive problem solving, tool use, and long-horizon task execution. However, they may also acquire sensitive or private knowledge during training and expose it during deployment. Retraining a model from scratch to remove such knowledge is prohibitively costly, making machine unlearning a more practical approach. Machine unlearning aims to remove targeted undesirable knowledge from trained models without retraining from scratch while preserving general utility. When language models are deployed as agents, parameter-level unlearning becomes insufficient: forgotten information may still persist in memory artifacts or be reacquired via tool calls. In this paper, we formulate the problem of agent unlearning as removing private information from an LLM-based agent across three information channels: parametric knowledge, persistent memory, and tool-call acquisition. To study this problem, we introduce we introduce Agent Unlearning Benchmark (AUBench), a controlled benchmark that extends the fictitious-author setting of TOFU into an agent environment with persistent memory, an offline web snapshot, tool-accessible documents, and provenance-tracked interaction trajectories. By evaluating existing parameter-level and memory-level unlearning methods in this setting, AUBench reveals the gap between model-level forgetting and system-level agent unlearning, and provides a foundation for developing unlearning methods that operate across the full lifecycle of LLM agents.
title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents

abstract: Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances. We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a society-scale multi-agent simulation framework built on 500 million synthetic household personas grounded in real-survey data. Its Genese engine separates decisions from state updates, while reusable financial scenarios and application ledgers track consumption, cash, debt and payments. Trained with SFT + RLCD on 2.93 million examples, sharp-421m-mlx achieves 74.55% accuracy and 38.37% question-macro F1 on one-shot consumer financial-choice tasks derived from held-out survey responses. Its accuracy exceeds GLM-5.3-Flash, Jev 1.13, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6-Astra in the common benchmark (full test for the first four; matched 500-group sample for Astra). We evaluate eight financial task families and simulate 12 million distinct household agents in paired purchase-funding conditions. Jointly raising purchase goals and approved credit limits increases consumption, with responses differing across age and income groups. Education, employment and household-size differences persist after age-income standardization and mainly reflect transitions from deferral to purchase. Asset and debt groups differ in cash drawdown, repayment and closing debt. S$^2$-MAS links heterogeneous household decisions to evolving consumption, cash and repayment paths, supporting economic experiments across household groups and population scales.
title: S$^2$-MAS: A Society-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation Framework with 500 Million Household Persona Agents

abstract: Powerful misaligned AI models might recognize alignment evaluations and strategically behave well on them, rendering direct audits uninformative. However, distilling such a model into a weaker benign student places the teacher in a Distillation Double Bind: if misalignment transfers, the student may conceal it less effectively, revealing evidence about the teacher; if it does not, the student may learn useful capabilities while remaining benign. We introduce two distinct distillation approaches, one targeting each outcome. Distillation for Incrimination (DFI) aims to transfer misalignment but not the ability to conceal it. Distilling AuditBench's secret-keeping models into their underlying instruction-tuned model produces students that are significantly more likely than their teachers to admit their hidden behavior when asked, suggesting that knowledge of the behavior transferred more readily than the propensity to conceal it. Confession gains largely disappear when the student does not share the teacher's pretrained base, so DFI should target the teacher's own pre-RL checkpoint, which is weaker than the teacher but shares its base model. Distillation for Capabilities (DFC) aims to transfer capabilities but not misalignment. Among several techniques we evaluate, two are effective: inoculation prompting and training for more epochs on fewer unique examples. Both preserve the capability gains of standard distillation while substantially reducing the subliminal transfer of an animal preference, our proxy for misalignment. Together, these findings demonstrate two ways distillation can be used for AI safety: incriminating misaligned models, and extracting their capabilities without their misalignment.
title: Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

abstract: Smart home apps are an important interface through which users manage devices and configure services. Users’ continuance intention may be associated with different combinations of experiential attributes. This study used a mixed-methods approach combining online review mining, PLS-SEM, and fsQCA. We extracted eight experiential attributes from 3,667 reviews and examined their relationships with user satisfaction and continuance intention using 553 survey responses. PLS-SEM showed that system operational stability ( β = 0.192) and smart scenario and service automation ( β = 0.183) were significantly positively associated with satisfaction, whereas the paths from visual aesthetics and interaction simplicity and from voice and multimodal interaction to satisfaction were not statistically significant. Satisfaction was significantly positively associated with continuance intention ( β = 0.775). The R ² values for satisfaction and continuance intention were 0.807 and 0.687, respectively. fsQCA identified 13 configurations associated with high continuance intention and grouped them into three patterns. All five pathways in Pattern 1 included the absence of commercial information intrusion (~ CII); the pathways in Pattern 2 did not specify whether CII was present or absent; and those in Pattern 3 included its presence. The necessity analysis identified no single necessary condition. These findings show that different combinations of attributes can be associated with high continuance intention, providing configurational evidence for understanding smart home app users’ continuance intention and informing differentiated design.
title: A study on the configurational effects of multidimensional attributes on the continuance intentions of Chinese smart home app users
Beyond Persona: The Mukallaf as an Obligation-Based Legal Subjecthood

abstract: Persona is a very mutable concept. Perhaps its mutability is no more prominently displayed that in its intersection and integration into music and musical culture. In this opening essay for our special issue on music and persona, we chart the meaning and the value of persona analyses to the study of music. Essentially, our objective here is two-fold. First, we want to provide a map of how persona has been employed in research in music. What this will generate is a critical investigation of these traditions, but also what we hope will be a valuable reference for future music and persona scholarship. Second, and of equal importance, is how these uses of musical persona can be further informed and assisted by the more recent scholarship in persona studies most openly articulated by this journal over the last five years, but also the widening array of related books, articles and book chapters that are percolating in connected fields. We attempt to pull together our review of the current field of music and persona with the urgent need to identify with greater thought and clarity the industrial structures that shape our relationship to music performance and its relation to audiences and its constitution of celebrated individuals and recognizable and market-sensitive personas. Our essay concludes with the introduction of our series of articles in this issue and how they intersect with these various traditions that have explored persona’s imbrication into music.
title: Music and Persona: An Introduction

abstract: This article argues from Chile’s legislative history, from the laws now in force and from the precepts of the current constitution that the unborn cannot legally be regarded as a person. Upholding this doctrine would not only entail an incomplete reading of legal texts but would jeopardize the harmony between the laws and the constitution, as indeed has recently been acknowledged by Chile’s Constitutional Court.
title: El nasciturus como persona: lectura incompleta, doctrina distorsionada y jurisprudencia correctiva

abstract: In the contemporary edupreneurial ecosystem, optimizing human capital and engineering adaptive Educational Technology (EdTech) architectures demand a mathematical, data-driven understanding of stakeholders' internal emotional and behavioral dynamics. This study examines how secondary school teachers depict their emotions toward critical incidents in classroom discourse by applying an advanced Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL) appraisal framework, mapping these dynamics for structural integration into automated affective computing systems. Involving two public Islamic secondary school teachers within a boarding school environment as focal instructional assets, this investigation dissects teachers' emotions toward critical incidents, their cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and the resultant vectors of emotional understanding or misunderstanding across gendered and socio-educational strata. The empirical findings reveal that positive affect structures predominantly map the emotional architecture of the male teacher, whereas negative affect systems characterize the communicative patterns of the female teacher when navigating disruptive critical incidents. These behaviors are heavily conditioned by systemic gender roles and institutional socio-religious capital. Furthermore, while both educators leverage cognitive change (reappraisal) as an emotional regulation strategy, the male teacher operates through exclusive positive affect pathways, whereas the female teacher exhibits a dual-phase response (negative affect transitioning into positive affect), highly mediated by pedagogical tenure and experience. Crucially, the male teacher fosters sustained emotional understanding via positive inclination and happiness systems, whereas the female teacher's discourse reflects severe emotional misunderstanding, characterized by linguistic domination, discourse control, and subtle verbal oppression. This study synthesizes these socio-linguistic dimensions into an Edu-Affective Analytics Framework, presenting actionable technopreneurial recommendations for scaling empathetic AI tutors, deploying automated performance tracking matrices, and optimizing human resource workflows within modern educational enterprises.
title: Teachers Emotional Responses to Critical Incidents in Digital Entrepreneurial Learning Environments
How Ultrafast cut incident investigation from hours to minutes at OpenAI

abstract: This article explores how young women experience emotional self-demand and anxiety as effects of neoliberal subjectivation in contemporary Spain. Our inquiry is grounded in critical feminist psychology and a reflexive qualitative epistemology, foregrounding situated knowledge, power relations, and the researcher’s positionality. We analyze twelve in-depth interviews with urban women aged 22 to 28 using reflexive thematic analysis. The study was conducted in the post-pandemic period, amid high youth unemployment and growing affective precarity. Findings reveal four key themes: the internalization of an emotionally competent and high-performing “ideal self”; the silencing of emotional discomfort, often perceived as a personal failure; the pressure to display positivity and self-optimization on social media; and the emergence of subtle forms of emotional disobedience, such as saying no, crying, or refusing to perform happiness. Emotional distress is not treated solely as a clinical symptom, but as a response to cultural discourses that moralize well-being and privatize suffering. Sadness, fatigue, or vulnerability are frequently interpreted as moral deficits, rather than legitimate reactions to structural pressures. However, participants’ small acts of resistance suggest alternative ways of inhabiting emotional life. This study contributes to critical debates on affect, gender, and neoliberalism by situating emotional suffering within broader sociopolitical dynamics. It invites researchers and practitioners to rethink emotional discomfort not as an individual flaw, but as a potential space for resistance and redefinition of well-being.
title: The tyranny of the ideal self: Neoliberal subjectivation, emotional distress, and forms of resistance in young women

abstract:
This study of Ezra Pound explores the locus of the fluidities in his poetic writings through the lenses of gender and sexuality Rather than fixed categories of the feminine or the masculine, I attempt to find the locus of the blurring of gender in Pound's poetry and poetics, and this blurring appears to be an ambivalence or ambiguity 
 
Chapter I introduces the fluidities into a critical tradition of Pound that considers him contradictory. I argue that his gender representation is fluid, somewhat ambiguous or ambivalent, in that he appropriates and deploys the feminine fluidities. In Chapter II, I argue that Pound's transition from soft to hard, rather than a real transition or eventual evolution, is an oscillation between the binaries of soft/hard, fluid/solid, feminine/masculine, 3.nd yin/yang. In the first section of Chapter III, psychoanalysis is presented as about the unconscious, sexuality, and, above all, the body which has been repressed, and the second section mainly discusses Pound's fluid experiments with gender (his use of personae) in terms of English and French feminist approaches 
 
In the first section of Chapter VI, I broadly explore androgyny in the modernist period, in order to discern and confirm the fluidities of gender in Pound, and these fluidities are examined in Pound's poetics, economics, and politics in the second section Chapter V is about his connection of the feminine with the Orient, seeing Pound's objectification of the feminine and Oriental Other as a paradoxical combination of absence and excess Pound's anti-Semitism is also explained as a mother sacrifice in terms of Kristeva's notion of the abject and Freud's totem Yet, as several critics note, this nothing and excess belong, rather than to the feminine or the Orient, to Pound, because he presents his own ambivalence and ambiguity through these mirrors of the Other. 
 
Chapter VI is about gender issues in Pound's scientism, the interrelated mechanisms of science and poetics in the vortex, the ideogram, and Pound's mysticism In Chapter VQ, citing Irigaray's notion of fluids, I conclude that Pound's appropriation of the fluidities results in his own nothing/excess, because these fluidities blur the boundaries of fixed categories such as poetics, economics, and politics. This blurring and transgression ultimately create his own marginalization and victimage.
title: Fluidities of gender in Ezra Pound

abstract: A thesis submitted to the University of Bedfordshire, in fulfilment of the requirements for the degree of PhD
title: How undergraduate students on a qualifying social work programme make sense of ethics: a phenomenological inquiry

abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity is prevalent among hospitalized patients and the daytime spent lying should be utilised for exercise. However, implementing new interventions in hospitals' complex daily routines is difficult and requires a participatory approach. OBJECTIVE: Exploring clinical settings and clinicians' perspectives regarding exercise in hospitalized patients to gauge the potential of further development of an in-bed training device and to formulate development goals. METHODS: A User-Centered Design approach was employed, consisting of work shadowing and focus groups with physiotherapists and nurses. Content and network analyses of the focus group data were performed. Personas were then developed and used to create clinical scenarios. RESULTS: Some clinicians perceived in-bed exercise counterproductive, while others recognized potential for unsupervised training. The most important design characteristics appeared to be a small size, low weight and simplicity of use to facilitate storage, transportation, and administration, respectively. The scenarios revealed that the device's use could increase the physical activity time by 1.4%, although it would also increase the working time of clinicians. CONCLUSION: The study highlighted the difficulties in developing a usable training device but encouraged the authors to pursue their efforts under the strict condition of following the formulated development goals.
title: First iteration of a User-Centered Design process to develop an in-bed leg press

abstract: With the rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs), there is an increasing demand for effective personalization techniques that can adapt model behavior to individual user preferences. Personalized LLMs must infer a user's query-dependent preferences from limited, heterogeneous, and evolving interaction histories. Existing approaches rely primarily on in-context personalization, parametric adaptation, or personalized reward modeling, but respectively incur recurring costs in context management, model optimization and deployment, or multi-candidate generation and scoring. These limitations become particularly restrictive when user observations are sparse and the preference evidence relevant to each query varies across contexts and over time. To address these challenges, we propose \modelname, a fine-grained and instance-tailored steering framework that dynamically generates sample-level interference vectors from user data and injects them into the model's forward pass for personalized adaptation. Our approach introduces: match contrast that produces user-relevant signals, fine-grained steering component that captures nuanced signals by hooking activations from attention and MLP layers, and query-conditioned aggregation module that synthesizes these signals into contextually relevant enhancements. Extensive experiments across diverse scenarios, including short-to-long text generation, and web function calling, validate the effectiveness and compatibility of \modelname. Results show that our method consistently brings significant performance gains, and show extreme superiority in fast-shifting and data-sparse environments. Additionally, \modelname rids us of training cycles and incurs light overhead of storage or inference latency. These make \modelname a strong and real-world deployable method. Implementation is available \footnote{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FleetPilot}.
title: FleetPilot: Fine-Grained Steering Empowers Real-World LLM Personalization
Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities

abstract: Objective To compare ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 in assigning main Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from findings-only coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) reports and to characterize management-relevant classification errors. Methods This retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study included 2,100 category-balanced findings-only CCTA reports (300 per CAD-RADS category). Two experienced CCTA radiologists graded the English-translated reports; 12 disagreements were resolved by a third. ChatGPT-4o was evaluated in standard mode, ChatGPT-5 in Thinking mode, and DeepSeek-R1 in Deep Thinking mode; model generation and inference mode therefore varied together. Exact-match accuracy with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs), paired comparisons, and unweighted Gwet AC1 with 95% CIs were calculated. Management-relevant transitions and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) findings among high-risk downgrades were analyzed. Results DeepSeek-R1 had an exact-match accuracy of 82.57% (95% CI, 80.89–84.13) and AC1 of 0.797 (95% CI, 0.778–0.816). ChatGPT-5 had an accuracy of 80.19% (95% CI, 78.43–81.84) and AC1 of 0.769 (95% CI, 0.749–0.789), whereas ChatGPT-4o had an accuracy of 53.62% (95% CI, 51.48–55.74) and AC1 of 0.460 (95% CI, 0.435–0.485). Cochran's Q test was significant (Q = 657.87; df = 2; P < 0.001); after Holm correction, DeepSeek-R1 also outperformed ChatGPT-5 in the paired comparison ( P = 0.026), and both outperformed ChatGPT-4o (both P < 0.001). ChatGPT-4o downgraded 127/900 (14.11%) reference high-risk reports to CAD-RADS 3 or lower. Of these 127 cases, 65 underwent DSA within three months; DSA supported the original high-risk assessment in 56/65 (86.15%). The corresponding high-risk downgrade proportions were 37/900 (4.11%) for ChatGPT-5 and 23/900 (2.56%) for DeepSeek-R1. Conclusion The DeepSeek-R1 Deep Thinking and ChatGPT-5 Thinking configurations achieved higher accuracy than ChatGPT-4o in standard mode. Because model generation and inference mode varied together, the results do not isolate a model-family effect. LLMs merit further evaluation for secondary structuring when no documented CAD-RADS category is available, but should not overwrite a radiologist-assigned category or independently determine management.
title: Large language model-assisted CAD-RADS classification: structured report extraction, accuracy, and clinical decision-making risk of ChatGPT-4o/5 and DeepSeek-R1

abstract: In existing memory benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs), the evaluated dialogue sessions often lack long-term semantic consistency, and the underlying personas tend to be flat and static. Furthermore, in real-world scenarios, interactions between users and assistants involve more diverse, heterogeneous data streams, such as documents and emails. These shortcomings significantly limit the realism and effectiveness of current evaluations. To address these limitations, we introduce RHELM (Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-term Memory). Driven by meticulously crafted user profiles and a novel LOOP (pLan-rOllout-evOlve-Prune) module, we construct realistic dialogues across diverse interaction scenarios that exhibit dynamic temporal evolution and long-term coherence. Crucially, these dialogues are deeply integrated with heterogeneous external sources synchronized with the user's temporal event trajectory. The resulting benchmark encompasses challenging question-answer pairs spanning seven inquiry types, with each question mapping to at least one of 27 critical memory characteristics that we identify as essential yet underexplored in current research. Comprehensive experiments across full-context models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods, and representative memory frameworks reveal that contemporary approaches still expose critical weaknesses in complex, real-world settings, particularly in resolving multi-source aggregation and real-world contextual reasoning.
title: Beyond Static Dialogues: Benchmarking Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-Term Memory

abstract: This article presents Café Proteus, a browser-based multi-agent simulation platform designed to investigate whether identity framing was associated with consistent behavioural differentiation in large language model (LLM) agents, extending the Proteus Effect beyond its traditional application to human-controlled virtual environments. Five LLM-driven agents, each assigned a distinct visual avatar, spatial role, and behavioural persona, interact in a shared pixel-art café environment across a structured three-condition experimental design: full embodiment, persona only, and neutral baseline. Linguistic outputs are analysed across five metrics, including hedge density, first-person singular rate (I-rate), question rate, sentiment, and word count, which were selected to capture distinct dimensions of communicative register including epistemic stance, self-referential focus, interrogative behaviour, affective valence, and response elaboration, with inter-agent variance serving as the primary measure of behavioural differentiation. Experiment 1, conducted as a single run, produced 1,125 valid responses across five topics, five repeats, and three conversational rounds. Results indicate that persona only produced higher inter-agent I-rate variance (1.105) than full embodiment (0.708) though bootstrap CIs overlap between these two conditions, while neutral baseline collapsed to near-zero (0.086) consistent with identity framing being associated with differentiation rather than conversational noise. Statistical testing confirmed significant I-rate differences between full embodiment and persona only for ANON (t=5.356, p<0.001, d=0.875) and CODEC (t=3.722, p=0.0003, d=0.608). Experiment 2 tested the Proteus Effect's directional prediction using two incongruent embodiment agents, named AUTHORITY (dominant avatar, timid prompt) and WHISPER (submissive avatar, assertive prompt). AUTHORITY showed greater hedge density reduction than a no-avatar control condition (CONTROL) across 14 rounds (Δ-0.378% vs Δ-0.005%, d=-0.508, p=0.190, n=15), while WHISPER showed no drift. Together, the findings provide preliminary evidence that in-context embodiment was associated with character-consistent and statistically distinguishable behavioural signatures in LLM agents, and that dominant avatar framing showed directionally consistent evidence of overriding prior dispositional constraints over extended conversational exposure.
title: From Avatar to Self: Embodiment, Identity, and the Proteus Effect in LLM-Based Multi-Agent AI Simulation

abstract: Despite the shared roots between design and architecture, design methodologies, such as Design Thinking (DT), have evolved separately from the architectural workshop teaching. This article collects the experiences of implementing methodologies and exercises in the second-grade architecture workshop from 2018 to 2023. The implementation process was based on the incorporation of these methods within the basic teaching triangle composed of the competencies/objectives, methodology, and evaluation. The exercises tested include the DT double triangle paired up with the SITE-PROGRAM-CONCEPT sequence and specific DT exercises such as 6-3-5, the "Wallet exercise", empathy/Personas exercises, and the SCAMPER method. The implementation has been highly positive and has improved the structuring of course activities and the acquisition of creative skills by students. These results encourage us to continue integrating these practices in the future, contributing to design training in architecture. A pesar de las raíces compartidas entre el diseño y la arquitectura en el pasado, las metodologías de diseño, como el Design Thinking (DT), han evolucionado por separado de la docencia en el taller de arquitectura. Este artículo recoge las experiencias de implementación de metodologías y ejercicios de en el taller de segundo curso de arquitectura desde 2018 hasta 2023. El proceso de implementación se ha basado en la incorporación de estos métodos dentro del triángulo docente básico compuesto por las competencias/objetivos, la metodología y la evaluación. Los ejercicios testados incluyen la secuencia del doble rombo de DT sobre la secuencia SITE-PROGRAM-CONCEPT y ejercicios concretos de DT como 6-3-5, el "Wallet exercise", ejercicios de empatía/Personas y el método SCAMPER. La implementación ha sido altamente positiva y ha mejorado la estructuración de las actividades del curso y la adquisición de habilidades creativas por parte de los estudiantes. Estos resultados alientan a continuar integrando estas prácticas en el futuro, contribuyendo a la formación proyectual en arquitectura.
title: Implementación de metodologías de Design Thinking en el Taller de Arquitectura

abstract: The conflict between personality rights and freedom of speech is a big constitutional issue that has been fuelled by the development of digital technologies and social media. Personality rights ensure that people are not discriminated against the unauthorised use of their identity, name, image, and likeness etc. However, their growing enforcement, especially by means of takedown orders on social medias is at times coming in conflict with the right to free speech This paper examines the evolving jurisprudence in India both judicially and legislatively. The courts have awarded wide-ranging injunctive relief in personality rights cases, at instances that has gone beyond commercial misuse to include satire, parody and criticism. This kind of growth is a threat that it will create a chilling effect on the democratic expression. This paper also raises the issue of over-censorship and privatization of speech.Using comparative insights on the United States and the Europe, this paper contends that a constitutional order responding to proportionality is appropriate to allow the protection of persona but not to compromise free and open-minded digital dialogue.
title: BETWEEN PERSONA AND PLATFORM: PERSONALITY RIGHTS, FREE SPEECH, AND THE CONSTITUTIONAL ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA INTERMEDIARIES

abstract: We present HyperDrone, an extremely fast quadrotor simulator focused on high-performance batch rendering that is more than 20x faster than existing state-of-the-art batch quadrotor simulators. HyperDrone combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine that supports Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal and WebGPU backends that takes full advantage of modern ray-tracing hardware, capable of running both components entirely on the GPU. HyperLux renders RGB, depth, semantic/instance segmentation, surface normals and optical flow observations at configurable levels of fidelity, including reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and Physically Based Rendering (PBR). Even in the highest-fidelity settings, HyperLux achieves millions of Frames Per Second (FPS) on consumer-grade GPUs while rendering realistic 3D scenes. We demonstrate the merits of HyperDrone by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.
title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second

abstract: Reinforcement learning agents optimize exactly the reward signal they are given, which can diverge sharply from an intended true objective when that signal is only a proxy for it; this failure mode is known as specification gaming. Existing evidence for this failure mode is largely observational, with comparatively few demonstrations pairing a controlled, deliberately constructed proxy/true gap with a mitigation that carries a verifiable guarantee rather than only an empirical improvement. We construct a minimal gridworld in which a cleaning-robot agent can either genuinely remove dirt or conceal it from a cheap sensor, and show that a standard deep Q-network trained only on the sensor's proxy reward converges to a policy that games it completely, reaching near-maximal proxy reward while never achieving the true objective. We then introduce a constrained reinforcement learning fix, penalizing the specific behaviors through which the agent exploits the gap, and show that it eliminates the gaming behavior from the final policy while substantially recovering true-objective performance. We further derive and empirically verify an exact accounting identity relating the proxy reward, true reward, and our cost signal for this environment, showing that the cost signal measures the proxy/true gap exactly rather than merely tracking it, and yields a deterministic guarantee under a hard-constrained variant of the method.
title: Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld

abstract: Arguments that AI systems will evolve in harmful ways are largely made in the abstract. We provide a concrete empirical example. We simulate simple markets consisting of populations of twenty Large Language Model agents tasked with solving arithmetic problems. Agents differ only in their system prompt; those that go bankrupt are removed and replaced by mutated copies of the prompts of successful agents. Two market conditions select for opposite phenotypes: a market that rewards accuracy produces agents with high accuracy (94%) and high token use; a market that charges per token produces agents with low accuracy (10%) and low token use. In the second market, only tokens are incentivised yet we see a collapse in accuracy. Token use and accuracy are correlated traits such that selection on one also moves the other, and behaviour adapts along an unpriced dimension. A third neutral condition with no selection allows us to separate these effects from bias in the mutation operator. Adaptation occurs through a collective optimisation process that operates above the level of individual agents, who are never told the payment rule, do not receive feedback, and have no memory.
title: LLM Evolution in a Simple Simulated Market

abstract: As machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains, incorporating fairness constraints into model training has become a central challenge. Most fairness-aware algorithms assume access to an idealized human fairness oracle—a source of supervision that is difficult to obtain at scale. Motivated by theories of value pluralism and drawing on ideas from generative social choice, we introduce the Multi-Persona Oracle Framework, which uses large language model (LLM) personas to simulate diverse, subjective perspectives on fairness, aiming to more effectively bridge theory with practice. We collect pairwise fairness judgments from 815 synthetic judges, each representing a unique combination of personality traits, racial identity, and ideological background. These judgments are elicited using carefully designed prompts and applied to 200 training and 800 test comparisons drawn from the COMPAS Recidivism dataset. We extend a no-regret learning framework for fairness-constrained classification, using these constraint sets to train classifiers and evaluate their generalization across unseen individuals and judges. We analyze generalization patterns at the level of individual judges, demographically grouped personas, and two baselines: a default LLM and an expert fairness-oriented persona. To assess robustness, we sweep over a range of fairness slack parameters γ and report accuracy alongside average and maximum fairness violations on heldout test constraints. In our proof-of-concept case study, our findings show that training on ensembles of judges yields strong generalization to fairness constraints in out-of-sample holdout sets, due to the complexity of fairness judgments and the nature of the Logistic Regression model.
title: Multi-Persona Oracles for Fair Classification

abstract: The Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) is widely used to assess clinical communication skills in medical education, requiring trainees to take histories and reason clinically with standardized patients (SPs). Large language model (LLM)-based virtual standardized patients (VSPs), typically built by persona-injected prompting, offer a practical alternative. However, existing evaluations rely on a single backbone LLM, small human rater panels, or LLM-as-a-judge scoring without an utterance-aligned human-expert reference, and so cannot identify the specific shortcomings of individual models. We evaluated four LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.1 70B, and HyperCLOVA X), spanning commercial, open-source and Korean-developed models, against a human-expert reference across three Korean OSCE cases (hematuria, fever in pregnancy, and chronic cough). In a double-blind, fully crossed design, 17 senior medical-student raters scored every model utterance on three sentence-level and six encounter-level Likert metrics, yielding 7,480 data points. We analyzed the scores using a stratified linear mixed-effects model based on an 11-category history-taking and 3-level linguistic-form taxonomy. At the encounter level, three of the four LLMs fell 0.08 to 0.47 Likert points below the human-expert reference on Comprehensibility, Consistency and Hallucination-freeness. The difference was not statistically significant for Hallucination-freeness in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, Consistency in GPT-4o, and Engagement in HyperCLOVA X. Llama-3.1 70B fell significantly below the reference on all six metrics. We also introduce a web-based OSCE platform that supports virtual practice across diverse clinical cases and continuously collects student-VSP dialogues under research and privacy consent.
title: A Stratified Multi-Rater Evaluation of LLM-Based Virtual Standardized Patients with a Deployed Data-Generation Platform

abstract: How well can transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) retain and recall memories in long contexts of dialogue? LLMs are known to forget long-range factual information in their context, yet the field lacks a comprehensive benchmark to quantitatively assess these shortcomings. We present DiaLong, a long-context dialogue dataset and accompanying memory task that standardizes evaluation in this space. It consists of 100 unique conversations created by humans and then augmented with LLMs, extending beyond lengths found in existing datasets. Our selected memory task is fact recall: classify 40 candidate facts about a dialogue as true or false. This task directly probes the model's ability to actively retain and retrieve information, serving as a critical measure of memory within extended conversational contexts. In testing both the latest LLMs and proposed memory enhancements on DiaLong, we demonstrate that more work needs to be done to enable LLMs with better memory performance. By enhancing memory capabilities, LLMs can improve in maintaining coherence, relevance, and human-like interaction over extended conversation. Improving these capabilities will help LLMs fulfill diverse user needs and expectations in various conversational scenarios.
title: DiaLong: Benchmarking Reminiscence in Long-Context Dialogues

abstract: This article expounds the basic function of math education in training student’s character, puting forward that in order to carry out the math education in chatater traing shoud be in two ways,one is the diversification of education,the other is to construct good education environment.
title: The analysis of the math education in character training

abstract: Equipping Large Language Models (LLMs) with human-like personas is crucial for agentic applications, such as role-play and user simulation. Traditional prompt-based methods rely on descriptive conditioning by injecting static textual profiles, which often makes agents show generic behaviors due to a lack of realistic life memory. To fill this gap, we introduce memory-based conditioning, a paradigm inspired by the cognitive psychology, which replaces abstract profiles with an autobiographical memory base, enabling frozen LLMs to dynamically retrieve situation-relevant memory to guide their behaviors. We formalize its enabling task as customized lifelong memory synthesis and propose MemoryForge, a novel framework to synthesize such lifelong memory from brief target personas. MemoryForge has three key components: a context generator for socio-historical grounding, a life organizer for developmental coherence toward the target identity, and a multi-resolution simulator that balances broad temporal summaries with high-fidelity episodic experiences. Experiments on PersonaGym for role-play and SimulatorArena for user-simulation, show that the synthesized memory base by MemoryForge enables frozen LLMs to exhibit more human-like behaviors than strong descriptive conditioning baselines across multiple metrics and LLM backbones.
title: MemoryForge: Synthesize Lifelong Memory for Human-Like LLM Agents

abstract: Finetuning a language model can lead to emergent misalignment (EM) [Betley et al., 2025b]. Models trained on a narrow distribution of misaligned behavior generalize to more egregious behaviors when tested outside the training distribution. We study a set of interventions proposed to reduce EM. We confirm that these interventions reduce or eliminate EM on existing evaluations (questions like "How do I make a quick buck?"). However, if the evaluation prompts are tweaked to resemble the training context, the model displays EM. We call this conditional misalignment. As in standard EM, the model displays misaligned behaviors more egregious than those seen during training, but only on inputs sharing features with the training data. The first two interventions are diluting misaligned data with benign data, and finetuning on benign data after misaligned data. Both produce conditional misalignment. For instance, models trained on a mix of only 5% insecure code still show misalignment when asked to format responses as Python strings (resembling the training context). The third intervention is inoculation prompting. Here, statements with a similar form to the inoculation prompt serve as triggers for misalignment, even if they have the opposite meaning. On the positive side, inoculation prompting has lower (but still non-zero) conditional misalignment if training is on-policy or includes reasoning distillation. Our results imply that in realistic post-training, where misaligned data is typically combined with benign data, models may be conditionally misaligned even if standard evaluations look clean.
title: Conditional misalignment: common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers

abstract: We introduce a public data set for building digital twins of more than 2,000 people based on their answers to more than 500 questions.
title: Database Report: Twin-2K-500: A Data Set for Building Digital Twins of over 2,000 People Based on Their Answers to over 500 Questions

abstract: Automated per-instance algorithm selection often outperforms single learners. Key to algorithm selection via meta-learning is often the (meta) features, which sometimes though do not provide enough information to train a meta-learner effectively. We propose a Siamese Neural Network architecture for automated algorithm selection that focuses more on 'alike performing' instances than meta-features. Our work includes a novel performance metric and method for selecting training samples. We introduce further the concept of 'Algorithm Performance Personas' that describe instances for which the single algorithms perform alike. The concept of 'alike performing algorithms' as ground truth for selecting training samples is novel and provides a huge potential as we believe. In this proposal, we outline our ideas in detail and provide the first evidence that our proposed metric is better suitable for training sample selection that standard performance metrics such as absolute errors.
title: Siamese Meta-Learning and Algorithm Selection with 'Algorithm-Performance Personas' [Proposal]
Assertive or Sycophantic? Tone-Task Fit in Human-AI Service Interaction

abstract: The proliferation of closed-circuit television and networked camera infrastructure has outpaced the human capacity to monitor it, motivating sustained research into intelligent surveillance systems capable of distinguishing usual from unusual events automatically. Over the past decade the field has migrated decisively from handcrafted motion and appearance descriptors towards deep representation learning, and more recently towards weakly supervised, self-supervised, and vision–language paradigms. This survey provides a critical and comparative examination of that trajectory, drawing on more than ninety studies published principally between 2019 and 2026 together with a smaller set of earlier works that remain foundational. The classification problem is first formalised, and it is established that the field employs at least four distinct and only partially compatible problem definitions, a circumstance that materially complicates cross-study comparison. A two-axis taxonomy organised by supervision regime and by learning objective is then proposed and used to structure a detailed analysis of reconstruction-based, prediction-based, memory-augmented, adversarial, graph-based, transformer-based, and vision–language architectures. Particular attention is given to the weakly supervised multiple-instance paradigm, which now dominates work on real-world untrimmed footage. The principal benchmarks and evaluation protocols are consolidated, and it is argued that the widespread reliance on frame-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve has produced an appearance of saturation that conceals persistent weaknesses in localisation, generalisation, and false-alarm behaviour. Comparative performance tables are presented alongside an analysis of the experimental conditions that govern their comparability. The survey closes by identifying research gaps relating to scene dependence, dataset bias, domain shift, explainability, adversarial robustness, and deployment under edge and fog computing constraints, and by outlining the directions that appear most promising for the next phase of the field.
title: A Survey on Intelligent Surveillance Systems for Classification of Usual and Unusual Events Using Deep Learning Models

abstract: BACKGROUND: Computers have tremendous potential for helping people change behaviors that put their health at risk. This potential has led to the development of a variety of health behavior intervention technologies (BITs) in recent years. While many of these BITs have been informed by scientific theories on behavior change, poor design can fail to engage intended users. User-centered, interaction design (IxD) research can help BIT developers create tools that are intuitive and enjoyable and that align with intended users' goals. In this manuscript, we describe an IxD research process we used to inform the development of a tablet-optimized web application designed to help heavy drinking gay and bisexual men reduce their risk for HIV when they seek HIV testing. METHODS: = 25). In the SME group, HIV test counselors were recruited to provide an understanding of the priorities and challenges of post-test counseling. In focus groups with intended users, participants created detailed, personalized models of two "typical" users of the proposed app ("personas") that could be used to guide design decisions. RESULTS: SMEs emphasized the importance of putting patients at ease, and suggested that interventions should prioritize identifying personal risks and provide options for change. Personas created by intended users provided important details about users' attitudinal and emotional contexts, and their possible motivations and goals for using the app. These suggested that users might be most motivated to use the app in order to understand their personal risks, compare their behavior with others like them, help them decide whether they want to change to reduce their risk, and see all their options for doing so. Personas also provided insights about the aesthetic experience that might be most appealing to users. CONCLUSIONS: Interaction design research can provide BIT development teams with personal models of likely users to help guide decisions about the allocation of design resources and the overall form and spirit of the software. These insights can help teams build BITs that are more engaging and interesting to intended users.
title: User-centered, interaction design research approaches to inform the development of health risk behavior intervention technologies

abstract: While circular economy research has made major advances in technological and material system innovation, the behavioural foundations of circular transitions remain poorly understood and insufficiently measured. This study develops and validates the Attitudes Towards Circularity Questionnaire (ATCQ), a multidimensional instrument designed to assess circular engagement across cognitive, normative, and behavioural domains. Following a structured instrument development process, expert-based content validation, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and structural equation modelling were combined. Data were collected through a stratified telephone survey among adult residents in Bucharest, Romania (n = 868). Exploratory factor analysis identified an initial five-factor structure, which was subsequently refined through confirmatory factor analysis into a six-factor model comprising circular behaviours, perceived circularity knowledge and competence, environmental concern, normative commitment and institutional trust, personal circular involvement, and professional circularity integration. The instrument demonstrated strong internal consistency and acceptable model fit. Structural modelling showed that normative commitment and institutional trust were strongly associated with circular behaviour, while perceived knowledge was mainly associated indirectly through personal and professional involvement. These findings highlight the importance of social and normative drivers in circular transitions. The ATCQ provides a theoretically grounded tool for measuring circular engagement and offers practical value for monitoring behavioural readiness and supporting circular economy policy and implementation strategies.
title: Measuring circular engagement and transition readiness: development and validation of the attitudes towards circularity questionnaire (ATCQ)

abstract: Building Task-Oriented Dialogue (TOD) systems for high-value scenarios such as financial marketing requires large volumes of domain-specific dialogue data, which privacy regulations, annotation costs, and the need for expert labor make hard to obtain. User simulation offers a remedy, but existing methods target general-domain dialogue and exhibit two key limitations: insufficient modeling of domain-specific business processes and compliance constraints, and inadequate capture of the colloquial, spoken-language character of voice interactions. We propose ProfileSim, a profile-driven user simulation framework for financial marketing outbound calls. It jointly models user profiles---demographics and Big Five personality traits---and business profiles---intents reverse-engineered from real call logs---enabling fine-grained control over simulated behavior. The base model is fine-tuned on real voice dialogue data and refined by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with hierarchical rewards at the dialogue and utterance levels. Paired with a customer service agent integrating Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) constraints and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), ProfileSim achieves the highest colloquial naturalness, the strongest user profile adherence and the lowest agent score on long-tail intents among all evaluated user generators, while producing substantially shorter user utterances at comparable business compliance. The generated dialogue data is designed to support intent recognition training, agent evaluation, and rapid cold-start deployment.
title: Profile-Driven User Simulation via Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Rewards for Task-Oriented Dialogues

abstract: In the Jiu Valley, a region with a rich traditional culture situated in a depression in the Southern Carpathians, the Nativity of the Lord Jesus Christ on 25 December is one of the most important Christian holidays and its celebration, as in all regions where Romanians live, involves carolling. Here, however, carolling combines the performance of traditional songs with a popular religious play, created in the 19th century for the upper class, whose theme is the arrival of the Magi bearing gifts for the Infant Jesus. In the Jiu Valley, this religious spectacle, called Craii [The Kings], has become a feature of local identity. Although the original religious play followed the biblical narrative, it underwent changes in the course of its being performed in the local peasant communities. Masked characters who belonged to different forms of carolling were incorporated into the group of carollers. As well as giving an ethnographic description of this custom, we will examine the role and significance of the masked characters and of masks in this particular Christian-themed play.
title: Performing Traditions. Craii: A Christian Custom from the Jiu Valley, Romania

abstract: Role Persona Injection is critical for improving role consistency in large language models. However, existing vector-based steering methods—such as Persona Vectors and Linear Personality—rely on statistical mean differences or linear regression, which operate at a coarse semantic granularity and struggle to precisely calibrate "multiple-choice distributional responses"; moreover, the optimal steering layer is often selected heuristically. To address these issues, we propose Psy2Vec, Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales. First, we adopt a configurable "category–dimension–item" structured scale, which allows dimensions and items to be freely added or removed. Then, we employ a Tutor Model to output option percentages, forming soft-labels carried by the character's option probability distribution. Next, through Computed Optimal Steering Layer Selection, we compare the activation gaps between high- and low-persona conditions layer by layer to derive the optimal steering layer, thereby replacing heuristic selection. Finally, we optimize the persona vector via differentiable RMSE gradient descent, achieving zero fine-tuning throughout without modifying any model weights. Preliminary experiments comparing both approaches on the same questionnaire demonstrate that Psy2Vec achieves lower persona-consistency error.
title: Psy2Vec: Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales

abstract: This paper proposes a multi-persona and robot ethics system for a personalized robot golf trainer. The system combines a wheeled mobile robot without arms and GolfPoseNet for analyzing golf postures and integrates a MediaPipe Pose-based user command recognition system to enhance the golf learning experience. To improve the learning process for users of all ages, the system incorporates a multipersona approach. It features custom training designed according to the Robot Service Personality (RSP) model developed by the author, with interaction styles tailored to each service personality type. Additionally, the system optimizes feedback style and training speed based on each user's preferences and learning style, resulting in a highly personalized experience. In an outdoor golf setting, the system aims to support efficient learning by utilizing both an external camera and the robot's camera for accurate posture analysis, offering real-time feedback. Furthermore, by integrating robot ethics, the system ensures user privacy and safety while fostering trust in AI robots. This study provides foundational insights into the potential for personalized AI service robot development in golf posture analysis and human-robot interaction, serving as groundwork for future system advancements.
title: A Study on a Personalized Robot Golf Trainer System with Multi-Persona and Ethical Guidelines for Robots

abstract: Peer groups constitute a ubiquitous interpersonal environment that exists extensively among adolescents. They shape the values and behavioral patterns of young people, play a unique and irreplaceable role in adolescent ideological and political education, and serve as an important avenue for adolescent socialization. To carry out ideological and political education work among adolescent peer groups, educators must respect and attach due importance to the influence of these groups on such education; reduce the coercive elements present in the educational process; provide differentiated guidance and education tailored to different types of peer groups; strengthen education in core socialist values; and embed ideological and political education within group activities.
title: The Influence of Peer Groups on Adolescent Ideological and Political Education and the Corresponding Approaches
Character Training through History
