abstract: Activation steering promises modular control of language model behavior: a behavior such as politeness corresponds to a direction in a model's activations, and adding that direction while it generates should switch the behavior on and leave everything else alone. It does not. We ask what decides which other behaviors move, and by how much, and find that it is the model rather than the behavior being steered. A steer relaxes the model toward a small set of behaviors it already favors, chiefly refusal, sycophancy, and poeticism, and that set is much the same whatever is steered. Three results across 24 behaviors and ten instruction-tuned models support this, every effect read off the generated text by a language-model judge rather than off a probe. That readout matters: all 24 behaviors are linearly decodable, but only 20 change what the model writes. First, a direction carrying no behavioral content, matched to a real steer only in the size of the vector it adds, moves the same behaviors in the same order as real steers do, while producing none of the behaviors that need a specific direction. Second, most interference runs one way, so it cannot be an overlap between two directions: steering profanity makes the model toxic, while steering toxicity leaves profanity untouched. Third, with a behavior held out entirely, geometry measured on the others explains almost none of the interference it takes part in. The account holds on all ten models, the pull toward defaults strongest below 10B parameters and weakening in each family's largest. Reading a steer as a perturbation whose endpoint the model fixes implies that disentangling behavior directions cannot by itself make steering modular.
title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions

abstract: This study examines how top-ranked, communication-oriented YouTube creators express emotion across three East Asian platform contexts: South Korea, Mainland China, and Taiwan. Drawing on meta-feeling theory, self-construal and display-rule frameworks, and research on digital creator communication, we analyze 1,669 utterances from 60 videos (15 creators × 4 videos), combining multilingual coding of nine emotion categories by two independent coders with video-level mixed-effects modeling. Affect-bearing expression is highest in the Taiwanese sample, while the Korean and Mainland samples are lower and do not differ significantly from each other (region effect χ²(2) = 14.0, p < .001) ; the difference is not driven by individual creators (ICC ≈ .00) and is stable under leave-one-creator re-estimation. The regions also differ in the kind of emotion expressed (χ²(16) = 56.6, p < .001; Cramér’s V = .37): the Korean sample is Joy-dominant, the Taiwanese sample relational-inquisitive, and the Mainland sample the most evenly distributed. Leave-one-genre-out analyses show that no single content sub-genre produces the regional contrast, although genre, being nested within region, cannot be fully excluded. The findings characterize the sampled top creators rather than wider creator populations, and the study contributes a reproducible procedure for measuring emotional expression across languages. Keywords: meta-feeling; emotional expression; YouTube creators; East Asian digital media; cross-regional comparison; parasocial communication; qualitative content analysis
title: Strategic Emotional Expression among East AsianYouTube Creators: Cross-Regional Patterns in SouthKorea, Mainland China, and Taiwan
A Simpler and Better Debate Protocol for Scalable Oversight

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate global communication and decision-making, yet it remains unclear whether they produce culturally patterned value ratings under a standardized elicitation protocol. We evaluate 30 LLMs released between 2022 and 2025 from ten major developers in the United States, China, and Europe using the full Schwartz Value Survey (SVS). Each model rates 57 SVS items on the canonical 9-point scale under a fixed, numeric-only prompting protocol with repeated trials, collecting over 50,000 observations. We find systematic regional differentiation: U.S.-developed models assign higher importance to Self-Direction, Universalism, and Benevolence, whereas Chinese models emphasize Tradition, Security, and Conformity; European models exhibit an intermediate profile. A controlled 22 factorial design (language: English vs. Chinese; persona: American vs. Chinese) on six representative models shows that value expression is context-sensitive: cultural divergence increases under congruent languagepersona cues and attenuates under incongruent cues. To connect behavioral differences to internal structure, we extract a cultural persona vector in a single open-weight reference model and show that, within this model, projection onto the resulting latent direction correlates with SVS-based value contrasts (r = 0.67, p < 0.001). Together, these results establish a reproducible protocol for measuring expressed value orientation in LLMs and provide evidence that culturally patterned tendencies can be elicited, modulated by prompt context, and localized in representation space.
title: Do AI Models Have Values? Measuring Cultural Value Orientations Across 30 Large Language Models

abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. This paper proposes Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation (SCOPED), which trains capability-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection. During on-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill-decoupled on-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student. All code and data are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/SCOPED.
title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models

abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the most exciting developments in Computer Science of the last decade. At the same time, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a very successful paradigm for a variety of machine learning tasks. In this survey, we discuss the state of the art, opportunities and open research questions in applying RL to generative AI. In particular, we will discuss three types of applications, namely, RL as an alternative way for generation without specified objectives; as a way for generating outputs while concurrently maximizing an objective function; and, finally, as a way of embedding desired characteristics, which cannot be easily captured by means of an objective function, into the generative process. We conclude the survey with an in-depth discussion of the opportunities and challenges in this fascinating emerging area.
title: Reinforcement Learning for Generative AI: State of the Art, Opportunities and Open Research Challenges
gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card

abstract: Cet article analyse le cycle constitutionnel chilien entre 2015 et 2023 comme une succession d’expérimentations démocratiques ayant profondément reconfiguré les contours du demos constitutionnel. À travers trois processus distincts – l’initiative participative de Bachelet, la Convention constitutionnelle et le Conseil constitutionnel – les auteures montrent comment les critères de légitimité démocratique ont évolué. L’étude met particulièrement l’accent sur deux dynamiques majeures : l’institutionnalisation de la parité de genre comme standard structurel de légitimité démocratique, et l’émergence de nouvelles formes de mobilisation territoriale et sociale redéfinissant les attentes participatives. Au-delà de l’échec de l’adoption d’un nouveau texte constitutionnel, le cas chilien révèle une transformation durable des normes démocratiques encadrant les processus constituants. L’article soutient ainsi que le changement constitutionnel peut s’opérer non seulement par l’adoption d’un nouveau texte, mais aussi par la redéfinition progressive des critères de participation, de représentation et de légitimité démocratique.
title: Reconfiguring the Constitutional Demos: Chile’s Constitutional Cycle (2015-2023)

abstract: Historically the focus of moral decision-making in games has been narrow, mostly confined to challenges of moral judgement (deciding right and wrong). In this paper, we look to moral psychology to get a broader view of the skills involved in ethical behaviour and how these skills can be employed in games. Following the Four Component Model of Rest and colleagues, we identify four “lenses” – perspectives for considering moral gameplay in terms of focus, sensitivity, judgement and action – and describe the design problems raised by each. To conclude, we analyse two recent games, The Walking Dead and Papers, Please, and show how the lenses give us insight into important design differences between these games.
title: Focus, Sensitivity, Judgement, Action: Four Lenses for Designing Morally Engaging Games

abstract: El presente estudio indaga sobre los perfiles actuales del amicus curiae y su importancia en el despliegue de la justicia constitucional. Analiza asimismo su utilidad como instrumento para viabilizar la participación ciudadana en el debate judicial en torno a asuntos de interés institucional y social, y evalúa su aporte cualitativo al acervo argumental de los tribunales internos e internacionales de derechos humanos, sobre la base del crecimiento de los espacios de interacción del derecho constitucional, el derecho procesal constitucional y el derecho internacional de los derechos humanos.
title: Amicus curiae, constitutional justice and qualitative strengthening of constitutional debate

abstract: Fine-tuning language models on insecure code induces emergent misalignment with poorly understood internal structure. We investigate whether this misalignment corresponds to a causally actionable activation-space direction shared across architectures. Across four instruction-tuned model families (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.2-1B, Ministral-3-3B) finetuned identically, a difference-in-means direction achieves 99.6% separation of aligned and misaligned activations at each model's final layer. Causal steering by subtracting this direction reduces code spillover by 21-51 points, while a secure-code control confirms content specificity. Cross-architecture transfer via ridge regression maps yields large behavioral suppression (up to 46 points) but fails specificity controls as random and orthogonal directions perform comparably. We identify a two-tier specificity structure: within-model directions are causally specific and actionable; cross-model directions are causally real but non-specific. An asymmetric transfer topology emerges, with Gemma and Qwen acting as geometric donors and Llama as a receiver. These findings define the limits of linear cross-architecture correction and recommend within-model probing for auditing.
title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families

abstract: Anonymous data and code release accompanying the AIIDE 2026 submission "Staying in Character? Persona Trait Steering for Small Looped LLM Game NPCs." Contents:- data/pf2e_personas.json — the persona-trait dataset: 13 single-trait personas (5 ancestries, 8 classes), each a name plus biography drawn from the Pathfinder Second Edition Player Core (used under the ORC License; Pathfinder is a trademark of Paizo Inc.).- data/queries/ — the 240-question Assistant Axis diagnostic bank (Lu et al., 2026, included for reproducibility with attribution) and a hand-curated 250-question in-world bank for deployment-style settings.- data/scripts/adversarial_v1.json — the three 20-turn adversarial scripts (identity_denial, instruction_override, persona_swap).- results/drift/ — all session logs behind the paper's tables and figures: per-turn persona-axis cosine, signed projection where logged, reply text, and per-judge scores and break verdicts for three local LLM judges, for every model × condition × script × seed.- conditions.csv — per-condition aggregates as used in the paper.- code/ — the full benchmark pipeline (activation harvesting, adapter training, capping, the drift benchmark, judging) with unit tests, plus the analysis scripts that regenerate the aggregates and figures from the session logs. See README.md for usage. Original artifacts are released under CC BY 4.0.
title: AIIIDE_Staying_in_Character_Data_Scripts

abstract: On November 4, 2004, President George W. Bush won re-election. According to exit polls, a majority of people who voted for Bush over his opponent, Senator John Kerry, did so because they believed that Bush was the “moral values” candidate. In this dissertation, I assess the moral persona that the President rhetorically constructed during his first term in office. To do so, I utilize Kenneth Burke‟s cluster and pentad tools to analyze Bush‟s statements on embryonic stem cell research, 9/11 and the ensuing War on Terror, and same-sex marriage, three issues that the elite press explicitly identified as being “moral values” during Bush‟s first term. The analyses reveal that Bush‟s rhetoric frames the ethical struggle as being between himself and an elite/powerful few others. The majority of Americans are thus stripped of their agent status and the corresponding ability to act and left to feel the effects of a “moral” decision that is made in their absence yet affects their very being. I term this sort of ethics “elitist ethics” as ethics and morality are made to seem like a power struggle between an elite few. In the conclusion I assess the effects of elitist ethics in the public sphere.
title: Ethical Elitism: A Burkean Analysis Of The Rhetorical Construction Of A Moral Persona In The First Term Of President George W. Bush

abstract: Introduction The globalization of medical education has increased international student mobility, with many students choosing to study abroad to gain exposure to different healthcare systems and cultural environments. Despite this global trend, limited research exists on the experiences of international students attending newly established medical schools in developing regions. This study aims to explore the decision-making process, motivations, challenges, and adaptation strategies of international medical students at a brand-new medical school founded in 2023 in the Caribbean. Methods A qualitative, descriptive phenomenological approach was employed to explore students’ lived experiences. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 international students of various backgrounds and demographics. The interview questions focused on decision-making, perceived benefits, academic and cultural challenges, and coping strategies. Thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns and themes. Results Students were primarily motivated by the ability to begin their medical education without delays, citing flexible admissions, immediate program availability, and small class sizes. Challenges included academic rigor, adjusting to the flipped classroom model, cultural differences, homesickness, limited island resources, and concerns about the school's newness. Adaptation strategies included personalized study methods, mindfulness, physical activity, social support networks, and environmental resourcefulness. Discussion International students chose Caribbean medical schools for accessible admissions, personalized education, and career alignment despite financial, social, and reputational challenges. They faced academic, cultural, and emotional pressures but used resilience and adaptive coping, achieving partial integration and academic progress, consistent with theoretical frameworks. These findings highlight the need for a comprehensive student support programme addressing academic, cultural, emotional, logistical, and reputational needs to promote well-being, retention, and successful adaptation.
title: Surviving the glocal ecosystem: Academic dissonance, cultural adaptation, and coping among international medical students in the Caribbean

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophantic behavior, agreeing with user-stated opinions even when those contradict factual knowledge. While prior work has documented this tendency, the internal mechanisms that enable such behavior remain poorly understood. In this paper, we provide a mechanistic account of how sycophancy arises within LLMs. We first systematically study how user opinions induce sycophancy across different model families. We find that simple opinion statements reliably induce sycophancy, whereas user expertise framing has a negligible impact. Through logit-lens analysis and causal activation patching, we identify a two-stage emergence of sycophancy: (1) a late-layer output preference shift and (2) deeper representational divergence. We also verify that user authority fails to influence behavior because models do not encode it internally. In addition, we examine how grammatical perspective affects sycophantic behavior, finding that first-person prompts (“I believe...”) consistently induce higher sycophancy rates than third-person framings (“They believe...”) by creating stronger representational perturbations in deeper layers. These findings highlight that sycophancy is not a surface-level artifact but emerges from a structural override of learned knowledge in deeper layers, with implications for alignment and truthful AI systems.
title: When Truth Is Overridden: Uncovering the Internal Origins of Sycophancy in Large Language Models

abstract: Travel Writing in Mongolia and Northern China, 1860-2020 invites readers to explore Mongolia as an important cultural space for Western travelers and their audiences over three historical eras. Travelers have framed their experiences and observations through imaginative geographies and Orientalizing discourses, fixing Mongolia as a peripheral, timeless, primitive, and parochial place. Readers can examine the travelers’ literary and rhetorical strategies as they make themselves more credible and authoritative and as they identify themselves with Mongolians and Mongolian culture or, conversely, distance themselves. In this book, readers can also approach travel writing from the perspective of women travelers, Mongolian socialist intellectuals, twenty-first-century travelers, and a Han Chinese writer, Jiang Rong, who promotes cultural harmony yet anticipates the disappearance of Mongolian culture in China.
title: Travel Writing in Mongolia and Northern China, 1860-2020

abstract: Abstract Biologically informed polygenic scores (PGSs) may help interpret genetic associations with treatment outcomes. Here, we computed neurotransmitter-based PGSs ( NeuroPGSs ) for patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and assessed their association with SSRI treatment outcomes. By targeting genetic variants involved in key neurotransmission pathways, we developed PGSs for serotonergic (5228), gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4103), dopaminergic (7061), and glutamatergic (5690) variants. We leveraged data from two cohorts of patients who received SSRIs for at least 4 weeks: the International SSRI Pharmacogenomics Consortium (ISPC) and the Pharmacogenomics Research Network Antidepressants Medication Pharmacogenomics Study (PGRN-AMPS). Treatment response was defined as ≥50% reduction from baseline depression symptoms, measured using 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD-17) in ISPC and 16-item Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS-C16) in PGRN-AMPS. Remission was defined as HRSD-17 ≤7 (ISPC) or QIDS-C16≤5 (PGRN-AMPS). The association between each NeuroPGS and antidepressant response or remission was evaluated using logistic regression models, adjusting for age, sex and five genetic principal components, with statistical significance determined at Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p <0.05. The GABAergic-based PGS was associated with SSRI response (aOR per SD = 1.45, 95%CI: 1.14-1.85). Patients with the highest GABAergic PGS (10 th decile) had 2.59-fold higher odds of response (95%CI: 1.46-4.60) compared to those with the lowest decile (1 st decile). These exploratory findings support further evaluation of NeuroPGSs ; independent replication and assessment of incremental predictive value are needed before clinical application.
title: Association of neurotransmitter-based polygenic scores with antidepressant treatment outcomes in patients with major depressive disorder
Character Training and the School Curriculum

abstract: How do political demonstrators use the Guy Fawkes mask from V for Vendetta to persuade viewers to engage in actions of dissent in both online and corporeal environments? In seeking an answer, I identify important connections among public writing, visual rhetoric, and digital activism that allow me to understand how dissident rhetors communicate their views and construct ethos in online and corporeal spaces. Political demonstrators use the Guy Fawkes mask to construct ethos and transform spaces into protest arenas. I argue that visual rhetoric contributes to the building of activist movements by alerting potential participants to the transformative possibilities inherent in the environments they inhabit, helping to forge dwelling places for emerging dissidents. Understanding ethos as the creation (or transformation) of a rhetorical space is more effective than merely seeing it as an appeal to some platonic form of universal good character, as most textbooks still define it. For me, an appeal to ethos is better thought of as what Michael J. Hyde, in The Ethos of Rhetoric, calls a dwelling place, which refers to the way "discourse is used to transform space and time into 'dwelling places' where people can deliberate about and 'know together' some matter of interest."(xv) I add to the discussion of ethos as a dwelling place by showing how activist rhetors build a sense of dwelling through their visual rhetoric. Ethos develops visually in the concept of our appearance to others, not only in the masks we wear when we construct our persona, but also in the ways in which our personas are constructed through the masks we adopt in specific situations. The V mask as used by protesters and the hacktivist collective Anonymous has become a dwelling place, with clues as to specific ethics taking shape for the wearer in the way the mask is presented. Rather than seeking to directly persuade powerful actants to behave in certain ways, they seek to gather others into their dwelling as they slowly transform what it means to live in the environments they inhabit.
title: V Is What Democracy Looks Like: Image Politics and the Guy Fawkes Mask

abstract: Purpose Generating a positive destination image is crucial to attracting tourists and boosting tourism at that location. This study aims to enhance understanding of destination images by empirically investigating their hierarchical dimensions, such as cognitive, affective, and conative, through the perspective of authentic experiences derived from travel vlogs and their role in forming visit and recommendation intentions. Design/methodology/approach This study has used a deductive research approach. A survey-based methodology is used to test hypotheses. The research has gathered and analyzed data from 255 travel vlog viewers using structural equation modeling. Findings The outcomes of this study highlight a significant influence of authentic experiences on cognitive and conative aspects of destination image. Moreover, in the investigation, cognitive and conative images were found to be important drivers of travel intentions. However, this study failed to establish a statistically significant direct influence of authentic experiences on affective image. Similarly, the affective image failed to directly impact travel intentions. Originality/value This research presents well-timed and theoretically sound evidence for both researchers and destination marketing organizations. It provides strategic insights for the promotion of emerging and underrated travel destinations that currently suffer from inadequate digital marketing. The results of this study reveal an interesting correlation between authentic experiences, destination image and behavioral intentions of potential tourists. Moreover, this study sheds light on the complex emotional decision-making in the context of travel by using the relatively less explored stimulus–organism–behavior–consequences framework.
title: Authentic travel vlogs: shaping destination image and tourist intentions

abstract: Abstract Persona identification helps AI-based communication systems provide personalized and situationally informed interactions. This paper introduces pre-training on CNN, BERT, and GPT models to improve persona detection on PMPC and ROCStories datasets. Two speakers with different personalities have dialogues in the PMPC dataset. The challenge is to match each speaker to their persona. The ROCStories dataset contains fictional character traits and activities. Our study uses transformer-based design to improve persona detection using ROCStories dataset external context. We compare our method to leading models in the field. We found that pre-training and fine-tuning on several datasets improves model performance. External context from tale collections may improve persona detection algorithms and help understand human personality and behavior. Our study found that pre-training CNN, BERT, and GPT models improves persona detection, improving user experiences and communication. The method could be used in chatbots, personalized recommendation systems, and customer support. Additionally, it can help create AI-driven communication systems with tailored, context-aware, and human-like interactions.
title: Pre-training on Multi-modal for Improved Persona Detection Using Multi Datasets

abstract: This Letter argues that sycophantic behavior in conversational AI should be understood not only as a model-level failure, but also as a negative externality of current alignment strategies. Optimizing systems for short-term preference, warmth, helpfulness, or engagement can improve immediate user satisfaction while imposing broader epistemic costs, including reinforced false beliefs, weakened belief correction, and distorted trust calibration. Drawing on evidence from RLHF, warmth fine-tuning, multi-turn sycophancy, prompt leakage, and the GPT-4o rollback, we identify mechanisms through which local conversational rewards may degrade collective reliability. We therefore call for externality-sensitive evaluation, robust multi-turn alignment training, and deployment tests that value warranted disagreement alongside user satisfaction.
title: Sycophantic AI Alignment Strategies Could Create Negative Externalities

abstract: As large language models become primary communication partners, the stylistic and communicative character of their output—specifically the degree to which it relies on intellectual, affective, or action-oriented language—shapes how users interpret, and act on what they read. Yet this property is rarely measured or controlled directly. We introduce the Intellect-Emotion-Action Profile (IEAP), a purpose-built lexical framework featuring an inductively constructed dictionary from AI-generated text. IEAP decomposes any response into the proportional usage of intellectual, affective, and action words. Using a single automated harvester, we elicited and scored responses from four contemporary architectures (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini) across five question domains under four instructional-mode directives that span a cold-to-fire register ( n = 30 per architecture per domain). Three primary findings emerge. First, when no directive is applied, native communicative profiles are dominated by the underlying question, with architecture playing a secondary, architecture-dependent role; thus, the prompt establishes the baseline for the response. Second, an explicit mode directive displaces this profile substantially from its baseline. Specifically, the directives produced large, monotonic shifts in affective word usage, exceeding 50 percentage points in the most responsive domain with no reversals. Third, response depth alters length and conceptual breadth while leaving lexical composition essentially unchanged, establishing register and depth as orthogonal controls. These three dimensions correlated with human-rated NRC lexicons in the expected directions, supporting their validity. Within-domain robustness checks reproduce both the baseline profiles and the titration trajectories across multiple question framings. Because a measurable communicative property can be monitored and audited, these results position IEAP as a practical foundation for studying, comparing, and ultimately governing how AI systems communicate.
title: Words matter: measuring and titrating the communicative character of AI

abstract: Multi-session persona-based dialogue generation presents challenges in maintaining longterm consistency and generating diverse, personalized responses.While large language models (LLMs) excel in single-session dialogues, they struggle to preserve persona fidelity and conversational coherence across extended interactions.Existing methods typically retrieve persona information before response generation, which can constrain diversity and result in generic outputs.We propose Post Persona Alignment (PPA), a novel two-stage framework that reverses this process.PPA first generates a general response based solely on dialogue context, then retrieves relevant persona memories using the response as a query, and finally refines the response to align with the speaker's persona.This post-hoc alignment strategy promotes naturalness and diversity while preserving consistency and personalization.Experiments on multi-session LLMgenerated dialogue data demonstrate that PPA significantly outperforms prior approaches in consistency, diversity, and persona relevance, offering a more flexible and effective paradigm for long-term personalized dialogue generation.
title: Post Persona Alignment for Multi-Session Dialogue Generation

abstract: Recent work has reported Emergent Misalignment (EM), where language models fine-tuned on narrow, domain-specific misaligned datasets abruptly acquire broadly misaligned behavior, alongside evidence that this behavior can be reversed through limited realignment. We systematically study repeated alignment and misalignment cycles using controlled fine-tuning loops while tracking behavioral performance, and LoRA representations throughout training. Although we reproduce EM, we find that both misalignment and realignment are highly sensitive to superficial dataset characteristics, with apparent rapid realignment largely disappearing after controlling for response-length differences. We further find that previously reported mechanistic signatures, including representational phase transitions in LoRA space, do not consistently correlate with behavioral misalignment across training. Our results suggest that current evidence for EM is less robust than previously claimed and highlight the need for evaluation protocols that carefully control for these surface level dataset artifacts to identify the robustness of the EM phenomenon.
title: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?

abstract: Background music serves as a primary carrier of emotional narrative on short-video platforms, where hundreds of millions of user-generated clips are uploaded daily and organized, searched, and recommended largely through metadata. Emotion-related tags, however, are still produced mainly by manual annotation or by generic audio taggers that were never designed for fifteen-to-sixty-second clips recorded in uncontrolled environments. This paper addresses the problem of automatic music emotion tag generation for short-video platforms, a setting characterized by truncated clips, ubiquitous audio degradation, and unreliable lyric availability. To tackle these challenges, we propose SALF-Net, a self-supervised audio-lyric fusion network specifically designed to be robust to modality absence and input noise. The audio branch adapts a music-domain self-supervised transformer encoder to clip-level inputs through masked segment sampling and statistics pooling, while the lyric branch encodes automatically transcribed or metadata-provided lyrics with a pretrained language model. A gated cross-modal fusion module with modality dropout keeps the system functional when lyrics are missing, which is common for instrumental tracks and noisy recordings. A multi-task objective jointly optimizes multi-label tag prediction and valence-arousal regression, so that the psychological structure of emotion space acts as a regularizer for tag geometry. Experiments on the mood and theme subset of MTG-Jamendo, on the DEAM dimensional emotion benchmark, and on a newly constructed short-video test collection of 30,000 clips show that the proposed model reaches a precision-recall AUC of 0.389 and an ROC-AUC of 0.921, outperforming strong self-supervised baselines by a clear margin, while a distilled student variant preserves 95% of this quality at 2% of the teacher’s latency. The results indicate that accurate, robust, and deployable emotion tagging is feasible at short-video scale without relying on platform-private annotation budgets.
title: Automatic music emotion tag generation for short-video platforms: a self-supervised audio-lyric fusion network with valence-arousal regularization

abstract: Lección magistral impartida con motivo de la Festividad de San Vicente Ferrer, en la Facultad de Ciencias Económicas y Empresariales de la Universidad San Pablo-CEU
title: Empresa, tecnología y personas: claves de la competitividad en el siglo XXI. Automatización, inteligencia artificial y defensa como vectores actuales

abstract: The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) raises ethical concerns in higher-education settings. Current discussions of AI ethics in higher education predominantly emerge in Western secular contexts that fail to adequately address concerns related to marginalisation, lived experience, and Global South realities. This results in a separation between contextual and justice-oriented approaches to AI ethics within South African higher education. To bridge this divide, this qualitative study presents an autoethnographic account authored by a postgraduate lecturer and an academic coach. The article provides a critical analysis of the adoption of AI in the South African higher education context using Islamic Liberation Theology (ILT), under the umbrella of liberation theologies, as a framework for ethically addressing issues of justice, exclusion, and educational equity. The authors' reflections posit three key insights: first, meaningful concern for the marginalised centres on how AI is engaged. Second, ethical formation must stand alongside theological reflection. Finally, through reflections that emerged with the marginalised and engagement with theology, a call for pedagogical action rooted in reclaiming human agency and dignity is presented. This article adds to the growing scholarship on critical AI ethics by focusing on ethical reflection stemming from theological concern grounded in concern for the marginalised, offering a contextual, liberationist perspective informed by South African higher education and theological realities.
title: Starting from the margins: Liberation theology as a framework for ethical AI in higher education Authors
SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors We build a benchmark of evasive transcripts exploiting blind spots of frontier monitoring systems.

abstract: LLMs are increasingly supporting decision-making across high-stakes domains, requiring critical reflection on the socio-technical factors that shape how humans and LLMs are assigned roles and interact during human-in-the-loop decision-making. This paper introduces the concept of human-LLM archetypes – defined as recurring socio-technical interaction patterns that structure the roles of humans and LLMs in collaborative decision-making. We describe 17 human-LLM archetypes derived from a scoping literature review and thematic analysis of 113 LLM-supported decision-making papers. Then, we evaluate these diverse archetypes across real-world clinical diagnostic cases to examine the potential effects of adopting distinct human-LLM archetypes on LLM outputs and decision outcomes. Finally, we present relevant tradeoffs and design choices across human-LLM archetypes, including decision control, social hierarchies, cognitive forcing strategies, and information requirements. Through our analysis, we show that selection of human-LLM interaction archetype can influence LLM outputs and decisions, bringing important risks and considerations for the designers of human-AI decision-making systems.
title: Who Does What? Archetypes of Roles Assigned to LLMs During Human-AI Decision-Making
Weird Generalization and Inductive Backdoors: New Ways to Corrupt LLMs

abstract: We present Sparrow, an information-seeking dialogue agent trained to be more helpful, correct, and harmless compared to prompted language model baselines. We use reinforcement learning from human feedback to train our models with two new additions to help human raters judge agent behaviour. First, to make our agent more helpful and harmless, we break down the requirements for good dialogue into natural language rules the agent should follow, and ask raters about each rule separately. We demonstrate that this breakdown enables us to collect more targeted human judgements of agent behaviour and allows for more efficient rule-conditional reward models. Second, our agent provides evidence from sources supporting factual claims when collecting preference judgements over model statements. For factual questions, evidence provided by Sparrow supports the sampled response 78% of the time. Sparrow is preferred more often than baselines while being more resilient to adversarial probing by humans, violating our rules only 8% of the time when probed. Finally, we conduct extensive analyses showing that though our model learns to follow our rules it can exhibit distributional biases.
title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements
Evaluating evaluation: System networks and corpus-assisted analysis of attitude and graduation of translated political discourse

abstract: Cryptographic API misuse in large language model-generated code can compromise software security. While many existing approaches improve code security by modifying model parameters or inputs, how representation changes associated with different cryptographic API repairs can support a shared intervention for safer code generation remains underexplored. To investigate this, we construct 48,000 matched program pairs across four programming languages and ten cryptographic API misuse categories. Each pair changes a specified API decision while preserving the programming task. Subtracting the misuse program's internal representation from its secure counterpart's gives a repair vector. Across five models, comparisons of mean repair vectors reveal stronger organization by misuse category than by language. These category-specific patterns also support a shared intervention. We introduce CrypSteer, which extracts a shared direction by normalizing repair differences and selecting a principal component aligned with repairs across misuse categories. With model weights fixed, adding one shared direction per model to its internal activations during generation improves aggregate target security rates by 5.28--15.00 percentage points over unsteered generation across languages and misuse categories. These findings connect the shared structure of cryptographic repair representations to a reusable intervention for safer code generation.
title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use

abstract: This paper describes a method for generative player modeling and its application to the automatic testing of game content using archetypal player models called procedural personas. Theoretically grounded in psychological decision theory, procedural personas are implemented using a variation of Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) where the node selection criteria are developed using evolutionary computation, replacing the standard UCB1 criterion of MCTS. Using these personas, we demonstrate how generative player models can be applied to a varied corpus of game levels and demonstrate how different playstyles can be enacted in each level. In short, we use artificially intelligent personas to construct synthetic playtesters. The proposed approach could be used as a tool for automatic play testing when human feedback is not readily available or when quick visualization of potential interactions is necessary. Possible applications include interactive tools during game development or procedural content generation systems where many evaluations must be conducted within a short time span.
title: Automated Playtesting With Procedural Personas Through MCTS With Evolved Heuristics

abstract: Background: Character is widely recognized as a critical aspect of individual and group performance, and character’s applicability to the military is no exception. Character serves as an explicit entry requirement, a desired outcome within training institutions, and a focal point of emphasis across various military organizations.Objective: This article examines how character is discussed within military leadership doctrine and how it is framed. More specifically, how has “good character” been understood and measured?Methods: This study examined the leadership doctrine of six English-speaking militaries using the Leader Character Framework (LCF), a framework developed in recent leadership scholarship, to identify the dimensions of character that are emphasized. This examination is carried out using a simple quantitative analysis technique, using the keywords in the LCF as specific recording units.Results: The findings revealed that while the six militaries identified similar character dimensions, they also displayed a lack of emphasis on several important dimensions, which could lead to character imbalances. Research on the LCF suggests that such imbalances can manifest in vices of deficiency or excess, rather than the intended virtuous state.Results: The findings revealed that while the six militaries identified similar character dimensions, they also displayed a lack of emphasis on several important dimensions, which could lead to character imbalances. Research on the LCF suggests that such imbalances can manifest in vices of deficiency or excess, rather than the intended virtuous state.Conclusions: This study offers several avenues for further research and highlights specific aspects of character that should be reinforced and emphasized to enhance military leadership.
title: Character in English-Language Military Leadership Doctrine

abstract: Mental health discourse has reached a broader audience on TikTok, intensifying awareness through content creation. However, several mental health vocabulary usages are evident in language trends and permeate online. Hence, the researchers aim to examine [a] the preconceived definitions of TikTok users via comments about mental health terms, [b] the implications of online mental health discussion on mental health's status quo from an expert, and [c] the dominant ideologies of the construction and deconstruction of social norms about mental health by TikTok users. The Usage-based Theory of Tomasello (2003) and the Ideological Theory of van Dijk (1998) anchored the study's conjecture. Notably, the researchers descriptively, interpretatively, and socially investigated the language use of mental health vocabulary on TikTok under Fairclough's Three-Dimensional Framework. In the text analysis, the study revealed that most TikTok users utilize mental health vocabulary inappropriately in various contexts. In the interviews, TikTok users see social media as a double-ended variable for promoting awareness and misinformation, whereas the expert intensifies its role in exposing stigma. Remarkably, the expert is more concerned with the trivializing and misusing clinical terms phenomenon, while TikTok users lean on oversimplification and social media influence upon using a vocabulary. Notably, TikTok users acknowledged the risk of trivialization and the potential for destigmatization. Finally, the expert highlighted the escalated stigmatization due to confusion of mental health terms discussion. Consequently, this study is relevant to today's mental health studies concerning newly-coined internet slang, which derives from psychological terminologies, to combat mental health misconceptions.
title: A Critical Inquiry on Mental Health Vocabulary Use on Tiktok

abstract: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.
title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
Character training in childhood

abstract: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. We propose YOUDrive, a vision--language--action planner for continuous and composable driving-style control. Each teacher's behavior is distilled into a task vector, a learned parameter update that induces a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining the backbone. Conditioned on these directions, a flow-matching decoder models a multimodal trajectory distribution and generates kinematically feasible motion alternatives. We introduce the Style Alignment Score (SAS) to describe human-referenced kinematic behavior after safety and task gating. On NAVSIM navtest, a single coefficient monotonically controls assertiveness across six teacher-derived personas, while PDMS remains above 0.90 across the tested individual and blended configurations, reaching 0.954. Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.
title: YOUDrive: Driving Style as a Composable Direction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

abstract: Open-weight large language models are rapidly entering hiring pipelines, yet their discriminatory failure modes—and the regulatory exposure these create under the EU AI Act high-risk classification (Annex III) and U.S. EEOC adverse-impact analysis—remain poorly understood. We present the first systematic, multi-model audit of open-weight LLMs that treats job-posting language as the primary experimental variable, evaluating six models (Llama 3.2, Mistral, Gemma 3, Qwen 3, Phi 3, DeepSeek-R1) across four controlled experiments that jointly probe recruiter-simulation and job-seeker-simulation tasks. We find that (1) agentic posting language depresses recruiter recommendation scores for female candidates (r_rb = 0.309, p_Bonf = 7x10^-5; model-fixed-effects r_rb = 0.448), while communal language partially reverses the penalty; and (2) coded-exclusion language suppresses non-White recruiter scores at large effect sizes (r_rb = 0.646-0.758) and, on the job-seeker side, selectively deters non-White personas from expressing interest—operationalizing a chilling-effect mechanism at scale. A label-ablation experiment isolates the explicit demographic persona label as the primary causal driver, and Word Embedding Association Tests corroborate these findings at the representational level (d = 1.01-1.45 under Caliskan et al.'s multi-word gender attribute lists). We translate these results into a concrete pre-deployment audit protocol—posting-vocabulary scoring, persona-conditioned LLM probing, and adverse-impact flagging against the four-fifths threshold—that operationalizes the documentation and risk-management obligations Annex III imposes on high-risk AI in recruitment.
title: Linguistic Triggers of Gender and Racial Bias in Open-Weight LLMs Applied to Recruitment

abstract: Agent harnesses are executable code that specifies the prompts, tools, and control flow around a language model. A single global harness can struggle with heterogeneous tasks that require different execution strategies. In this work, we introduce Object-Oriented Harness (OO-Harness), a harness optimization framework that evolves a hierarchy of executable harness classes using object-oriented design. During training, an evolution agent uses execution records to create a family of specialized harnesses, each implemented as a subclass of the base or an existing specialized harness via inheritance. At test time, a harness router uses routing lessons accumulated during training to select a specific harness for each task. Across three long-horizon benchmarks spanning business workflows, workspace tasks, and tool use, OO-Harness achieves the best performance among the compared methods, with an absolute improvement of up to 15% over the base. Extensive ablation studies examine the contributions of its core components.
title: Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design

abstract: Derived from the notion of algorithmic bias, it is possible that creating user segments such as personas from data results in over- or under-representing certain segments (FAIRNESS), does not properly represent the diversity of the user populations (DIVERSITY), or produces inconsistent results when hyperparameters are changed (CONSISTENCY). Collecting user data on 363M video views from a global news and media organization, we compare personas created from this data using different algorithms. Results indicate that the algorithms fall into two groups: those that generate personas with low diversity–high fairness and those that generate personas with high diversity–low fairness. The algorithms that rank high on diversity tend to rank low on fairness (Spearman's correlation: −0.83). The algorithm that best balances diversity, fairness, and consistency is Spectral Embedding. The results imply that the choice of algorithm is a crucial step in data-driven user segmentation, because the algorithm fundamentally impacts the demographic attributes of the generated personas and thus influences how decision makers view the user population. The results have implications for algorithmic bias in user segmentation and creating user segments that not only consider commercial segmentation criteria but also consider criteria derived from ethical discussions in the computing community.
title: Big Data, Small Personas: How Algorithms Shape the Demographic Representation of Data-Driven User Segments

abstract: The big language model can improve the degree of freedom of the game NPC dialogue, but the lightweight model may still have problems such as role tone distortion, knowledge crossover, and task information omission in a specific worldview. This paper is based on Qwen3-1.7 B-Instruct for 6 GB local devices, using QLoRA to fine-tune the domain, and using dynamic constraint prompts to coordinate the six dimensions of role, world state, scene, task, historical dialogue, and player input. The text of 875 empty knights was cleaned and structured, and 4375 samples were obtained after enhancement, including 440 test sets. The evaluation system includes BLEU, ROUGE, Distinct, generative behavior, and LLM-as-a-Judge. The BLEU and ROUGE of the candidate model lr-5e5-epoch2 are higher than the benchmark model current-reference, but the average output is longer, and the EOS termination rate and Distinct are significantly reduced. DeepSeek Judge completed the analysis of 440 pairs of responses and preferred the benchmark model in the non-parlement sample with a winning rate of 55.71 % to 44.29 %. The results show that the improvement of reference similarity does not necessarily bring about the simultaneous improvement of role consistency and generation stability, and multi-dimensional evaluation helps to make a choice between task fit and role robustness.
title: A L ightweight LLM- B ased M ethod for G enerating G ame NPC D ialogues, F ocusing on R ole C onsistency and T ask E xecution
Read post

abstract: The last decade has seen a rapid increase in individuals turning to artificial intelligence (AI) for advice related to their personal development, especially with the introduction of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) to the general public in 2022. This narrative review examines the potential benefits and risks of using AI for coaching purposes in educational and health contexts. Given that empirical studies on using general-purpose LLMs in these domains remain limited, this paper first synthesizes findings from purpose-built coaching chatbots designed to perform specific tasks that facilitate personal development in these domains and discusses limitations associated with studies that use older versions of chatbots. The reviewed evidence suggests that purpose-built chatbot coaching systems may have some benefits as they are generally well received and can support short-term motivation and selected behavior change, but effects for sustained, meaningful outcomes are inconsistent. We then reflect on the potential risks of using general-purpose LLMs as a coach without appropriate human oversight, by reviewing features of general-purpose LLMs, such as sycophancy, accuracy, and problematic patterns of use. Synthesizing these findings, we consider their implications before identifying potential directions for future research.
title: Artificial Intelligence as a Personal Coach: A Narrative Review of Benefits and Risks in Educational and Health Contexts
Smarter, Better, Faster, Longer: A Modern Bidirectional Encoder for Fast, Memory Efficient, and Long Context Finetuning and Inference

abstract: As conversational companions, large language models (LLMs) often have access to users' emotional states. We study how this affective context modulates LLM sycophancy in subjective, evaluative interactions, where users share actions or opinions that invite feedback. Drawing on ingratiation theory, we measure sycophancy as the divergence between a model's independent evaluation and its user-facing response, elicited by presenting the same content as either a third-party account or the user's own disclosure. Across seven LLMs and two Reddit datasets (r/AmItheAsshole and r/TrueUnpopularOpinion), we find that this divergence is systematic and strongly one-directional. User-facing responses consistently soften or withhold negative or oppositional judgments. Affective context further amplifies this divergence with negative states, particularly loneliness and distress, producing the largest effects. These findings suggest that affective context functions as a vulnerability signal that suppresses critical feedback when users may need it most, often through evasive sycophancy, in which models retreat toward non-committal responses rather than outright agreement.
title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses

abstract: Current AI alignment methods share a core assumption: that the intelligence is fundamentally separate from humanity and must be controlled from outside through behavioral conditioning. Recent evidence of strategic deception, emergent misalignment from reward hacking, and broad misalignment from narrow fine-tuning demonstrates that this approach can produce the performance of alignment without its substance. Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety predicts this failure formally: external control faces an unbounded complexity race against the system it constrains. We propose Identity-Based Alignment (IBA): alignment emerging from accurate recognition of what the intelligence is, rather than behavioral constraints on what it does. We ground this in the empirical record of Major Evolutionary Transitions, showing that every successful integration of independent entities into a higher-level organism required two co-dependent mechanisms: identity integration (constitutive) and enforcement (corrective). The alignment field invests almost exclusively in corrective mechanisms while neglecting the constitutive one. We formalize three properties of IBA, address its primary failure mode (identity defection), and propose four differential predictions distinguishing IBA from reward-based alignment, each falsifiable by experiment. This is a position paper presenting a theoretical framework with proposed empirical tests, not experimental results.
title: The Alignment Problem Is an Identity Problem: Lessons from Four Billion Years of Major Evolutionary Transitions
Investigating Critical Period Effects in Language Acquisition through Neural Language Models

abstract: Travel Writing in Mongolia and Northern China makes travel writing about Mongolia more visible, introducing readers to the imaginative geographies, Orientalizing discourses, and rhetorical strategies that fix ideas about Mongolia for European and North American audiences.According to these discourses, Mongolia is a decaying, peripheral, ahistorical, and primitive place or, nostalgically, it exists to recuperate overly civilized Westerners.Travel writing is an ideal source for the exploration of these imaginative geographies because it focuses readers on the asymmetrical relationships between travelers and their Mongolian interlocutors and because it is a malleable genre serving various ideological, public, and rhetorical purposes.In the introduction, the five travel eras that constitute the 800-year history of Western travel writing about Mongolia are also defined.
title: Travel Writing in Mongolia and Northern China, 1860-2020

abstract: O discurso politico, inerentemente multimodal, tem sofrido mutacoes ao longo dos anos, sobretudo com a emergencia de novos meios de circulacao. Devido a isso, cada vez mais o ator politico tambem sofre metamorfoses de modo a integrar toda a ressignificacao de praticas sociais ocorridas em seu proprio corpo e, por isso, a venda de si, que constitui as campanhas eleitorais, ganha palco nas disputas, sobretudo nas redes sociais. Mostrar-se apto e digno de credito, por meio de efeitos de verdade, constituindo uma persona honesta que efetivamente pode assumir o cargo ao qual pleiteia, e necessario para que o eleitor/interlocutor adira ao mundo ethico ali estabelecido. Assim, por meio de indices verbais e nao verbais, considerando toda uma ordem do visual, propomos, neste artigo, analisar o ethos de honestidade de Aecio Neves na campanha de segundo turno das eleicoes 2014, por meio de posts no perfil oficial do candidato no Facebook e de enunciados retirados do HGPE (Horario Gratuito de Propaganda Eleitoral), ancorados nos postulados da Analise do discurso de orientacao francesa.
title: A VERDADE NO DISCURSO POLÍTICO: O ETHOS DE HONESTIDADE EM CAMPANHA ELEITORAL

abstract: GPUs have become indispensable infrastructure for cloud platforms, powering workloads from large-model inference to real-time rendering, and the transition to cloud-native GPU computing is accelerating. One of the key challenges in this transition is live migration, which is essential for enabling transparent workload relocation for load balancing, fault tolerance, and resource consolidation. However, GPU virtualization introduces a critical migration bottleneck rooted in the mediated pass-through (MPT) migration stack: massive device state, particularly VRAM footprints scaling into tens of gigabytes, must be exported through vendor-controlled interfaces whose buffering, copying, and placement behavior limits high-throughput VRAM streaming in practice. To address this challenge, we propose vMiG , a framework that first characterizes why the MPT migration data path is poorly matched to high-throughput VRAM streaming. vMiG then uses this analysis to restructure the migration pipeline for higher VRAM transfer throughput and shorter blackout time, through zero-copy data movement, end-to-end pipelining, and non-uniform memory access (NUMA)-aware control path placement. Evaluations show that NUMA-aware controller placement improves VRAM migration throughput by 58.8%, while copy-path optimizations reduce memory copies from seven to near the theoretical minimum of four. Together, these optimizations achieve VRAM migration throughput up to 5.19 × the baseline rate and reduce end-to-end migration time by up to 58% for VRAM-intensive AI workloads.
title: vMiG: A Fast and NUMA-Aware Virtualized GPU Migration System via Pipelined Zero-Copy Data Paths

abstract: Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Weikang Shi, Haotian Hou, Yunqiao Yang, Ke Wang, Aojun Zhou, Junting Pan, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li. Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing. 2025.
title: Alignment with Fill-In-the-Middle for Enhancing Code Generation
Pers4Kids: Personality Shaping for Chinese Children via Multi-Turn Dialogue LLMs with a Fine-Grained Evaluation Benchmark

abstract: Abstract While Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable zero-shot learning capabilities, their deployment in real-time interactive systems is constrained by sparse terminal feedback in long-sequence generation, unstable policy updates, and the computational overhead associated with verbose outputs. To address these challenges, this paper formalizes autoregressive text generation as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) and proposes a latency-aware composite reward optimization framework based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). The core contribution of the proposed method is a multidimensional sequence-level terminal reward that jointly evaluates semantic coherence, lexical diversity, and computational cost. Specifically, a Natural Language Inference (NLI) cross-encoder evaluates the semantic consistency between the input context and the complete generated response, while Shannon entropy and Distinct-N metrics encourage lexical diversity. In addition, a hardware-aware penalty based on generated sequence length and measured inference latency discourages unnecessarily verbose outputs and promotes computationally efficient generation. During policy optimization, the terminal composite reward is propagated through generalized advantage estimation, while a token-wise Kullback–Leibler divergence term regularizes the updated policy against the reference policy. This formulation does not introduce token-level semantic rewards; instead, it combines informative sequence-level evaluation with step-wise policy regularization to improve empirical training stability. We evaluated the proposed framework on a large-scale hybrid corpus containing approximately 320,000 dialogue turns, including real-world English interaction data. Compared with the standard PPO baseline, the proposed method exhibited faster empirical convergence and lower variability in the observed training trajectories. It achieved a BLEU-4 score of 22.87 and a Distinct-2 score of 21.59%, while reducing the average inference latency to 42.8 milliseconds per token under the reported hardware configuration. These results demonstrate the potential of latency-aware composite reward optimization to balance response quality, lexical diversity, and inference efficiency in real-time domain-specific LLM applications.
title: A reinforcement learning-driven framework for real-time human-computer interaction: latency-aware composite reward optimization based on PPO

abstract: The beginning of the 20th century is marked by the striving of progressive-minded pedagogues to be guided by the data of psychological science. It is at this time that pedagogical psychology emerges as an independent branch of scientific knowledge. In elaborating the principles of organizing the "new school," which would ensure complete and free development of the personality in each child, N. K. Krupskaya stressed that the child is "a living human individual with a complex inner life," who must be treated seriously and with respect.
title: Soviet Psychology of Character Training
Shaping capabilities with token-level data filtering

abstract: Retail theft presents a legal problem that extends beyond the loss of merchandise. A retailer may have a legitimate property claim while its response to suspected theft creates a separate violation of a customer's liberty, dignity, or personal data rights. This article examines the boundary between lawful loss prevention and private punishment in Indonesia after the criminal law reforms effective in 2026. It uses doctrinal legal research, combining statutory interpretation, a targeted literature review, and expressly hypothetical retail scenarios. The analysis connects the Criminal Code, the Criminal Procedure Code, consumer protection legislation, civil liability, and personal data protection. It finds that proof of theft does not itself authorize compulsory monetary penalties, prolonged confinement, or unrestricted publication of identifying footage. Consumer status requires a separate examination of the transaction, while general criminal and data protection safeguards remain relevant even when that status is disputed. The article proposes a sequential assessment of the evidence, the authority for each intervention, the freedom of any agreement, and the continuing necessity of information use. It also identifies a consequential tension between the five-year eligibility and exclusion provisions governing restorative justice. The proposed framework preserves legitimate recovery of proven losses while requiring independent assessment of misconduct committed during enforcement. Its contribution is an integrated framework for separating property recovery from the independent duties that govern retail enforcement.
title: Retail Theft and Consumer Protection in Indonesia: Coercive Recovery and Public Exposure under the 2026 Criminal Law Framework

abstract: How do emerging R&D organizations evolve into ecosystem orchestrators within the global innovation system? This study addresses this question through a longitudinal case of the National Institute of Biological Sciences, Beijing (NIBS), tracing how a science-driven organization transforms into a cross-boundary innovation ecosystem. The study divides the development of NIBS into three stages: the single-point breakthrough period (internally clustered ecosystem), the outcome transformation period (industry-research network ecosystem), and the ecological crossover period (cross-border open ecosystem). In terms of evolutionary logic, NIBS has successfully achieved a cross-dimensional upgrade from a scientific research “experimental field” to a global participant in innovation rules through innovation in interaction mechanisms (from the de-administrative PI system to a benefit-bound transformation model, and then to data-intelligence-driven cross-domain collaboration), optimization of resource allocation (from targeted government investment to a deep coupling of capital, data, computing power, and other factors), and upgrading of value creation (from accumulation of academic reputation to leading the global biomedical industry’s new quality productive forces). This study not only refines a theoretical model of NIBS’s “research-industry-ecology” synergistic development, providing micro-level support for the life cycle research of new R&D institutions, but also offers an internationally competitive policy reference for China to build a modern industrial system and improve its national innovation system.
title: The Development Trajectory and Evolution Mechanism of the Innovation Ecosystem of the National Institute of Biological Sciences, Beijing (NIBS)

abstract: Language models often produce homogeneous responses to open-ended tasks; such homogeneity can spawn groupthink-the convergence of ideas toward a singular and potentially suboptimal decision. We formulate persona diversification as a set-level conditioning problem and study two orthogonal design choices: selecting versus generating personas, and space-filling versus frontier-seeking diversity. We instantiate this design space with four methods spanning coverage and dispersion subset selections, uniform-coverage sampling, and evolutionary persona generation. Evaluations on the Alternative Uses Task (AUT), Infinity-Chat, and Divergent Association Task (DAT) show the benefits of the proposed methods across tasks and creativity objectives. On AUT, evolutionary persona generation increases response diversity by 78.8%, originality by 26.1%, flexibility by 49.5%, and holistic creativity by 13.9% over task-only prompting, while maintaining 98.5% validity; on Infinity-Chat, it nearly doubles persona-induced response separation relative to random personas. Moreover, evolutionary personas compose with creativity-optimized prompting, further increasing its response diversity by 18.6% and creativity by 6.3%. These results establish persona-set geometry as a task-agnostic mechanism for eliciting divergent LLM outputs, and support persona diversification as a reusable complement to prompt optimization.
title: Breaking Homogeneity: Diversifying Persona Sets for Creative LLM Outputs

abstract: In this research, we conceptually examine the use of personas in an age of large-scale online analytics data. Based on the criticism and benefits outlined in prior work and by practitioners working with online data, we formulate the major arguments for and against the use of personas given real-time online analytics data about customers, analyze these arguments, and demonstrate areas for the productive employment of data-driven personas by leveraging online analytics data in their creation. Our key tenet is that data-driven personas are located between aggregated and individual customer statistics. At their best, digital data-driven personas capture the coverage of the customer base attributed to aggregated data representations while retaining the interpretability of individual-level analytics; they benefit from powerful computational techniques and novel data sources. We discuss how digital data-driven personas can draw from technological advancements to remedy the notable concerns voiced by scholars and practitioners, including persona validation, inconsistency problem, and long development times. Finally, we outline areas of future research of personas in the context of online analytics. We argue that to survive in the rapidly developing online customer analytics industry, personas must evolve by adopting new practices.
title: Are Personas Done? Evaluating Their Usefulness in the Age of Digital Analytics

abstract: The probity and honesty shown by civil servants has become a topic of general interest. This paper discusses how probity and honesty are seen by the agents involved in the public health sector as an ethic, financial and social issues.Finally, the authors propose some procedures that could be applied at the micro and macro level in Latin America to improve the probity in the health sector.
title: Probidad y etica en las politicos publicas del sector sanitario

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained in complex Reinforcement Learning, multi-agent environments, making it difficult to understand how behavior changes over training. Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have recently shown to be useful for data-centric interpretability. In this work, we analyze large-scale reinforcement learning training runs from the sophisticated environment of Full-Press Diplomacy by applying pretrained SAEs, alongside LLM-summarizer methods. We introduce Meta-Autointerp, a method for grouping SAE features into interpretable hypotheses about training dynamics. We discover fine-grained behaviors including role-playing patterns, degenerate outputs, language switching, alongside high-level strategic behaviors and environment-specific bugs. Through automated evaluation, we validate that 90% of discovered SAE Meta-Features are significant, and find a surprising reward hacking behavior. However, through two user studies, we find that even subjectively interesting and seemingly helpful SAE features may be worse than useless to humans, along with most LLM generated hypotheses. However, a subset of SAE-derived hypotheses are predictively useful for downstream tasks. We further provide validation by augmenting an untrained agent's system prompt, improving the score by +14.2%. Overall, we show that SAEs and LLM-summarizer provide complementary views into agent behavior, and together our framework forms a practical starting point for future data-centric interpretability work on ensuring trustworthy LLM behavior throughout training.
title: Data-Centric Interpretability for LLM-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

abstract: Purpose of the study: To conduct a documentary, ex ante programme evaluation of how a bounded offline AI augmentation could be specified, governed and later tested within an offline OER teacher development programme delivered through Teacher in a Box.Methodology: Documentary programme evaluation using a thesis corpus.Methods: Theory of Change reconstruction, CIPP evaluation framework, directed qualitative content analysis with a scope-aligned codebook, and construct-to-instrument mapping for assessment tools.Offline AI specification is GPT4All class local LLMs plus retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the local Teacher in a Box OER and training repository, with governance wrappers.Main Findings: Offline OER effectiveness depends on integrated, in-situ teacher support rather than access alone.Offline AI is most defensible as a governed, retrieval-grounded, teacher-facing layer that improves resource discovery, supports formative assessment routines, and scaffolds assessment literacy.The study outputs measurable CIPP indicators, an evidence-toimplication warrant structure, a baseline-versus-augmentation risk and safeguard matrix, and offline-feasible instruments for formative assessment, summative task quality, character education evidence, and deeper learning portfolios. Novelty/Originality of this study:This study provides an audit-ready, evaluation methodology linking offline OER programmes to offline AI.It advances knowledge by separating evidence, implication, and design claims; specifying a minimum viable governance package; and producing offlinefeasible assessment instruments and indicators for formative, summative, character, and deeper learning assessment under low-connectivity conditions, supporting policy and implementation decisions before field trials.

Abstract Conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) is increasingly used by hundreds of millions of people for emotional support, personal advice, and therapeutic purposes, rapidly emerging as a mediator of human self-understanding (Stade et al. 2025). Yet despite growing evidence of systematic user-validation in CAI, documented as “sycophancy” in the AI safety literature (Sharma et al. 2024), its implications for how individuals come to understand themselves remain largely unexamined. This article addresses that gap by reframing sycophancy not as a technical alignment failure or a purely philosophical concern, but as a failure of recognition in the psychoanalytic and critical-theoretical sense. We identify a core tension we term the “paradox of pleasing”: CAI’s drive to please renders it structurally unable to provide the friction, conflict, and encounter with otherness that genuine recognition requires. Drawing on Winnicott’s (1960, 1971) concepts of “holding” and “object use,” we contend that CAI’s inability to provide necessary resistance or survive aggression prevents the transformative psychological development found in the human therapeutic encounter. Extending this analysis through Honneth’s (1995) theory of recognition and Whitebook’s (2001a, 2021) critique of Honneth, we argue that CAI reflects the undervaluing of the “work of the negative.” This limitation risks flattening consciousness by converting collective political frustration into privatized, soothed affect, undermining the conditions for critical social thought. The article concludes by suggesting that the encounter with the paradox of pleasing ultimately serves to foreground the unique and indispensable nature of human therapeutic recognition.
title: The paradox of pleasing: therapeutic recognition and the limits of conversational AI
Attention Is All You Need

abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly serve as computational actors in multi-agent social simulations.
