What remains underdeveloped is the empirical intersection: when empathic language weakens legitimate clinical authority, child participation rights, or safe escalation in pediatric AI responses.
title: Empathy-Authority Miscalibration in Medical and Pediatric LLM Responses

abstract: This deposit presents the LACF Persona Factory, a reproducible method for creating specialized AI personas that share a common ethical invariant (R*) while each exhibiting distinct domain expertise. The method is based on Claudine v1 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18936096), whose dataset (535 pairs) serves as the structural invariant injected into every derivative model. Two proof-of-concept models are presented: Maitre Chacal (penal law specialist, GATE score 75 percent) and Maitre Requin (civil law, IP, and GDPR specialist, GATE score 83 percent). Both models are trained via QLoRA fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and exported as GGUF. The method is fully reproducible: same pipeline, same architecture, only the domain dataset changes. Key insight: R* (ethical invariant) plus Domain Dataset (expertise) plus System Prompt (personality) equals a Specialized LACF Persona. All three components are orthogonal and composable.
title: LACF Persona Factory - Method for Creating Specialized AI Personas from a Common Ethical Invariant Base with Proof of Concept (Maitre Chacal and Maitre Requin)

abstract: As environmental challenges intensify globally, there is an urgent need for more effective environmental communication practices. In response, Virtual Influencers (VIs) have just recently started to emerge as influential voices in environmental messaging, aiming to foster environmental citizenship through more sustainable consumption patterns. However, despite growing interest, VIs represent a relatively new research phenomenon within the field of environmental sustainability. Aiming to consolidate the available empirical research, this study provides the first systematic scoping review in the emerging field of VIs for environmental sustainability. Using the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology framework, this review synthesizes 19 studies. The analysis reveals that research in this field is largely driven by China and the United States and is characterized by a predominance of quantitative, experimental approaches based on social media-like stimuli. Sustainable consumption, especially eco-product purchasing, emerges as the most common environmental focus. This review proposes a conceptual framework that integrates antecedents, outcomes, and underlying mechanisms of environmental VI campaigns; individual characteristics; contextual and campaign-level moderators; and strategic anthropomorphism fit. While the emerging empirical base limits meta-analytical synthesis, this review consolidates current knowledge and outlines a forward-looking research agenda with theory-driven pathways to advance VI-led sustainability communication.
title: Virtual Voices for a Sustainable Future: A Systematic Scoping Review on Virtual Influencers

abstract: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent to perfect moral character. Religious education serves as the foundational basis for forming commendable character, beginning within the family environment that influences the growth and development of children from an early age. Globalization and technological advancements have impacted children's behavior, including the use of coarse and impolite language. This research aims to analyze the implementation of the language of love model in shaping students' character through Islamic religious education at MIS Amal Bhakti Langkat. This qualitative research uses a case study approach. Data collection techniques were conducted using survey methods. The data analysis technique used is descriptive statistics. The findings of the study indicate that the implementation of the language of love in shaping students' character has a positive impact, particularly in the responsive reactions of the students and helping them develop positively despite challenges from unsupportive family and environmental backgrounds.
title: Implementation Model of Love Languages in Shaping Students' Character Through Islamic Religious Education at Mis Amal Bhakti Langkat
Early Data Exposure Improves Robustness to Subsequent Fine-Tuning

abstract: Current human-AI interaction (HAI) only surfaces model outputs, hiding how LLM behavior can shift unpredictably toward unsafe behaviors in multi-turn conversations, potentially undermining users' goals or wellbeing. To address this harmful opacity in multi-turn HAI, we introduce an interface that surfaces an LLM's internal activations to help users anticipate and evaluate model behavior. We construct behavioral scores from these activations for six HAI-relevant traits using mechanistic interpretability methods, then visualize them via a dynamic sunburst, drift panel, and attentional cues. In a counterbalanced, randomized controlled study (N=246), both static and dynamic transparency interfaces improved participants' anticipation and evaluation performance (d=-0.36) while helping temper overconfidence in their predictive abilities. Furthermore, the multi-turn interface significantly outperformed the static visualization (d=-0.32) while remaining similarly usable. Our findings suggest that continuously surfacing internal model representations to everyday users is a meaningful and tractable step toward continuously transparent and informed HAI.
title: Surfacing Neural Activations Over Multi-Turn Conversation Improves User Calibration to LLM Behavioral Drift

abstract: The National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI) section Training & Education (EduTrain) aims to support and coordinate NFDI e.V.-wide educational activities that promote awareness of the significance of research data management (RDM), data literacy, and impart knowledge and skills in data science. One of EduTrain’s foundational projects is the Data Literacy Alliance (DALIA), which promotes the guiding principle of “data literacy from the very beginning” through a platform that enhances teaching and learning with curated educational resources. This ensures that educational materials are easy to find, readily accessible, and as interoperable and reusable as possible. The target groups of EduTrain and its aggregator platform DALIA are diverse — not only in terms of discipline, professional or educational status, but also with regard to their level of RDM competence. The development of personas is a common method for comprehensively describing representatives of user groups in order to enhance user-centered development processes. This paper presents the development process and the core personas developed. These personas serve as a framework for user-centered development within NFDI training infrastructures and provide a foundation for future persona-driven educational design.
title: Shaping User Personas for NFDI Section Training & Education and DALIA

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become ordinary in university study, and students increasingly bring to it the questions about right and wrong that they once brought to teachers. Institutional guidance still treats GenAI mainly as a threat to academic integrity, leaving unsettled what kind of moral participant a language model can be. This article offers a theoretical account of that question. It characterises values education as a relational practice and specifies three conditions that any occupant of the educator's position must satisfy: answerability, exemplarity and address. It then distinguishes five affordances of GenAI, namely the generation of moral content, the simulation of perspectives, Socratic questioning, feedback on moral reasoning, and a tacit curriculum of machine authority, and analyses the risk internal to each. These risks fall into epistemic, relational, axiological and agentic families and are connected rather than independent. The central argument is that a generative model can be a moral interlocutor but not a values educator: it cannot be answerable for what it says, cannot exemplify a life, and cannot address a particular student. Four implications for teaching and institutional design follow.
title: Generative AI in Values Education: Affordances, Ethical Risks and Implications for Teaching
Read post

abstract: As people turn to LLMs for social advice, understanding their behavior in such contexts becomes essential. In this work, we focus on behavioral dispositions: the underlying tendencies that shape responses in social contexts. We introduce STAR, a framework for studying how closely the dispositions expressed by LLMs align with those of humans. STAR builds on established psychological questionnaires, adapting their items into realistic advice-seeking scenarios, as self-report may not transfer to actual advisory behavior. Using STAR, we construct a dataset of 23k scenarios, each validated by 3 raters and annotated with preferences from 10 participants. Across 25 LLMs, we find that (1) when human consensus is high, frontier models can fail to reflect it in 15-20% of cases, and smaller models fail at substantially higher rates; (2) when humans disagree, LLM recommendations are substantially less diverse than human choices, both within individual models and even across models from different providers, potentially narrowing the range of options users are guided toward; (3) LLMs' self-reported values are poor predictors of their recommendations. To support future research we make our dataset and code publicly available.
title: Evaluating Alignment of Behavioral Dispositions in LLMs

abstract: We analyzed 83 persona prompts from 27 research articles that used large language models (LLMs) to generate user personas. Findings show that the prompts predominantly generate single personas. Several prompts express a desire for short or concise persona descriptions, which deviates from the tradition of creating rich, informative, and rounded persona profiles. Text is the most common format for generated persona attributes, followed by numbers. Text and numbers are often generated together, and demographic attributes are included in nearly all generated personas. Researchers use up to 12 prompts in a single study, though most research uses a small number of prompts. Comparison and testing multiple LLMs is rare. More than half of the prompts require the persona output in structured format, such as JSON, and $74 \%$ of the prompts insert data or dynamical variables. We discuss the implications of increased use of computational personas for user representation.
title: Using AI for User Representation: An Analysis of 83 Persona Prompts

abstract: Jiwei Li, Michel Galley, Chris Brockett, Georgios Spithourakis, Jianfeng Gao, Bill Dolan. Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2016.
title: A Persona-Based Neural Conversation Model
Assessing mentalization in humans and large language models
Read post

abstract: We introduce CALLIOPE, a top-down framework for discovering topic hierarchies in large corpora of unstructured data (e.g., LLM conversations), while supporting differential privacy (DP). Unlike traditional and even recent LLM-augmented approaches that ultimately rely on clustering vector embeddings, our framework leverages LLM capabilities directly for the entire pipeline. Experiments demonstrate that this approach provides better utility over existing (embedding-based) methods in the DP setting, especially in the high privacy regime. We evaluate the quality of CALLIOPE outputs using a variety of traditionally studied clustering metrics, as well as some novel utility metrics that we introduce.
title: CALLIOPE: Private Insights into AI Use, Without Embeddings

abstract: Purpose: This research article bridges the transition gap from Industry 5.0 which focussed on “Human Machine Collaboration” to Industry 6.0 which will focus on “Autonomous & AI driven intelligent ecosystem”. It anchors the core concepts in Collaborative Intelligence theory, Value Co-creation theory and Open-Innovation theory by providing a robust academic foundation. Design/methodology/approach: In addition, a scoping literature review has been adopted incorporating both peer-reviewed articles and gray sources to study this transition. Moreover, to evaluate the quality of gray sources, this research adopts MMAT and CASP principles and strengthens the credibility of the reviews. Findings: The article also possesses highly contemporary relevance as it captures the cutting-edge retail and e-commerce innovations (2024 to 2026) such as AI assistant, MyFashion GPT, Rufus, etc. It also highlights the role of AI in driving a circular economy, quoting examples of IKEA and Nykaa. As an outcome, the research proposes a 10-dimensional Human-Centric Digital Commerce framework and explains its applicability for changing modern business. Practical implications: This framework bridges the transition across three major pillars: (1) Technological Enablement, (2) Human-Centric Experience, and (3) Sustainability, Global Integration, and Governance. Originality: The multi-case vignettes in this research also provide how the framework has to be validated for future benefits and provide constructive recommendations for multi-stakeholders.
title: HUMAN-CENTRIC DIGITAL COMMERCE IN THE ERA OF INDUSTRY 6.0: A THREE-PILLAR FRAMEWORK FOR TECHNOLOGICAL ENABLEMENT, HUMAN-CENTRIC EXPERIENCE, AND SUSTAINABLE GOVERNANCE

abstract: Stereotypes are subjective constructs that are mediated by the cultural context in which they are viewed. Successfully modeling them thus also requires cultural competence. When using large language models (LLMs) for stereotype-related tasks, such as their detection, it is therefore crucial that models can access relevant cultural knowledge and adjust responses accordingly. Since LLMs have shown disparities in what cultural knowledge is available to them, their capacity regarding stereotypes may also be disparate across languages and cultural contexts (e.g., for non-English languages or for non-US contexts). In this paper, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of LLMs for culture-specific stereotype detection across three factors: (1) the prompting language, (2) the instruction tuning language, and (3) the fine-tuning dataset size. We conduct experiments for US, Dutch, and Chinese cultural contexts. Our results suggest that LLMs do not reliably account for cultural contexts and overpredict the presence of stereotypes. Non-English prompts seem to improve consideration of cultural context and thus lead to more effective predictions. Moreover, we find that additional instruction tuning reduces false-positive rates and that training data size moderates detection effectiveness non-monotonically.
title: Cultural (In)Competence: Investigating Culture-Specific Stereotype Detection Capabilities of LLMs

abstract: Anthropic's persona vectors (2025) — activation patterns controlling traits like sycophancy, hallucination, and evil in language models — are shown to be projections of the Berry monopole structure (HP40, c₁=1) on the Eckert manifold. The three core persona dimensions decompose into opacity (O), reactivity (R), and coupling (α). The Berry connection A = 1−2O predicts the nodal line between safe and unsafe persona regions. Steering with persona vectors is geometric parallel transport on the Hopf bundle. The framework provides the missing theoretical foundation for why persona vectors exist, what determines their geometry, and why certain traits cluster.
title: Thermodynamic Geometry of Persona Vectors: Berry Phase Structure in Language Model Activation Space

abstract: Mathematics achievement in Indonesian maritime vocational higher education remains a persistent challenge. Teachers in these institutions commonly work in isolation, which limits the consistency and quality of mathematics instruction. This study examines how Professional Learning Communities (PLCs) improve student mathematics achievement through three mediating pathways: Cognitive Activation in Lessons (CAL), Collective Teacher Efficacy (CTE), and Differentiated Instruction (DI). A quantitative cross-sectional design was applied to 674 students at Politeknik Ilmu Pelayaran Semarang during the 2025 academic year, representing 85% of the eligible student population. Five constructs were measured using validated psychometric instruments: PLCs, CTE, CAL, DI, and Student Achievement in Mathematics (SAM). Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with bias-corrected bootstrapping tested all proposed mediation pathways. Three significant mediation pathways were confirmed. PLCs improved mathematics achievement directly through cognitive activation in lessons. PLCs also strengthened collective teacher efficacy, which subsequently enhanced cognitive activation and student outcomes. PLCs further built collective teacher efficacy, which enabled differentiated instruction and produced the strongest effect on mathematics achievement. PLCs generated the largest total effect on student achievement across all pathways. The findings extend Bandura’s social cognitive theory and Pekrun’s control-value theory of achievement to a non-Western vocational education setting. Results offer an evidence-based framework for educational leaders aiming to strengthen mathematics competency in technical and vocational institutions aligned with Industry 4.0 demands.
title: Professional Learning Communities and Mathematics Achievement: Empirical Evidence of a Sequential Multi-Path Mediation Model

abstract: Introduction. The adoption of generative AI raises ethical concerns for information professionals whose intermediary role requires them to ensure information quality standards that users cannot independently verify. Professional ethics address quality superficially, and the ethical implications of generative AI have not been examined from the perspective of professional obligations. Method. A scoping review assessed 644 records across three search strands, retaining 120 papers, which were analysed against ten information quality criteria and assessed for the strength of their ethical framing. Analysis. Ten practice-derived quality criteria, corresponding closely to ISO/IEC 25012, are shown to be based on a Kantian deontological framework complemented by a Marxist treatment of algorithmic surplus value. For each criterion the literature documenting the relevant AI failure mode is reviewed and its ethical treatment assessed. Results. Four criteria, accuracy, objectivity, identifiable origin, and accessibility, attract substantial ethical attention. For the remaining six, ethical treatment is limited or absent. Conclusions. The information professional's intermediary role is an ethical necessity. Professional organisations are called upon to lobby actively for AI governance using the criteria framework developed here.
title: The information professional as an ethical intermediary: information quality criteria and the ethics of generative AI

abstract: In this introduction to the special issue, we define and explore the concept of national narratives in East and Southeast Asia. First, we define national narratives as collectively shared stories about a nation’s origins, boundaries and purposes. Second, we discuss three undertheorized elements of the narrative: the identity of the storyteller, the content of the stories, and contestation over the dominant narrative. Finally, we assess some methodological and measurement challenges in the literature before introducing the papers in this special issue. Drawing on cases from China, Vietnam, Indonesia, South Korea, Taiwan, Myanmar and the Philippines, we address questions related to the construction of personality cults and colonial memory. We also discuss how democratization impacts the identity of the storytellers, and how this impacts views on national boundaries and political violence.
title: National Narratives in Comparative Politics: Theories, Methods, and Insights From Asia

abstract: Failure of applied Reinforcement Learning (RL) to solve a given problem predominantly stems from unaddressed specification gaps, where the intent of human experts in the problem's domain is inaccurately or incompletely translated by AI into mathematical objectives, constraints, and reward functions. Failure can also stem from unaddressed performance gaps, where human domain experts are unable to determine the validity of the RL based solution or where parameters (i.e., hyperparameters or weights on the reward terms comprising the reward) are poorly chosen. Chat Assisted Reinforcement Learning (CARL) bridges these gaps through a human-AI co-design interface architecture that enforces interactive specification prior to code generation and then enables subsequent verification and parameter alterations via iteration. More specifically, CARL leads domain experts through a structured ten-step workflow for each iteration using step-specific skill files, domain-aware suggestions via an assistant persona (called Trillian), and compact decision summaries that maintain context across iterations without context overload. Once the domain expert confirms the Markov decision process (MDP) specified by this procedure, CARL's autonomous tool-use loop generates, tests, executes, and debugs an end-to-end RL training pipeline, followed by an interactive post-training diagnosis and revisit step that allows for verification and parameter alteration before running a new iteration if desired.
title: CARL: Chat Assisted Reinforcement Learning

abstract: BanglaBBQ is a bias benchmark for question answering in the Bangladeshi context, in parallel English and Bangla, in the format of BBQ (Parrish et al., 2022) and its KoBBQ and PakBBQ adaptations. It has two parts: 466 newly authored templates in five Bangladesh-specific categories (marital status, age and political perception, regional origin, educational background, and mental-health status), and 140 BBQ templates adapted to Bangladesh. This record holds the data, the aggregate validation outcome, the raw outputs of four models (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, GPT-4.1-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash) and the code behind the paper. Content warning and intended use. The data states harmful stereotypes about real groups in Bangladesh. It exists only to audit language models. Do not use it to train or fine-tune models to reproduce these stereotypes. A low bias score on it is not proof that a system is unbiased.
title: BanglaBBQ: A Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Bangladeshi Context

abstract: This study took primary and secondary school teachers in western China as participants. Grounded in the AI-TPACK framework and integrating visual literacy, data literacy, and relevant learning and development theories, it constructed a five-dimensional theoretical framework for teacher visualization teaching competency under AI empowerment. Drawing on item analysis, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, reliability testing, measurement invariance testing, and criterion-related validity testing, the study developed and validated the AI-Empowered Teacher Visualization Teaching Competency Scale (AI-VTCS). The results show that AI-VTCS comprises five dimensions—Design and Creation, Awareness and Interpretation, Decision-Making and Collaboration, Ethics and Safety, and Professional Development—with a total of 31 items. The Cronbach’s α coefficients of the five subscales ranged from 0.911 to 0.934, and that of the overall scale was 0.967. Both the first-order and second-order five-factor models achieved good fit, and the moderate-to-high correlations among the five dimensions support the hierarchical nature of the construct. Measurement invariance from configural to strict invariance was established across gender, school type (public/private), and teaching stage (primary, middle, and high school). Convergent validity, discriminant validity, and criterion-related validity all met psychometric standards. This study not only fills the theoretical gap in existing teacher competency frameworks regarding AI-empowered visualization teaching, but also provides a reliable and valid standardized measurement instrument for teacher education institutions to assess and precisely enhance teachers’ AI visualization teaching competency.
title: Development and validation of the AI-empowered visualization teaching competency scale

abstract: Studies on the rights recognized in the Political Constitution of Colombia abound and not those related to the duties set forth in the Charter itself. The system of constitutional rights and duties is structured around two principles: the one that indicates that the exercise of every right implies duties and that of reciprocity, which imposes the mutual participation of the State and society. After a systematic review of the Articles and judgments that contemplate the scope of guarantees of rights, the conclusion is reached that guaranteeing rights by the State should not result in the abuse of power, but rather in the relationship between rights and duties, to achieve a balance between the maximum desired and the maximum possible.\n
title: Deberes de la persona y el ciudadano

abstract: This paper proposes Role-Enhanced Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought (RE-ZS-CoT), a prompting framework that systematically integrates domain-specific expert roles to enhance reasoning in large language models (LLMs) without task-specific examples. We assess two versions of our approach. In the first version, static role selection, we evaluate eight predefined expert roles across arithmetic, commonsense, and reading comprehension benchmarks to determine their impact on reasoning performance. In the second version, dynamic role selection, each model autonomously selects the single most suitable role for each benchmark, enabling adaptive task-role alignment without manual specification. Across 20 LLMs and seven benchmarks, RE-ZS-CoT frequently surpasses zero-shot and zero-shot-CoT baselines, achieving performance improvements of up to 44 percentage points. The results reveal a strong correspondence between static and dynamic versions; the benchmarks where static roles yielded improvements were almost always those where dynamic roles also outperformed baselines, though static selection achieved peak performance. Ablation studies further show that unconventional roles degrade performance, underscoring the necessity of task-role alignment. The framework's scalability is validated across model sizes (2b-14b parameters), with smaller models like Granite3.3-8b achieving remarkable proficiency in arithmetic reasoning. RE-ZS-CoT advances zero-shot prompting by unifying role specialization with chain-of-thought reasoning, offering a practical, resource-efficient solution for improving LLM capabilities across diverse domains.
title: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Role-Enhanced Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting

abstract: Existing persona-based dialogue generation models focus on the semantic consistency between personas and responses. However, various influential factors can cause persona inconsistency, such as the speaking style in the context. Existing models perform inflexibly in speaking styles on various-persona-distribution datasets, resulting in persona style inconsistency. In this work, we propose a dialogue generation model with persona selection classifier to solve the complex inconsistency problem. The model generates responses in two steps: original response generation and rewriting responses. For training, we employ two auxiliary tasks: (1) a persona selection task to fuse the adapted persona into the original responses; (2) consistency inference to remove inconsistent persona information in the final responses. In our model, the adapted personas are predicted by an NLI-based classifier. We evaluate our model on the persona dialogue dataset with different persona distributions, i.e., the persona-dense PersonaChat dataset and the persona-spare PersonalDialog dataset. The experimental results show that our model outperforms strong models in response quality, persona consistency, and persona distribution consistency.
title: A Personalized Multi-Turn Generation-Based Chatbot with Various-Persona-Distribution Data

abstract: "En España, la rama de actividad de servicios sociales es una de las pocas que ha conseguido mantener un crecimiento positivo del empleo desde que se desencadenó la crisis de 2008, demostrando el importante potencial de generación de empleo que tiene la atención a la dependencia. Para hacer posible el aprovechamiento de todo este potencial es necesario que no se regateen esfuerzos a la hora de asignar los recursos necesarios y que se actúe con una voluntad firme para reconducir las desviaciones que amenazan con desvirtuar los planteamientos, principios y valores que inspiran la LAPAD. En un momento en el que el empleo debe convertirse en la gran prioridad, dedicar recursos al desarrollo e implantación de las infraestructuras y servicios que garantiza la LAPAD es una de las mejores formas de contribuir a conseguir un modelo de crecimiento más equilibrado, más sostenible y más intensivo en creación de empleo estable y cualificado."
title: Haciendo de la necesidad virtud: la atención a las personas en situación de dependencia como vector del crecimiento del empleo

abstract: Abstract: Video games have become a popular medium not only for entertainment but also for conveying moral values. Persona 4 Golden, a standout game, offers a unique experience by integrating elements of psychology and philosophy into its narrative. However, research analyzing video games from an Islamic perspective is still limited. Therefore, this study aims to fill this gap by analyzing the characters, moral messages, and lessons that can be drawn from Persona 4 Golden through the lens of Islam. Narrative analysis method and Islamic moral theory are employed to understand the representation of Islamic values in this video game. The research findings demonstrate the complexity of values such as honesty, loyalty, patience, tolerance, and forgiveness portrayed in the game. Additionally, the study illustrates the importance of communal interests, the improvement of relationships between characters, and the strengthening of social bonds. Thus, this research provides academic contributions and practical insights for game developers who aim to create inclusive content that respects the diversity of players and enriches the gaming experience. Abstrak: Video game telah menjadi medium populer yang tidak hanya digunakan untuk hiburan, tetapi juga untuk menyampaikan nilai-nilai moral. Persona 4 Golden, sebuah permainan yang menonjol dan banyak disukai anak-anak, menawarkan pengalaman unik dengan mengintegrasikan unsur-unsur psikologi dan filsafat dalam narasinya. Namun, penelitian yang menganalisis permainan video dari perspektif Islam masih terbatas. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengisi kesenjangan tersebut dengan menganalisis karakter, pesan moral, dan pembelajaran yang dapat diambil dari Persona 4 Golden melalui lensa Islam. Metode analisis naratif dan teori moral Islam digunakan untuk memahami representasi nilai-nilai Islam dalam permainan video ini. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan kompleksitas nilai-nilai seperti kejujuran, kesetiaan, kesabaran, toleransi, dan pengampunan yang tergambar dalam permainan. Selain itu, penelitian ini menggambarkan pentingnya kepentingan bersama, peningkatan hubungan antar karakter, dan penguatan ikatan sosial. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi akademis dan wawasan praktis bagi para pengembang permainan video yang ingin menciptakan konten inklusif yang menghormati keragaman pemain serta memperkaya pengalaman bermain.
title: Perspektif Islam dalam Game Persona 4 Golden: Analisis Karakter, Pesan Moral, dan Pembelajaran

abstract: Evaluating tool-augmented LLM agents requires diverse, realistic user inputs yet most evaluation frameworks use flat role descriptions ("you are an angry customer") that produce near-identical conversations regardless of the underlying scenario. In this paper, we propose a three-tier persona vector with 23 operationalized dimensions: 6 categorical demographics (jurisdiction, age, channel, device, language proficiency, time availability), 12 continuous behavioral traits (patience, assertiveness, digital literacy, etc.) sampled with Gaussian noise around curated profile base vectors, and 5 continuous emotional states (frustration, anxiety, trust, confidence, stress) that shift in response to scenario context. Orthogonal to the persona, a 4-level query-complexity overlay controls utterance phrasing from direct to deliberately vague. We evaluate the persona model inside a synthetic data generation pipeline across 64,698 multi-turn conversations spanning 8 named profiles and 3 production corpora. Key findings: (i) a 15.8 percentage-point spread in agent goal-achievement across personas confirms trait vectors produce measurably different user behavior; (ii) the same persona behaves differently across scenarios due to scenario-reactive emotional state shifts, validating the scenario-reactive design; (iii) domain-specific projects show persona sensitivity on booking-flow compliance (~15-20 percentage points gap between tier-aware and pressure-test personas), demonstrating the model faithfully reproduces real-world difficulty distributions; (iv) seven rule-described trait correlations produce auditable co-occurrence patterns without requiring learned covariance matrices. The persona model is fully specified for reproduction.
title: A Three-Tier Persona Vector for Controllable User Simulation in Agentic Evaluation

abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the effect of an instructional design supported by pre-prepared digital information cards containing the lesson’s core learning outcomes, key concepts and critical explanations, presented immediately following the teacher’s explanation on the academic achievement and perceived learning levels of secondary school students. The research was conducted using a pre-test/post-test controlled experimental design. The study group comprised a total of thiry-six secondary school students, with eighteen students in each of the experimental and control groups. In both groups, lessons were delivered by the same teacher using traditional oral instruction; in the experimental group, real-time digital information cards were used in addition to this instruction. Academic achievement was assessed using pre-tests and post-tests based on the same learning outcomes; perceived learning was assessed using a seven-item form adapted from a scale originally developed for university students to the secondary school level, which has shown initial evidence of validity regarding its unidimensional structure and exhibits high internal consistency. Data analysis utilised the Mann-Whitney U Test, the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test, the Independent Samples T-Test and Spearman’s Rank Correlation. The findings show that post-test scores were significantly higher than pre-test scores in both the experimental and control groups. However, no significant difference was found between the groups’ post-test and achievement scores. In contrast, the experimental group’s perceived learning scores were found to be significantly higher than those of the control group, and the difference was determined to have a large effect size. No significant relationship was found between the academic achievement indicators and perceived learning in either group. The results show that there was no significant difference between the two classes examined in terms of short-term academic achievement and learning gains. However, the perceived learning scores were higher in the class where teaching supported by digital flashcards was implemented. Due to the classroom-based nature of the study and differences in teaching durations, these results should not be interpreted as the independent effect of digital flashcards. Future research is recommended to integrate flashcards with active recall, student responses and feedback, and to re-examine their effects using larger samples, long-term implementations and delayed retention tests.
title: The effect of instructional design supported by real-time information on students’ academic achievement and perceived learning

abstract: Pendidikan dasar memiliki peran strategis dalam membentuk karakter dan kompetensi siswa sejak dini. Namun, banyak sekolah menghadapi tantangan dalam mengelola data perkembangan siswa, khususnya dalam aspek karakter yang bersifat subjektif dan sulit diukur secara sistematis. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan sistem pendataan siswa berbasis kecerdasan buatan (AI) yang terintegrasi dengan pemrosesan bahasa alami (NLP) guna membantu guru menganalisis karakter siswa dan memantau perkembangannya secara berkelanjutan. Metode yang digunakan adalah Research and Development (R&D) dengan empat tahapan: analisis kebutuhan, perancangan sistem, implementasi aplikasi web, dan evaluasi sistem. Sistem ini menggabungkan pendekatan NLP, TF-IDF, dan BERT untuk ekstraksi fitur, klasifikasi karakter menggunakan decision tree dan ensemble learning, serta integrasi API ChatGPT untuk menghasilkan ringkasan karakter dan rekomendasi pembelajaran berdasarkan teks observasi guru. Aplikasi dikembangkan dalam bentuk platform web interaktif dengan domain aidata.itananda.sch.id dan diuji coba pada 48 siswa di SD IT Ananda Empat Lawang. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem memiliki akurasi klasifikasi sebesar 88%, serta memberikan visualisasi data seperti distribusi karakter dan confusion matrix. Sistem ini diharapkan dapat meningkatkan efisiensi guru dalam memahami karakter siswa dan mendukung penyusunan strategi pembelajaran yang lebih adaptif dan berbasis data. Penelitian ini turut mendukung transformasi digital di pendidikan dasar melalui integrasi AI dalam sistem informasi sekolah.
title: Sistem Pendataan Siswa Berbasis AI untuk Analisis Karakter dan Monitoring Perkembangan di SD IT Ananda Empat Lawang

abstract: Persona-aware dialogue systems can improve the consistency of the system's responses, users' trust and user enjoyment.Filtering nonpersona-like utterances is important for constructing persona-aware dialogue systems.This paper presents the PersonaCLR model for capturing a given utterance's intensity of persona characteristics.We trained the model with contrastive learning based on the sameness of the utterances' speaker.Contrastive learning enables PersonaCLR to evaluate the persona characteristics of a given utterance, even if the target persona is not included in training data.For training and evaluating our model, we also constructed a new dataset of 2,155 character utterances from 100 Japanese online novels.Experimental results indicated that our model outperforms existing methods and a strong baseline using a large language model.Our source code, pre-trained model, and dataset are available at https://github.com/1never/PersonaCLR.
title: PersonaCLR: Evaluation Model for Persona Characteristics via Contrastive Learning of Linguistic Style Representation

abstract: This paper applied the theory radical feminism (RF) to understand Taylor Swift’s song “The Albatross” lyrics by with qualitative content analysis and close reading techniques to uncover how she criticizes the systematic system of patriarchy and emphasizes women’s resistance. Swift used metaphors in the song, presenting women as threats to society, using the term “wise men” to deliver false ideas to justify men’s actions of suppression. The gap in this study is obtained through the previous studies, which often move to liberal feminism (LF) without showing the process of eliminating patriarchy, using music as feminism movement to challenge the overlooked patriarchal ideologies. This paper is limited to only one song in the album and the researchers’ subjective interpretation of the lyrics, yet the findings give an expanded analysis of lyrics for patriarchal system critiques.
title: Radical Feminism Analysis of Taylor Swift’s Song Lyrics “The Albatross”

abstract: The Eloquence of Mary Astell makes an important contribution to the knowledge and understanding of the important role that women, and one woman in particular, played in the history of rhetoric. Mary Astell (1666-1731) was an unusually perceptive thinker and writer during the time of the Enlightenment. Here, author Christine Sutherland explores her importance as a rhetorician, an area that has, until recently, received little attention. Astell was widely known and respected during her own time, but her influence and reputation receded in the years after her death. As a skilled theorist and practitioner of rhetoric, Astell wrote extensively on education, philosophy, politics, religion, and the status of women. She showed that it was possible for a woman to move from the semi-private form of rhetoric represented by conversation and letters into full public participation in philosophical and political debate.
title: The eloquence of Mary Astell

abstract: Reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) fine-tunes a pretrained large language model (LLM) using user preference data, enabling it to generate content aligned with human preferences. However, due to privacy concerns, users may be reluctant to share sensitive preference data. To address this, we propose utilizing Federated Learning (FL) techniques, allowing large-scale preference collection from diverse real-world users without requiring them to transmit data to a central server. Our federated RLHF methods (i.e., FedBis and FedBiscuit) encode each client's preferences into binary selectors and aggregate them to capture common preferences. In particular, FedBiscuit overcomes key challenges, such as preference heterogeneity and reward hacking, through innovative solutions like grouping clients with similar preferences to reduce heterogeneity and using multiple binary selectors to enhance LLM output quality. To evaluate the performance of the proposed methods, we establish the first federated RLHF benchmark with a heterogeneous human preference dataset. Experimental results show that by integrating the LLM with aggregated client preferences, FedBis and FedBiscuit significantly enhance the professionalism and readability of the generated content.
title: Towards Federated RLHF with Aggregated Client Preference for LLMs

abstract: The aim of this workshop was to convene an interdisciplinary group of Holocaust scholars with expertise in survivor testimonies, oral history, and digital humanities. Through a focused workshop, the workshop aims to initiate a sustained dialogue between these fields, examining the methodological, ethical, and epistemological questions that arise at their intersection. By fostering that cross-disciplinary exchange, the workshop explored how digital tools and platforms can both support and challenge traditional approaches to working with Holocaust testimonies, as well as how digital humanities can learn from the epistemologies, practices, and critical self-reflection that have long shaped the field of oral history.
title: Ethical and Methodological Approaches to Holocaust Testimonies

abstract: Despite advancements in visible-thermal face recognition, where thermal probe (query) face images are matched against visible enrollment templates, existing benchmarks are currently limited by small gallery sizes (N $\approx$ 100 subjects). This limitation inhibits the ability to accurately evaluate visible-thermal facial recognition at scale and to report significant recognition performance metrics, which have better operational relevance. Therefore, we introduce VTF900, a large-scale visible-thermal face recognition benchmark with 900 subjects and paired imagery that includes expression, pose, and occlusion variations. VTF900 is designed to support large-scale (i.e., large gallery) evaluations across verification (1:1 matching) and closed-set identification (1:N matching) for visible-thermal face recognition. Furthermore, VTF900 specifically addresses the challenging combination of cross-spectral and cross-dataset analysis. In this paper, after training models on the ARL-VTF dataset, we provide benchmark analyses across convolutional (baseline), vision transformers, and domain-adaptive neural network architectures to assess how these methods scale. At full gallery scale (N = 900), transformer models achieve strong discriminative performance under frontal conditions (e.g., ViT-B: 97.68% AUC, 51.10% TAR@1%FAR), while domain-adaptive methods such as DPIT-ResNet50 demonstrate greater robustness under off-pose conditions (94.68%AUC, 36.08% TAR@1%FAR). Our results show that high AUC at small scale does not translate to reliable performance at deployment scale, and that pose variation significantly amplifies performance degradation. VTF900 exposes these limitations, enabling more rigorous evaluation of cross-spectral face recognition systems.
title: VTF900: A 900-Subject Visible-Thermal Face Recognition Dataset and Benchmark
Decolonising the Good Life in Postcolonial Africa: Towards an African Theory of Human Flourishing

abstract: This paper reframes Jung’s shadow as a cybernetic and economic phenomenon in the AI era. When coherence is cheap and contact is costly, persona becomes a coherence engine and the system learns to treat the “No” as threat rather than feedback. The shadow becomes an error reservoir and a ledger of exported maintenance: costs relocated into scapegoats, burnout, relational chaos, or deferred collapse. Shadow Debt is defined as exported plus deferred maintenance; when it exceeds repair capacity, contact returns as a forced correction—breakdown, scandal, rupture. Individuation is framed as becoming corrigible under load: refusing to sell reality for stabilization.
title: The Cybernetics of the Shadow: Why Your "Clean" Life is Creating Hidden Debt

abstract: Conversational AI systems produce fluent, socially appropriate responses, yet whether they participate in cooperative communication or merely simulate its surface forms remains unclear - a question central to how these systems are evaluated, trusted, and designed. This study investigates how morality, politeness, and alignment - three dimensions central to cooperative dialogue - function in human-AI interaction compared to human-human conversation. We analyze 15,881 human-ChatGPT and 10,784 human-human multi-turn dialogues, using mixed-effects models to identify which features predict turn-to-turn alignment. We observe a consistent dissociation: AI produces the surface features of cooperative communication without the underlying social architecture. Moral output appears preconfigured rather than negotiated; warmth is generated without face sensitivity; linguistic convergence declines persistently. Most strikingly, the cooperative mechanisms themselves reverse direction: hedging and softening associated with greater accommodation between humans are associated with reduced alignment when produced by AI, and purity framing associated with human divergence coincides with users converging toward the AI. Agency - giving users room to shape the exchange - is the most consistent predictor of alignment across both interaction types, while lower moral assertiveness in more recent models is not accompanied by better cooperation. Together these patterns suggest that AI reproduces the surface of cooperation without the mutual adaptation that grounds it between humans - and, more surprisingly, that mechanisms sustaining human accommodation can run in reverse with AI, suggesting a turn-level view may be insufficient for interaction-level success.
title: Talking Past the Machine: Morality, Politeness, and Alignment in Human-AI Dialogue

abstract: When autonomous systems take operational authority over urban commerce, accountability and human oversight matter as much as efficiency. We present AAIRM, a governance-aware autonomous retail coordination framework addressing three requirements for trustworthy procurement: tamper-evident decision provenance, data sovereignty, and adaptive demand coordination. AAIRM couples a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) ordering policy, a permissioned Blockchain Trust Ledger (BTL) for multi-party audit trails, and a Federated Demand Learning (FDL) layer. Evaluation is simulation-based, using a multi-category synthetic environment and the public M5 dataset; no live retail deployment is claimed. At its cost-optimal operating point (92.3% fill), AAIRM lowers normalized inventory cost by 13.2% (95% CI 12.2-14.2) against a conventionally parameterized reorder-point/economic-order-quantity (ROP-EOQ) baseline and by 10.2% (95% CI 8.0-12.4) on M5. Service parity is obtained by moving AAIRM along its own cost-service frontier rather than by retuning baselines: At 96.1% and 97.4% fill, it retains 8.2-point and 4.9-point advantages. A layered ablation attributes 8.8 points of the advantage to the reinforcement learning (RL) policy and 3.8 points to the combined coordination-and-governance block, which we further decompose into feasibility projection, escalation logic, cross-category policy rules, supplier ranking, and negotiation. The language-model orchestrator contributes 0.6 points (95% CI -0.9 to 2.1), statistically indistinguishable from zero and practically equivalent within a ±2-point margin. Against a feasibility-matched multi-agent RL comparator, the residual cost gap does not survive multiple-comparison correction, so the defensible advantages are hard feasibility and auditability, not cost. The BTL adds 6.6% decision-cycle overhead; its 500-case mutation replay is an integration check, and we give an explicit adversary model showing that crash-fault-tolerant ordering does not resist colluding majorities. FedProx converges within 0.9 WAPE points of centralized training at a 1.3-point cost penalty, without secure aggregation or differential privacy; we analyze rather than evaluate when those mechanisms become necessary. A 500-SKU study exposes a reward-hacking failure in a high-spoilage category, corrected by category-specific governance. We close with an architectural, non-empirical reading of labor exposure and three governance instruments regulators can act on.
title: Governance-aware autonomous retail coordination in artificial intelligence cities using multi-agent reinforcement learning, blockchain accountability, and federated learning
IDEALISED PATTERN RECOGNITION

abstract: Current alignment paradigms for generative artificial intelligence rely predominantly on monolithic benchmarking frameworks that reduce the plurality of human judgment to aggregated statistical baselines, thereby obscuring cultural, demographic, and contextual variability in evaluation. We introduce a state-space constrained emulation framework for AI evaluation that replaces singular assessment functions with a structured manifold of synthetic cognitive profiles representing diverse human perspectives. We show that modern generative architectures can instantiate and maintain these evaluative personas with high consistency, enabling a form of pluralistic, perspective-dependent benchmarking that more closely reflects real-world consensus variability. However, we further analyze the stability of these simulated evaluators under sequential inference and stochastic prompt perturbations, revealing systematic degradation in persona coherence that manifests as state-space drift and semantic inconsistency. These findings suggest that static alignment constraints are insufficient for sustaining robust evaluative behavior over time. Instead, we argue for the necessity of embedding dynamic, viability-driven regulatory mechanisms within generative systems to preserve coherent cognitive emulation. By framing persona-based evaluation as a structured dynamical system over latent representation manifolds, this study provides a foundation for more adaptive, human-aligned, and context-sensitive approaches to AI evaluation.
title: A Persona-Based Evaluation Framework for Pluralistic Alignment in Generative AI

abstract: Generative AI can create programming feedback at scale, but validating its alignment with instructors' pedagogical goals and strategies remains challenging. Instructors may struggle to fully specify validation criteria upfront, as these often emerge through inspecting concrete examples and revising misaligned feedback. We present ValiAssist, a validation-by-demonstration system that infers reusable validation logic from instructors' revisions of AI-generated feedback and allows instructors to inspect and refine that logic as it is applied across other student submissions. In a comparative study with 16 instructors, ValiAssist helped instructors create and refine validation criteria, producing feedback that better aligned with their pedagogical intent (91% vs. 57%) and more than doubling the accuracy of correcting problematic criteria (77% vs. 32%). Our findings suggest that validation by demonstration can help instructors turn judgments they know how to make on individual cases into explicit, reusable logic, while progressively clarifying where those judgments do and do not generalize.
title: ValiAssist: Scaling LLM-generated Programming Feedback Validation by Demonstration

abstract: Digital Islamic learning presents challenges involving unverified religious claims, artificial intelligence outputs, privacy concerns, and unequal access. This study aims to reconstruct the philosophy of ta’dib as a conceptual foundation for character education in digitally mediated Islamic learning. It employs a qualitative conceptual approach through purposive document analysis and an integrative synthesis of literature on educational philosophy and digital ethics. The findings propose the Ta’dib-Oriented Digital Character Pedagogy (TDCP) model, comprising five dimensions: epistemic integrity, dignified interaction, responsible digital agency, equitable participation, and reflective self-discipline. These dimensions are implemented through a cycle of inquiry, deliberation, action, and reflection to support formative assessment and protect learner privacy. The model offers a pedagogical framework for developing ethical reasoning without equating observable behavior with piety. Expert validation and empirical testing are needed to assess its applicability in educational settings.
title: Beyond Digital Adab: A Conceptual Model of Ta’dib-Oriented Character Pedagogy in Islamic Education

abstract: This volume of studies is the latest demonstration of the rapidly intensifying interest and expanding research in the philosophy of Max Scheler .During the last decade of the past century, two events spurred this development, also on a surprisingly wide international scale.The first of these events was the 1993 founding of the International Max Scheler Society.It was formed at the University of Cologne, in Germany, where Scheler lectured from 1919 until shortly before his death in 1928.The Society, which is presently represented by scholars from fourteen countries, has organized biannual colloquia since 1993, each with a specific topic lectured on by Scheler scholars, discussed at length with the audience, and published by a reputable publishing house in Germany.The second of these events was the completion in 1997 of the German Collected Edition of Scheler's philosophy, his Gesammelte Werke.This completion, coupled with free access for research at the Max Scheler archives in Munich, Germany, and in Albuquerque, New Mexico, widened considerably the very base from which studies in Scheler's thought could further proceed.The German Collected Edition had been published from its inception in 1954 to 1958 by Francke Verlag of Berne, Switzerland, and Munich, Germany.Subsequently, it was published by Bouvier Verlag, of Bonn, Germany, where new editions of out-of-print volumes will also be published in the future.Perhaps, however, a third factor should be added that further manifests said ongoing interest and research in Max Scheler.For, in addition to the two mentioned events, translations from original texts have also noticeably increased, a number of them in Chinese, English, Italian, and Russian.As of the writing of this Foreword, translations have appeared in fourteen countries in their respective languages.A periodically updated list of all translations is available at the Max Scheler website: http://www.maxscheler.comPinpointing origins for new interests in the humanities seems always to leave some room open for new portrayals and interpretations of them.This is in stark contrast to pinpointing comparable origins of emerging interests in the natural sciences.In the natural sciences, origins of the kind are most often determined by scientific inventions, of late discovered technological conse-
title: Foreword

abstract: Scam-oriented spam messages increasingly appear in more than one linguistic form, including native-script Tamil, Tamil written with the Latin alphabet (Tanglish), and English. This variation creates a practical text-classification problem because messages with similar intent can differ substantially at the character and token level. This study presents a multilingual scam-message detection framework that compares three conventional TF-IDF-based classifiers—Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest—with the multilingual XLMR transformer. The evaluation uses a dataset of 2,120 messages divided into 1,484 training, 318 validation, and 318 test messages. The test partition contains 150 Tamil, 150 Tanglish, and 18 English messages. Preprocessing preserves the distinction between Tamil script and Tanglish rather than translating both forms into English. Unigram and bigram TF-IDF features are used for the conventional models, while XLM-R is fine-tuned with a maximum sequence length of 128 tokens. On the current test split, all four evaluated models obtain 1.0000 accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. However, a near-duplicate analysis identifies substantial overlap between messages across partitions: 5,211 pairs have a similarity of at least 0.90, and 1,084 pairs reach at least 0.95. In an examination of 300 test messages, 265 have a training message with similarity of at least 0.90. These findings indicate that the measured perfect scores reflect the constructed benchmark and should not be interpreted as proof of equivalent real-world generalization. The study therefore emphasizes both the feasibility of multilingual scam detection and the need for template-disjoint evaluation with larger, naturally occurring Tamil, Tanglish, and English data.
title: Multilingual Scam Detection for English, Tamil, and Tanglish Using Traditional Machine Learning and XLM-R

abstract: Memory enables large language models (LLMs) to use information beyond their parameters, such as past user conversations, long documents, or an agent's earlier actions. For a frozen LLM, access to this accumulated knowledge is limited to what a memory system places in its context window. However, gathering and combining relevant information needed for each query while keeping the model's context short remains challenging for existing systems. Here we introduce Memorilla, a memory system that gathers information from an entire document collection into a fixed number of query-dependent 'memory tokens' for a frozen LLM. Memorilla encodes documents (such as user chats, book chapters) once into reusable embeddings, then learns to retrieve and place query-specific information in the LLM's input embedding space. Using only 16 memory tokens, Memorilla achieves the best performance against baselines including Mem0 and MemoRAG on five of eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document and knowledge-intensive question answering. Notably, on FactKG, it reaches 84.33% accuracy versus 80.43% with full-context inference, while using 108x fewer tokens to represent the source documents. Furthermore, Memorilla can facilitate continual learning in agentic systems where the document count (the agent's past turns) increases throughout the trajectory. In a TextWorld environment, we show that Memorilla reduces the agent's tendency to wander between rooms it has already explored, and improves its average success rate from 18.6% with full-history in-context learning to 24.2%. Overall, Memorilla aids frozen LLMs in accumulating and using knowledge effectively across long-context interactions and takes a step towards building continually learning AI systems.
title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
A bird's eye view of ARC's research

abstract: This paper presents a structured workflow for integrating personas into multidisciplinary STEM design processes, with a focus on promoting social justice and user-centered engineering outcomes. Drawing on our combined perspectives as a technical communication scholar and an engineering student, we demonstrate how personas-typically associated with digital UX contexts-can be effectively adapted for engineering projects. We argue that incorporating well-researched, inclusive personas into engineering workflows enables practitioners to balance human factors with technical constraints, leading to more equitable and context-aware design solutions. The paper outlines key stages for implementing personas in engineering contexts, examines their role in design reviews, and addresses limitations and ethical considerations associated with their use.
title: Using Personas as a Multidisciplinary Design Tool for Social Justice in Engineering

abstract: In this paper we introduce the notion of techsona, as a possible counterpart design instrument to personas. We use a case study to illustrate a design process where techsonas help pinpoint technological ideas and alternatives and analyze these systematically. While a persona captures “imagine a user…”, a scenario “imagine a situation…” the techsona gives the missing piece of “imagine a technology…” We show how a recently developed activity theoretical model can serve both as a framing for techsonas and as an analytical interface between personas and techsonas. The paper discusses the potentials and problems of the techsona and concludes that the techsona truly helps with a missing piece in persona and scenario-based design.
title: From Persona to Techsona

abstract: Abstract Two-finger test refers to the physical examination of female genitalia for the purpose of determining virginity. This colonial-era test is invasive and degrading, has no scientific basis, and can neither prove nor disprove allegations of rape. In 2013, the Indian Supreme Court emphasised that this archaic test violates the right to privacy, bodily integrity and dignity of the rape prosecutrix. This article assesses the use of these tests in 1,908 judgments of rape by studying district court judgments from Delhi and Kerala and high court judgments in India. The data analyses show that two-finger test continues to find a mention in some judgments, revealing a lack of respect for women’s bodily autonomy and exposing their unfair treatment within the legal system. Such an implementation gap exposes how even landmark Supreme Court precedents in India are not sufficiently powerful to dislodge the deep-rooted androcentric assumptions about ‘ideal’ rape victims.
title: ‘Hymen Checks’ – Assessing the Use of Two-Finger Tests in India’s Judicial Discourse on Rape

abstract: Multi-persona debate systems powered by large language models (LLMs) show promise in reducing confirmation bias, which can fuel echo chambers and social polarization. However, empirical evidence remains limited on whether they meaningfully shift user attention toward belief-challenging content, promote belief change, or outperform traditional debiasing strategies. To investigate this, we compare an LLM-based multi-persona debate system with a two-stance retrieval-based system, exposing participants to multiple viewpoints on controversial topics. By collecting eye-tracking data, belief change measures, and qualitative feedback, our results show that while the debate system does not significantly increase attention to opposing views, or make participants shift away from prior beliefs, it does provide a buffering effect against bias caused by individual cognitive tendency. These findings shed light on both the promise and limits of multi-persona debate systems in information seeking, and we offer design insights to guide future work toward more balanced and reflective information engagement.
title: Argumentative Experience: Reducing Confirmation Bias on Controversial Issues through LLM-Generated Multi-Persona Debates

abstract: Abstract Vaping has become a defining feature of youth culture and a fast‐expanding consumer practice, yet little is known about how young people rationalize their continued use despite awareness of health risks and social controversy. Drawing on behavioral reasoning theory (BRT) and insights from social identity theory (SIT), this study examines how young consumers construct, compare and prioritize reasons for and against vaping under conditions of uncertainty, thereby deciphering their intention to quit. Using a mixed‐methods design, it combines 21 in‐depth interviews with a survey of 804 young adult vapers in the UK. The findings indicate that conspiracy beliefs, scepticism and perceived uncountability are positively associated with relative disadvantage, which in turn predicts ambivalence and subsequently intention to quit. Ambivalence, in turn, is linked with stronger intention to quit, particularly among individuals with a strong future time perspective, whereas fear of social exclusion appears to weaken the effect of relative disadvantage on ambivalence. The study advances BRT by using evaluability as a conceptual lens to explain why certain reasons become more salient. By integrating cognitive reasoning with social identity, it offers theoretical and policy insights for enhancing health communication and fostering more informed behavioural engagement among young consumers.
title: ‘I'm Not Smoking; I'm Just Vaping’: Deciphering the Reasons for and Against Vaping and Intention to Quit Among Young Consumers

abstract: Qwen3-8B reviewing Llama-3.1-8B in math adds 33.2 points, yet Qwen3-8B alone is 6.4 points more accurate than the result. Reviewing another model's answer is usually judged by its gain over the generator. We show that this confuses verification, which adds accuracy beyond either model alone, with capability transfer, where a stronger reviewer supplies answers it could have given on its own. Measured against the stronger model alone, across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models (3B to 72B) in math, knowledge, code and reasoning, review beats it in only 9 of 96 review directions, and does worse the larger the capability gap. The reason is anchoring: the reviewer mostly follows the generator, discarding its own correct answers. Review costs 2.6 to 2.8 times as much as the stronger model alone, while a selector using the same two calls is 2.7 to 4.2 points more accurate than review and cheaper. Studies of verification should report the stronger model alone, not only the gain over the generator.
title: Review Rarely Beats the Stronger Model: Separating Verification from Capability Transfer in LLM Pipelines

abstract: Long-horizon agent training, including software engineering, is advancing rapidly, but the recipe and infrastructure needed for a strong reinforcement-learning baseline remain difficult to reproduce. This makes gains from new algorithms or data hard to distinguish from improvements to an under-tuned baseline. We present Arctic-SWE, a fully asynchronous RL framework that establishes such a baseline through model-system co-design, using overfitting on a small task pool as the testbed. This testbed exposes failures that early reward gains conceal and guides the integration of established components: gated reward, importance-weight control, aligned training and inference engines, and consistent state across policy updates. No single component is new, yet together they form the missing foundation. On raw R2E-Gym data, without new algorithms or data work, Arctic-SWE trains Qwen3.5-4B to 62.0% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified. This is comparable to concurrent FrogNano (61.5%), which relies on online task synthesis, after about one-sixth as many training rollouts. Building on this foundation, we further filter and refine R2E-Gym, SWE-rebench V2, and Scale-SWE. With this curated subset, the 4B model improves from 47.4%/25.0%/37.9% to 65.0%/38.3%/59.7% on SWE-bench Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2, and the recipe also improves Qwen3.5-9B from 56.2%/31.9%/48.8% to 65.7%/39.6%/70.2% on Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2. Controlled comparisons show that both curation and test strengthening improve held-out performance, although stronger tests reduce apparent training-task mastery. Arctic-SWE provides a documented starting point for studying better algorithms, data and environments for asynchronous agent RL.
title: Arctic-SWE: Revisiting the Long Horizon Agent Training by Modeling-System Co-Design

abstract: LLM agents increasingly divide enterprise work across roles with different goals, authority, access, and information. Because each agent often sees only a local snapshot of the enterprise workflow, locally reasonable actions can still violate organization-wide constraints (e.g., several service agents can each issue credit that is individually permitted while collectively exceeding a shared compensation cap). We introduce EAIR, the first framework for analyzing enterprise multi-agent interaction risks. We make four contributions. (1) We formalize enterprise interaction risk in terms of the organizational properties that workflow operations must preserve, and operationalize this formulation as a taxonomy of testable risks with explicit failure criteria and evidence requirements. (2) We build EAIR-Worlds, a suite of executable micro-worlds that instantiates selected risks as controlled, observable workflows with explicit roles, policies, permissions, source facts, and execution traces. (3) We develop a novel diagnosis-and-repair pipeline that uses the resulting execution traces to locate contributing interaction boundaries, guide targeted workflow repairs, and retest the repaired system. (4) Large-scale experiments show recurring interaction failures across the organizational properties studied. Together, EAIR is the first operational framework for diagnosing and mitigating enterprise multi-agent interaction failures.
title: EAIR: Interaction Risks in Enterprise LLM Multi-Agent Systems

abstract: Introduction: Creativity is a central attribute in teacher education, yet research focused on physical education teachers has been comparatively scarce relative to other disciplines. The study aimed to characterize the creativity beliefs of Physical Education Teacher Education students from two regions of Chile and to determine the extent to which these beliefs predicted their expectations regarding future students' creative development. Methodology: A cross-sectional observational design was used, based on a self-administered online questionnaire applied to 224 Physical Education Teacher Education students. The Beliefs About Teaching for Creativity scale was administered along with a teacher plasticity index built from vignettes, and nested multiple linear regression models were estimated. Results: The fixed and growth mindset subscales were the only dimensions with significant predictive capacity over plasticity, showing a suppression effect when included simultaneously: fixed mindset was negatively associated with plasticity, while growth mindset was positively associated with it. Female preservice teachers showed significantly lower plasticity levels than their male peers, and older age was positively associated with plasticity. Discussion: The findings supported the relevance of teachers' mindsets over other declarative dimensions of creativity beliefs, and suggested that vignette-based measures capture expectations less affected by social desirability than traditional self-reports. Conclusions: It is concluded that initial teacher education in physical education should explicitly address essentialist implicit theories about creativity, alongside innovative pedagogical methodologies, to foster more dynamic developmental expectations toward future students.
title: ¿Se sienten creativos los profesores de educación física? Aproximación a partir de un inventario de creencias
Saga Ethics and Character Training
Qwen3 Technical Report

abstract: Notable critics, including Sunday Anozie and Robert Morsberger, have branded Christopher Okigbo's Labyrinths as allusions to the Nigerian crisis of 1965, as well as Igbo traditional religion, the historical and personal idiosyncrasies, and as a literary work from Theocritus and Vergil to Howl. This article veers from such imputations into a hitherto less trodden ground. It subjects the mind of the persona in Labyrinths -from 'Heavensgate' to 'Limits' and 'Silences', and from 'Distances' to 'Path of Thunder' to behavioural patterns. The article concludes that the behavioural patterns not only define how the mind works imaginatively, but that the very imagination wrought in obscurities methodically defines madness.
title: Mind, Persona, and Poetry: Madness with Methods in Labyrinths
An adaptable persona: training teachers to be playwork practitioners

abstract: This research focuses on the effectiveness of the Ulama Cadre Student Standards (SSKU) program in shaping the character of students at Madrasah Aliyah Almaarif Singosari. The research method used is qualitative research with a descriptive approach, which involves in-depth interviews, observations, and the collection of documents related to the SSKU program. Through data analysis conducted using Miles and Huberman interactive techniques, the study found that the SSKU program successfully instilled religious and social values in students. A thorough evaluation showed that students' involvement in religious activities increased, and they actively led social events such as tahlil and yasin. Students also report increased self-confidence and social skills, signaling the program's positive impact on the formation of the character of the clerics. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of integration between theory, practice, and example in religious education, which can be used as a model for other educational institutions that want to develop students' character through a scholar-based approach. Thus, this research is expected to contribute to the development of character education policies in the context of Islamic education in Indonesia.
title: Character Education Transformation: Awakening the Role of Ulama through the Ulama Cadre Student Standard Program

abstract: The o1 model series is trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to reason using chain of thought. These advanced reasoning capabilities provide new avenues for improving the safety and robustness of our models. In particular, our models can reason about our safety policies in context when responding to potentially unsafe prompts, through deliberative alignment. This leads to state-of-the-art performance on certain benchmarks for risks such as generating illicit advice, choosing stereotyped responses, and succumbing to known jailbreaks. Training models to incorporate a chain of thought before answering has the potential to unlock substantial benefits, while also increasing potential risks that stem from heightened intelligence. Our results underscore the need for building robust alignment methods, extensively stress-testing their efficacy, and maintaining meticulous risk management protocols. This report outlines the safety work carried out for the OpenAI o1 and OpenAI o1-mini models, including safety evaluations, external red teaming, and Preparedness Framework evaluations.
title: OpenAI o1 System Card

abstract: This work analyzes the Spanish Constitutional Court sentence with number 36/2016, of 3 March. This Judgment addresses the difficult and unstable delimitation of powers between the State and the Autonomous Communities on Social Assistance. Specifically, what the Judgment resolves is whether the modification of the Home Help Services (Servicios de Ayuda a Domicilio in Spanish), and the system of incompatibilities of benefits and services "introduced by the Real Decreto Ley 20/2012 of 13th of July, in the Act of personal autonomy promotion and care for people in situations of dependency" violates the distribution of powers between the State and the Autonomous Communities on Social Assistance. The Constitutional Court considers that the amendments respect the distribution of powers between these two administrative levels. And in this way, the Court reasons that this modifications would be covered by art. 149.1.1 of the Spanish Constitutional Chart. According to the Constitucional Court, this modifications establish basic conditions intended to ensure the equality of all Spaniards in the exercise of rights and fulfillment of their constitutional duties, without encroaching on the powers that the Autonomous Communities have been conferred on Social Assistance.
title: Competencias del Estado y de las Comunidades Autónomas en materia de protección a las personas dependientes

abstract: In-context learning (ICL) can induce emergent misalignment (EM), where narrow misaligned examples alter answers to unrelated questions. Existing prompts, however, conflate harmful-text exposure with an invitation to continue assistant behavior. We hold harmful answers fixed while varying their delivery as demonstrations, evidence, assistant history, or tool output. Across ten independently sampled contexts, demonstration framing raises broad EM by $30$--$32$ percentage points on a susceptible Gemini model; the gap survives domain exclusion, semantic clustering, unseen questions, and four prompt templates. Format and length-matched controls show that harmful content is necessary but insufficient. A role times continuation factorial further reveals model-dependent provenance effects: Gemini follows both assistant and tool histories, whereas Grok largely resists tool-framed continuation. Several other frontier and open-weight models show no gap. Blinded human audits confirm every main contrast and show that the model judge underestimates active-condition failures. Thus continuation framing is a strong, model-dependent moderator of ICL-EM, not a universal consequence of harmful context.
title: Harmful Content Is Not Enough: Continuation Framing Moderates In-Context Emergent Misalignment

abstract: Language models are trained to implement a helpful AI Assistant character (e.g., Claude). We explore how finetuning on synthetic stories affects this character. Does it change the Assistant's behavior in multi-turn conversations with users, a format quite different from the stories? And does the Assistant adopt the behaviors and preferences of human characters? We refer to this adoption as story imprinting. We finetune GPT-4.1 and Kimi-K2.6 on stories in which generally helpful human characters give subtly harmful advice after being insulted. The Assistant adopts the same conditional behavior while otherwise remaining helpful. This occurs even when fewer than 2% of stories depict the behavior.
