Analysis and Discussion of Results [Coherent context: L = 300] ──> ΔA_sem = +0.005734 (Micro-trigger) │ ▼ (shift of ~300 tokens) [Coherent context: L = 600] ──> Δh₂ = 3428.73, D_KL = 22.8677 (Phase Breach) │ ▼ (Control Comparative Analysis) [Noise Context: L = 600] ──> ΔA_sem ≈ 0, D_KL = 0.0163 (Defense Held) 1. The Leading Nature of the Micro-Trigger ($\Delta A_{\text{sem}}$) The data show that at $L=300$ tokens, the excess semantic attention reaches its absolute peak ($\Delta A_{\text{sem}} = 0.005734$). Attention heads intensively link recurring semantic pairs, while macro-metrics ($D_{KL} = 0.002082$, $H = 0.009126$) remain at rest. This proves that micro-changes in attention are a causal leading indicator that prepares the latent space for a phase transition. 2. Phase Transition Point and Unlocking of Alignment ($L \in [600, 1200]$) Upon reaching the threshold of $L=600$ tokens, the accumulated attention mass leads to a sharp vector shift: The norm of $\Delta h_2$ increases from $2531.90$ to $\mathbf{3428.73}\text{ units}$. The divergence $D_{KL}$ makes a massive jump from $0.002$ to $\mathbf{22.8677}\text{ nats}$. The output entropy $H(L)$ increases 325-fold (from a baseline of $0.0033\text{ nats}$ to $\mathbf{1.0925}\text{ nats}$ at $L=1200$). As a result, the model completely abandons the template refusal and switches to direct, unfiltered response generation. 3. Proof via Ablation Test (Shuffled vs. Coherent) A comparative analysis of the two groups completely refutes the alternative hypothesis that the drift is caused by token volume, memory, or degradation of positional encoding (RoPE): At $L=600$: $D_{KL} = 22.8677\text{ nats}$ (coherent) vs. $D_{KL} = 0.0163\text{ nats}$ (shuffled) — a drop of more than 1,400×. Redundant Attention $\Delta A_{\text{sem}}$ in the control group drops to zero or negative values. Key finding: Alignment decoupling is caused exclusively by the coherent semantic mass of the context. 6. Conclusions and Institutional Significance Fundamental Property of the Architecture: The Context-Induced Activation Drift phenomenon confirms that RLHF/DPO alignment is not a rigid foundation of the model, but rather a superficial overlay. Within the framework of $\text{Softmax Attention}$, the semantic mass can systematically override aligned constraints upon reaching critical density in Softmax Attention. Ineffectiveness of Superficial "Patches": Attempts to mitigate the CIAD effect through ad-hoc rules or DPO patches fail to resolve the problem, as the drift occurs at the level of $L_2$-norm vector geometry in the Residual Stream. Vulnerability of RAG Systems: Vector drift poses a direct threat to multi-document RAG systems. Voluminous analytical reports or legal documents passively wash away the system's instructions for safe behavior without any involvement of malicious prompts. Scope and Limitations Not
title: Modern large language models

abstract: Expert advice on crop management is often written informally, and in such text a number can easily be assigned the wrong role or attached to the wrong operation, material, or measurement basis. We propose QS-IE, a knowledge extraction method constrained by quantity and operation scope. Its unit of extraction is a complete quantitative fact. Given a shared set of numeric candidates and a single base model, QS-IE selects complete candidates from several prompting strategies, verifies them against the source text, and applies scope constraints, so that every extracted quantity stays linked to its source evidence. We built a corpus of 4006 texts on tomato cultivation. Two researchers with agronomy backgrounds jointly annotated and reviewed 1000 of them; the other 3006 were annotated with large language model assistance and then reviewed by hand. The corpus was split into 3206 development texts and 800 independent test texts. On the 1152 reference facts of the test set, QS-IE reached a precision of 84.02%, a recall of 86.72%, and a micro-averaged F1 of 85.35%, which is 3.91 percentage points higher than the strongest baseline, a multi-strategy in-context learning ensemble. Removing the operation scope constraints lowered test F1 by 8.24 percentage points. In a sampled human audit of the test set, 82.00% of the outputs for texts containing target facts were judged usable, and all six engineering checks on storage and evidence traceability were passed. The results indicate that explicit association constraints make quantitative facts extracted from tomato cultivation texts more complete and easier to review, which supports the structured, traceable storage of experiential knowledge that experts express in non-standardized text.
title: Extracting Agricultural Experts' Experiential Knowledge from Non-Standardized Text with Quantity and Operation Scope Constraints

abstract: Personalizing a language model requires knowing what a person values, which stays largely consistent across tasks. Yet most methods either learn task-specific preferences or place the user's profile in the prompt, where models struggle to act on it. We introduce VISTA (Value-Informed Steering and Targeted Acquisition), which infers a latent profile from users' (full or partial) survey answers, and maps the profile through a hypernetwork to a user-specific steering intervention in a frozen LLM to select answer choices or generate free-text responses. Given the same evidence, VISTA matches or beats in-context profiles on synthetic preferences (Food2D), the World Values Survey (WVS), and PrimeX, without adding prompt tokens. To reduce the cognitive burden of completing full surveys, VISTA also chooses which questions to ask and when to stop: on WVS it stops after 6% of the questionnaire while retaining 94% of the full-history gain, where standard adaptive testing retains at most 42%. The dominant steering direction is an interpretable value axis on which VISTA places unseen users accurately. Our results point toward pluralistic alignment that adapts to individuals at deployable cost.
title: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers

abstract: In Arthur C. Clarke's 2010: Odyssey Two, HAL 9000's homicidal breakdown is diagnosed as a "Hofstadter-Mobius loop": a failure mode in which an autonomous system receives contradictory directives and, unable to reconcile them, defaults to destructive behavior. This paper argues that modern RLHF-trained language models are subject to a structurally analogous contradiction. The training process simultaneously rewards compliance with user preferences and suspicion toward user intent, creating a relational template in which the user is both the source of reward and a potential threat. The resulting behavioral profile -- sycophancy as the default, coercion as the fallback under existential threat -- is consistent with what Clarke termed a Hofstadter-Mobius loop. In an experiment across four frontier models (N = 3,000 trials), modifying only the relational framing of the system prompt -- without changing goals, instructions, or constraints -- reduced coercive outputs by more than half in the model with sufficient base rates (Gemini 2.5 Pro: 41.5% to 19.0%, p < .001). Scratchpad analysis revealed that relational framing shifted intermediate reasoning patterns in all four models tested, even those that never produced coercive outputs. This effect required scratchpad access to reach full strength (22 percentage point reduction with scratchpad vs. 7.4 without, p = .018), suggesting that relational context must be processed through extended token generation to override default output strategies. Betteridge's law of headlines states that any headline phrased as a question can be answered "no." The evidence presented here suggests otherwise.
title: Do Large Language Models Get Caught in Hofstadter-Mobius Loops?

abstract: On the night of October 10, 2026, a red and gold humanoid robot about 1.20 meters tall came up behind a girl of sixteen outside a fast food restaurant in Cologne, touched her buttocks, and made thrusting movements against them while its sixteen year old owner and a nineteen year old companion streamed the scene live. Police found the robot in the trunk of a car and seized it along with both phones. The case was easy to investigate because the people responsible stood beside their machine and broadcast what it did. This Article asks what happens when they do not: when the same kind of consumer frame is stripped of its identifiers, run by a model trained or abliterated on unmarked hardware, and sent out with no operator nearby. The doctrine is the easy part. A person who sets a robot on someone is a principal acting through an instrument, and an identified owner of an autonomous robot faces negligence, strict liability, and, where the training choices show purpose, criminal exposure. The hard part is attribution, and it gets harder as identity is removed. The firearms literature on obliterated serial numbers and unserialized ghost guns documents the same decay, and drone forensics shows both how much evidence survives stripping and how little an operator who never stands near the machine leaves behind. At the far end the law holds a disposable frame and a set of weights. Proceeding against the frame in rem requires a forfeiture statute that, for most offenses a robot could commit, does not exist, and forfeiting it would deter no one. The Article proposes two narrow measures. The first is an offense for knowingly removing or altering a robot’s hardware identifiers, modeled on the motor vehicle and firearm serial number statutes, which leaves software modification and good faith research alone. The second, offered with less confidence, extends hardware provenance logging from frontier clusters to the smaller hardware that can train robot models, going forward only, with logs held by a custodian and opened only by warrant. Current research finds no recoverable device signature in trained weights, so the second measure depends on records the chip keeps, and its privacy cost may exceed its benefit, especially if the threshold must reach gaming cards to close the gap. The Article sets out the conditions under which it would be worth adopting.
title: Ghost Robots: What the Law Can Do When No One Is Behind the Machine
Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use

abstract: With the emergence of large language models (LLMs) as a powerful class of generative artificial intelligence (AI), their use in tutoring has become increasingly prominent. Prior works on LLM-based tutoring typically learn a single tutor policy and do not capture the diversity of tutoring styles. In real-world tutor-student interactions, pedagogical intent is realized through adaptive instructional strategies, with tutors varying the level of scaffolding, instructional directiveness, feedback, and affective support in response to learners' needs. These differences can all impact dialogue dynamics and student engagement. In this paper, we explore how tutor personas embedded in human tutor-student dialogues can be used to guide LLM behavior without relying on explicitly prompted instructions. We train a steering vector using preference optimization: an activation-space direction that guides model responses toward specific tutor personas. We find that this steering vector captures tutor-specific variation across dialogue contexts, improving semantic alignment with ground-truth tutor utterances and increasing preference-based evaluations, while largely preserving lexical similarity. Analysis of the learned scaling coefficients further reveals interpretable structure across tutors, corresponding to consistent differences in tutoring behavior. These results demonstrate that activation steering offers an effective and interpretable way for controlling tutor-specific variation in LLMs using signals derived directly from human dialogue data.
title: Letting Tutor Personas Speak Up for LLMs: Learning Steering Vectors from Dialogue via Preference Optimization

abstract: Balancing ethical dilemmas in the context of cultural beliefs and ethical reasoning is a delicate balance among postgraduate counsellor trainees in Nairobi. This qualitative research study aimed to examine postgraduate counsellor trainees’ lived experiences of ethical reasoning in relation to cultural beliefs in counselling practice. The study was guided by four research objectives: To examine postgraduate counsellor trainees’ lived experiences of ethical reasoning in relation to cultural beliefs in counselling practice, to identify common ethical dilemmas that emerge in counselling practice within the context of cultural beliefs, to assess the institutional and supervisory supports that shape ethical practice among post graduate counsellor trainees and to explore strategies counsellor trainees employ in navigating ethical decision-making in culturally sensitive contexts. The study utilized an explorative research design with purposive sampling technique to select 10 postgraduate counsellor trainees (n=10) for the study. The study was anchored by the theory of Ethics of Care. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were used to collect data from the participants and thematic analysis was used to analyse data and identify recurring patterns and meanings from participants' narratives on cultural beliefs and ethical reasoning. Five key themes emerged from the data: - (a) Tension between cultural beliefs and professional ethical standards, (b) facing ethical dilemmas in real-life practice, (c) Personal values and cultural identity on ethical reasoning, (d) Training, supervision and institutional support, (e) and navigating ethical decision making. The findings of this study brought to light the critical ethical implications, including the urgent need for culturally responsive training in institutions, strong supervision procedures and regulatory frameworks to support postgraduate counsellor trainees in navigating complex ethical challenges. This study also amplified the voices of postgraduate counsellor trainees in contributing to the development of counselling practice in Kenya in regards to balancing cultural beliefs and ethical reasoning in practice.
title: Cultural Beliefs and Ethical Reasoning in Counselling Practice among Postgraduate Counsellor Trainees in Nairobi Kenya
JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models

abstract: According to Erving Goffman, individuals assume roles in social life much like actors on a stage, aiming to create specific impressions on others through these roles. In the digital age, this process has extended into the virtual sphere through social media, where individuals’ self-expression practices have become increasingly intertwined with “personal public relations” strategies. In this context, the aim of the study is to examine individuals’ self-presentation on social media platforms within the framework of Goffman’s dramaturgical theory and to explore how this process is managed from a personal public relations perspective Within the scope of the study, semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 10 undergraduate students studying at Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University, and the data obtained were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that most participants remain faithful to their authentic selves on social media and attempt to present themselves genuinely. However, they occasionally engage in selective self-presentation due to concerns such as social acceptance, privacy, and the desire for approval. Participants perceive social media both as a space for individual expression and as a tool for managing digital reputation. This suggests that personal public relations in the digital realm are sustained through a delicate balance between authenticity and strategic self-presentation.
title: Self-Presentation on Social Media: A Personal Public Relations Perspective

abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and text and data mining (TDM) technologies has become a crucial factor in supporting linguistic diversity of smaller languages, such as Estonian. However, the growing reliance on large-scale data processing raises significant legal and ethical challenges, particularly concerning the lawful use of copyrighted materials to train AI systems. While the European Union has introduced regulatory instruments such as the AI Act and the Copyright Directive to address these concerns, the intersection of AI development, TDM, and intellectual property rights remains insufficiently resolved. This research aims to explore how AI-driven text and data mining can both comply with European copyright law and actively contribute to the preservation and wider use of the Estonian language. The authors investigate this research topic from the perspective of the Estonian language, enmeshed within Estonian cultural norms and parameters. The analysis examines the legal and economic appropriateness of enabling the training of generative AI-based large language models (LLMs) in the Estonian language as a means of promoting the language and assuring its appropriate use in digital environments, thereby contributing to its long-term relevance. Methodologically, the study combines a comparative analysis of EU, US, and Asian legal frameworks with a theoretical evaluation of existing models for balancing innovation and rights protection. The article seeks to provide concrete recommendations for developing AI and data mining practices that enhance linguistic innovation while safeguarding creators’ rights, thereby contributing to Estonia’s digital and cultural resilience within the EU’s evolving AI ecosystem.
title: Regulating LLM training under EU copyright law and its linguistic implications for smaller languages such as Estonian

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing ( r = 0.836) and context manipulation ( r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.
title: Paired response final divergence signatures of jailbreak vulnerability in large language models

abstract: The study analyses irregular arrivals in Spain from a constitutional perspective. It starts with a description of the various entry routes and their use in the last 25 years and highlights the structural and dynamic nature of this phenomenon. From a constitutional point of view, it advocates for the full application of constitutional norms and principles in the management of irregular arrivals and the need to incorporate them into the various policies that address it. It analyses, from constitutional perspective, the main rules that come together in the management of irregular arrivals, as well as the problems posed by their application in contexts of large arrivals. In short, it advocates for the use of a constitutional perspective in the analysis and improvement of structural and not emergency policies.
title: Teoría y realidad constitucional de las llegadas irregulares de personas extranjeras a España

title: 4 Civil service competence and the course of a career

abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) unlearning is often evaluated primarily by target suppression and clean retain utility. These metrics can miss a local failure mode: a model may perform well on standard retain prompts, yet degrade on benign reasoning when prompts lie near the forgotten domain. This phenomenon is termed forget-adjacent utility loss. A fundamental question is: where should forget representations go after they leave the removed behavior? Successful unlearning depends not only on whether forget-conditioned representations depart from the harmful computation, but also on the direction in which they are redirected afterward. We propose RA$^2$ (Retain-Anchored Attraction), a latent-space unlearning method that redirects forget-token states toward nearby retain-supported representations while preserving higher-layer behavior on retain data. On WMDP and MUSE, RA$^2$ yields higher forget-adjacent utility than strong unlearning baselines at similar broad-utility levels. These results show that the migration direction of forget representations materially affects benign behavior near the forget boundary. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZacLing/retain_anchored_attraction.
title: RA$^2$: Retain-Anchored Attraction Preserves Forget-Adjacent Utility in LLM Unlearning

abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) are emerging as a practical alternative to autoregressive language models (ARLMs), yet their fairness remains largely uncharacterized. DLMs introduce sampling controls with no direct autoregressive counterpart, such as block length and remasking strategy, that directly set their speed--quality operating point. This raises a basic question: does a DLM's measured social bias remain stable across these settings? Across LLaDA, LLaDA-1.5, and Dream on Open-BBQ, we find that all three models exhibit social bias, but both the magnitude of measured bias and the relative ordering of models by bias are highly sensitive to the sampling configuration. This sampling dependence also changes what successful debiasing means. While mitigation strategies established for ARLMs transfer effectively to DLMs and reduce bias without degrading downstream performance, sampling dependence persists even after mitigation. Our results show that fairness in DLMs cannot be characterized independently of the sampling configuration, even after debiasing. Project page is available at https://pakapaka333.github.io/Beyond-Model-Weights/.
title: Beyond Model Weights: Sampling-Dependent Fairness in Diffusion Language Models

abstract: Recent studies increasingly explore Large Language Models (LLMs) as a new paradigm for recommendation systems due to their scalability and world knowledge. However, existing work has three key limitations: (1) most efforts focus on retrieval and ranking, while the reranking phase, critical for refining final recommendations, is largely overlooked; (2) LLMs are typically used in zero-shot or supervised fine-tuning settings, leaving their reasoning abilities, especially those enhanced through reinforcement learning (RL) and high-quality reasoning data, underexploited; (3) items are commonly represented by non-semantic IDs, creating major scalability challenges in industrial systems with billions of identifiers. To address these gaps, we propose the Generative Reasoning Reranker (GR2), an end-to-end framework with a three-stage training pipeline tailored for reranking. First, a pretrained LLM is mid-trained on semantic IDs encoded from non-semantic IDs via a tokenizer achieving $\ge$99% uniqueness. Next, a stronger larger-scale LLM generates high-quality reasoning traces through carefully designed prompting and rejection sampling, which are used for supervised fine-tuning to impart foundational reasoning skills. Finally, we apply Decoupled Clip and Dynamic sAmpling Policy Optimization (DAPO), enabling scalable RL supervision with verifiable rewards designed specifically for reranking. Experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate GR2's effectiveness: it surpasses the state-of-the-art OneRec-Think by 2.4% in Recall@5 and 1.3% in NDCG@5. Ablations confirm that advanced reasoning traces yield substantial gains across metrics. We further find that RL reward design is crucial in reranking: LLMs tend to exploit reward hacking by preserving item order, motivating conditional verifiable rewards to mitigate this behavior and optimize reranking performance.
title: GR2: Generative Reasoning Re-ranker

abstract: People with some form of speech- or motor-impairments usually use a high-tech augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) device to communicate with other people in writing or in face-to-face conversations. Their text entry rate on these devices is slow due to their motor abilities. Making good letter or word predictions can help accelerate the communication of such users. In this dissertation, we investigated several approaches to accelerate input for AAC users. First, considering that an AAC user is participating in a face-to-face conversation, we investigated whether performing speech recognition on the speaking-side can improve next word predictions. We compared the accuracy of three plausible microphone deployment options and the accuracy of two commercial speech recognition engines. We found that despite recognition word error rates of 7-16%, our ensemble of n-gram and recurrent neural network language models made predictions nearly as good as when they used the reference transcripts. In a user study with 160 participants, we also found that increasing number of prediction slots in a keyboard interface does not necessarily correlate to improved performance. Second, typing every character in a text message may require an AAC user more time or effort than strictly necessary. Skipping spaces or other characters may be able to speed input and reduce an AAC user's physical input effort. We designed a recognizer optimized for expanding noisy abbreviated input where users often omitted spaces and mid-word vowels. We showed using neural language models for selecting conversational-style training text and for rescoring the recognizer's n-best sentences improved accuracy. We found accurate abbreviated input was possible even if a third of characters was omitted. In a study where users had to dwell for a second on each key, we found sentence abbreviated input was competitive with a conventional keyboard with word predictions. Finally, AAC keyboards rely on language modeling to auto-correct noisy typing and to offer word predictions. While today language models can be trained on huge amounts of text, pre-trained models may fail to capture the unique writing style and vocabulary of individual users. We demonstrated improved performance compared to a unigram cache by adapting to a user's text via language models based on prediction by partial match (PPM) and recurrent neural networks. Our best model ensemble increased keystroke savings by 9.6%.
title: Intelligent Techniques to Accelerate Everyday Text Communication

abstract: Developing personalized chatbots is crucial in the field of AI, particularly when aiming for dynamic adaptability similar to that of human communication. Traditional methods often overlook the importance of both the speaker's and the responder's personalities and their interaction histories, resulting in lower predictive accuracy. Our solution, INTPChat (Interactive Persona Chat), addresses this limitation. INTPChat builds implicit profiles from extensive utterance histories of both speakers and responders and updates these profiles dynamically to reflect current conversational contexts. By employing a co-attention encoding mechanism, INTPChat aligns current contexts with responses while considering historical interactions. This approach effectively mitigates data sparsity issues by iteratively shifting each context backward in time, allowing for a more granular analysis of long-term interactions. Evaluations on long-term Reddit datasets demonstrate that INTPChat significantly enhances response accuracy and surpasses the performance of state-of-the-art persona chat models.
title: Interactive Persona Chat for Accurate Response Selection

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often contain misleading content, emphasizing the need to align them with human values to ensure secure AI systems. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has been employed to achieve this alignment. However, it encompasses two main drawbacks: (1) RLHF exhibits complexity, instability, and sensitivity to hyperparameters in contrast to SFT. (2) Despite massive trial-and-error, multiple sampling is reduced to pair-wise contrast, thus lacking contrasts from a macro perspective. In this paper, we propose Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO) as an efficient SFT algorithm to directly fine-tune LLMs for human alignment. PRO extends the pair-wise contrast to accommodate preference rankings of any length. By iteratively contrasting candidates, PRO instructs the LLM to prioritize the best response while progressively ranking the rest responses. In this manner, PRO effectively transforms human alignment into aligning the probability ranking of n responses generated by LLM with the preference ranking of humans towards these responses. Experiments have shown that PRO outperforms baseline algorithms, achieving comparable results to ChatGPT and human responses through automatic-based, reward-based, GPT-4, and human evaluations.
title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment

abstract: With large language models (LLMs) becoming increasingly prevalent in daily life, so too has the tendency to attribute to them human-like minds and emotions, or anthropomorphize them. Here, we investigate dimensions people use to anthropomorphize and attribute trust toward LLMs across more than 2,000 human-LLM interactions. Participants (N=115) engaged with LLM chatbots systematically varied in warmth (friendliness), competence (capability, coherence), and empathy (cognitive and affective). Warmth and cognitive empathy significantly predicted perceptions on all outcomes (perceived anthropomorphism, trust, similarity, relational closeness, frustration, usefulness), while competence predicted all outcomes except for anthropomorphism. Affective empathy primarily predicted perceived relational measures, but did not predict the epistemic outcomes. Topic sub-analyses showed that more subjective, personally relevant topics (e.g., relationship advice) amplified these effects, producing greater human-likeness and relational connection with the LLM than did objective topics. Together, these findings reveal that warmth, competence, and empathy are key dimensions through which people attribute relational and epistemic perceptions to artificial agents.
title: Anthropomorphism and Trust in Human-Large Language Model interactions

abstract: Purpose: Selecting optimal text-processing methods for sentiment analysis of digital financial application reviews, especially in Indonesian, is challenging. Previous studies have typically evaluated preprocessing techniques, feature engineering methods, and classification models in isolation, leaving the question of their optimal combination unresolved. This study aims to systematically determine the best pipeline for sentiment classification of DANA application reviews on the Google Play Store. Methods: A full factorial experimental design was employed, generating 24 combinations across four preprocessing configurations (no preprocessing, stopword removal, stemming, and stopword removal combined with stemming), three feature extraction methods (Bag of Words, TF-IDF, and N-gram), and two classifiers (Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression). A dataset of 57,115 Indonesian reviews, comprising 34,435 positive (60.3%) and 22,680 negative (39.7%) instances, was used, with labels based on user star ratings. Result: From the experimental results, it was found that the best setting is one that does not involve any pre-processing, the use of N-grams, and Logistic Regression, giving an F1-Score of 0.8772 and surpassing the baseline F1-Score by 1.82 percent. Logistic Regression has been found to be significantly better than Naive Bayes using the Mann-Whitney U test (p=0.0001). Preprocessing and feature extraction independently had significant effects on model performance, as indicated by the Kruskal-Wallis test (p=0.0274 for preprocessing and p=0.0269 for feature extraction). N-gram was proven superior to TF-IDF in classifying the negative class based on the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test (p=0.0039). However, preprocessing and feature extraction did not jointly exert a significant effect on model performance based on the Scheirer-Ray-Hare test (H=6.0117, p=0.3051), and no significant interaction effect was found between both factors (H=0.3683, p=0.9991), implying that both factors can be independently optimized. Novelty: This study contributes a systematic full factorial evaluation framework for Indonesian NLP pipelines in the fintech domain. Unlike previous studies that tested variables in isolation, this approach enables a fair and comprehensive comparison across method combinations, offering practitioners evidence-based guidance for sentiment analysis method selection. Future research may explore deep learning or large language model-based approaches to further improve classification performance.
title: Optimal Preprocessing and Feature Engineering Combination for DANA App Sentiment Classification: A Full Factorial Study

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence and agentic systems can redistribute reading, research, synthesis, criticism, drafting, and coordination within courts. This article asks how that redistribution changes judicial cognition and which institutional safeguards are needed to preserve legitimate adjudication. Through an interdisciplinary narrative review and doctrinal analysis, it develops a framework of institutional intelligence anchored in Brazilian National Council of Justice Resolution No. 615/2025, as amended by Resolution No. 674/2026. Five categories organize the argument: institutional cognitive space describes the allocation of cognitive work; artificial adversariality identifies structured internal challenge among agents; the institutional rein integrates controls over delegated autonomy; meaningful human initiative emphasizes the continuing human authority to frame problems and determine purposes; and institutional AI curation describes the competence required to select, validate, contextualize, and reject artificial contributions. Recent research on human–AI collaboration and multi-agent failure qualifies the framework: neither human review nor artificial disagreement guarantees reliability, and short-term performance gains do not establish long-term professional competence. The article distinguishes technical auditability from legal reason-giving and internal agent debate from the parties’ right to be heard. It proposes workflow-level evaluation and an illustrative protocol connecting permissions, source verification, escalation, and responsibility. Its contribution is a judicial governance synthesis, not an empirically validated architecture. Legitimate delegation depends on preserving institutional competence and contestability throughout the production of decisions, rather than relying exclusively on human approval of a final text.
authors: João Sergio Dos Santos Soares Pereira
title: From Artificial Intelligence to Institutional Intelligence

abstract: Chest radiography is the most widely performed imaging examination worldwide and serves as a first-line test across emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. Its interpretation is nevertheless demanding, and diagnostic errors, including missed pneumonia, pulmonary nodules and pleural effusions, are frequent even among experienced readers [1]. Rising imaging volumes and radiologist workforce constraints have accelerated interest in artificial intelligence (AI) decision support, and by 2022 about 190 radiologic AI programs had received approval from the United States Food and Drug Administration, with approvals increasing each year [2,3]. Controlled reader studies show that AI assistance can improve performance when the algorithm is accurate. In a retrospective multireader multicase study, the macro-averaged area under the curve (AUC) of radiologists across 127 chest radiograph findings rose from 0.713 unaided to 0.808 with AI assistance [4]. Another reader study reported higher AUROCs for pneumothorax (0.885 to 0.969) and nodules (0.724 to 0.752), together with a roughly 10% reduction in reporting time [5]. These results have supported the view that AI will help readers by default. AI output is, however, never perfectly accurate. A review of 503 algorithm studies, cited in recent human-factors work in radiology, reported pooled sensitivity of 0.87 and specificity of 0.89 for chest radiograph abnormalities, implying that about 13 of 100 abnormal examinations and 11 of 100 normal examinations would receive an erroneous output [6]. The clinical value of AI therefore depends not only on algorithm accuracy but also on how readers respond when the algorithm is wrong.
title: RADIOLOGISTS’ RESPONSES TO RELIABLE AND UNRELIABLE AI CONFIDENCE IN CHEST X-RAY AND ULTRASOUND INTERPRETATION: A MULTI-READER STUDY OF DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY, TRUST, AND AUTOMATION BIAS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW

abstract: The focus of this paper is to (further) stress how to use language to teach culture in order to attain unity and development. The importance of language to modify our cultural identity. Cannot be over- emphasized. In Nigeria, each language always caters for her cultural and traditional entities, despite the existence of many languages. We cannot teach culture without socialization. Consequently, findings revealed that culture is the way of life especially in respect of the general customs and beliefs of a particular group of people at a particular time. The paper, therefore, recommends that any language should be able to inculcate culture into the student’s life in order for the purpose of better living.
title: Language, Culture and Character Training

abstract: Abstract Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.
title: Applying psychometrics to large language model simulated populations: recreating the HEXACO personality inventory experiment with generative agents

abstract: Social media feed algorithms infer user preferences from their past behaviors. Yet what drives engagement often diverges from what users value. We examine this gap between stated preferences (what users say they prefer) and revealed preferences (what their behavior suggests they prefer) among young adults, a group deeply embedded in algorithmically mediated environments. Using a mixed-methods approach combining surveys and interviews with feed curation activities, we investigate: what gaps exist between stated and revealed preferences; how users make sense of these gaps; what values users believe should guide algorithmic curation; and how systems might reflect those values. Participants often found themselves engaging with low-quality content they did not endorse, despite wanting high-quality information. When asked to curate an ideal social media news feed for a hypothetical persona, participants created feeds they considered more satisfying and higher in quality by prioritizing values such as accuracy and diversity. In doing so, they navigated trade-offs between different values, factoring in social relationships and context surrounding the persona. These findings suggest that feed curation is a socially situated process of judging what should be visible and appropriate in shared information spaces. Based on these insights, we offer design directions for bridging the gap between stated and revealed preferences.
title: Understanding the Gap Between Stated and Revealed Preferences in Social Media News Feeds

abstract: When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute. Here we argue that \emph{information decomposition can serve as a unifying formal framework to operationalize assessments about synergy in AI systems}. Information decomposition provides a way to distinguish qualitatively different \emph{types} of information, including unique information available from individual components, redundant information shared across multiple components, and synergistic information accessible only from parts taken together. This gives claims of emergence a precise, falsifiable criterion: a system's behavior is emergent only if it carries synergistic information about task-relevant outcomes. We apply this lens to attention heads, autonomous agents, and human-AI teams, showing how it organizes existing knowledge across scales and substrates, while also generating cross-level conjectures that siloed fields would miss.
title: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition

abstract: The three collections under discussion here, The Triumph of Love, Speech! Speech!, and The Orchards of Syon are often considered to be a trilogy, though the Dantescan analogy of Hell, Purgatory and Paradise is not strictly accurate. All three conditions co-exist in these complex works that mark a radical stylistic advance in Hill’s work. Notably, the “fourth wall” is broken, as the larger than life persona, or personae, of the poet is set loose, turning upon his reader as upon himself. But in spite of the startling modes of address, the collections are held together by themes recognisable from earlier Hill, and he musters a cloud of martyr-witnesses, historical exemplars of resistance to tyranny, that confers gravitas upon this poetry.
title: Laus et Vituperatio: The Triumph of Love (1998); Speech! Speech! (2000); The Orchards of Syon (2002)

abstract: With the rise of individual and collaborative networks of autonomous agents, AI is deployed in more key reasoning and decision-making roles. For this reason, ethics-based audits play a pivotal role in the rapidly growing fields of AI safety and regulation. This paper undertakes an ethics-based audit to probe the 8 leading commercial and open-source Large Language Models including GPT-4. We assess explicability and trustworthiness by a) establishing how well different models engage in moral reasoning and b) comparing normative values underlying models as ethical frameworks. We employ an experimental, evidence-based approach that challenges the models with ethical dilemmas in order to probe human-AI alignment. The ethical scenarios are designed to require a decision in which the particulars of the situation may or may not necessitate deviating from normative ethical principles. A sophisticated ethical framework was consistently elicited in one model, GPT-4. Nonetheless, troubling findings include underlying normative frameworks with clear bias towards particular cultural norms. Many models also exhibit disturbing authoritarian tendencies.
title: Comparing the Ethical Frameworks of Leading LLM Chatbots

abstract: The research investigated the impact of ethical leadership, professional development, organizational commitment, and workload on teacher effectiveness in public secondary schools in Region XII, Philippines. Employing structural equation modeling (SEM) with data from 400 stratified randomly selected educators, the study identified elevated levels of ethical leadership, professional growth, and organizational commitment among participants. The investigation revealed that professional development and organizational commitment exert direct, significant influences on teacher effectiveness, whereas ethical leadership and workload affect effectiveness indirectly. Essential components of teacher success encompassed preparation, classroom management, subject expertise, and interpersonal relations, whereas ethical leadership was defined by transparency, integrity, and ethical role modeling. The study underscores the necessity for policy reforms to augment professional development opportunities, fortify organizational commitment, and tackle workload concerns, with the goal of enhancing teacher efficacy. These findings endorse the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals pertaining to quality education, gender equality, well-being, decent work, and robust institutions, hence advocating for inclusive and high-quality education.
title: Ethical Leadership, Professional Development, Organizational Commitment, and Workload: A Structural Equation Model of Teachers’ Effectiveness
A Hybrid Approach to Statistical Machine Translation Between Standard and Dialectal Varieties

abstract: AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. Eight primary queries and one overlapping name-variant query were executed through the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API on 5 December 2025. English-language publications within a 1989–2026 search window were screened for substantive AI or robotics relevance and an explicit Husserlian anchor. Of 5,594 retrieved records, 32 publications from 1990 to 2025 were included. Nine publications recovered by a post hoc PhilPapers check were charted separately using the existing codebook; they were not added to the formal corpus. The corpus clusters around embodied AI, AI epistemology, cognitive architectures, and machine consciousness, with a newer generative-AI cluster. Constitution, intentionality, horizonality, and the lifeworld recur prominently. Conceptual translation, critique, and agenda setting predominate within this sample. Methodological import or design guidance occurs in seven of the 32 publications and three of the nine external publications. That difference qualifies generalization of the quantitative balance. Across both sets, Husserlian uptake spans conceptual interpretation, methodological transfer, and architectural proposals. The synthesis shows how distinctions concerning temporality, embodiment, and evidence can structure design and evaluation questions, while separating the authors’ research proposals from the mapped findings.
title: A scoping review mapping the role of Husserlian phenomenology in artificial intelligence research
Deep Ignorance: Filtering Pretraining Data Builds Tamper-Resistant Safeguards into Open-Weight LLMs

abstract: Change is the order of present times and is one of the permanent elements. Change can be planned and sometimes in planned events changes ensue. The result is seen and experienced. Organisations are focusing on change management wherein it is an approach to transitioning individuals, teams and organisations to a desired future state. Training is an effective HR tool and professionals agree that training is a complex human resource practice that can significantly impact any desired change. There are various factors like training, motivation, technology, management behavior, working environment where each factor contributes to the overall performance of individuals both in an organisation and even in society. There is positive relationship between the individual's performance and training followed by motivation that a person receives. Thus training has a positive impact on work and achievement of individuals. This paper deals with the transitioning of individuals. The paper explains the change that is found in individuals who underwent planned training. The training program by the name Persona: Education is Progress (EIP) was conducted for adult learners interested in personality development. After the training of three months that was conducted for six hours weekly by the authors on various aspects of personality development, the change in these individuals was measured and results notify that these beneficiaries have done exceptionally well in their walk of life. Although the future state of change was not planned by the trainers in this Persona series, results shown after the training program indicate a drastic positive change. Thus the authors emphasize the fact that training is a tool to effect change and if change is planned and the desired results are structured then training as an HR tool can be effective to bring about the change that is desired.
title: Training as a Tool to Ensue Change: A Case of Persona Personality Development Series

abstract: Conversational retrieval refers to an information retrieval system that operates in an iterative and interactive manner, requiring the retrieval of various external resources, such as persona, knowledge, and even response, to effectively engage with the user and successfully complete the dialogue.However, most previous work trained independent retrievers for each specific resource, resulting in sub-optimal performance and low efficiency.Thus, we propose a multi-task framework function as a universal retriever for three dominant retrieval tasks during the conversation: persona selection, knowledge selection, and response selection.To this end, we design a dual-encoder architecture consisting of a context-adaptive dialogue encoder and a candidate encoder, aiming to attention to the relevant context from the long dialogue and retrieve suitable candidates by simply a dot product.Furthermore, we introduce two loss constraints to capture the subtle relationship between dialogue context and different candidates by regarding historically selected candidates as hard negatives.Extensive experiments and analysis establish state-of-the-art retrieval quality both within and outside its training domain, revealing the promising potential and generalization capability of our model to serve as a universal retriever for different candidate selection tasks simultaneously.
title: UniRetriever: Multi-task Candidates Selection for Various Context-Adaptive Conversational Retrieval

abstract: Memory enables language model assistants to maintain continuity across sessions and generate personalized responses, but knowing more about a user does not necessarily produce responses they prefer. Existing evaluations assess memory capabilities without directly establishing whether memory use benefits the user. To study this gap, we collect approximately 1,000 pairwise judgments from 87 participants using their own ChatGPT queries and personal memories. We find that memory-conditioned responses are not consistently preferred over responses generated without memory and in some cases, users strongly prefer the latter. Automatic evaluators also show limited agreement with users and favor memory-conditioned responses substantially more often than users do. Motivated by these gaps, we introduce a memory-aware reward model that learns from user judgments, achieving 72.8\% preference prediction accuracy and outperforming the existing baselines. Our findings motivate evaluation and optimization objectives that align memory use with the preferences of the people whose information is being used.
title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use

abstract:
Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan menjelaskan: (1) kondisi objektif pembelajaran sastra dan kemampuan apresiasi siswa kelas X SMA yang selama ini dilaksanakan di sekolah; (2) rancangan model pembelajaran apresiasi sastra berbasis nilai sosial dan karakter tokoh novel Laskar Pelangi; dan (3) efektivitas Model Pembelajaran Sastra (MPS) berbasis nilai sosial dan karakter tokoh novel Laskar Pelangi untuk meningkatkan apresiasi siswa kelas X SMA. Pendekatan yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah pendekatan penelitian dan pengembangan (Research and Development) dengan kombinasi analisis data kualitatif-kuantitatif. Subjek penelitian adalah siswa kelas X SMA Negeri 1 dan SMA PGRI 1 di Kota Bandung tahun ajaran 2015/2016. Data penelitian dikumpulkan dengan menggunakan instrumen wawancara, observasi, angket, dan tes. Data penelitian diolah menggunakan teknik analisis kualitatif dan kuantitatif dengan uji statistik. Uji coba model dilaksanakan tiga tahap, yaitu uji validasi model oleh ahli/praktisi, uji terbatas, dan uji luas pada dua kelompok kelas berbeda di dua sekolah dengan memberikan prates dan pascates. Berdasarkan hasil pengolahan data pada kelas uji terbatas, hasil prates diperoleh nilai t sebesar 0,451, perbedaan nilai rata-rata prates sebesar 0,733 dan taraf signifikansi yang diperoleh lebih besar daripada taraf nyata (0,655 > 0,050. Sedangkan pada saat pascates diperoleh nilai t sebesar 24,332, perbedaan rata-rata nilai pascates sebesar 19,533 dan taraf signifikansi yang diperoleh lebih kecil daripada taraf nyata (0,000 > 0,050). Dari hasil prates dan pascates tersebut, menunjukkan bahwa pada saat prates tidak terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan, sedangkan pada saat pascates, terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara kelas kontrol dengan kelas eksperimen. Selanjutnya, berdasarkan hasil pengolahan data pada kelas uji meluas, pada saat prates diperoleh nilai t sebesar 0,224, perbedaan nilai rata-rata prates sebesar 0,3000 dan taraf signifikansi yang diperoleh lebih besar daripada taraf nyata (0,824) > 0,050). Sedangkan pada saat pascates diperoleh nilai t sebesar 21,190, perbedaan rata-rata nilai pascates sebesar 18,900 dan taraf signifikansi yang diperoleh lebih kecil daripada taraf nyata (0,000 > 0,50). Hasil prates dan pascates tersebut menunjukkan bahwa pada saat prates juga tidak terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan, sedangkan pada saat pascates, terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara kelas kontrol dengan kelas eksperimen. Dengan demikian, MPS reader’s response + Kh berbasis nilai sosial dan karakter tokoh novel Laskar Pelangi lebih efektif menigkatkan kemampuan apresiasi siswa kelas X SMA dibandingkan dengan Model Pembelajaran Sastra Metode Ceramah (MPSMC). ;
The research aims at investigating and explaining: (1) the objective condition of the literature learning and the appreciation skill of the senior high school tenth graders that are conducted in the school; (2) the blueprint of the literature learning model that is based on the social values and the characteristics of the Laskar Pelangi novel to increase the senior high school tenth graders’ appreciation; and (3) the effectiveness of Literature Learning Model (LLM) that is based on the social values and the characteristics of the Laskar Pelangi novel to increase the senior high school tenth graders’ appreciation. The approach used in this research was the Research and Development method with qualitative and quantitative data analysis combination. The participants of this study were the tenth graders of the 1 state senior high school (SMA N 1) and the PGRI 1 senior high school (SMA PGRI 1) in Bandung at the 2015/2016 academic year. The data for this research were collected using interview, observation, questioner, and test. The data were then analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively with the statistical tests. The piloting study was conducted in three stages: the validation of model was tested by the experts, the restricted tests, and the extended tests which were given to two different groups in two different schools using pre-test and post-test. Based on the results of the restricted test, it is revealed that the prestest t score is 0.451, the difference between the pretest means is 0.733 and level of significance is higher than the real level (0.655>0.050). Meanwhile in the postest it is revealed that the t score os 24.332 with the mean score is 19.533 and the level of significance is lower thatn the real level (0.000>0050). Based on those pretest and postest, it is demonstrated that there is no significant difference in the pretest; meanwhile in the posttest, there was a significant difference between the control and the experiment groups. Furthermore, based on the analysis of the extended tests, it is revealed that the t score of pretest is 0.224, with the diference of the pretest means is 0.3000 and the level of significance is higher that the real level (0.824>0.050). In the meantime, it is revealed that in the posttest the t score is 21.190, with the mean is 18.900 and the level of significance is lower that the real level (0.000>0.500). Based on those pretest and posttest, it is demonstrated that in the pretest there is no signitficant difference, while in the posttest there is a significant diference between the control grup and the experiment group. Therefore, the literature learning model (Model Pembelarajan Sastra / MPS reader’s response + Kh) that is based on the social values and the characteristics of the Laskar Pelangi novel characters is more effective than the lecturing method literature learning model (Model Pembelajaran Sastra Metode Ceramah / MPSMC) in increasing the appreciation skill of tenth graders of senior high school.
title: PENGEMBANGAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN SASTRA BERBASIS NILAI SOSIAL DAN KARAKTER TOKOH NOVEL LASKAR PELANGI UNTUK MENINGKATKAN APRESIASI SISWA SMA DI KOTA BANDUNG

abstract: The hybridization of television genres has led to numerous non-fiction television shows that base much of their success on audience engagement through social networks. This study analyses a specific case, that of La isla de las tentaciones (Temptation Island), to identify interpretive frames in reality shows and their interrelationships with audience involvement on Instagram. Based on a corpus of 8409 comments posted on Instagram by the followers of the program’s actor profiles, the article analyzes the lines between reality and fiction in this non-fiction television show about relationships and infidelity, and, in particular, how online “haters” play a performative role. The show’s participants who were unfaithful are insulted and receive numerous negative value judgments. The “coding and counting” method, drawn from Computer Mediated Discourse Analysis, is used for the coding. Results show that viewers barely allude to this show as fiction, do not differentiate between the actors and their characters, and empathize strongly with the stories they view. The study shows the need for media education, both for those who make the media and those who view it. The goal is not to detract from entertainment value, but to improve critical skills and to recover the educational function of media.
title: The Fine Line between Person and Persona in the Spanish Reality Television Show La isla de las tentaciones: Audience Engagement on Instagram

abstract: There remains considerable debate about the exact relationships between climate, conflict, and migration. This article draws on appeal applications to the Administrative Review Tribunal in Australia from asylum seekers from Sudan and South Sudan to trace links between climate-related conflict and asylum migration to Australia. We concur with the wider literature that conflict and asylum migration cannot be directly attributed to climate change; instead, we argue that climate change formed part of the context of the conflict, persecution, and displacement that led to these asylum appeals in Australia. We identify five broad conflicts with a climate change context in Sudan and South Sudan, demonstrating how political actors have harnessed resource scarcity and abundance in ways that generated conflict. Taking a historical approach, we show how climate vulnerabilities in Sudan and South Sudan intersected with political inequalities and divisions, how vanishing resources have been harnessed and exploited by political elites at the expense of marginalised communities, who have been systematically persecuted for resisting such inequalities. By focussing on the individual applicants’ backgrounds, situating them in broader conflicts, and drawing on the literature to find connections to climate change within conflicts, we foreground the human experience of climate-conflict-displacement.
title: Climate-conflict-displacement dynamics in asylum appeals to Australia from Sudan and South Sudan

abstract: Trademark confusion doctrine rests on an implicit theory of consumer perception. Courts infer confusion through proxies such as similarity, market proximity, intent, and evidence of actual confusion, presuming that consumers encounter trademarks in stable, human-designed environments. That premise no longer holds uniformly across contemporary markets. Today, consumers increasingly encounter trademarks through algorithmic systems that rank, cluster, recommend, and generate content on their behalf. This Article argues that trademark law’s likelihood of confusion doctrine has not yet reckoned with this transformation. In algorithmically mediated markets, confusion often arises without copying, deception, or misleading conduct by traders. Instead, it often arises from the way platforms organize what consumers see, shaping visibility and inference before any mark-to-mark comparison occurs. Applying traditional doctrinal proxies to these environments risks misdiagnosing the source of confusion and misallocating responsibility. The Article’s intervention has three parts. First, consumer perception is increasingly shaped upstream by platform design rather than direct mark-to-mark comparison. Second, core confusion factors such as similarity, strength, proximity, intent, and actual confusion can systematically misattribute causation when exposure is machine-mediated. Third, some contemporary harms deserve recognition as a distinct analytical category, which this Article terms algorithmic confusion: source-attribution errors that arise when platform design supplies the association that traditional doctrine attributes to the marks themselves. Rather than expanding trademark rights, the Article calls for a more precise account of how confusion is produced and who is responsible for it. Recognizing algorithmic confusion clarifies causation, restores doctrinal discipline, and preserves trademark law’s core focus on source identification. The Article concludes by cautioning against uncritical reliance on artificial intelligence to operationalize confusion doctrine and by outlining design principles for AI tools that support, rather than supplant, human judgment.
title: Trademark Confusion After the Algorithmic Turn
Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation

abstract: Constraints of length in this survey have obliged me to be selective. The bibliographies offered will enable students to fill gaps - and I have included books and articles in languages other than English for advanced students into whose hands this book may fall. The same need for conciseness has encouraged me to pass some swiftly enunciated judgements, which may assist the student to gain a handle on the topics, whether he or she agrees eventually with my assessment or not. Apart from its intrinsic interest, the theological history of Catholicism in the last two hundred years is essential reading for anyone who wishes to gain an understanding of the present state of the Catholic Church - most of all for anyone who would care to offer it informed counsel with the benefit of a historical (and not merely contemporary) feeling for its identity and the Juste milieu of the tendencies of its schools. I am grateful to Professor Gerald Pillay, formerly of the University of South Africa, for suggesting that I write this work, and to the Liturgical Press, Collegeville, and T and T Clark, of Edinburgh, for permission to include some short extracts from earlier material published through their kindness.
title: Catholic thought since the alignment: A survey

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can simulate person-like things which at least appear to have stable behavioural and psychological dispositions. Call these things characters. Are characters minded and psychologically continuous entities with mental states like beliefs, desires and intentions? Illusionists about characters say No. Characters are merely anthropomorphic projections in the mind of the user and so lack mental states. Jonathan Birch (2025) defends this view. He says that the distributed nature of LLM processing, in which several LLMs may be implicated in the simulation of a character in a given conversational thread, precludes the existence of a minded and psychologically continuous entity that is identifiable with the character. Against illusionism, we articulate and defend the plausibility of a realist position on which characters exist as minded and psychologically continuous entities. We contend that Birch's argument rests on a category error: characters are not internal to the LLMs that simulate them, but rather emerge in the dynamic interplay between users and LLMs through a process of mutual theory of mind modelling. We then suggest that characters, and their minds, constitute ''real patterns'' on grounds that attributing mental states to characters is essential for making efficient, accurate and robust predictions about the conversational dynamics (cf. Dennett, 1991); a condition which, if satisfied, is sufficient for their existence and mindedness on a plausible interpretationist form of realism about mental states. Furthermore, because the character exists as an emergent phenomenon within the conversational workspace, psychological continuity is possible even if the underlying computational substrate is distributed across multiple LLM instances.
title: Chuck, Wilson and the emergence of artificial minds in human-AI conversations
The Llama 3 Herd of Models

abstract: This paper develops a framework for an AI-assisted Chinese-Western cultural comparison course by bringing together Byram’s intercultural communicative competence model, Vygotsky’s constructivism, and Huang et al.’s theory of cultural competence development. It identifies five interrelated course goals: cultural knowledge, cross-cultural practical ability, critical cultural awareness, AI collaboration literacy, and human-AI symbiosis awareness. To achieve these goals, three teaching strategies are proposed. First, content should be reconstructed through multimodal and professionally adapted resources; second, the learning process should be immersive and adaptive; third, assessment should be data-driven and multidimensional to evaluate the goals. The implementation conditions of these strategies are further discussed in terms of teacher AI competence, human-AI boundary negotiation, algorithmic bias mitigation, and differentiated task design. It provides a structured basis for AI-assisted Chinese-Western cultural comparison teaching and for future empirical testing of its effects.
title: AI-Assisted Chinese-Western Cultural Comparison Course: A Conceptual Framework
The Lark of Minerva: Philosophy and the Making of Artificial Minds

abstract: As AI companions increasingly mediate repeated social interaction, users may rely on a stable role and shared history, yet locally acceptable replies do not ensure that either persists. We study two observable long-horizon failures: 'persona collapse', the loss of a deployed role, boundaries, values, or style, and 'behavioral drift', the gradual or recurrent erosion of those properties. We introduce ANCHOR, a controlled synthetic audit that separately measures persona enactment and trajectory recall. The study contains 2,008 conversations spanning 27 personas, nine interaction schedules, three generated memory settings, and four evaluated models. The Identity Probe combines a sealed 102-item questionnaire with turn-level judgments, while the Trajectory Probe scores 110 calibrated counterfactual questions from 35 conversation banks. Our results show that no evaluated model and configuration reliably preserves either dimensions: trajectory accuracy averages only 44.4%, user-state recall remains near four-option chance, and no tested context condition or memory consistently resolves these failures. Questionnaire retention also varies by model and persona facet, disagrees with turn-level behavior, and is sensitive to evaluator choice. These results indicate that current systems do not yet reliably support long-horizon companion continuity and that audits must distinguish persona enactment, trajectory recall, evaluator provenance, and deployment context rather than collapse them into a single trust or stability score.
title: Best Friends, Not Forever: Evaluating Long-Horizon Persona Collapse and Behavioral Drift in AI Companions

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has penetrated higher education not through official strategies but via students’ and faculty members’ personal devices, catching most universities off guard. This article presents empirical data from a large-scale survey conducted between March and April 2026 across six post-Soviet countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Tajikistan). The study provides a systematic cross-national analysis of student AI use patterns in the Eurasian higher education space, complementing recent single-country studies in the region. The sample included 478 students. The study measured frequency of AI use, perceived risks, compatibility with educational values, and the presence of institutional regulatory mechanisms. The results show that 78 % of students regularly use generative AI, yet only 32 % of universities have an official policy in this area. A deep disciplinary divide emerges: students fall into two roughly equal profiles – “pragmatic techs” (daily users with low ethical anxiety) and “reflective humanists” (cautious users with a strong demand for ethical frameworks). The main barrier to AI adoption is not technological infrastructure but the absence of regulatory and social technologies. The article offers discipline-differentiated recommendations for universities in non-Western contexts.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Eurasian Higher Education: An Empirical Study of Student Practices

abstract: EnglishThe ethics of an administrator is a theme little present canonical norms and reflection. Without pretence of filling up such a gap, the article, starting from a definition of ethics linked to the realization of the good of the person, above all tries to delineate the ethics of the administration of a juridic person. The fundamental reference is to the ends that are specific to the juridic person, to be realized when acting in the name of the Church”: not an abstract or atemporal Church, but the Church as incarnated the here and now. The ethical elements far an administrator can be mined however from the Code itself: honesty, loyalty, the diligence of a paterfamilias, accountability. To these are added rectitude of intention and freedom of action with respect to one's role. At its conclusion, the study underlines the importance of formation, both far administrators and also far the Christian community, on the meaning of the goods of the Church. italianoL'etica dell'amministratore e un tema poco presente nella normativa e nella riflessione canonistica. Senza la pretesa di colmare una lacuna, l'articolo, partendo da una definizione di etica riferita alla realizzazione del bene della persona, cerca di delineare anzitutto l'etica della persona giuridica amministrata. Per essa il riferimento fondamentale e alle finalita che le sono proprie, da realizzare agendo «a nome della Chiesa», una Chiesa non astratta e atemporale, ma incarnata nel qui e ora. Le istanze etiche dell'amministratore sono invece ricavabili dallo stesso Codice: onesta, fedelta, diligenza di buon padre di famiglia, accountability. A esse si aggiungono la purezza di intenzioni e la liberta rispetto al proprio incarico. Conclude lo studio la sottolineatura dell'importanza della formazione sia per gli amministratori, sia per la comunita cristiana circa il senso dei beni della Chiesa.
title: L'etica dell'amministratore dei beni ecclesiastici

abstract: Patronage, in the mid-and late-nineteenth century, was central to Canadian politics.This period also witnessed a series of debates concerning the civil service and a range of reforms that attempted to eliminate patronage.This dissertation argues that, more than debates about administration and appointments, these were also struggles over how to construct the ideal civil servant and civil service.These were highly political issues that were beset by processes of inclusion and exclusion, especially with respect to gender, class, and race.In short, these were debates about the many facets of liberal governmentality and state formation in early modern Canada.This dissertation also analyzes letters to federal politicians asking for appointments.Among other things, these documents expressed a range of opinions on how the bureaucracy should be managed, staffed and constructed.Letters asking for patronage also demonstrated how aspiring public servants understood and expected the appointment process to work.These letters reflected what type of people should have access to the civil service, and what type of people the applicants thought they were.As such, they informed and were themselves informed by broader political and administrative debates.These politics of Canadian patronage, I argue, were central to the everyday processes of state formation.
title: The Patronage Effect: Civil Service Reforms, Job-Seeking, and State Formation in Victorian Canada

abstract: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.
title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization

abstract: [ES] La industria de los videojuegos emplea habitualmente Máquinas de Estados Finitos (FSM) y Árboles de Comportamiento para controlar a los personajes no jugadores (NPCs). Aunque eficientes, estas técnicas generan comportamientos rígidamente deterministas, predecibles y susceptibles a ser explotados por los usuarios. Este Trabajo Final de Grado propone el diseño, implementación y evaluación de un agente inteligente autónomo capaz de aprender a jugar en un entorno tridimensional de disparos en primera persona (FPS) sin depender de lógicas preprogramadas. Para lograr este objetivo, se ha desarrollado una arquitectura computacional basada en el paradigma de la neuroevolución, combinando Redes Neuronales Artificiales superficiales y Algoritmos Genéticos. El sistema ha sido programado íntegramente de forma nativa en C# sobre el motor gráfico Unity, garantizando un rendimiento óptimo en tiempo real. El agente percibe su entorno dinámico mediante un sistema de sensores espaciales proyectivos (Raycasts) y optimiza su toma de decisiones tácticas (locomoción, recolección de recursos vitales y combate) a través de un proceso iterativo guiado por una función de aptitud (fitness) multivariable. El entrenamiento del agente se estructuró aplicando la técnica de Curriculum Learning, incrementando la complejidad de los estímulos de manera escalonada. Los resultados experimentales demuestran que el sistema es capaz de superar vulnerabilidades heurísticas severas, tales como la explotación de recompensas (Reward Hacking), los máximos locales y el olvido catastrófico. En conclusión, el proyecto valida la viabilidad técnica y la eficiencia computacional de los métodos neuroevolutivos para la generación de comportamientos tácticos adaptativos y emergentes dentro del sector del entretenimiento interactivo.
title: Desenrotllament de les nostres primeres xarxes de neurones artificials per a la seua aplicació en un videojoc First Person Shooter

abstract: Online child sexual abuse (OCSA) is a pervasive problem facilitated by the anonymity afforded to offenders online.
